6/12/26

Dang its been a while since I worked on the deck. I've been chatting with other Waveshaper players about tech and what the deck looks like in the post "Heirloom Lost / Mirage" world. Silver Bullet is gone for Meat Hook. There has been a lot of buzz about that card in the Waveshaper circle and I'm excited to try it. Same is true for Giant Shark. It's one of the original cards that made me obsessed with water in this game. The Sharks just dominate the body of water until answered, helping vs minion strategies, and pairs insanely well with Meat Hook. They're replacing Gloam Toads who had been feeling extra clunky recently. I've cleaned up the land base too to make it less susceptible to Heirloom Lost / Mirage.


Guile Sirens and Lacuna Entity are on notice. I love Lacuna Entity, but he might be redundant with the Giant Sharks.


3/1/26

Played a handful of games against Savior. The matchup feels totally fine. I did lose one game to a clunky hand and them drawing the nuts, but I won the rest without much issue.


2/23/26

6-2 at SorceryCon, and top Waveshaper. Going into the event I thought the deck would be competent, but it actually felt extremely good. The only decks I lost to all weekend between side events, the main event, and testing, were mono fire Pathfinder decks and a fire Sorcerer. Doing the math it works out to a 60% win rate which I'm very happy with. I don't think its worth trying too hard to make major adjustments for the bad fire match up. You can definitely still win those games and I'm not trying to over correct.


I'll add more to this primer when I get time. I've got thoughts. For now, check out @Zenatheshadow's Drown in the Deep primer. Its very in depth (unintentional joke) and expresses how I feel about the deck archetype.

decks.name: SCRCON 2026 | 7th Place | Constructed Championship
decks.primer:
"Evil, Fliers and Ranged, OH MY!"


The TLDR:


Evil:

  • Vile Imp, Redmayne Hyena, Spore Spouts and Desecrate. Do the math.
  • You know who loves Desecrated Ground? Evil minions. What's better than a 5 power Legion of Gall? A 6 power Legion of Gall.


Fliers:

  • We've got 14 fliers and over half of them are 4+ power and either gain us life, wreck our opponent's Collection, or just cause a friggin headache!


Ranged:

  • A playset of Stygian Archers and Skirmishers of Mu? Yes. And I'd play more if I could!
  • Shout out to MTR Joseph (the one and only Realm Eater pilot in the Constructed Championship at SCRCON) for enlightening me on how disgusting Skirmishers can actually be. To be continued in full primer...


Ideal Early Game Plays:

  • T1 Tower > Forsaken into a T3 Desecrate to mess with our opponent's Affinity
  • T2 Spore Spouts > Vile Imp into a T3 Desecrate
  • T3 Jack the Ripper their Aino or Morgana into a T4 Desecrate


omg why does this guy love Desecrate so much...


Desecrate:

  • Think back at games you lost because of a well placed Smokestacks, Thin Ice, Troll Bridge, Bottomless Pit, Perilous Bridge, etc... yea. Desecrate handles that.
  • Buff your minions. Forsaken seems innocent until it hits for 3, Desecrates for 3, and then becomes a 4 power minion. "We have Lugbog Cat at home, sweetie".
  • Timing is everything, though. If you can't Move and Attack with your Evil minion without risking a trade then you're not set up for a Desecrate. But we're piloting AoA baby, oh and we have even more tech for that... stay tuned for the full primer!


Other Spells:

  • Arcane Barrage beats Ward as long as you can pay the minions power + 1. It wreaks havoc on tokens, is nightmare fuel against Imposter and can close out nearly any game thanks to AoA's inherent maneuverability.
  • Browse to hunt for Desecrate... (i know, i have a problem)
  • Disenchant. Because Ring and A. Fate exist.
  • Feast for Crows. F**k Mesmerism. (Both games I've lost to CJ at major events he beat me with Mesmerism... well, and because he's a top-notch player)
  • Grapple Shot and Whirling Blades. I don't need to explain these - but - imagine your opponent plays their Archangel and you've got a Stygian Archers in play with a Trinket and Grapple Shot in hand. You Trinket your Archers, Grapple the Archangel to break ward and Ranged strike for 4 while getting an Allied Skelly to boot. It feels, so, good. Now imagine casting Whirling Blades on your Archers and killing more than one enemy minion to then replace each of them with Allied Skellys? Disgusting. Wait, Skellys are Evil right? Did someone say Desecrate?
  • Infiltrate and Poison Nova: unarguably two of the most impactful Fire spells at the single-Fire threshold level. These two spells are what forced me into splashing fire. Trust me, I hate having to run the castles, Colour and Ruins in place of other Air or utility sites, but I truly believe Infiltrate and Poison Nova are worth it.


Full primer to come...


Cheers and great games to everyone I played at SCRCON 2026!!!

decks.name: Battledragon 2026
decks.primer:
Early game

Your goal early game is to mulligan sites and hopefully get a defensive site in your second forward spot, slowing your opponent down until you can get 5-6 mana, and 3 air threshold. Bottomless pits are top teir, with void, perilous bridge and great wall also being great options. Play the rest of your sites in the back row, being mindful of you threshold being cutoff from atlantean fate. If you get witherwing heights make sure to have them nearby to Bottomless pit and Void to toss unwanted attackers.


Mid game

Your gonna hope for an early poison dagger, so you can remove any 1 enemy for 3 mana with your avatar. When this happens, all the pressure will be on your opponent and the game will feel easy. You want equip most relics onto your avatar, unless you have a move you can do alot of damage in 1 turn, or door your opponent. This part of the game is a balancing act where your trying to keep the board clean hopefully with your creatures but using avatar as necessary. The healthier you stay in this part of the game the better, using vampires and grappleshot and whirling blades to clear board and heal.


End game

At this point you will be playing mostly 1 card a turn, trying to hold a grappleshot,toolbox, tactical move while positioning for the deathblow. This is of coarse if you didn't equip a dagger and ring of morrigan and watch your opponent flip the table when they feel the full power of Adtonitum.


Things to watch out for

Avatar of air doesn't care for your sites placement as they play similar and can use your defensive sites against you.


If your playing against a water deck, and instead of building sites around your defensive sites, they start placing minions in the back row, your about to get ruler of thul/polor explorered. Place sites and minions accordingly to counter there attack.


Fire decks HATE to see bower hit the field. Boudicca/morgana/courtesian thias/saracen raiders all turned into puny beasts. The only mortal your running is princess which is worth nerfing to shut opponents heavy hitters off. Most of the time you can mulligan bower but if you know your against fire, hold onto it.

decks.name: 12th Place SCG DC Grand Contest - Whirling Auras (AF Enchantress)
League 10 Top 8 - F/W/A SIA Mage
decks.primer:
F/W/A SIA Mage


Sirprise It's Agrrovaine


A unique 3 element threshold intensive deck with high roll potential.


The thresholds are designed primary around 3/2/1 - F/W/A respectively. Primary goal is to get to 2/2 F/W, splashing air mostly for grapple shots and toolbox goodies. The third fire covers Morgana and Immolation.


Note: Technically new threshold reqs are 3/3/1 due to the addition of plague of frogs


The Mulligan


You're primary goal for an opening hand is two things, hit threshold and have a decent three drop.


Openers


Site placement is critical for success in more difficult games. The most important site you place is the your center forward site. What site you want there is match up dependent. If you're against aggro you want a troll bridge. If you're the aggressor whether your primary launch pad is water or land makes a big difference. The answer is that you want the opposite of whatever you're playing against. As an example if you're playing against a geomancer, you want your launch pad to be a water site because it allows you to drop threats safely to apply pressure on a site that can't have things buried on it. If you're against water you want a land site as a launch pad so your opponent can't drown minions on your own forward sites.


3 Drop & Sink'em

If on the play with the correct threshold play a sinkhole as your third site. Followed by a three drop minion, such as a cat or dragonettes. Immediately followed by blowing up the sinkhole to knock your opponent back down to one mana. On the next turn a good follow up is a grapple, a second three drop, or a swap.


Red Rover, I send my Doggie Over

If you're opening hand contains a Cerberus and a Grapple Shot, Cerberus can be forcefully moved away. Meaning an undefended avatar can take 10 damage on your turn 4, 3 if you started with a core or a P. Stone. If you're reading removal, this can be followed up by moving your battlemage forward to teleport Cerberus back safely depending on the match up.


Mini Combos


Dragonettes + Shrink

With a spellcaster (usually your battlemage) in position to shrink a minion along with a dragonettes that can be moved into position or cast from hand into line of site unobstructed allows you to shrink and kill a minion with your dragonettes.


Sir Pelleas + Blaze

A fun interaction unique to this element combination, elevated by the current meta of water. Pelleas free movement, along with blaze's defintion allows you to blaze many many locations depending on the board. My current understanding is free movement can't repeat steps, but this still allows him to freely deal 2 to large portions of a water based board.

decks.primer:
Yo! Welcome to the primer for my DS Self Mill Deck!

To start things off a quick history on me a tcgs and why im choosing this deck as my main passion project for the Sorcery tcg.


Basically for as long as ive been playing tcgs (started with Invasion block for mtg) ive loved using the graveyard as a resource. So naturally in mtg I was the reanimator guy and when I got a good collection I competed in legacy format events using a deck called Tin Fins and Dredge as a back up. I loved every minute of it too until mtg started doing things I heavily disagreed with and I dropped the game about 7ish years ago. When Sorcery was announced on KS it immediately gave me those mtg vibes I loved as a kid so I backed it. When I got my product I saw DS and knew this was the avatar for me and ive been working on making this deck as fun as I can so here we are haha.


So for the start behind this self mill deck is ever growing as I play more games against various avatars and opposing strats. The idea is pretty simple though, mill yourself to get that advantage asap. The advantage here is tons of card draw with those wizards and lots of minion generation with the necromancers. I also run a solid ordinary package that answers various problematic cards that exist in the game. The way I look at avatars is that each one offers the player a "cheat code" to help them win paired with piloting the deck correctly. DS "cheat code" is obviously using the graveyard as a second hand. When all this self mill stuff got printed in gothic my face lit right up and I felt at home haha. Something ive learned though is to not fill that yard up too fast, especially if the opponent is on fire, the bigger a yard you have the juicier a target it can become. Try to keep it minimal until you need new targets and go from there. In my maybe board I have a short stack of cards im considering and site hate is something ive added to it thanks to that unique fire site that kills my deck lol. Youll also notice I dont run ring, p stone, cores or other obvious "staple competitive cards" and I do that for a reason. I dont find those cards fun at all to play and im all about having fun here. If you want to run those no shame on you and feel free to edit the deck as you see fit to run the cards you want to run. Im choosing to run the token generating stuff to offer me good chump blockers or easy ping damage to opposing sites. Tokens in general are just annoying so it felt right to me and so far its been fun. Hotwheel has also been an all star for me. Killing random dudes or even putting in that finishing blow has been great. 3 might be overkill but I like running max copies of stuff when I can. I will say the mvp of the deck though is Skeleton Mage. I. Love. That. Card! Its so so good at everything this deck wants to do and casting Common Sense a million times in a game just feels criminal lol. But really it helps me always have an answer to my opponent with all the 1 of ordinary cards I run to be fetched with Common Sense. I also run some pet cards that happen to be very strong like good ol pudgy but besides that I tried making the deck with cards that function in my hand and graveyard to really abuse that "cheat code" I mentioned.


Hopefully this probably poorly written primer helps you all make your own sick DS decks and show my passion for the deck! So go out there and resurrect the realm in a fashion that fits you best!

decks.name: Dust Reanimator 8th SCGCon Richmond (3-2)
decks.primer:
Hi there! Please note that this Primer is a work in progress as I have time to write down my thoughts on the deck. In general this deck was an experiment to see if this archetype is currently viable (and because I love and always want to play Deathspeaker). As of right now I think that this deck, while fun and sometimes very powerful, is probably too high variance to post good results consistently. It has some very busted possible openings and can have a strong late game, but struggles a bit in the mid-game as it's minions start to get outclassed. Water is also a tough matchup due to having so much burrow removal, which is rough in the current water-heavy meta. All that being said, if you like to have explosive starts reanimating a vampire on turn 2 or 3, and like to grind incremental value out of your graveyard, this deck is a blast to play.


Minions

The Deathspeaker's bread and butter, minions with genesis or genesis-like abilities. This deck currently runs 39 minions, of which 26 have a genesis ability. It's my opinion that while you want a lot of genesis with DS, you really want to prioritize the cheap genesis minions and look for higher impact minions in the 4+ parts of the curve. I rarely want to deathspeak the more expensive minions in this deck, preferring instead to double spell one with some removal or another cheap minion. The exceptions to this are those minions like Bane of Aventis or Archangel Michael that can shore up a tough matchup, get you back in the game, or win out of the graveyard. The knights, pudge, witherwing, returned king, and the vampires are just there as strong minions at their point in the curve, and for undead to work with carrionette.


Auras and Artifacts

I originally had the two relevant cores in the deck and decided for this playstyle that they just aren't necessary. You'd rather be milling or reanimating in the early turns and the cores don't really help with that, and they always feel terrible to draw in the late game. Ring is ring, it's just too good not to play, even though we aren't super mobile with our avatar. Book of the dead provides additional recursion to help us profit from the self mill, and can get back some of our non-undead stuff in the late game. The black plague is our best answer to root spider and coy nixie, and the deck is otherwise soft to those most annoying of minions.


Magic

Our magic is generally one for one removal and sweepers, with the additional reanimates in 3 Carrionettes. I think Carionette is just great with the 5 vampires, and I love to see it early or late. The Bolts and Burys are just ways to help keep pace with stronger minions in the early game. Gift of the wolf is great with the small minions and the vampires as a way to trade up or gain some extra life, or both. Earthquake does a lot of work to stabilize, though it often will get less value than you want because of the abundance of water sites running around. Craterize has been good occasionally, but I intend to cut it from the deck. I almost always am too far gone/on DD to play it effectively, or have enough relevant minions that I don't want to kill them. I will probably add the fourth Gift of the wolf and maybe another Bury instead, or possibly keep just one.


Sites

Building a wall up front of bridges, hollows, and heights is ideally what you want to be doing, which you can then fly around later or traverse with your small minions. Gumming up the ground for the first few turns is pretty critical against the more aggressive strategies. The self-mill sites are so good in this deck, it can't be overstated. I often mulligan aggressively to find one, especially if I have Boneyard or Orpheus' Crossing in hand.


Both Boneyard and Orpheus' Crossing are high risk, high reward plays, but I think the potential is worth it. Both feel insane on turn 2, though you have to be very careful with Crossing to consider how your opponent might kill you the next turn. Having blockers for minions and projectiles is highly recommended. Both the reanimate sites feel bad in the mid-game unfortunately, and I sometimes got stuck holding them. However, if you can get a Gargantula in the cemetery it effectively negates whatever your opponent might summon on Boneyard (for the most part). Crossing is also amazing for getting you back in the game if you are already on DD.


I often drew Apex of babel without the Base, and I would probably cut these sites for something better. The idea is fun, but I can't run the full 3 bases without making cuts to better sites. Would consider replacing them with Mount Ussar Sanctuary and a watchtower or other air utility site. The misers lookout is just another ordinary site to help mitigate Atlantean Fate blowouts.

decks.name: 1st Place GenCon HOT SPRINGS
decks.primer:
Hi Team,


Excited to share about the deck, but first would be remiss if I didn't give credit and thanks to my team, Chris @Ismarkthelesser and Nick @Astronomonov, as well as John @PorkchopSandwitches and Blake @Collision for the insight and countless games that provided the context into many of these choices. As much your win as mine!


Also, to Pascal, my finals opponent. Thank you for one of the hardest, funnest, and friendliest games I've ever played. Despite the stakes, I appreciate how we approached the game as though we had already felt like winners just being in the seat, and counter each other. You are a champion.


Hot Spring has been a work in progress for ~8 months, after countless iterations, this is where we have landed currently.


Original deck list of where it all started.


GenCon 2025 Finals Match


Deck spotlight with Chase and EC team.


Now, into the deck.


Weaknesses: Fire and Water offer NO aura hate (outside of Scorched Earth), which means impactful auras stick around. Generally, you can outpace a deck with aura strategies, but not always. This also means no Monument hate either. This wouldn't have been a problem pre-Archimago's rise to fame, but now we're seeing more and more Orbs. Luckily, you are able to capitalize on the orb as well, with double Shatter Strikes and Minor Explosions worst case. This has changed with the inclusion of Swap; however, these problems do persist. Ironically, I think the biggest nemesis to the deck is itself, as in the last 5 major tournaments, I lost in the top 16 or higher against the mirror match. It was my bane.



A quick breakdown of each section of the deck and logic behind the card:


Auras:

  • Jihad: Self-explanatory. One of the most powerful fire cards ever printed. This card allows 5 power Monstrous Lions on turn 3 with a pond.


  • Atlantean Fate: Look at that, also one of the best cards ever printed. This primary function is to allow you to disrupt the Archimago's and other greedy threshold decks. It also provides a path to clear out popular problematic sites, like Free City, Pebbled Paths, and even Perilous Bridges. Also kills root spiders if they are on a sight that can be affected.


Artifact:


  • Torshammar Trinket: Druid can abuse this by always having access to Tawny. Probably a 3 of in most decks at this point.


  • Ring of Morrigan: IMO the strongest card in a vacuum ever printed, but particularly abusable in this deck. In conjunction with Drums, the ability to IG-88 your way through your opponent's team while also gaining life is backbreaking to say the least.


  • Mask of Meyham: With the strike change, we felt this or GG were too valuable to run, but the questions were, which one, and how many copies? Assuming there would be a concentration of Archimagos, we felt 1 Mask and 1 drums was the right call, as drums can feel dead against the few creatures in most Archimago's lists. This has a synergy with Sir Agravaine (we will cover that on his bullet point) and with the concentration of smaller minions, we thought the mask was better than GG.


  • Drums of Doom: Can lock down the game in a (candidly) un-interactive way. In a minion-heavy meta, expect druids to have 2x of these in their deck. Ring + this. Deserts, Tawny, vile Imp, all kill spells now. Also, the only way to protect against Nymbus Djinn otk.


Minions:


  • Polar Explorers: This quickly became one of my favorite cards in the deck. It enables SO much and makes cards like Redcap Poweries and Monstrous Lion have less drawback by evading problematic sites.


  • Vile Imp: 2 damage on entry, Kill spell with Drums. Takes out knights holding lances often and is just one of the best 2 drops in the game.


  • Kobolds: With the 3 of trinkets, and the prominence of Gnome Hollows, these angy little dudes provided, in most cases, bare minimum, 3 extra copies of Vile Imp, but with an insane ceiling. Also combos with strike synergy, kills tough airborne minions like Plumed Pegasus if comboed with deserts or Trinket. Very easy to deal with their tempo play with one of these early.



  • Lugbog Cat: Amazing tempo play with Pond, can reach into opponents' site with Floodplain. Solid beast.


  • Morgana le Fay: Soooo much value with this card. Boneyard target at the very least for more cards. Helps in grindy games.


  • Redcap Powries: Cheapest charge minion for the stats. Almost no downside at this point with the immobilized nerf.


  • ***MVP Sir Agravaine***: Self-protecting unit that buffs Tawny's attacks. Has proven to be a huge problem and is not answered with non-targeting damage. Enables one to turn deaths doors with only a few minions striking the avatar. With the recent attack trigger change, he will always strike the *original* target. Meaning, while adjacent to an enemy avatar being attacked, he will ALWAYS strike the avatar regardless of whether there are blockers around. This singlehandedly won me 2 of my games late in the bracket and is an absolute kill on site card.



  • Boudicca: Buffs Tawny and can just be a sudden death's door machine. Boneyard target for surprise extra damage due to getting value off her passive immediately. (if they aren't already dead by then).


  • Monstrous Lion: Has been one of the biggest standout cards. Combos with Pond, great target for Guyer to be used as a kill spell on a body. Great with all of the Battle Mages, as it gets value immediately, and also serves the 3 power.


  • Selfsame Simulacrum: After the recent revision of how multiple Bruins interact, this became too good not to run, though it never came up in my finals match. With multiple other targets, or your opponent's best minion, plenty of value to be had with this card.


  • Ruler of Thul: Similar role to Boudicca. Burst potential. Awesome surprise play with flipping Druid into Bruin, then following that up on the next turn with a Ruler for 8 in their back row with the free unit in Bruin. Also recursive with Lady of the Lake.


  • Sir Gaheris: Decent stats, and it does play well against many aggro decks, by being able to keep life parity and block, which is nice.


  • Panorama Manticore: Similar role to Phoenix, early bruiser that is hard to deal with. Untaps regularly and trades well.


  • Questing Beast: Also a Bruiser, awesome burst potential with attack from stealth and shatter strike. Mastering the art of the end-of-turn step turns this card from a great card to an absolute menace! With the ability to attack, then step back onto a watersite protects this to get you multiple strikes of 25% of their starting health.



Magics:


  • Geyser: Started out as a way to deal with Root Spider has quickly become one of my favorite cards. Providing airborne to these units increases their lethality dramatically, allowing them to avoid many problematic defensive sites. Also is a good combo with Blaze as it really extends the range with + movement and the ability to fly nearby.


  • Pollimorph: hard removal is pivotal right now with the abundance of 5+ power minions and vampires' abilities to Deaths Door you and heal for a billion while attacking sites. Also, the fact that it banishes the transformed card is actually a huge boon.


  • Minor Explosion: I started with 3 firebolts; however, the prevalence of Morgana Le Fey ultimately had me consider this instead. The indiscriminate 3 damage has a higher ceiling and, with the reach of Tawny, can easily be a 2 for 1.


  • Disintegrate: Similar to Pollimorph. Hard removal easily cast from Tawny.


  • Pact with the Devil: This has been one of my favorite cards. Combining with Tawny, Adept Illusionist, and Morgana (more niche) allows you to keep up with Sorcerer and Archimage in the mid-late game.


  • Swap (Placeholder in deck as Font of Life because they have the same mana and threshold): My friends and I had a feeling this card would be absolutely broken, and it sure felt good. This replaces Shatter Strike in the deck, and I have 0 regrets. Super flexible, and stealing Pstone and Rings while putting your guy directly on them feels AMAZING.


Key Sites:


  • Floodplain: Always been one of my favorites due to its ability to allow you to play more greedy with your threshold in Water, but also serves the purpose to kill root spiders and other burrowed minions and to extend reach on Lugbog cat.


  • Pond: MVP site: So many beasts in the deck make a dramatically increased impact by coming out a turn earlier. Tower for beasts, but better. Also amazing that with the prominence of earth still, being summoned onto a water site protects the beast you curved out from burry effects.


  • Desert: Are key to taking momentum. Also protects against enemies, Atlanian Fate turning off the critical threshold needed to cast key spells.


  • Boneyard: Though I never saw it at gencon, in my testing this card has been an amazing addition to the atlas. With several of the hard removals banishing, and access to Funeral Pyre, you can construct a sided resurrection. Also, with the concentration of charge units, you are able to bring back a Redcap, for instance, and attack with it, and because the unit they brought back entered the same turn, it will have summoning sickness. It also lets you bring back your "Win button" unique for its powerful genesis or passive abilities. Lastly, in what I presumed to be a Archimago heavy meta, the lack of minions they generally have allow this to be onesided even more regularly. It was my favorite spice in the deck.


  • Kelp Cavern: I originally hated this card when it was first printed. I thought the lack of "may" made it unplayable. I was wrong. This lets you comfortably mulligan to get better gas early, then go back and find your spells later when needed. I have been very, very impressed with it.


You may notice a lake of Smokestacks. I found, with a number of key genesis, and the draw cadence of the deck, you end up having to play it earlier than you'd like. This turns off your important sites, like deserts and flood plains, which can be really detrimental. Also, with flooding being an ability, smokestacks removes your ability to flood and kill rootspider. So I found it more detrimental than helpful in many matchups.

Two events played. Was 10-1 until I lost both of games #7 and #8 in the swiss rounds of the main event. Better luck next year!


Was planning on playing my earth build in the main event but after doing so well on Friday I ended up playing my mono air list for the main event. I beat 3 water necros in swiss on day #1. The main way this deck counters water builds is by using phyxis and sinkhole. Then aggro'ing them out. The idea is to be as sticky as possible w/ voidwalk, airborne and stealth. The Hounds of Ondaros are all-stars. Having airborne and whirling blades is so crucial for removal.


The main removal of the deck is to play the sites strategically and hopefully pull a bottomless pit, the void, or manor. If I don't get one of those sites in my starting hand I hard mulligan all 3 sites. Relying on this removal strategy works when it works. Its problematic when it doesn't work. Fire Pathfinder that I played at Sorcery Con 2026 - took 12th place on tiebreakers (6-2) with a very narrow loss in the last round (got the door first but didn't manage to top deck the kill - really epic fight and super well played by my opponent Ismark the Lesser). Pretty simple deck, not much to say about it. Definitely still lots of fine points to playing it though. In the current meta I think one of the big tricks with this deck is not overplaying onto the board while maintaining pressure. Especially into the "Creature Control" meta with lots of Water and Water/Air midrange decks this deck wins on tempo, but loses big to mass removal. You want to mulligan for minions early (maybe keep a single removal spell if you also have some low cost minions but top priority is having 2 and 3 drop minions to start the pressure game. Once you have a minion or two on board though you are just trying to maintain that.


The other common way to win with this deck is setting up a big turn where you blast in a bunch of damage with something like warp spasm, blaze of glory, betrayal, etc. Lots of other cards that go well in this deck, but everything is fighting for slots. Would love to run Shatter Strikes or maybe even Critical Strike to lean more into burst damage turns.


Really torn about Baba Yaga - I don't want more than 5 non fire sites (including mirror realm), so is the extra motion potential that is useful like 50% of the time it is played worth it, or am I better off just running a lone tower to get that ramp value..... Or wizard's Den for the extra card?

decks.name: Silent Fury SorceryCon 17th place
decks.primer:
This deck was very good, and I feel like a good choice for the field of decks present at SC. It's essentially the fury road shell with an emphasis on silence effects. I went 6-2 with this list at Sorcery Con 2026, losing round 2 to mud Geomancer, and round 8 to AoA. It won against 3 Necro decks, Avatar of Earth, fire pathfinder, and an Elementalist brew.


Notable cards:

Sister Stefánia - this card is a power house. I don't think any of the games I had it were close.

Sinterfee - this card is very good against the water decks. Paired with jihad it's amazing.

Corruptor freak - harasses well and can just move to sites forcing multiple interactions to answer it often into a just summoned fatty blocker

Rift valley/smokestacks - these are kind of the same slot because they let us bypass our opponents annoying sites. Expect your opponents to have very good sites. Having ways around them was very helpful.

Earthquake - this card does everything this deck wants. It helps get around sites, it kills stuff allowing you to attack, and most the time just moving the opposing avatar close to your attackers is good enough, get them on DD even if they are on all water sites.

Flame strike (collection) - I think I killed more avatars with this than anything else. You are pretty much always one step away from a hit on DD with this.

Onslaught - I think in many ways this is better than gift of the wolf even without the card draw. It makes spiders worthless, gives you a little charge when needed the spread out damage buff is often better than +2 on a single creature. It also lets you do silly things with your silence/disabled effects like play a slobermaw silenced then give it charge. Or allowing a sleeping giant to wake itself up by attacking a unit. I'll be testing with two copies.


Cards I'm considering cutting:

Blightstone - I got a little sold on this card by a friend. I didn't draw it very often, and each time it was kind of dead in my hand. There were a few times I wanted it. But sinterfee is almost always better.

Hyena - there's just not enough demons that are worth playing. I played it a lot as a 2 power creature, and had mixed feelings about it.

Leadworks - while annoying sites can be problematic for this deck this card never quite lined up the way I wanted. Its really hard in a deck that only wants to play 4 sites to have this line up with a threat in play and a site you need to deal with for a turn.

Slumbering giantess - this card was harder to wake up than I'd like. I still think it's good but it probably needs some other tweaks (more deserts?) to make worth it.

Critical strike (collection) - this was always supposed to be a spin attack, but I get these two chronically confused. Luckily they're pretty close to the same effect.

decks.primer:
This is a mean deck. It won’t win you many friends but it will win you many games. The name of the game is burn it down or beat them down fast. Using site destruction to slow down or cripple your opponent or minions with immediate impact (i.e. charge, damage on genesis, damage at end of turn). The deck is purposefully built low to the ground for a quick start and eventually multi-spelling at higher mana totals.


Site Destruction Strategies

The main strategy of this deck is site destruction. It utilizes [[Hamlets Ablaze]] and [[Castles Ablaze]] to target defensive sites and your opponents threshold. There’s nothing worse than having a hand full of double pip spells and you constantly lose the threshold to cast them. [[Raze]] can be used to destroy opponents sites but more importantly their artifacts. It’s great for dealing with [[Dank Omphalos]] and its brethren, [[Battlemage]] with a shload of equipment, and if need be popping [[Roots of Yggdrasil]] for a complete board clear. Twice in the tournament, I cast [[Raze]] on my avatar and destroyed Roots the turn it came into play and that won me the game.


TO BE CONTINUED

decks.name: Silenced Bones - 3rd Place Elemental Series Q1 2026 (Sydney, Australia)
decks.primer:
Silenced Bones is a Necromancer mid-range deck supported by a Beast package and a Silence package.


Silence got a huge buff in Gothic with [[Silent Hills]] (and [[Sister Stefania]]) and I believe the archetype can be a great anti-meta option.


The Silence part of the deck shuts down the majority of the card pool, and manh ability-based archetypes like Ward. It is also the enabler for many parts of the Beast package, and other above curve minions such as [[Pirate Ship]] and [[Dalcean Phalanx]]. [[Silence]] itself is (W), so we include this element in the deck.


(E), on the other hand, is the nature (pun not intended) of the Beast archetype, and it is also the only archetype that works with Silence. The mana efficient minions like [[Sedge Crabs]] become a menace, while [[Pudge Butcher]] can transition between a hook thrower and a 4-cost 5-power demon. [[Assorted Animals]] is a 2+ card advantage for you if [[Haystack]] is not in play.


The general strategy is to pump out skeletons to attack AND defend (Silenced skeletons are great blockers!) using [[Necromancer]] with spare mana whenever possible, while taking favourable trades with above-curve Silenced minions. The deck either overwhelms the board or stalls enough time with Silence and defensive sites like [[Troll Bridge]] and [[Babbling Brook]] for a [[Craterize]] straight to Death's Door, followed by a finisher such as [[Zap]] or [[Ice Lance]].


Peculiar card choices:

  • [[Sir Yvain]] screams BEAST. If you're playing Beast, you should play him.
  • [[Garden of Eden]] is your wincon against any draw-heavy decks like [[Sorcerer]] and [[Deathspeaker]]. HARD MULLIGAN for it (3 sites + scry the sites deck). Otherwise, you'd better pray you out-draw them with [[Algor Omphalos]] or win the game in 5-6 turns (you won't, but you can try!).
  • [[Carrion Beetles]] is the vegetable that everyone refuses to play (graveyard hate) and is searchable via [[Common Sense]] and [[Assorted Animals]] with just (1).
  • [[Porcupine Pufferfish]] is an Ordinary Beast with Lethal for (1) (Don't silence him, let him speak!).
  • [[Harvest Festival]] is essentially a (3) spell for 4 in the form of two 2-power bodies. Very underrated!
  • [[Goat for Azazel]] is another good (1) Beast. You can use Silence to turn off his ability when you need to put him down early.
  • [[The Flood]] is a very good late-game board wipe in this particular deck because we play so many types of minions, letting us keep our board while deleting everything without Submerged (Silence also remove Submerged!).
  • [[Forlorn Keep]] is a 3-power body in the form of a site. Sometimes you may want to play this turn 3 to churn out [[Penitent Knight]], or turn 4 with an extra skelly instead of playing cards from your hand. [[Peculiar Port]] serves similar roles, but having an Evil minion may be disadvantaged in some matchups such as [[Persecutor]] or any [[Consecrated Ground]] users.
  • [[Pebbled Paths]], [[Impenetrable Copse]], and [[Haystack]] are interchangeable depending on your local meta. My local meta loves cards like [[Grapple Shot]] and [[Firebolts]].


Overall, this is a really fun deck to play and learn the basics of the game while being very budget-friendly. The list is kept as-is and may need to be optimised for future tournament plays (for example, [[Sister Stefania]] would be a great inclusion, if I had it...).


Shout out to Dean Gouskos and Allen Thrun for hosting the event and carrying the Sydney community on their backs!

decks.primer:
Edit after local tournament (ended up 3:2)

Added extra sinterfree as an answer to those Coy Nixies and also 1 Infernal legion which can be realy great finisher.


Overview

This is a standard aggro build with some spicy inclusions from the Gothic set. The deck aims to apply early pressure, spread threats across the board, and force your opponent into a defensive death door as quickly as possible.


Key Card Choices

Draught — A silver bullet for water-heavy matchups. If the meta shifts toward water decks, this card can completely swing the game in your favor, especially when drawn early.

Gift of the Serpent — Excellent cycle card that also enables your low-value minions to trade up into larger threats. Never underestimate the tempo this provides.

Sinterfee — Fantastic removal bait. Opponents often feel compelled to answer this card immediately, which clears the way for your actual key threats. Whether it eats a removal spell or sticks on the board, you're winning either way.


Site Selection

Since this avatar doesn't rely on drawing a site for its power, I've included utility sites that disrupt common strategies:

  • Garden of Eden — Shuts down control decks that depend on card draw
  • Temple of Moloch — Provides extra mana for explosive combo turns
  • River of Blood — Neutralizes Ring of Morrigan healing, which works in our favor as the aggressor
  • Kor Krematory — Absolutely devastating against graveyard-reliant avatars

Mulligan Guide

Look for strong 2–3 drops. War Horse is particularly valuable for establishing sites in enemy territory, which is almost always advantageous for our gameplan.


General Tips

  • Don't stack minions together — cards like Earthquake and Atlantean Fate punish clustering
  • Spread your threats across the board
  • Prioritize attacking sites to accelerate your opponent's deaths door
  • Accept that aggro has variance — your first three draws heavily influence your win rate


Good luck and go fast!

decks.primer:
If you’re wondering “Why not card X?” Well…I’ve been playing this game for less than a month if you can believe it. I fell in love with the game and dove right in. During the event I traded my tickets for AL packs and opened the ring you see in the list at the end of round 4!!! I was so excited =). No Decklists…so in it went. Edit: I was asked to add a note to the primer. Judges were aware that I replaced a card in the middle of our no decklist tournament that wasn’t at compREL. Is it technically allowed? I honestly don’t know. I wasn’t shy about how excited I was and was telling everyone around me though =)


There were a lot of cards that didn’t really come into play much, but the early game and the repeated value are the core of the deck. We can play 1:1 removal because we’re going to get SO much value out of our cards. The mill sites were amazing. Observatory plus rats is incredible. Archangel Michael and Gargantula along with grandmaster wizard and master necromancer are our all star value cards to play from the cemetery.


The bolts and gifts were very often used to surprisingly put our opponent to door when they least expect it, doing 10 or more quite suddenly in one turn using the skeletal mages.


I’ve already taken the silver bullets out. Added a shrine of the dragon lord picked up at the event and making room to bump apprentice and novice back up to 4. Removed Gall as well. My opponents just weren’t using their collections enough, although I could see those coming back later in the year.


I want to try the 6 cost angels but I’m just trying to stay VERY focused on our plan at the moment and they don’t do anything from our cemetery.


My first 3 rounds all involved root spiders. I read the card before the event but didn’t realize so many people play these things. They constantly locked down angels, but I still found a way to chip damage and close with blots plus zap. After my third round I brainstormed with my opponent how to kill root spiders and all we could come up with is a burrowed rat with gift of the wolf for now. Every time I drew a toolbox I made sure to ask myself “should this just be zap or do I need it now”.


Water opponents are a problem. I lost to Mitch who played an unanswered Lilith into Pied Piper, two cards I didn’t even read before the event. After reading pied piper I just said “uh…yeah okay, I’m gonna go walk the hall. Congratulations.” lol…maybe I should have toughed it out, but he had already lured a unit, got a hit off of Lilith and established a frontline of troll bridge and thin ice. It was round 5 and I made the choice to relax before the last round.


6 rounds of Sorcery was incredible. I would repeat that day several times over if given the choice. I’ll definitely be back! Thanks for reading =)


Things I want to try next: I want to find some more room for top end. We can get a bit grindy with our tiny dudes and have some trouble closing. The bolts and gifts are really important for pushing damage but a touch more top end or mid could help. I want to try splashing red, but I feel like the double threshold sites really reward us for playing two elements right now with these powerful angels and triple threshold cards like gargantula. I do see how the red cards could give more closing power though. I didn’t like the tap requirement of silver bullets and the fact that we only have 2. I’m not sure what else to do with our collection yet but honestly it could just be 10 ordinaries.


I also want to try playing all of the cores with the red splash and the tri sites to have more access to playing from the opponents cemetery. ATM I do think the consistency of two elements is worth it.

decks.name: 1st Place Cornerstone w/Gothic (6-0) The Red Comet
decks.primer:
I registered for my LGS’s Cornerstone (we put in a lot of effort to get that status - should out to Battlegrounds in Richmond, VA!) but hadn’t played for five months. Going into the tournament, I needed 1) an Avatar I had at least some experience with 2) a deck that was pretty easy to pilot 3) something that could hopefully win or not make me look entirely foolish ;)


After looking at my old pre-Gothic decks, I landed on the “red deck wins” Pathfinder in a dusty deck box. I figured, “there have to be some cool new toys and more fire sites,” and I was pleasantly surprised. There’s a fair amount of Gothic in this deck as a result! I would add a Horns of Behemoth for the Wasteland if I had pulled one and I totally overlooked Vindictive Nation, which is also an easy add in lieu of one of the duals.


The Avatar pilots no differently than before, you have to attempt the optimal pattern to enable a path to at least six sites, but either via Giant, Warhorse, or just walking over a few sites, you can easily get to 10+ simply because of the tempo you have.


The deck archetype is classic sligh/red deck wins. You simply want to be as aggressive as possible. Gift of the Serpent, especially with Dragonettes, is AWESOME for taking out problematic minions. Searing Truth is an MVP as it gets you even more cards if you need them, but can also kill an Avatar instantly on DD. I’d definitely figure out a way to cut some things (I.e. Minor Explosion) to get up to max for each of those. I didn’t bother with any of the collection artifacts as they are simply too slow. The only collection card is a Hounds in case you elect to cast it from Molten Maar.


If you’re looking for something than can simply

blitz out a win, particularly before folks figure out deck efficiency and the meta, this may be a good choice for you. I’d you’re looking for something with some neat combos and cool interactions, there are a few, but really this is all about the burn. Enjoy the heat!

decks.name: GenCon 11th - F/W/A Sirprise it's Aggrovaine
decks.primer:
Font of life = +1 Swap


F / W / a Steam Mage

Elements: Fire, Water, Air

Archetype: Midrange Tempo


It's an update version of these decks:

  • Detroit 2024 - https://curiosa.io/decks/cm3iwz25l0018bpm7ka2yh6bq
  • Explorer Series Ohio - https://curiosa.io/decks/cmc4tb7bw003nkw0491vbl26g
  • League 8 Top 16 - https://curiosa.io/decks/cm3iwz25l0018bpm7ka2yh6bq


Event Information

I piloted this deck to 11th place in the first crossroads event at Gencon 2025. Below are game recaps as best I can recall them.


I went 5-2 at Gencon, losing to Duo (the Champ) and CJ (another 6-1 player).


Game 1: vs Druid (win) Murray - Turbo Redneck

Great first match that came down to the wire. Managed to maneuver my way into a win with a well timed shrink + grapple shot. Was against a fellow league player who was playing large charge minions. I managed to stabilize and find a good turn for door, where I moved over to shrink a Pellinore preventing my opponent from dooring me the following turn. Followed by a grapple shot to get across the map with a Cerberus in Chains in tow to door him.


Game 2: vs Archi (win) - IDK

I had a semi slow start on this game, but the Archi was attempting to burn me out instead of removing early threats. I drew into Ring cleared his few minions and doored him a turn before he could craterize.


Game 3: vs AoA (win) - Nick

Cerberus in Chains put in a lot of work this game, before getting polli'd. A very scary game where I had Grim in hand with the opponent at 12. I drew into a lighting bolt hoping my opponent would think that a cloud city was enough to get away. I doored him in those two turns while he doored my through hippogriffs. And the opponent did move onto cloud city to get out of line of sight.


Game 4: vs Druid Steam (win) Bruce - Golden Eagle

Extremely close game, where I made a huge mistake in playing a grapple that I shouldn't have been able to. Which would have been a near 20 to door play. Golden handled my mistake really well and we managed to reset the game state to where the error occurred. It was easily the most intense game of sorcery I've played in my life where every little maneuver mattered. After a decent back and forth I managed to stabilize by drawing into a ring and making odd plays like casting a grapple into nothing just to kill a minion with a ring ping.


Game 5: vs Druid Steam (lose) Nate - Duo

Very close game that in retrospect I could of won. I missed a game winning play through defenders that I'm kicking myself pretty hard about. The setup was my BM with on his forward center site, with a Cat and Adept behind. A twany to the left and an Agravaine with his Avatar, I was not aware of a rule change to Agravaine trigger where he now hits the original attack target. An embarrassing blunder since I play the card so frequently. It's hard to explain my head state during the game, but I was definitely thrown for a loop. After trinketing his Agravaine, and moving it into a space out of his next play a Mask of Mayhem I didn't have a way to not end up at door. I ended up not blocking the Twany which was the right move. But my brain went a bit haywire and kept thinking the cat could die to Agravaine. So with no mana left for my opponent I should have blocked the avatar attacking my BM with the cat in addition which would have doored my opponent on his own turn and left me with two attackers to one blocker. But alas Duo took a risk and it paid off, he played well and patiently and the better player won the game. Was a fun but disheartening game.

Also it was the game of a Twins revenge since Duos brother is the AoA I had beat in round 3.


Before the last turn I also believe I made a few other mistakes that include

  • Placing my third site incorrectly allowing my opponent to connect a land bridge onto my side, which allowed him to kill my first adept. I ended up drawing into the second, but if I had been able to pull the other out I would of had another card to help me fight. The misplacement of the site also led me to use my minor explosion to get rid of a 3 power charger, a card that would have been very useful against Agravaine.


Game 6: vs Druid Shapeshift (lose) CJ

Nerves got to me after my first loss and I got hyper aggressive too early with bad reads into a hand that was well suited against my deck. They were the kind of mistakes that you can't make at that level and against a player as good as CJ who won't hesitate to capitalize. Very quick game


Game 7: vs Druid (win) Seth

A scary start turned into a steam roll of a game. Starting sites were two troll bridges + a tower. For spells I had Polar explorers and Rhongomyniad. I think the winning play was moving BM to backline with polar explorers, leaving them with Rhon to throw killing a Leprechaun and Phalanx after shrinking it, while also hitting the opponent for 6. All to have the BM pick up the spear on the opponents back row to start applying real pressure. I slow played it a bit after that to get thresholds right for Morgana and drowned the opponent in card advantage.


The Game Plan:

Build an efficient and sticky early game board, win the board with efficient removal and good movement tech. Then transition to hard hitting combos and don't let up the pressure. There's also a couple of very early game doors hidden in here with the right board state.


The Deck:

A long continuation of a deck I started back when decks were still 40/20. I've brought a variation of this deck to every tournament I've gone to with some decent success. Opening hands vary quite a bit, but it has a lot of hard and fast hitting lines to find. Early minion & site placement matter a lot, and typically you'll want to play sites more defensively than you might first guess.


Packages:

Here's an outline of how I think about what roles each card fills, with some duplication entries as there are cards that fill multiple roles.


Pull package: reduced down from it's original iteration but still a strong way to build an early board and thin the deck.

  • [[Adept Illusionist]] -> [[Adept Illusionist]]
  • [[Highland Falconer]] -> [[Palliburrie Bats]]

I choose bats over scarabs for a couple of reasons, bats having 2 power makes a huge difference. Especially with the prevalence of druid. The bugs might be better against Vamps, but bats feel stickier because they have burrow and don't immediately die to a desert.


First Strike:

  • Forges
  • Rhongomyniad


Heavy Hitters - Well statted minions

  • [[Lugbog Cat]]: A 4 for 3 that can be placed on top of a enemy water site, which I would highly recommend is possible.
  • [[Cerberus in Chains]]: 5 power for 3 that can produce extra pressure or extra defense. Don't forget that this can move with forced movement like grapple shot. Typically better in games you want to be offensive in


Finishers - Get them to door

  • [[Ruler of Thul]]: Skip the road blocks if any and add extra damage the turn you play him, turning the pull package into real threats.
  • [[Sir Agravaine]]: Get him into a position where he can at least be near the enemy avatar on the next turn, then swing as many dorks directly into their avatar as you can stacking extra 3 damage for each. I've had a turn five 20 to door (sorry Glenn).
  • [[Cerberus in Chains]] + [[Grapple Shot]]


Ramp - Get more mana make things cheaper

  • [[Ruby Core]]: Early ramp, easier to hit that third fire threshold
  • [[Philosopher's Stone]]: Don't be afraid to hold this back if drawn later for a huge swing turn, and try to play knights second so they don't take up 2 color slots.


Equipment Package - Turn your avatar into a direct threat

  • Increase power: [[Torshammar Trinket]]
  • [[Rhongomyniad]]: Permanent first strike on your battle mage, making it easier to use your avatar as removal + card draw


Removal - Deal with minions to save your life total

  • [[Shrink]]: Best on big minions but can also turn the tides against aggro
  • [[Pollimorph]]: Best single target removal in the game currently for [[Battlemage]]
  • [[Grapple Shot]]: Can remove larger minions by following up with an attack. Also useful to remove a flying unit if you don't have a [[firebolts]] or [[lightning bolt]]


Sites:

Sites are almost completely focused around hitting threshold requirements while drawing the least amount of sites possible. You want 3-5 mana depending on your opening hand and subsequent draws with a real cap at 6. If you have a stone or a core in your opening hand it's usually safer to mulligan less sites and keep a lower count before putting on pressure. If going up to 5 or 6 it's often weaved into a turn after moving onto the opponents side.


In the end 3 Fire, 2 Water, 1 Air is what you're looking for. Theres are two triple fire threshold in [[Morgana le Fay]] & [[Immolation]]. This means if you have 3f, 2w, 1a in your opening hand you're golden on sites. A good opening hand typically has 2f, 2w, 1a. I've done quite a few pulls, if you don't hit 2f, 2w, 1a by site 5 that's typically rare. By 6 you should commonly see all your thresholds, but at 5 sites total pretty consistently.


Sites that produce Fire & Water are the best, sites that produce multiple threshold are good, and usually more water sites will keep your minions safer until you decide to move out since they can't be buried and drowning effects seem less meta.


Mulligans:


Mulligans for spells

The deck shuffles a decent amount so don't be too discouraged if you have to pitch a higher cost card that might be great later in the game, it might not stay at the bottom of the deck for long!


I feel like Mulligans in this deck require a decent understanding of how it needs to play against different avatars in different ways. Mixed with watching your thresholds and finding lines to consistently win the board in the early game, which can vary greatly. There are cards that are good against Archi, that will do less against Druid and vice versa. There are site placements you really want to hit against Druid that don't matter in other matchups.


An example to look at is sinkhole vs troll bridge. Sinkhole CAN be good against druid, but you won't always know what you're sitting across from before starting the game. Sinkhole is however amazing against Archi, even if you're going second. It delays their mass removal by an extra turn, allowing you to push their life lower earlier and possibly unexpectedly by removing their center forward defensive site. Troll bridge, doesn't usually do a lot against Archi, but a center forward site against a druid allows you to funnel their twany and other charge minions into a meat grinder.


Mulligans for sites

If you see 3f 2w 1a, you're golden and it's usually not worth pitching sites. If you see 2f, 2w, 1a you likely still want to keep that hand 90% of the time.


Match Ups

Aggro: You want forges some early minions. You often still want to get to 3-4 lands so early minions are more important than equipment. If you survive to the mid to late game [[Rhongomyniad]] can put in work, but you need early minions to get there.


Control: If it seems like it's a non-minion based deck it's ok to hang some creatures back and wait for something that will give a big burst of damage. Especially if you're going second! You can build a board on the back line waiting for the right timing of [[Polar Explorers]], [[Ruler of Thul]]. This is of course contingent on them hitting their defensive sites at the right times.


Some interesting hands I've seen.


The Big Doggy

[[Ruby Core]], [[Cerberus in Chains]], [[Grapple Shot]], [[Ruins]], [[Sinkhole]]. These five cards allow you to play out Cerberus on turn two followed up by grappling him into their face. The last site doesn't even matter that much. The hardest question you'll have to ask yourself is if you grapple shot the BM or the Cerberus.


[[Adept Illusionist]] can pair really well with troll bridge. It can sometimes work well with forge depending on your opponents hand.

decks.name: GenCon 2025 Crossroads 6th Place, 6-1 (E/F Sorcerer 55/31)
decks.primer:
Ideally, you want an aggressive or low to the ground start with some sort of card advantage. If you have multiple 4 cost minions in hand pitch them and dive deeper for more aggression and value.


Infiltrate is usually a snap keep in opener along with kettletops, imps and other aggro pieces under 4 mana. Slumbering giants is also a keeper but I will usually hold a desert to play on turn 4 if I don't have another way to wake her. From there get to 5 sites and start double drawing spells until you need the additional mana to outvalue the opponent by casting 2 spells per turn.


Don't get greedy with board presence if you have control, play this like a midrange build that has the capacity to go aggressive. Don't be afraid to sandbag spells you don't necessarily need to play and always be aware of Atlantean fate when moving around onto your sites. The ordinary sites in the deck will naturally help with this, but still be aware of wide area removal as it will almost always happen eventually. Just do your best to minimize risk.


Thanks for checking this out, I hope this helps!

This is my exceptional mono fire deck! The goal of this list is to put early pressure on the opponent with efficient minions, eke out card advantage where we can, and hopefully land a killing blow with a lucky burn spell.


We are aiming for a consistent and efficient early game. That is why the curve is low and does not include a lot of big finishers like [[Panorama Manticore]]. That is also why we are sticking with one element and not running Steam Druid. A big benefit of being mono fire is we get to run fun utility lands for extra value! 

  • [[Town]]: early ramp, a lot of the minions are exceptional and town will smooth out your early game.
  • [[Sinkhole]]: Removes problems like [[Pebbled Paths]] or [[Perilous Bridge]]. 
  • [[Wizards Den]]: Free card advantage-ish!!
  • [[Rift Valley]]: Sometimes deals with problematic sites, sometimes a free movement spell.

7 to 8 colorless sites seems to be the sweet spot if you consistently want to get (F)(F) early.



Mulligans 

Spells:

  • Mulligan all magic spells (except [[Pact with the devil]]... maybe), we want minions for early pressure.
  • Mulligan any finishers namely [[Rebecks]] & [[Boudicca]].
  • Remember what magic and finishers you mulligan, as they will not be outs later!!
  • Always keep [[Torshammer Trinket]].
  • Always keep [[Jihad]].
  • Don't clog your opening spells with lots of 4 drops if you don't have [[Town]].

Sites:

If your hand has a good curve of minions you can be very aggressive with Site.

  • If you are playing against control or earth dig for [[Sinkhole]] or [[smokestacks]].
  • [[River of Flame]] is one of the few answers to [[Root Spider]].
  • If your not playing against [[Archimago]] you can mulligan [[Funeral Pyre]].
  • If your not playing against [[Druid]] you can mulligan [[Arid Desert]].
  • [[Forge]] is strong in your opening hand, but you only need 1. 
  • If your opening hand is 3 (F)sites mulligan 1 or 2 unimportant ones in hopes of Hitting [[Town]] or [[Sinkhole]]. 
  • [[Town]] is super strong in your opening. 
  • Always mulligan [[Wizard Den]].
  • Its often poor to keep both [[Town]] and [[Sinkhole]], you will need (F)(F) early, use best judgment.


Game Play

Don't be afraid to play a [[Vile Imp]] or [[ Clamor of Harpies]] for no value. Its okay if [[Quarrelsome Kolbolds]] has to hit your [[Druid]] for 2, there is value in keeping up tempo and keeping your opponent under pressure. In that vain sometimes its okay to throw a [[Minor Explosion]] at the opposing avatar in the name of mana efficiency. Keep the games short and limit your opponents options. While the deck can play the value / control game (and sometimes you have to), we will often lose the late / long game.


It is usually correct to draw from your spell book. Only draw from your atlas if you can not make a play or REALLY need to double spell in a turn.


You can be pretty aggressive moving and attacking with your Avatar. You can double spell most the deck with 6 or 7 sites, so don't be afraid to skip a site draw or placement if you can get good value off it. Don't flip [[Druid]] unless it buys you a turn preventing a killing blow. Most of the time Tawny is more valuable.


"If you can be one thing, you should be efficient."

decks.name: Avatar of Air - 1st Place Cornerstone Championship
decks.primer:
This is a Gothic mid-range Air/Earth deck with Avatar of Air for mobility. It's not too different from the typical air/earth mid range gameplay that encourages an aggressive early-mid game with late-game finishers. With the changes to Guisarm and other "Strike" effects, you're not going for the OTK and instead looking to constantly apply pressure.


---------- Artfiacts:

Onyx Core is to help ramp and fix Earth Threshold. Torshammer Trinkets are to help deal more damage and make trades more favorable. Toolbox is to provide answers when you need them but more often than not it is to pull Zap! out from the collection to kill your opponent at Death's Door. You could argue running a 3 of to add consistency to access to the cards.


Rolling Boulder is a typical card to have in an Avatar of Air deck, however with Gothic we have a brand new toy to play with in Lord of Greed. You can now roll the boulder and have Lord of Greed bring it back at the end of turn.


---------- Minions:

Most minions don't' need explanation as they are typical valuable creatures to fly into your opponent's board with AoA.


Men of Leng is a personal pet card of mine that if played at the right time can be very hard to deal with and can take a few cards from your opponent. Use your Blinks, Wuthering Heights, and AoA to fling them to the back row and force some discards.


Skeleton Mage is a fantastic new addition to the roster of air minions as it not only lets you recast your magic, but you can also cast opponent magics that you may need (specifically says "a cemetery" not "your cemetery").


All of the ranged units become extremely difficult to play around with air's mobility. Stygian Archers are one of my favorite new additions. Kill stuff, gain benefits. Doesn't get more satisfying than that.


Daperyll Vampires are probably the most questionable minion on the list. With the changes to how they work in that you no longer get health when striking a site, they lost a lot of luster. However, they are still an airborne minion that is hard to deal with sometimes. They are the most likely to be replaced for lower-cost aggressive targets. And they've also been outclassed by one of my new favorite Airborne minions which are:


Legion of Gall are a fantastic minion. Never would they have printed a 5 mana 5 power Airborne unit in Beta, but they did it in Gothic and gave it an upside. These guys are a monster to deal with, especially early with a tower. On top of them dominating the air, they also remove cards from your opponent's collection. So you get to see what kind of answers they may have and remove their best options.


Lord of Fear is a game ender. Enemies can't defend alone is a huge effect and makes your offense feel so much more powerful. You get to trade better. You get to attack without being blocked. And most importantly Death's Door is scarier than ever.


Lord of Greed is an answer to your opponent's artifacts and he has an upside of having some fun synergy with Rolling Boulder. I debated over 2 of Fear over Greed but there are just too many good artifacts in this game that you want to shut them down as often as you can. We don't have Swap so this is one of our best and consistent answers to artifacts.


---------- Magic:

There are a lot of typical tempo spells you will see in a deck like this but there are a few cards that I want to talk about. Namely Gift of the Wolf and Vanishment.


Gift of the Wolf is a fantastic new card and I feel it might be overlooked very often at first glance. This card is so good at making trades, or just getting extra damage in with a ranged strike or site attack. The fact that it replaces itself and also is a great target for Skeleton Mage is what helped it earn its slots in the deck. I replaced Gigantism with this because Gift of the Wolf more easily fits into turns. Gigantism is still good, but often your opponent will have chump blockers making it have less opportunities to be used.


Vanishment is another one of my own personal pet cards. I like cards that replace themselves, and this does so and protects your board state. Plenty of times I find myself just ahead enough and Vanishment guarantees I stay ahead on my opponent's next turn most of the time.


---------- Sites:


My site choices are very defensive. Stuff like Perilous Bridge, Mountain Pass, and No Man's Land let you take advantage of AoA's mobility while shutting down your opponent's ability to strike back. The quality of sites drastically increased in Gothic. Double threshold sites are an amazing new addition. Learning how to mulligan sites is a process with this deck. Placement of air sites and defensive sites is something you will get used to after playing for a bit. Wuthering Heights is a new site that replicates AoA's ability. This lets you double fly units and get them further in to enemy territory.


Collection:

3 Ghouls

1 Amazon Warriors

1 Bury

1 Dispel

1 Disenchant

1 Murder of Crows

1 Gift of the Raven

1 Zap!

decks.primer:
Finished 5-2


Shifty's Revenge


Shifty crouched low in the underbrush, his fingers pressing into the cold earth. The mountain air bit at his skin, but he welcomed the chill — it reminded him of the battle he lost, the shame he carried. That day still burned in his mind, the moment another druid shatter struck and sent him tumbling from victory’s peak. But Shifty was no coward. He was no forgotten warrior. He was back.


A sharp screech cut through the twilight. Tawny, his ever-loyal hawk, circled above, scouting their prey. Shifty smirked. His enemy thought themselves untouchable, but he had learned, he had adapted. They might have won before, but this time, the mountain itself would strike for him.


He gave a subtle signal, and Tawny dove, talons releasing a carefully perched boulder from the ridge. The massive stone rumbled down, gathering speed, picking up a thick layer of snow as it roared toward the unsuspecting enemy camp below. Shifty was already moving, his team of quick-footed raiders darting through the shadows, ready to charge the moment the chaos erupted.


A satisfying boom echoed through the valley as the avalanche of stone and ice slammed into their defenses. Cries of panic filled the air.


Shifty emerged from the frost-laden mist, a wry grin on his lips. “Remember me?” he called, his voice carrying through the shattered battlefield.


This time, revenge would be his — and with it, his Pact with the Devil would be complete.

decks.name: Roots in 2026?
decks.primer:
A wise community member once told me that [[Roots of Yggdrasil]] would never work in a 50/30 format.


He was probably right... but things should be different now that we're 60/30/10.


Hear me out...


Warning: Complicated math involving intricate theories and calculations below on how this works. You have been warned.


  • Assuming we really want to start with [[Roots of Yggdrasil]] in our opening hand, the odds of doing so with 3 sites mulliganed would be 19.99%.


  • With [[Magician]], we get to filter up to 10 cards in our starting hand, that's 1/6 chance of drawing the key combo piece. Hold up, that's only 16.6% chance to dra-... Maybe we can look at this from another angle.


I swear I got it this time, please hear me out again...


What's so different with [[Magician]] and what makes it the best avatar to pull this combo in the Gothic era?


It's no secret that the effectiveness of this combo is linearly correlated with the Atlas size; the smaller the Atlas, the stronger the combo. We can all agree on this right?


Now read the first four words of the [[Magician]]'s ability.


"You have no atlas..."


I rest my case.
