filteredDecks.name: Top 8 Pittsburgh Excalibur - Maidenless Motherless Croneless
filteredDecks.primer:
7/14/2026 -

Current Meta ((E)/(F), (W)/(A), Mono (F))

Archimago, Pathfinder, Imposter, Necromancer, Persecutor, Battlemage


Maidenless Motherless Croneless

[[Waveshaper]] has been seen as a mid tier avatar for quite a while but with the release of gothic I believe it's able to not only hang with the cool kids at the meta table but also come out ahead of most of the meta with the right cards.


This deck maxes out at 6 cost spells and is low enough to the ground to keep up with the faster aggro strategies. Controlling the game and pressuring the opponent is the gameplan and surprising your opponent with a 10-20 damage turn is a real possibility. A healthy smattering of removal and an absolute boatload of movement effects make this a fun deck to pilot.


Opening the Game ###########

Sites are extremely important for this deck to perform well and there is a lot of site disruption out there. The decision to cut out as many non essential elite and unique sites is completely valid with cards like [[peasant revolt]] and [[heirloom lost]] running loose in the meta, but even with a decision like this we have so many powerful options in the ordinary and exceptional slots. [[autumn river]], [[river rapids]], [[maelstrom]], or [[kelp cavern]] tend to be my favorite turn 1 plays.


[[overflow]] is such a powerful card that it can often times be one of the best openings in our game plan to get to 5/6 mana as soon as possible. We run 3 main deck overflow and 3 [[toolbox]] with 6 possible overflow draws.

Some notable overflow options to cast while you have them in hand are [[babbling brook]] to get you to a 5 mana turn often times without needing to worry about anything pressuring you early.

[[bog]] is a new include in my deck specifically to slow down a [[persecutor]] or [[battlemage]] and to completely stop a [[pathfinder]] or [[imposter]] from developing early with pathfinder by forcing them to take a turn to get back to an edge of their sites.


If no overflow combination is in hand my other favorite options would be [[troll bridge]] and [[thin ice]] being a classic turn two sites to play but if you have a [[coy nixie]] in hand it can be the perfect combination to start holding down your side of the board from enemies entering your water. [[mudflow]] makes coy nixie even more annoying than it already is for your opponent by constantly dipping underneath your thin ice each turn and popping up for free on your turn.

[[tufted turtles]], [[shellycoat]], [[aino]], [[lugbog cat]], and [[order of the sacred oak]] are also great opening hand minions to begin pressuring early or defensively developing your own board presence without being pressured yourself.


Mid Game ###########

Setting up card advantage if possible is almost always best in this turn 4 or 5. [[algor omphalos]], [[dank omphalos]], [[maiden, mother, crone]], [[lilith]], and [[captain baldassare]] are the types of cards that can open up that greater advantage for us. Playing these on a home row [[river rapids]] can give you the opportunity to safely cast them and use them to attack from your back row.


if you managed to ramp into a turn 4 fifth site drop you have some very interesting plays that can completely shut off your opponent.

[[atlantean fate]] is an aura that can just flat out win you the game on turn 4 by shutting off an opponents sites and leaving them with no threshold.

[[archangel raphael]] being cast right next to them after you ramp into their side can be overwhelming.

[[giant shark]] can just come down underneath your body of water and wreak havoc on anything being cast or moving in this body of water.


At 34 minions we have plenty of strong options to come down during these turns.

I tend to hold onto [[abaddon succubus]], [[ruler of thul]] and [[assimilator snail]] until I have a good reason to play them for removal or massive damage.


End Game ###########

Once we get to 5 mana I will typically stop playing sites and begin flooding their sites with specific minions on them. If we draw [[lord of lies]], [[mester stoor worm]], [[the green knight]], or [[call of the sea]] we would typically draw that mana if we don't already have it and spend the turn to impact the board in such a more impactful way whether it be by dealing a massive hit to our opponent or wiping out all of their minions in one turn. This is when we look at how we can finish our opponent off and try to deal the maximum amount of damage possible.


[[mester stoor worm]] is a huge threat with 7 power, [[mudflow]] can make this minion a much harder to deal with threat by giving it the ability to be safely summoned submerged to come out and attack next turn or better yet just use a [[meat hook]] to pull our opponent into our body of water.


[[lord of lies]] even with his recent nerf is another massive threat especially with so many ways to pull or force our opponent into another location. [[undertow]], [[riptide]], [[coy nixie]], [[nelly longarms]] and [[meat hook]] are all excellent ways to achieve this. It hits big and it can be used as removal for multiple minions at once or just be used to get an extra hit from another minion onto our opponent.


[[giant shark]] is the final big finisher in the deck rounding it out to 7 major threats total. This minion is so special in fact that I have an entire section later on explaining how to use it properly.


Using Sharks ###########

Movement effects are the sharks best friend, the shark will most likely not survive very long because the first thing out of our opponents mouth when they read it for the first time is "oh shit you mean every water site?" There is a two card combo with the shark and [[the rack]] which is very funny to use but it's too cute to have it be used competitively.


DO NOT place a shark down into a full board unless you want it to die and kill some of our opponents minions. All they need to do is chump any minion into a water site nearby to have our pet swim right to any water site of their choice to then take care of it with some nearby or adjacent removal effect.


ONLY place a shark for the following reasons.

  1. We fully intend to be able to use it the turn it comes down by having movement effects ready to be used that turn, [[coy nixie]] or [[nelly longarms]] on the board already, [[riptide]] ready in hand with the mana to cast it, a [[meat hook]] already on a minion in position, or an [[undertow]] ready to move our opponent.
  2. We can turn off its ability for a turn cycle to set up a massive attack the following turn. [[bog]] and [[babbling brook]] are able to put a leash on our pet for a turn.
  3. We have a sparse enough board state that the shark can safely survive a turn in play. This is usually a gamble
  4. We have an [[assimilator snail]] in hand ready to come down and become a previously murdered shark. What's better than 3 sharks? How about 5 of them.


The more sites we can move our opponent through the more damage we can do, [[meat hook]] is particularly brutal since it can usually pull them through at least 2 water sites and sometimes 3, each of those water sites they enter is 5 damage, if you are able to also attack then that is a 20 point damage turn and deaths door from one single minion.


[[giant shark]] is a double edged sword, if our opponent moves us in our own body of water the shark will bite us and if we summon any minions into it's body of water the shark will travel to that minion to fight it. There are a few notable minions and one site that are able to survive being summoned into the sharks tank and also allow the shark to live as well.

  1. [[order of the sacred oak]] - ward breaks
  2. [[tufted turtles]] - tanks the first hit
  3. [[sacred stag]] - ward breaks
  4. [[archangel raphael]] - ward breaks
  5. [[the green knight]] - big defense stat tanks the hit
  6. [[mudflow]] - acts as a safe place to summon new minions since it is land.


One last note for the shark is that our ability allows us to perform a "tank change". Since the shark has waterbound it becomes disabled while on land, once we summon what we need to summon we are able to flood the position that the shark is on to effectively turn it back on and pass the turn.



When to Flood ###########

Our ability is powerful on [[waveshaper]] and it almost always takes the opponent by surprise when they learn that the site we choose to flood is not only NEARBY but it remains flooded UNTIL WE DO IT AGAIN. This give us amazing reach into our opponents side of the board.


There are only two reasons to use our ability. Sometimes we care about both but most of the time it boils down to one reason or the other.

  1. Flooding to create a water site where there was not one before.
  2. Tapping down minions without submerge.


Aggro strategies may require us to tap down a site earlier than we would normally want to. [[mazuj ifrit]] is an early threat that is very good to tap down since it will slowly sap the life from your opponent. One other situation where it’s fine to use our ability early is if we have an overflow in hand to tap down a minion or two and still develop our sites.


Our ability can be used for more than just tapping things nearby down. If we have a shark on board and a pull effect or two we can potentially create an extra water site for the opponent to stumble into for an extra 5 damage.


That flooded site of an opponent may also be the perfect jumping in point for a waterbound minion to attack or if we are afraid the opponent has an earthquake or bury in hand, we can simply flood the site for any minion to attack into and feel a sense of safety that it cannot be buried.


If none of these options are available then we can instead draw an extra site for the turn.


Toolbox ###########

There are 3 [[toolbox]] in the deck and I will never be upset to draw one because they are so very useful. I chose to go with 7 toolbox choices and will go over each choice here.

  1. [[overflow]] : This is self explanatory, 5 copies in the deck now. Sites are powerful and ramp is so important.
  2. [[drown]] : This acts as the standard removal slot in the toolbox collection but it also acts as the artifact removal which is sometimes more important.
  3. [[ice lance]] : This is the standard death's door finisher of the toolbox side of the collection, it can also be used as removal or mask breaking against [[imposter]].
  4. [[riptide]] : If I had to choose one magic in the waveshaper's arsenal that is it's bread and butter, this would be that spell. I would run 10 of this spell if I could.
  5. It can move yourself out of harms way.
  6. It can move your opponent into harms way.
  7. It can trigger a [[giant shark]] attack.
  8. It can disrupt a [[pathfinder]]'s way.
  9. It can force warded minions into unsafe water locations.
  10. It can force stealthed minions into unsafe water locations.
  11. It can be used as a psuedo death's door finisher.
  12. It replaces itself with another card after you use it.
  13. [[return to nature]] : This is another utility spell that other waveshapers have utilized much better than I ever have by using it on themselves in conjunction with [[deep sea mermaids]] or [[kelp cavern]] to reuse a powerful spell that was put into your cemetery. But it is very useful against [[archimago]], [[deathspeaker]], [[flamecaller]], and any cards that want to use things in a cemetery.
  14. [[extinguish]] : A recent addition to my collection due to the amount of fire minions are in the meta currently and the only real way to deal with [[jihad]] or the dreaded [[drought]].
  15. [[makeshift barricade]] : If you find yourself on deaths door against an aggro deck very quickly this might be the solution. It has saved me more than once by nullifying deaths door finishers like [[zap]] or [[firebolt]]. It also protects us from the inevitable [[craterize]] that [[archimago]] is so fond of.


Silver Bullet ###########

There is a single [[silver bullet]] in my list and it gives me the option for 3 very powerful exceptional spells.

  1. [[swap]] : This is such an incredible utility spell, being able to trigger a shark for removal or using this to steal a powerful artifact right out of your opponents hands and replacing it with one of your own minions is just so satisfying. This can also shut off something like an omphalos by placing it on your site where your opponent cannot cast minions to, this does not protect you from the magics or auras cast from there.
  2. [[snowball]] : This spell is removal and finisher wrapped into one. Great to use your own minions like [[tufted turtles]], [[order of the sacred oak]], [[sacred stag]], [[archangel raphael]], and [[the green knight]] since none of these will likely die from this due to ward or just great defensive abilities. Make sure you roll as many of your opponents minions in the ball as well directly into them and dealing a massive blow, bonus points if you cast [[plague of frogs]] right before this goes off.
  3. [[meat hook]] : This is a powerful effect to be given to any minion on your team, it can pull your opponent into your location and trigger a [[giant shark]] attack that can sometimes just put our opponent on death's door. It can also be used to pull our avatar out of harm's way or back into a body of water. It is a bit awkward to tap for [[silver bullet]] and tap to use this ability so it might be removed for [[wave of eviction]].

filteredDecks.name: SorceryFest 11th Place | Fire (Air-Splash) Imposter
filteredDecks.primer:
Flamecaller Fetish for Beginners


Intro

After a hiatus from other TCGs, I decided to give another game a chance. I previously played MTG Legacy and Premodern, and I picked up Sorcery in mid-May 2026. I immediately fell in love with the artwork, the gameplay, and the community. After a few games at my local LGS, I found out about the Summit (a big thank you goes to the organizing team). I got my ass handed to me pretty badly in my first few games. However, after a while and with a lot of support and coaching from the other players, I started to find a deck that I enjoyed. Once again, the community has been amazing. I then decided to give the whole TCG tournament experience a try. This was the first TCG tournament I had ever travelled to attend. Below is a quick report on my experience and some of my notes


Overall Record: 11th place out of 128 players at SorceryFest 2026


Matchups

  • Archimago (Win)
  • Fire Pathfinder (Win)
  • Mud Sorcerer (Loss - Opponent ended in 10th place overall)
  • Interrogator (Win)
  • Deathspeaker (Win)
  • Water Pathfinder (Loss - super close game, made a misplay with [[Warp Spasm]], but at least I learned my lesson)
  • Archimago (Win)


Tournament Notes


Comments on key spells:

  • [[Flamecaller]] was the MVP, dealing more than 8-10 damage in four matches. Paired with [[War Horse]] movement or [[Flanking Maneuver]], it can catch the opponent completely off guard
  • The early ramp from [[Mix Ignis]] and [[Four Waters of Paradise]] once again proved that this is exactly what an Imposter wants. Cheating out threats early gives you more room to breathe when using the Pathfinder mask. Two plays stood out: (i) playing [[Mix Ignis]] into [[Morgana le Fay]] on turn one felt almost disgustingly good and (ii) using [[Four Waters of Paradise]] in the late game to cast an [[Infernal Legion]] and then teleport it with [[Flanking Maneuver]] to put the opponent at death’s door and clear the blockers made a compelling case for why the card is strong in both the early and late game
  • [[Courtesan Thaïs]] was incredibly strong against Archimago. She won me Game 7 by blowing up the Archimago with his own [[Major Explosion]]
  • I was not sure about [[Inquisition]] before the tournament, but it turned out to be a real MVP. Sniping a key card from the opponent’s hand and later animating it with [[Deathspeaker]] is incredibly strong
  • [[Asmodeus]] felt great in testing, but was somewhat clunky during the tournament. Without a way to move him onto an enemy site on the turn he enters, you lose much of his immediate impact. Note: moving him via [[Wuthering Heights]] or [[War Horse]] worked well in testing
  • Cutting two [[Redcap Powries]] to make room for [[Swiven Scout]] felt like a good decision. I was hesitant to give up three points of charge damage, but knowing the opponent’s hand had a meaningful impact in two or three games
  • I am considering replacing one [[Infiltrate]] with one [[Betrayal]]. Infiltrate is good, but sometimes you need the immediate damage - or simply want to steal the minion and [[Warp Spasm]] it immediately
  • [[Peasant Revolt]]: There is not much to say about this card. Every time it hits the board, it feels like an “I win” button. The only thing that felt mediocre this time was my inclusion of more Elite sites, such as [[Wizard’s Den]]. When I played it against the Deathspeaker opponent, however, it destroyed five sites on my opponent’s side and two Elites on mine, which felt like a good trade
  • [[Seasoned Sellsword]] is a highly debatable card. The one time it came up, however, it was extremely relevant. I played it beneath my Imposter after pathfinding, well outside the enemy Pathfinder’s range. My opponent had to respect it and make a suboptimal trade. The dream scenario would have been using [[Blaze of Glory]] with the Sellsword to wipe the opponent’s board


A few observations on the sites:

  • I never had a problem casting an Air spell when I wanted to. Of course, you need to think carefully about your mulligan and the sequencing of your site draws once you are off Pathfinder and have not yet seen an Air site
  • The heavy Fire focus allows you to play more colorless sites, such as [[Sinkhole]] and [[Wizard's Den]], which felt great. [[Wizard's Den]] was especially strong as a home site
  • [[Fields of Phyxis]] and [[Smokestacks of Gnaak]] are MVPs against decks with defensive sites, such as Archimago or Necro, although I did not face Necro at the tournament. I would always mulligan aggressively for these sites because they can be backbreaking for the opponent


Special thanks to Aadu for driving innovation within this archetype of aggressive Flamecaller Imposters - for more details about the deck philosophy & composition visit his primer

filteredDecks.primer:
“Earth, Wind, Fire, Water, Heart. With your powers combined.”


“I’m gunna save you the heart break, three colours won’t work. You will variance your way out of this tournament.” – Geoffrey


This deck came 2nd in the SorceryFest 2026 Grand Contest in Leeuwarden, The Netherlands.


THE DECK PHILOSOPHY

Shout out to @Aadu who I think was the first person to really figure out the Imposter theory I’m using – hit hard and early, and force your opponent to choose between putting their resources into removing the Pathfinder Mask, or removing the early game pressure we aim to apply. The first generation of decks we brewed with this philosophy (that I was involved with) were running Mixes and Four Waters, but in Earth/Fire at the moment I don’t think they are required as there are plenty of powerful 3-drops we can deploy.


The deck is designed to incrementally accrue a value differential with the opponent on board by trading with 4+ power minions, whilst drawing 1 additional card per turn with the Pathfinder Mask early.


In the late game, you have the flexibility of the 9 other masks in the collection, as well as a number of ‘tricks’ to deploy across 3 colours.


We stretch to:

4 pips for Earth (for Michael, Gargantula, and Paladins) though majority 2 pip.

3 pips for Fire (for Peasant Revolt, and Morgana) though majority 2 pip.

1 pip for Air. Towers are good enough to run in non-Air mono element decks in my opinion. That we gain access to some incredible spells is just icing on the cake.


THE ATLAS

The site selection is almost entirely threshold based, and ordinary as much as possible. 

By simulating drawing 7 sites off the top of a shuffled deck, I was able to verify that not hitting my thresholds is highly improbable (though obviously still possible) post mulligan.


I have 8/30 opportunities to hit the single air threshold I need.

I only run 3 Elite/Unique sites:

Mount Ussar – So many Sorcery games come down to a double death door situation, and fleeing with a Ward can allow you to tie-break these games.

Valley of Delight – Flexible threshold selection allows 3 elements to work.


The other benefit of this site selection is a partial immunity to Atlantean Fate (which can win games on turn 5) via the 12 ordinary sites – there will almost always be somewhere to stack up minions.


THE SPELLBOOK


Minions Package

The minion package is a fairly generic Earth/Fire selection, with a focus on being able to drop a threat on turn 3 OR a Stefania to disrupt the opponent (depending on draws and matchup). We have a reasonable curve up to 7 mana maximum.

Pudge Butcher is one minion I think has been under-rated for some time. 4 mana for 5 power, with the ability to yoink the opposing avatar or annoying minions across the realm is incredibly valuable. He can lock down columns, or be silenced/blinked to suddenly re-emerge as a threat. Far too frequently I see players ignore Pudge Butcher, because they don’t want to take a turn to step to the side, and instead rely on a blocker between themselves and the Butcher.


The Common Sense Package

I run 2xCommon Sense, which have 11 options:

1. 1xBlink – A Pudge Butcher enabler, a cantrip, or a kill spell.

2. 1xCritical Strike – One of the best ‘tricks’ in this deck, that can enable you to Door the opponent from 20 life. This works with Michael, and can also be played, flashed back with Magoo to allow you to hit the enemy avatar for 4x damage for 7 mana.

3. 1xDispel – Ompholoi and the Ring and Atlantean Fate are everywhere, this requires no explanation.

4. 1xFirebolts – Kills through Ward or blockers as the projectiles are one at a time, or just mops up token minions.

5. 2xGift of the Serpent – Excellent value with Collicky or Kobolds. Also a cantrip.

6. 1xGift of the Wolf – For value trading + a cantrip.

7. 1xLightning Bolt – Kills Ironclad.

8. 1xBury – Can be minion removal, but can also just waste an opponent’s Omphalos in minion heavy decks, or just get rid of Ring.

9. 2xGrapple Shot – One of the reasons I’m splashing Air, and an enabler for big bursty damage.


The extensive use of cheap spells means I can frequently drop a threat + gain value with a magic each turn from the midgame onwards. This also fills the Cemetery for Archimago Mask value in the late game.


The Board Wipes

1xPoison Nova – This card is so incredible, it was a tough choice to only run one. However I think given the Power of the minions being deployed, frequently I’m ahead on board, and this is more of a last resort OR fantastic in a situation where my opponent is racing me, and our minions are on opposite sides of the realm.

2xEarthquake – Really requires no explanation. Earth decks run this.

2xMajor Explosion – I chose this over Craterize because I don’t really want to be going over 7 mana if possible. This spell already does plenty enough damage.


Everything Else

1xTithe – As an Imposter, you will have games where the opponent has a Lightning Bolt from the mulligan, or some other way to get you off Pathfinder Mask quickly. In these games, Tithe enables you to continue drawing 1 spell each turn to out-value them.

1xPeasant Revolt – Truly the MVP of this deck. It can only hit 3/30 of our sites, and absolutely wrecks many other decks that have loaded up with Unique/Elite minions and sites. This card can single-handedly win the game against Air/Water Necro, who’s the big bad of this meta.

1xGigantism – Big attack good.

2xDisintegrate – Unconditional removal, and a banish for annoying deathrites or minions that could return (Green Knight).


1xRing of Morrigan – Every deck should run this, but I would mulligan it away against any Water deck. Swap is death.

2xTrinket – Value trade with your opponent! Get ahead on board.

1xRuby Core – Imposter loves ramp, and an extra Fire threshold doesn’t hurt.


THE MASKS

I think of the masks as incredible 3 mana spells, that can reuse their effect once per turn for 0 unless you take direct damage.


In rough order of importance:

Pathfinder – This is the heart of every Imposter deck. +1 card per turn.

Sorcerer - +1 card per turn from site 7 onwards.

Ironclad – Ironclad… on a Gnome Hollows… with a Spider under it…

Deathspeaker – With 3 colours, we have the opportunity to utilise our opponent’s graveyard a lot. Archangel Michael can be a big surprise.

Interrogator – One line you can take if PF Mask is destroyed, or if the opportunity presents itself, is Interrogator. The opponent will almost always allow you to draw, allowing you to draw sites for turn (effectively inversing the PF Mask).

Avatar of Earth – It’s an Earth meta at the moment, and this mask can swing for 6.

Archimago – Almost always just to flash back one spell for the finish, anything under 5 mana in the graveyard is up for grabs.

Enchantress – Almost entirely for removing the opponent’s Auras as I only run The Great Famine, but if you happen to need 4 extra damage…

Witch – Sometimes you just really need 2 damage. More rarely you can curse to stop a Craterize.

Savior – This was my flex slot, and I did consider Flamecaller instead. I think I only got value from this Mask once in the entire tournament, but if you don’t have anything else to do on a turn it can be quite threatening to leave up.


THE MATCHUPS

This deck was built to combat the AW Necro plague, and I can report it’s highly effective. We have deserts to ping skeletons, we have Dragonettes/Kobolds to ping skeletons. We have disables and defensive sites for their early big minions. We have Orders who stop skeleton production entirely. Pudge Butcher is ready to yoink them (or just remove 1 skeleton per turn for the rest of the game from the back row). And all the while they live in fear that the Peasants are coming…


The deck runs no Archimago hate, and the only 2 losses I took were to Archimago (one to Felix in the Swiss which was avenged in the semi-final, and to Geoffrey in the final). However the deck still has a decent chance (I would estimate 45:55 in favour of the Magoo). 


The games I played were:

Mud Sorceror

Water Pathfinder

Dragonlord Talamh Dreig (quite possibly the most terrifying game)

Dust Ramp Sorceror

2x AW Necro

3x Archimago

Mud Imposter

filteredDecks.primer:
Huge thanks to GOODLUCKBAD, For giving tips and being a huge inspiration

https://curiosa.io/decks/cm7mf7rrm001ele03o1xweti9?tab=view


AGGRESSIVE WATER? BUT HOW IS IT SO DEFENSIVE?


[[Druid]] is always the answer. Trying to play [[Druid]] in the year of 2026 is different. Without tawny respawn you have to fully utilize the rest of his kit. This wasnt an easy task, one that i probably still havent fully realised. But the revelation that led to this list was found in the deepest of dungeons.


Deck origin:

On a late evening; A while after i'd given up on the quest to play druid in a deck I enjoy, one that i felt utilized his kit to the fullest. I was playing VS my boy GOODLUCKBAD on the sorcerers summit. He was piloting his signature [[Spellslinger]] water list. After the match i said to myself, ive tried alot of color combinations for druid, but never mono colored. So unbeknownst to him i copied his masterpiece and swapped [[Spellslinger]] for [[Druid]]. A few games in with the deck i felt a breath of fresh air. I didnt win them all, however its strength commanded respect. Alot of the deck changed since that however there are still plenty of remenants.


Realising the potential of the unbroken body of water, consistency with spells such as [[Riptide]] and sites like [[Undertow]] and [[Maelström]]. Aswell as access to double Omphalos.

A little bit of tweaking to the sites. Maximizing the ammount of movement and adding some spells like coy nixie was all i did in the beginning. The beast had been unleashed.


Minions were flying left and right. Being dragged in by an [[Innsmouth Dock]], [[Riptided]] onto a river, pushed from said river onto a [[Wuthering Heights]], Bounced onto a [[Troll Bridge]]. All while being pinged down. This might be a juicer fellas.


Some time after these changes i felt comfortable enough to make even more changes, No more mixes, no more rivers. Alltough rivers still have a place in my heart im currently trying out more meta cards such as [[Thin Ice]], and utility colorless sites like [[Sinkhole]]. The rivers are certainly good and could come back in the future. The curve also lowered as i realised utilizing [[Bruin]] early is a way to success.


Strategy:

Tapping and flipping our avatar early is now the name of the game. I mulligan my entire hand most games unless i have a [[Lugbog Cat]], or a real 4 mana threat in hand.

The plan is to establish a good board presence early. Putting down minions such as [[Lugbog Cat]], [[Sea raider]] and [[Adept Illusionist]]. With all this we can safely flip our avatar. Playing out both bruin and someone else to push the pressure with some real threats.

This almost always happens on turn 5. The previous turn i should have put a 4 mana minion on board. Now it is time for our fluffy friend. Aswell as (hopefully) another hard to deal with dude. Prime examples would be [[Failed Mutation]], [[Sacred Stag]] or [[Captain baldassare]]. This swarm of minions will be hard to deal with. [[Earthquake]] is hopeless, [[Poison Nova]] is weird. Suffering from an [[Atlantean Fate]] is our biggest trouble here so focus on staying spread out and keeping atleast one of your guys alive.

This heavy pressure can be enhanced with a [[Sinkhole]]. After taking away their 4th mana i dont see many ways of dealing with all of this.


During most games i only draw 1 site at the beginning of my turn. Thats before flipping. Even after flipping i keep drawing spells. Simply tapping for sites. Trying to keep up the momentum of the double threat and draw through to as many good cards as possible. Unless i ofcourse have access to a game ender like [[Atlantean Fate]] or missing one threshold for [[Mesmerism]].


In the case that you didnt draw anything aggressive even after mulligans. The luck isnt out. This deck is great at fighting in the pocket. We still have a great defensive plan. No aggressive minions on hand can only mean one thing. Only defensive spells on hand. From here on out we try to utilize our [[Riptides]], [[Coy Nixie]] and [[Nelly Longarms]] in conjunction with the sites to remove any threats and bring forth 2 for 1s. This act of attrition will sooner or later end up in a draw that allows you to swing the momentum and end the game. Dont be afraid to sacrifice little [[Bruin]] if you have to.


A mix of these two gameplans is what happens most games, Being aggressive with the fluffy guy and using thorns and spells for removal. Always looking to spend as little cards for as much impact as possible.

This needs to happen since your only way to draw cards in this deck is Omphalos. We do not have the privelege of being able to tap to draw sites or turning skeletons into huge threats.


Theres also a secret minigame here that wins many games. Trying to pull the enemy avatar onto your sites. It will cause most players to panic. This provides alot of extra damage. Hard to defend against and leads to coy nixie and riptide being a death door finisher. More on this later on.


Tawny...

[[Tawny]] shouldnt be compared to her older brother bear. They are not the same and do not serve the same purpose. I try to get as many hits in as possible with her. Some games [[Tawny]] will deal 5 damage due to nobody wanting to spend cards to remove her. If they end up doing it later down the line it just feels worse because they ended up paying 5 life for their greed. Other use cases could be such as popping wards on critical threats, Going in for that last damage on a minion that survived a fight with 1 life or sacrificing her to a [[Troll Bridge]] if thats your only alley of attack. Drowning a [[Sacred Stag]] on [[Thin Ice]] is something she excels at.

At the end of the day going in for 1 or 2 damage is still good. How many times have you been 1 away from dooring someone?


SPELLS:

We begin to summarize the cards and maybe talk some use cases in this deck.


[[Atlantean Fate]]

Best card in the entire game. Draw an extra site for turn if you have this in hand please!


[[Ring of morrigan]]

Sweet on the defense in this deck. Sometimes you're missing that single ping to kill a minion. Otherwise obviously as a finisher which water doesnt have many of. Hold it in hand vs water decks. Play it freely vs any other element.


[[Torshammar Trinket]]

Currently only at one because you want a juiced hand not one filled with trinkets. Water minions already pack a punch aswell. Could be two but i dont know what to cut. Pairs really well with tawny to strike sites or vacuum up some skellies. Love to trinket a fey changeling aswell to get in some extra chip damage.


[[The rack]]

New addition to the deck so i havent tried it too much yet. Must feel good if you can get in atleast one hit with it. If the enemy avatar is on your side its very easy and the damage will jump through the roof with your thorns. Comboes with [[Plague of Frogs]]. Slapping it on [[Tawny]] to have her hit and die and maybe a cat can pick it up and strike again isnt bad at all. With enemy stretched to your side the game should be fairly easy to play.


[[Toolbox]]

Finishers, movement, utility. Only at two because the collection in water is horrifyingly bad.


[[Truesight Crossbow]]

Classic mono water death door technology. Many usecases for this one. Could be put on your [[Druid]] for that extra ping when someone is in your business. Other things include putting it on a stag to keep it even safer than it is. Killing airborne units, ETC.

A favorite is putting it on a [[Coy Nixie]] to deal with their [[Coy Nixie]] while keeping yours alive.


[[Dank Omphalos]], [[Algor Omphalos]]

Super good, one of these on board feels like game secured. Infinite access to cards. Easier to play than in most decks because you can always play it and summon bruin for atleast some board presence.


[[Meat hook]]

Sneaky meathook to pull their avatar into your territory. Pulled through thorns + trollbridge from bruin provides a respectful 9 damage. Probably forcing them to discard and ending the game on the spot. I only play with 1 because drawing two in one game would suck so much ass.


[[Adept Illusionist]]

Crazy good with [[Thin ice]]. Sacrificing a brother after riptiding or undertowing an enemy minion onto the ice. Early chip damage and lining up [[Snowball]] in the midgame. Aswell as working togheter with tawny to take down a 3 power minion basically for free. These guys end up being utility for anything that you might need, even sacrificing one for a trollbridge or sacrificing both of them incase you need to take drastic measures against a big guy in your territory.

If cemetary hate goes beyond what we have today this will go away. Things like [[Kor Crematory]], [[Mismanaged Mortuary]] and [[Bureau of Occult Control]] makes thes guys boring to play.


[[Pied Piper of hameln]]

A card im always on the edge about. Tokens arent in every game and this card is often useless. When its good its nice because it can really ruin certain decks aswell as hinder a necromancer for a couple of turns. One day this might change into another 3 or 4 drop if the meta doesnt call for it anymore.


[[Polar Explorers]]

These guys line up perfectly with our gameplan and are almost always happy to see. Main reason for them is getting [[Bruin]] active as quick as possible. Great to summon minions in your backrow safe from [[Gargantulas]] and [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]] etc. And avoiding back breaking defensive sites.


[[Aino]]

Puts pressure on an opponent and might force out a rootspider that we will later [[Geyser]]. Its not the most OP unique but when it does its thing it feels nice.

In mono water she kind of serves the purpose as a death door finisher with stealth. Definetley keep it in hand if you draw it late unless theres a more effective finisher.


[[Coy Nixie]]

Certainly feels overpowered here. She will open up attacks that werent previously discovered. Drag in the enemy avatar towards your sites. Functions as a death door finisher aswell if your opponent stepped up to cast a [[Poison Nova]] or other. She is one of the better minions in this deck.

Popping wards. The list goes on.

A key tech ive found works well is looking to build out sites on the third row in your opponents territory. This provides a safe haven when you flip for [[Bruin]] for avoiding atlantean fate. But more importantly serves as a spawning point for Nixie. Where you can instantly pull in the enemy avatar and potentially riptide them onto your thorns.


[[Fey Changeling]]

Used on the attack when opponent plays a minion infront of your [[Lugbog Cat]] and just start pushing damage. Damage is one of the most important things in this list. We want to end the game quickly and with as few roadblocks as possible.

Used defensively it simply buys you a turn but that could be enough. Way better on the offense.

After its been deployed i just look to hit an unblocked site, participate in killing a high powered minion or blocking.


[[Lugbog Cat]]

Just a great minion and when combined with a pond its such heavy pressure that opponent often folds before they can get their foot in the game.

Not much to say here other than to keep these in opening hand and if you have two it might be worth to go looking for a pond.


[[Nelly Longarms]]

Threaten their avatar with a drag. Play it on river rapids or use riptides to reposition. Good minion that makes it awkward to play.


[[Order of the Sacred Oak]]

At two since im so scared of [[Bane of Aventis]] but other than that i dont know why im only on two. I think i drew them too much and felt that their impact was lower than expected.

Alot of good decks will have access to a silencing effect, a desert or other that kind of ruins the purpose of them.


[[Sea raider]]

Great "Counter" to [[Plague of frogs]] and Foot Soldiers. This guy lets our hand be thick and gives access to other elements spells which can prove to be useful. This guy is meant to die in the name of card draw.


[[Abaddon Succubus]]

One of the goats here, 3 damage on flipped side. Pulling into a wuthering heights. Well you can imagine the damage. Meanwhile we are healing and leaving a 3 power body on the board. Just the best minion and will be a keep in opening hand. Works well with Geyser as people will try to play far away from it however do not expect an airborne attack.


[[Captain Baldassare]]

Love this ability and provides very interesting games. Certain choices are tricky to make but provide super interesting lines of play. Discarding bangers also feels soothing.


[[Failed Mutation]]

Beast at staying around. With this classic beater we can secure a healthym, strong boardstate alongside [[Bruin]]


[[Lord of unland]]

Great to power up [[Bruin]] when you are in a defensive position. Can also chase around the opponents [[Coy Nixie]] to get them off problematic sites. Very strong now that water is so popular giving the upper hand in trades. I will usually try to walk him in under opponents water site and go in for a strike further down the line. Often hes good to just stay submerged.

Comboes with [[Geyser]] and [[Floodplain]] in non water matchups.


[[Ruler of thul]]

This is the bomb of all bombs. Bruin + tawny + ruler is 10 damage with only 1 card from hand!!! Use him wisely and dont just play it whenever. The setup here is very important and do not greed to cast it early.


[[Sacred Stag]]

Stays around, It is a boring minion but very good. These guys feel extra good into another water deck that just played a stag because their stag cannot attack into your thorns. So you will keep a stag and they wont!


[[Selfsame Simulacrum]]

Selfsame is my favorite water card of all time. The ceiling on this card is endless and ive never experienced a match where i hadnt had the opportunity to cast it. Copy a [[Morgana le fay]], [[Gargantula]] their [[Gargantula]] or just copy one of your dudes. If you have other minions to cast i would wait until a juicer hits the bord that you can copy.


[[Archangel Raphael]]

Extra good when you pull their avatar to your side or if you manage to build your sites into their row. Alot of decks cannot finish you if you have the ward + [[Bruin]] or a [[Makeshift Barricade]]. Super grateful for this instant strike as dealing the killing blow is hard in mono water.


[[Questing Beast]]

Here comes another way to kill them at door or simply just deal alot of damage. Both of my 5 drops have a reason to exist in this deck. At that point in the game i am looking for a way to end my opponent and this just helps that.


[[Lord of lies]]

Is obviously quite an overpowered minion. Its hard not to include and helps alot when games drag out due to unforeseen reasons. I think the deck can function without it and sometimes i feel bad playing it because its so OP.


[[The green knight]]

Is a saving grace when you have fallen behind. With thorns this guy will deal 4 damage, 7 on a [[Troll Bridge]]. That is enough to boardwipe an entire offense. He can also be used aggressively in some capacity to tap down blockers. Comboes super well at door with [[Bruin]] and [[Makeshift Barricade]] making a nuisance to reach your avatar.


[[Plague of Frogs]]

The frogs are super versatile. They pick up trinkets, Adept users of [[The rack]] and friends of [[Ruler of thul]]. The blocking potential slows the enemies game down heavily.

They can also go gather drowned rings and other goodies.


[[Geyser]]

[[Rootspider]] puts a stick in our wheels but the solution even draws you a card. Airborne can be hard to deal with and who doesnt like an airborne lord of lies?

This is a great card but i will cycle it for another card if i draw it early on and dont see any use case for it.


[[Pollimorph]]

[[Tawny]] can cast it and the frog cant even enter your site. The downsides to this card are almost non existent. Thanks Eriks Curiosa.


[[Riptide]]

Movement, This deck is all about movement so why not have a really good one that works for both minions and avatars. The icing on the cake is that it draws you a card. Its also used on door to dig through your deck to find that sweet finisher you are looking for. Sweeping away blockers. Love to see a [[Riptide]] in the mid game and is one of the foundational cards that make this deck work.

I could easily go to 4 of these but having one in the toolbox also seems worth it to me.


[[Ice lance]]

Might look weird but we need another finisher. Obviously they cannot banish it using [[Legion of Gall]] or put a tax on it with [[Bureau of Occult Control]]. Which is why i dont just play another [[Toolbox]].

I save it for door unless i see a sweet 2 for 1 potential off [[Tawny]]. Such as killing a Vile imp and a Dragonette. Maybe killing off 2 [[Adept Illusionist]] is worth it. Im not sure.


[[Swap]]

1 swap because even though it is strong ive found that its a little bit situational. I think i can safely go to 2 and still be happy but 3 feels way too much when i am looking to put out minions. It is very versatile because it can be used on deaths door, steal things, put unsuspecting minions on a thin ice and more.


[[Mesmerism]]

Just game winning.


[[Stormy seas]]

Found that i needed a card that was non targeted removal to get around ward and stealth but also deal with artifacts. It can put a stop for someone trying to set up a huge ruler turn.

The ceiling is so high and for only 1 more mana than [[Drown]]. But 2 less mana than [[Call of the Sea]] which feels way too expensive and combined with the movement in our list can make for similar results.


[[Snowball]]

Last spell and it is another death door finisher!! Yes, when we eventually door them we need alot of things in our deck that we can find to kill them. Heres another one. Deals alot of damage at times if you need to. Ive also used this as a delivery mechanism for [[Bruin]] picking up a 3 powered enemy guy to kill them, Deal 3 to their avatar and then another 4 with [[Bruin]]. I like to keep my possibilites open and hence im playing with so many different deaths door finishers. This style of deckbuilding has proven to feel very flexible rather than just maindecking 3 snowballs or something like that. They all serve a similar purpose but do so in different ways.


SITES:


[[Bureau of Occult Control]]

I lacked when playing versus [[Imposter]]. This is here to remedy that. Also great because i am only playing 2 [[Toolbox]] so the pain in the ass isnt huge. Also, make sure to draw another site and play this last if you have peculiar port on hand.

I'll mulligan this if im not versus [[Imposter]] or [[Archimago]] in hopes of better sites.


[[Floodplain]]

Unleaches alot of cards that relate to your body of water. Great when your 4th site isnt a water site so you can still cast [[Mesmerism]] on turn 4 if needed. Making [[Rootspider]] bad is also a big positive.


[[Innsmouth dock]]

Enables thorns to finish someone off. Played upfront it also allows you to play minions safely in your back row and then pull them in to be ready for attack.


[[Maelström]]

More pulling, More goodness. Same as dock it can be played up front to pull your minions up. Full reach over the board versus another water deck feels real sweet, especially when your sites are spiky.


[[Mirror realm]]

Goes in any deck right? You have OP sites and you can have more. I have had 2 [[River Rapids]], A [[Wuthering heights]], and an [[Innsmouth Dock]]. Makes the game impossible to play. All thanks to mirror realm.


[[Peculiar port]]

Keeps up your hand size. Kind of a nonbo with Bureau and i had to cut something so im only playing 2. Great when you manage to cast a [[Horrible hybrids]] and make opponent discard a card due to a [[Troll bridge]] in the same game. Your hand size will be massive compared to opponent almost being in a topdecking situation without sacrificing any board presence.


[[Pond]]

[[Lugbog cat]], [[Sacred Stag]] and [[Questing beast]]. All out early swarming the board. A turn 2 cat followed by a turn 3 cat is breathtaking. I dont even hate this site later on in the game as it can allow for double casting for example a [[Pollimorph]] and [[Questing Beast]] while at 6 mana.


[[River Rapids]]

You know how this deck plays by now. Push them around. i like to have ordinary rivers to work with this aswell but we will see.


[[Sinkhole]]

Destroy the OP sites. Keep them off mana after you played some big stuff. Or keep it around if you need the mana yourself. Its a very versatile site. In some use cases you can even use it to pop your own site if they have a [[Lord of lies]] trying to get in. Its fringe but has won me games.


[[Tadpole pool]]

Generates some blockers, Attackers for [[Ruler of thul]] and snowball ammo.


[[Thin ice]]

Super good to kill minions free of charge with [[Coy nixie]], [[Adept illusionist]] and [[Tawny]]


[[Troll bridge]]

4 damage with thorns!!! they must be forced to discard a card!!! This staple site gets leveled up in [[Druid]] and has led many opponents to discarding multiple cards after pulling their avatar over this troll several times.


[[Undertow]]

MORE MOVEMENT. If i have to play this as a second site i will just put up my avatar so that i can get [[Bruin]] active quicker.


[[Wuthering heights]]

Last mention of movement, sorry but this site is OP. Be wary of playing your minions onto it versus earth.

A neat trick with this site is the mind games. Now your opponent has to play around a non existent [[Grapple shot]].


Collection:


Mono water collection is bad to say the least. Not much in way of aura removal or finishers.


[[Just a rock]]

Banish their ring seems good but you could also swap it.


[[Led astray]]

Sort of here as a non conditional [[Riptide]] you can walk minions into [[The void]] or just pull their avatar closer.


[[Old salt anchorman]]

The only real anti [[Coy nixie]] technology. Since it prevents the drowning of thin ice. Prevents [[Avatar of air]] of abusing your poor minions.


[[Riptide]]

Has been explained above. One in toolbox. Love that it draws you a card so your hand size stays up.


[[Drown]]

Removal.


[[Extinguish]]

As we are not in air this is all we get to remove auras. 2 for 1 when they play a jihad!! super good.


[[Horrible hybrids]]

Peculiar port.


[[Ice lance]]

The only finisher here! Cast it off any of your minions.


[[Makeshift Barricade]]

Excellent!! Traversing your sites to deal a finisher is already hard. Then getting through a barrier of 3 and dealing another damage. This card can easily buy you multiple turns.


[[Helpful hob]]

Never actually cast this but i see a world when lord of lies deals 18 damage.

filteredDecks.primer:
"Evil, Fliers and Ranged, OH MY!"


The TLDR:


Evil:

  • Vile Imp, Redmayne Hyena, Spore Spouts and Desecrate. Do the math.
  • You know who loves Desecrated Ground? Evil minions. What's better than a 5 power Legion of Gall? A 6 power Legion of Gall.


Fliers:

  • We've got 14 fliers and over half of them are 4+ power and either gain us life, wreck our opponent's Collection, or just cause a friggin headache!


Ranged:

  • A playset of Stygian Archers and Skirmishers of Mu? Yes. And I'd play more if I could!
  • Shout out to MTR Joseph (the one and only Realm Eater pilot in the Constructed Championship at SCRCON) for enlightening me on how disgusting Skirmishers can actually be. To be continued in full primer...


Ideal Early Game Plays:

  • T1 Tower > Forsaken into a T3 Desecrate to mess with our opponent's Affinity
  • T2 Spore Spouts > Vile Imp into a T3 Desecrate
  • T3 Jack the Ripper their Aino or Morgana into a T4 Desecrate


omg why does this guy love Desecrate so much...


Desecrate:

  • Think back at games you lost because of a well placed Smokestacks, Thin Ice, Troll Bridge, Bottomless Pit, Perilous Bridge, etc... yea. Desecrate handles that.
  • Buff your minions. Forsaken seems innocent until it hits for 3, Desecrates for 3, and then becomes a 4 power minion. "We have Lugbog Cat at home, sweetie".
  • Timing is everything, though. If you can't Move and Attack with your Evil minion without risking a trade then you're not set up for a Desecrate. But we're piloting AoA baby, oh and we have even more tech for that... stay tuned for the full primer!


Other Spells:

  • Arcane Barrage beats Ward as long as you can pay the minions power + 1. It wreaks havoc on tokens, is nightmare fuel against Imposter and can close out nearly any game thanks to AoA's inherent maneuverability.
  • Browse to hunt for Desecrate... (i know, i have a problem)
  • Disenchant. Because Ring and A. Fate exist.
  • Feast for Crows. F**k Mesmerism. (Both games I've lost to CJ at major events he beat me with Mesmerism... well, and because he's a top-notch player)
  • Grapple Shot and Whirling Blades. I don't need to explain these - but - imagine your opponent plays their Archangel and you've got a Stygian Archers in play with a Trinket and Grapple Shot in hand. You Trinket your Archers, Grapple the Archangel to break ward and Ranged strike for 4 while getting an Allied Skelly to boot. It feels, so, good. Now imagine casting Whirling Blades on your Archers and killing more than one enemy minion to then replace each of them with Allied Skellys? Disgusting. Wait, Skellys are Evil right? Did someone say Desecrate?
  • Infiltrate and Poison Nova: unarguably two of the most impactful Fire spells at the single-Fire threshold level. These two spells are what forced me into splashing fire. Trust me, I hate having to run the castles, Colour and Ruins in place of other Air or utility sites, but I truly believe Infiltrate and Poison Nova are worth it.


Full primer to come...


Cheers and great games to everyone I played at SCRCON 2026!!!

filteredDecks.primer:
F/W/A SIA Mage


Sirprise It's Agrrovaine


A unique 3 element threshold intensive deck with high roll potential.


The thresholds are designed primary around 3/2/1 - F/W/A respectively. Primary goal is to get to 2/2 F/W, splashing air mostly for grapple shots and toolbox goodies. The third fire covers Morgana and Immolation.


Note: Technically new threshold reqs are 3/3/1 due to the addition of plague of frogs


The Mulligan


You're primary goal for an opening hand is two things, hit threshold and have a decent three drop.


Openers


Site placement is critical for success in more difficult games. The most important site you place is the your center forward site. What site you want there is match up dependent. If you're against aggro you want a troll bridge. If you're the aggressor whether your primary launch pad is water or land makes a big difference. The answer is that you want the opposite of whatever you're playing against. As an example if you're playing against a geomancer, you want your launch pad to be a water site because it allows you to drop threats safely to apply pressure on a site that can't have things buried on it. If you're against water you want a land site as a launch pad so your opponent can't drown minions on your own forward sites.


3 Drop & Sink'em

If on the play with the correct threshold play a sinkhole as your third site. Followed by a three drop minion, such as a cat or dragonettes. Immediately followed by blowing up the sinkhole to knock your opponent back down to one mana. On the next turn a good follow up is a grapple, a second three drop, or a swap.


Red Rover, I send my Doggie Over

If you're opening hand contains a Cerberus and a Grapple Shot, Cerberus can be forcefully moved away. Meaning an undefended avatar can take 10 damage on your turn 4, 3 if you started with a core or a P. Stone. If you're reading removal, this can be followed up by moving your battlemage forward to teleport Cerberus back safely depending on the match up.


Mini Combos


Dragonettes + Shrink

With a spellcaster (usually your battlemage) in position to shrink a minion along with a dragonettes that can be moved into position or cast from hand into line of site unobstructed allows you to shrink and kill a minion with your dragonettes.


Sir Pelleas + Blaze

A fun interaction unique to this element combination, elevated by the current meta of water. Pelleas free movement, along with blaze's defintion allows you to blaze many many locations depending on the board. My current understanding is free movement can't repeat steps, but this still allows him to freely deal 2 to large portions of a water based board.

filteredDecks.name: Deathspeaker Self Mill (cornerstone deck)
filteredDecks.primer:
Yo! Welcome to the primer for my DS Self Mill Deck!

To start things off a quick history on me a tcgs and why im choosing this deck as my main passion project for the Sorcery tcg.


Basically for as long as ive been playing tcgs (started with Invasion block for mtg) ive loved using the graveyard as a resource. So naturally in mtg I was the reanimator guy and when I got a good collection I competed in legacy format events using a deck called Tin Fins and Dredge as a back up. I loved every minute of it too until mtg started doing things I heavily disagreed with and I dropped the game about 7ish years ago. When Sorcery was announced on KS it immediately gave me those mtg vibes I loved as a kid so I backed it. When I got my product I saw DS and knew this was the avatar for me and ive been working on making this deck as fun as I can so here we are haha.


So for the start behind this self mill deck is ever growing as I play more games against various avatars and opposing strats. The idea is pretty simple though, mill yourself to get that advantage asap. The advantage here is tons of card draw with those wizards and lots of minion generation with the necromancers. I also run a solid ordinary package that answers various problematic cards that exist in the game. The way I look at avatars is that each one offers the player a "cheat code" to help them win paired with piloting the deck correctly. DS "cheat code" is obviously using the graveyard as a second hand. When all this self mill stuff got printed in gothic my face lit right up and I felt at home haha. Something ive learned though is to not fill that yard up too fast, especially if the opponent is on fire, the bigger a yard you have the juicier a target it can become. Try to keep it minimal until you need new targets and go from there. In my maybe board I have a short stack of cards im considering and site hate is something ive added to it thanks to that unique fire site that kills my deck lol. Youll also notice I dont run ring, p stone, cores or other obvious "staple competitive cards" and I do that for a reason. I dont find those cards fun at all to play and im all about having fun here. If you want to run those no shame on you and feel free to edit the deck as you see fit to run the cards you want to run. Im choosing to run the token generating stuff to offer me good chump blockers or easy ping damage to opposing sites. Tokens in general are just annoying so it felt right to me and so far its been fun. Hotwheel has also been an all star for me. Killing random dudes or even putting in that finishing blow has been great. 3 might be overkill but I like running max copies of stuff when I can. I will say the mvp of the deck though is Skeleton Mage. I. Love. That. Card! Its so so good at everything this deck wants to do and casting Common Sense a million times in a game just feels criminal lol. But really it helps me always have an answer to my opponent with all the 1 of ordinary cards I run to be fetched with Common Sense. I also run some pet cards that happen to be very strong like good ol pudgy but besides that I tried making the deck with cards that function in my hand and graveyard to really abuse that "cheat code" I mentioned.


Hopefully this probably poorly written primer helps you all make your own sick DS decks and show my passion for the deck! So go out there and resurrect the realm in a fashion that fits you best!

filteredDecks.primer:
Hello there! Hope you having a lovely day.


I was recently at a tournament in Krems, Austria and did preety well for myself! Even though I am playing only for 5 months I still have a lot to learn about this wonderful game and I do believe that this deck is currently one of the strongest water decks out there.


This deck is not my own creation. The mastermind behind it is @Hicham and you should check his main decklist out on curiosa. He is a great guy, and helped me out immensely on learning the deck properly, and understanding the underlying principles of how he imagined things working.


I enjoyed playing with this deck, it is very good and for someone like me, that hasn't played much competitive rl tournaments and it made me not overthink about a lot of things, but rather play aggressive and focus on my own game plan.


The basis of the deck, if you are a magic player, this would be the most Simic experience you will have.


You want to ramp out your big guys, you want to overflow the board, and you want to use your spells to out position your opponents and do valuable trades. Card draw is king in a lot of scenarios where things go a bit late game, but in reality, water is so strong right now, that in the end you will have more value on the board compared to your opponents.


Silver bullet, Snowball, good Swaps will finish on door.


The meta is strong with Necromancers, but a Pied Piper or a Mester Stoor Worm can do a lot of work.


Hopefully you will try it for yourself and enjoy it in its own glory!


Take care and have fun sorcery buddies!

filteredDecks.name: Dust Reanimator 8th SCGCon Richmond (3-2)
filteredDecks.primer:
Hi there! Please note that this Primer is a work in progress as I have time to write down my thoughts on the deck. In general this deck was an experiment to see if this archetype is currently viable (and because I love and always want to play Deathspeaker). As of right now I think that this deck, while fun and sometimes very powerful, is probably too high variance to post good results consistently. It has some very busted possible openings and can have a strong late game, but struggles a bit in the mid-game as it's minions start to get outclassed. Water is also a tough matchup due to having so much burrow removal, which is rough in the current water-heavy meta. All that being said, if you like to have explosive starts reanimating a vampire on turn 2 or 3, and like to grind incremental value out of your graveyard, this deck is a blast to play.


Minions

The Deathspeaker's bread and butter, minions with genesis or genesis-like abilities. This deck currently runs 39 minions, of which 26 have a genesis ability. It's my opinion that while you want a lot of genesis with DS, you really want to prioritize the cheap genesis minions and look for higher impact minions in the 4+ parts of the curve. I rarely want to deathspeak the more expensive minions in this deck, preferring instead to double spell one with some removal or another cheap minion. The exceptions to this are those minions like Bane of Aventis or Archangel Michael that can shore up a tough matchup, get you back in the game, or win out of the graveyard. The knights, pudge, witherwing, returned king, and the vampires are just there as strong minions at their point in the curve, and for undead to work with carrionette.


Auras and Artifacts

I originally had the two relevant cores in the deck and decided for this playstyle that they just aren't necessary. You'd rather be milling or reanimating in the early turns and the cores don't really help with that, and they always feel terrible to draw in the late game. Ring is ring, it's just too good not to play, even though we aren't super mobile with our avatar. Book of the dead provides additional recursion to help us profit from the self mill, and can get back some of our non-undead stuff in the late game. The black plague is our best answer to root spider and coy nixie, and the deck is otherwise soft to those most annoying of minions.


Magic

Our magic is generally one for one removal and sweepers, with the additional reanimates in 3 Carrionettes. I think Carionette is just great with the 5 vampires, and I love to see it early or late. The Bolts and Burys are just ways to help keep pace with stronger minions in the early game. Gift of the wolf is great with the small minions and the vampires as a way to trade up or gain some extra life, or both. Earthquake does a lot of work to stabilize, though it often will get less value than you want because of the abundance of water sites running around. Craterize has been good occasionally, but I intend to cut it from the deck. I almost always am too far gone/on DD to play it effectively, or have enough relevant minions that I don't want to kill them. I will probably add the fourth Gift of the wolf and maybe another Bury instead, or possibly keep just one.


Sites

Building a wall up front of bridges, hollows, and heights is ideally what you want to be doing, which you can then fly around later or traverse with your small minions. Gumming up the ground for the first few turns is pretty critical against the more aggressive strategies. The self-mill sites are so good in this deck, it can't be overstated. I often mulligan aggressively to find one, especially if I have Boneyard or Orpheus' Crossing in hand.


Both Boneyard and Orpheus' Crossing are high risk, high reward plays, but I think the potential is worth it. Both feel insane on turn 2, though you have to be very careful with Crossing to consider how your opponent might kill you the next turn. Having blockers for minions and projectiles is highly recommended. Both the reanimate sites feel bad in the mid-game unfortunately, and I sometimes got stuck holding them. However, if you can get a Gargantula in the cemetery it effectively negates whatever your opponent might summon on Boneyard (for the most part). Crossing is also amazing for getting you back in the game if you are already on DD.


I often drew Apex of babel without the Base, and I would probably cut these sites for something better. The idea is fun, but I can't run the full 3 bases without making cuts to better sites. Would consider replacing them with Mount Ussar Sanctuary and a watchtower or other air utility site. The misers lookout is just another ordinary site to help mitigate Atlantean Fate blowouts.

filteredDecks.primer:
Two events played. Was 10-1 until I lost both of games #7 and #8 in the swiss rounds of the main event. Better luck next year!


Was planning on playing my earth build in the main event but after doing so well on Friday I ended up playing my mono air list for the main event. I beat 3 water necros in swiss on day #1. The main way this deck counters water builds is by using phyxis and sinkhole. Then aggro'ing them out. The idea is to be as sticky as possible w/ voidwalk, airborne and stealth. The Hounds of Ondaros are all-stars. Having airborne and whirling blades is so crucial for removal.


The main removal of the deck is to play the sites strategically and hopefully pull a bottomless pit, the void, or manor. If I don't get one of those sites in my starting hand I hard mulligan all 3 sites. Relying on this removal strategy works when it works. Its problematic when it doesn't work. Dan, who made top cut with AoA ended up splashing fire so he could have poison nova for removal. Great idea.

filteredDecks.primer:
Fire Pathfinder that I played at Sorcery Con 2026 - took 12th place on tiebreakers (6-2) with a very narrow loss in the last round (got the door first but didn't manage to top deck the kill - really epic fight and super well played by my opponent Ismark the Lesser). Pretty simple deck, not much to say about it. Definitely still lots of fine points to playing it though. In the current meta I think one of the big tricks with this deck is not overplaying onto the board while maintaining pressure. Especially into the "Creature Control" meta with lots of Water and Water/Air midrange decks this deck wins on tempo, but loses big to mass removal. You want to mulligan for minions early (maybe keep a single removal spell if you also have some low cost minions but top priority is having 2 and 3 drop minions to start the pressure game. Once you have a minion or two on board though you are just trying to maintain that.


The other common way to win with this deck is setting up a big turn where you blast in a bunch of damage with something like warp spasm, blaze of glory, betrayal, etc. Lots of other cards that go well in this deck, but everything is fighting for slots. Would love to run Shatter Strikes or maybe even Critical Strike to lean more into burst damage turns.


Really torn about Baba Yaga - I don't want more than 5 non fire sites (including mirror realm), so is the extra motion potential that is useful like 50% of the time it is played worth it, or am I better off just running a lone tower to get that ramp value..... Or wizard's Den for the extra card?

filteredDecks.name: Silent Fury SorceryCon 17th place
filteredDecks.primer:
This deck was very good, and I feel like a good choice for the field of decks present at SC. It's essentially the fury road shell with an emphasis on silence effects. I went 6-2 with this list at Sorcery Con 2026, losing round 2 to mud Geomancer, and round 8 to AoA. It won against 3 Necro decks, Avatar of Earth, fire pathfinder, and an Elementalist brew.


Notable cards:

Sister Stefánia - this card is a power house. I don't think any of the games I had it were close.

Sinterfee - this card is very good against the water decks. Paired with jihad it's amazing.

Corruptor freak - harasses well and can just move to sites forcing multiple interactions to answer it often into a just summoned fatty blocker

Rift valley/smokestacks - these are kind of the same slot because they let us bypass our opponents annoying sites. Expect your opponents to have very good sites. Having ways around them was very helpful.

Earthquake - this card does everything this deck wants. It helps get around sites, it kills stuff allowing you to attack, and most the time just moving the opposing avatar close to your attackers is good enough, get them on DD even if they are on all water sites.

Flame strike (collection) - I think I killed more avatars with this than anything else. You are pretty much always one step away from a hit on DD with this.

Onslaught - I think in many ways this is better than gift of the wolf even without the card draw. It makes spiders worthless, gives you a little charge when needed the spread out damage buff is often better than +2 on a single creature. It also lets you do silly things with your silence/disabled effects like play a slobermaw silenced then give it charge. Or allowing a sleeping giant to wake itself up by attacking a unit. I'll be testing with two copies.


Cards I'm considering cutting:

Blightstone - I got a little sold on this card by a friend. I didn't draw it very often, and each time it was kind of dead in my hand. There were a few times I wanted it. But sinterfee is almost always better.

Hyena - there's just not enough demons that are worth playing. I played it a lot as a 2 power creature, and had mixed feelings about it.

Leadworks - while annoying sites can be problematic for this deck this card never quite lined up the way I wanted. Its really hard in a deck that only wants to play 4 sites to have this line up with a threat in play and a site you need to deal with for a turn.

Slumbering giantess - this card was harder to wake up than I'd like. I still think it's good but it probably needs some other tweaks (more deserts?) to make worth it.

Critical strike (collection) - this was always supposed to be a spin attack, but I get these two chronically confused. Luckily they're pretty close to the same effect.

SorceryCon 11th place (6-2) Salt the Wound
filteredDecks.primer:
This is a mean deck. It won’t win you many friends but it will win you many games. The name of the game is burn it down or beat them down fast. Using site destruction to slow down or cripple your opponent or minions with immediate impact (i.e. charge, damage on genesis, damage at end of turn). The deck is purposefully built low to the ground for a quick start and eventually multi-spelling at higher mana totals.


Site Destruction Strategies

The main strategy of this deck is site destruction. It utilizes [[Hamlets Ablaze]] and [[Castles Ablaze]] to target defensive sites and your opponents threshold. There’s nothing worse than having a hand full of double pip spells and you constantly lose the threshold to cast them. [[Raze]] can be used to destroy opponents sites but more importantly their artifacts. It’s great for dealing with [[Dank Omphalos]] and its brethren, [[Battlemage]] with a shload of equipment, and if need be popping [[Roots of Yggdrasil]] for a complete board clear. Twice in the tournament, I cast [[Raze]] on my avatar and destroyed Roots the turn it came into play and that won me the game.


TO BE CONTINUED

This deck wants to play the [[Payload Trebuchet]] to fling big cost cards into your enemy's face.


To use a Trebuchet you need pairs of cheap minions that you don't mind tapping to use the Weapon instead of attacking. To that end we have lots of [[Foot Soldier (English)]] generation and low cost minions, especially ones that slow down the opponent or protect your cheap minions a little. The [[Siege Ballista]] are a simple alternative to this siege weapon. The [[Corpse Catapult]] is another option, and can work alongside the Trebuchet well, thorwing the card you just discarded in the same turn.


As ammuntion for the Trebuchet and Catapult you need lots of high cost cards. Lots of the Atlas is focused on stalling and slowing down your opponent until you can potentially cast these cards, in case you don't find your siege Weapons. You also have cost reducers and ramp options to help afford these big cost cards when you can.


[[Dwarven Digging Team]]s are just to try and protect your big cost Minions from being Buried.

filteredDecks.name: Silenced Bones - 3rd Place Elemental Series Q1 2026 (Sydney, Australia)
filteredDecks.primer:
Silenced Bones is a Necromancer mid-range deck supported by a Beast package and a Silence package.


Silence got a huge buff in Gothic with [[Silent Hills]] (and [[Sister Stefania]]) and I believe the archetype can be a great anti-meta option.


The Silence part of the deck shuts down the majority of the card pool, and manh ability-based archetypes like Ward. It is also the enabler for many parts of the Beast package, and other above curve minions such as [[Pirate Ship]] and [[Dalcean Phalanx]]. [[Silence]] itself is (W), so we include this element in the deck.


(E), on the other hand, is the nature (pun not intended) of the Beast archetype, and it is also the only archetype that works with Silence. The mana efficient minions like [[Sedge Crabs]] become a menace, while [[Pudge Butcher]] can transition between a hook thrower and a 4-cost 5-power demon. [[Assorted Animals]] is a 2+ card advantage for you if [[Haystack]] is not in play.


The general strategy is to pump out skeletons to attack AND defend (Silenced skeletons are great blockers!) using [[Necromancer]] with spare mana whenever possible, while taking favourable trades with above-curve Silenced minions. The deck either overwhelms the board or stalls enough time with Silence and defensive sites like [[Troll Bridge]] and [[Babbling Brook]] for a [[Craterize]] straight to Death's Door, followed by a finisher such as [[Zap]] or [[Ice Lance]].


Peculiar card choices:

  • [[Sir Yvain]] screams BEAST. If you're playing Beast, you should play him.
  • [[Garden of Eden]] is your wincon against any draw-heavy decks like [[Sorcerer]] and [[Deathspeaker]]. HARD MULLIGAN for it (3 sites + scry the sites deck). Otherwise, you'd better pray you out-draw them with [[Algor Omphalos]] or win the game in 5-6 turns (you won't, but you can try!).
  • [[Carrion Beetles]] is the vegetable that everyone refuses to play (graveyard hate) and is searchable via [[Common Sense]] and [[Assorted Animals]] with just (1).
  • [[Porcupine Pufferfish]] is an Ordinary Beast with Lethal for (1) (Don't silence him, let him speak!).
  • [[Harvest Festival]] is essentially a (3) spell for 4 in the form of two 2-power bodies. Very underrated!
  • [[Goat for Azazel]] is another good (1) Beast. You can use Silence to turn off his ability when you need to put him down early.
  • [[The Flood]] is a very good late-game board wipe in this particular deck because we play so many types of minions, letting us keep our board while deleting everything without Submerged (Silence also remove Submerged!).
  • [[Forlorn Keep]] is a 3-power body in the form of a site. Sometimes you may want to play this turn 3 to churn out [[Penitent Knight]], or turn 4 with an extra skelly instead of playing cards from your hand. [[Peculiar Port]] serves similar roles, but having an Evil minion may be disadvantaged in some matchups such as [[Persecutor]] or any [[Consecrated Ground]] users.
  • [[Pebbled Paths]], [[Impenetrable Copse]], and [[Haystack]] are interchangeable depending on your local meta. My local meta loves cards like [[Grapple Shot]] and [[Firebolts]].


Overall, this is a really fun deck to play and learn the basics of the game while being very budget-friendly. The list is kept as-is and may need to be optimised for future tournament plays (for example, [[Sister Stefania]] would be a great inclusion, if I had it...).


Shout out to Dean Gouskos and Allen Thrun for hosting the event and carrying the Sydney community on their backs!

Tournament Pathfinder
filteredDecks.primer:
Edit after local tournament (ended up 3:2)

Added extra sinterfree as an answer to those Coy Nixies and also 1 Infernal legion which can be realy great finisher.


Overview

This is a standard aggro build with some spicy inclusions from the Gothic set. The deck aims to apply early pressure, spread threats across the board, and force your opponent into a defensive death door as quickly as possible.


Key Card Choices

Draught — A silver bullet for water-heavy matchups. If the meta shifts toward water decks, this card can completely swing the game in your favor, especially when drawn early.

Gift of the Serpent — Excellent cycle card that also enables your low-value minions to trade up into larger threats. Never underestimate the tempo this provides.

Sinterfee — Fantastic removal bait. Opponents often feel compelled to answer this card immediately, which clears the way for your actual key threats. Whether it eats a removal spell or sticks on the board, you're winning either way.


Site Selection

Since this avatar doesn't rely on drawing a site for its power, I've included utility sites that disrupt common strategies:

  • Garden of Eden — Shuts down control decks that depend on card draw
  • Temple of Moloch — Provides extra mana for explosive combo turns
  • River of Blood — Neutralizes Ring of Morrigan healing, which works in our favor as the aggressor
  • Kor Krematory — Absolutely devastating against graveyard-reliant avatars

Mulligan Guide

Look for strong 2–3 drops. War Horse is particularly valuable for establishing sites in enemy territory, which is almost always advantageous for our gameplan.


General Tips

  • Don't stack minions together — cards like Earthquake and Atlantean Fate punish clustering
  • Spread your threats across the board
  • Prioritize attacking sites to accelerate your opponent's deaths door
  • Accept that aggro has variance — your first three draws heavily influence your win rate


Good luck and go fast!
