SCGCon Atlanta 2nd place 5-1 Deathspeaker Earth Air
filteredDecks.primer:
If you’re wondering “Why not card X?” Well…I’ve been playing this game for less than a month if you can believe it. I fell in love with the game and dove right in. During the event I traded my tickets for AL packs and opened the ring you see in the list at the end of round 4!!! I was so excited =). No Decklists…so in it went. Edit: I was asked to add a note to the primer. Judges were aware that I replaced a card in the middle of our no decklist tournament that wasn’t at compREL. Is it technically allowed? I honestly don’t know. I wasn’t shy about how excited I was and was telling everyone around me though =)


There were a lot of cards that didn’t really come into play much, but the early game and the repeated value are the core of the deck. We can play 1:1 removal because we’re going to get SO much value out of our cards. The mill sites were amazing. Observatory plus rats is incredible. Archangel Michael and Gargantula along with grandmaster wizard and master necromancer are our all star value cards to play from the cemetery.


The bolts and gifts were very often used to surprisingly put our opponent to door when they least expect it, doing 10 or more quite suddenly in one turn using the skeletal mages.


I’ve already taken the silver bullets out. Added a shrine of the dragon lord picked up at the event and making room to bump apprentice and novice back up to 4. Removed Gall as well. My opponents just weren’t using their collections enough, although I could see those coming back later in the year.


I want to try the 6 cost angels but I’m just trying to stay VERY focused on our plan at the moment and they don’t do anything from our cemetery.


My first 3 rounds all involved root spiders. I read the card before the event but didn’t realize so many people play these things. They constantly locked down angels, but I still found a way to chip damage and close with blots plus zap. After my third round I brainstormed with my opponent how to kill root spiders and all we could come up with is a burrowed rat with gift of the wolf for now. Every time I drew a toolbox I made sure to ask myself “should this just be zap or do I need it now”.


Water opponents are a problem. I lost to Mitch who played an unanswered Lilith into Pied Piper, two cards I didn’t even read before the event. After reading pied piper I just said “uh…yeah okay, I’m gonna go walk the hall. Congratulations.” lol…maybe I should have toughed it out, but he had already lured a unit, got a hit off of Lilith and established a frontline of troll bridge and thin ice. It was round 5 and I made the choice to relax before the last round.


6 rounds of Sorcery was incredible. I would repeat that day several times over if given the choice. I’ll definitely be back! Thanks for reading =)


Things I want to try next: I want to find some more room for top end. We can get a bit grindy with our tiny dudes and have some trouble closing. The bolts and gifts are really important for pushing damage but a touch more top end or mid could help. I want to try splashing red, but I feel like the double threshold sites really reward us for playing two elements right now with these powerful angels and triple threshold cards like gargantula. I do see how the red cards could give more closing power though. I didn’t like the tap requirement of silver bullets and the fact that we only have 2. I’m not sure what else to do with our collection yet but honestly it could just be 10 ordinaries.


I also want to try playing all of the cores with the red splash and the tri sites to have more access to playing from the opponents cemetery. ATM I do think the consistency of two elements is worth it.

filteredDecks.primer:
I registered for my LGS’s Cornerstone (we put in a lot of effort to get that status - should out to Battlegrounds in Richmond, VA!) but hadn’t played for five months. Going into the tournament, I needed 1) an Avatar I had at least some experience with 2) a deck that was pretty easy to pilot 3) something that could hopefully win or not make me look entirely foolish ;)


After looking at my old pre-Gothic decks, I landed on the “red deck wins” Pathfinder in a dusty deck box. I figured, “there have to be some cool new toys and more fire sites,” and I was pleasantly surprised. There’s a fair amount of Gothic in this deck as a result! I would add a Horns of Behemoth for the Wasteland if I had pulled one and I totally overlooked Vindictive Nation, which is also an easy add in lieu of one of the duals.


The Avatar pilots no differently than before, you have to attempt the optimal pattern to enable a path to at least six sites, but either via Giant, Warhorse, or just walking over a few sites, you can easily get to 10+ simply because of the tempo you have.


The deck archetype is classic sligh/red deck wins. You simply want to be as aggressive as possible. Gift of the Serpent, especially with Dragonettes, is AWESOME for taking out problematic minions. Searing Truth is an MVP as it gets you even more cards if you need them, but can also kill an Avatar instantly on DD. I’d definitely figure out a way to cut some things (I.e. Minor Explosion) to get up to max for each of those. I didn’t bother with any of the collection artifacts as they are simply too slow. The only collection card is a Hounds in case you elect to cast it from Molten Maar.


If you’re looking for something than can simply

blitz out a win, particularly before folks figure out deck efficiency and the meta, this may be a good choice for you. I’d you’re looking for something with some neat combos and cool interactions, there are a few, but really this is all about the burn. Enjoy the heat!

decks.primer:
Draft deck for the GenCon 2026 Limited Grand Contest.


I first picked Barging Barghest into Flame Strike, but the fire cards dried up rather quickly, but I started wheeling aggressive air minions so leaned air/fire aggro.


Pack 2 picked up some powerful red minions (Greater Blood Demon and Lord of Destruction) which solidified us into air/fire.


Pack 3 - Michael P passed me Harbinger and said no way you're playing this right? i initially passed it, but it came alll the back around and i last picked Harbinger. Turned it around and immediately sleeved it up to Michael's chagrin ;)



Game 1 (Quarterfinals): Joe G

Harbinger high-roll'ed with a portal on Joe's 2nd site. Turn 2 Earl of the Ivory Towers placed a lot of pressure on Joe. He ended up taking a lot of damage and losing a couple ordinaries to the Earl, until he drew a Silent Hills to turn off the Earl and trade for it. Brutal game for Joe.


Game 2: (Semifinals): Julian R

Harbinger mid-roll'ed with a portal on Julian's corner which allowed 2x Forsaken to start charging in early (Turn 1 forsaken, Turn 2 Bats; Turn 2 Forsaken + another 2-drop. Just a crazy start). Julian had The Void on his home site which actually wombo-combo'ed with my forsaken. He was in a very hard spot, but was able to battle back with larger more impactful minions and some 2:1's. Harbinger ran out of gas with Julian at 4 life, but were able to squeak out 4 more damage and get him to door. I had 2 very good cards in hand (Flame Strike and Zeppelin), but only 1 fire threshold, so I started drawing sites with Harbinger instead of moving up to try and knock on his door. Ended up drawing air sites and started to get worried. By this time, Julian has KO'ed most of my minons and stabilized the board. My life quickly ticked down from 20 to DD.


Finally i drew a fire site, played it and passed the turn. Julian surrounded my avatar with multiple minions and... passed the turn. Luckily, his minions were tapped so Harbinger could step up 1 site and Flame Strike his avatar on the other side of the board. Crazy game and I really want to give Julian credit for how he recovered from my crazy start.


OK onto the finals against xNattu. The last time he played he stomped my face in. I'm spooked.


Game 3 (Finals): Sean D (xNattu)

On Camera.

I have the play.

Harbinger rolls 2 bad portals, then hits a great spot. My 2nd site.

I have the actual nuts. Den of Evil. Portal on 2nd site. Greater Blood Demon. mull 1 site.

Turn 1: site. pass

Turn 2: Den of evil. Cast Greater Blood Demon (6 power) for 2 mana. Pass the turn.

Turn 3: Nattu is on full defense mode here and is playing sites on the back row. I play my 3rd site in his zone. Move up demon. Cast Hollow One (4 power) for 2 mana. I have 2 ways to kill his 2drop mortal, so i feel confident that i can disable the Hollow One quickly. Pass the turn. (10-power on Turn 2 in limited!)

Turn 4: Nattu has a 2drop mortal with ward and 3drop undead. Demon attacks the mortal & he allows it to pop the ward. Then I cast Ravenous Werewolf (4mana on my portal) to attempt to kill his mortal to wake up the Hollow One. He correctly blocks with an undead to trade. Hollow One is still disabled, but i'm feeling good. the Demon is still wreaking havoc on his side of the board. Pass to Nattu and drops his own Elite bomb which completed FLIPS THE GAME. Hyperparasite on his home site. Pick up and disable my demon. Hollow One is still disabled. Pass to me.

Turn 5-7: No minions in hand. A flame strike which can't kill hyperparasite. Full on panic sets in. Cycle a Gift and tank for about 6min after drawing another 3-dmg removal spell. This is essentially the end of the game.... pass to nattu. he double teams to kill the disabled demon. then kills my disabled hollow one. i land an Earl and a couple willing tributes and HOPE to draw witching hour to pump my earl then untap earl with the tributes... but alas the game is over. GG Nattu.

His list and game report are here: https://curiosa.io/decks/cmsde663u000c0akqcrl42bri?tab=primer


(After watching the replay, I think playing out the Accursed desert on turn 1 may have lost me the match... That would have been very helpful in killing the warded mortal and waking up my hollow one Sooner.... Alas I didn't sandbag it... Played it instead of a twilight bloom as I typically hold them to help with threshold costs. In Retrospect the bloom on 1 and desert on 3 might hang swung the game my way. Welp def need more practice!)


I had a great time and am so happy to have this story :D


Nattu and I are signing each other's Elite bombs (hyperparasite and greater blood demon) and exchanging them. Looking forward to a rematch at AotR.

decks.name: GenCon 26 Limited Grand Contest 1st - Forecast
decks.primer:
If you want to see the sealed list that got me here you can see that here:

https://curiosa.io/decks/cmsdce2et00040aj2txr7cgol?tab=view


The Draft:

I went into the draft wanting to pull mud, having successfully piloted a sealed version of it to 4-0. Ready and willing to adapt as needed but w/ a build in mind.

Over the course of the draft I managed to build up a decent mud back bone, but felt a bit light on the top end. Around pack two or early pack three I managed to pick up the [[dreadwing]] and then those who linger along with two [[den of evil]]. Meaning I'd be three element, but able to sneak some large threats without worrying about threshold as much.


Game 1 Cameron on [[Spellslinger]]:

I was going second, against another spell slinger iirc. He opened with a two drop. I had [[bitten]] in my hand, left my front square open opting to build to the side hoping to slow the game down to reach my bigger threats. He took my front square moved his 2 power minion up and dropped another 3 power minion in front of me. I ripped [[Instigator imp]] off the top, dropped two bodies down while removing his board. A play that caught him so off guard he couldn't help but express his... bewilderment. From there I wrapped my sites in a U around his froward site. Then I managed to build up some decent threats including [[Failed Mutation]], which he had no way to deal with. Eventually I got [[bull whip]] out my on avatar which allowed me to deal with a lot of skeletons efficiently while also getting effective trades. Bullwhip almost didn't make the cut, but ended up being huge for this game in allowing me to deal with the very wide boards Cameron threw at me.


Game 2 (Justin I think?) on [[Persecutor]]:

I don't remember the early game as well, but know that my opponent didn't put out many early game threats which was a huge boon for my build. The board ended up building to my right, his left because of how I wanted to position my [[peculiar port]]. We made some incremental trades and I started to take board control, leading into him dropping his first real threat, an [[undesirables]]. He ended up using a [[stage coach]] to move that away from the fight on the right. A play that had me cautious, because it left him open to taking damage that put him close to door. He opted to start swinging in to my center site with his [[persecutor]] his [[undesirables]] behind him. I felt as though I hadn't seen much removal so was hesitant but willing to drop the [[Ten-tonne slug]] on his face. Putting him in a position where he was 100% going to door the following turn. He gave me one last surprise by opting to swing at an the open site to the left with his avatar, allowing me to door him on his turn. He then swung in with his undesirables for 5 and followed it up w/ desecrate. I went close to door but not quite and had enough threats surrounding him that the game was over.


The Finals

Game 3 John aka FooPossum on [[Harbinger]]:

Another game where I lost the die roll. Meaning I'd be on the back foot but against a non-spell slinger flush with options and knowledge. I did not expect what was one of the craziest openers I've ever seen of a turn 2 [[greater blood demon]]. I did thankfully have a decent amount of anti-aggro tech, sitting on a [[holy warrior]] and [[hyper parasite]] in hand. I was hoping to pick up the demon and slay it before it dealt to much if any damage.


The turn 3 follow up of a [[Hollow one]] changed my perspective. Knowing when my warrior died it would enable the hollow one that was sitting on the site in front of me. Looking at my hand I have a [[Penitent Knight]] and [[Crawler]], and I know this is a play I can not mess up. I need to play the crawler to help ensure my [[holy warrior]] survives. Keeping his hollow one at bay. Doing my best to keep my poker face on because I want him to swing in with the GBD, knowing I'll go to 4 mana next turn to disable it with [[hyper parasite]].


I also know that if the holy warrior dies too soon the board will turn against me fast. I pass the turn with a warded holy warrior and crawler facing down a GBD and disabled hollow one. Praying he doesn't have a trail by fire, or another way to remove the warrior once it's bare. He swings with GBD, my holy warrior lays bare, I anxiously await to see my fate. Foo follows it up with a Ravenous werewolf for 4, a very unexpected play from my side. It trades with the crawler keeping the hollow one still disabled and unable to trade with my hyper parasite. I managed to take the right gambit. He passes I draw, immediately deal with the GBD by swinging at the disable minion with the parasite and holy warrior, successfully flipping the board.


I then follow that up by playing a forward site to the right and dropping dread wing, opting to take the damage. The following turn he manages to kill my holy warrior to turn on his hollow one and attempts to remove the hyper parasite. I opt to block with my dreadwing, knowing that with no mana left next turn the hyper parasite can land a hit on his site making his next blocks awkward. From there I continue to build a larger board through turns dropping a Penitent knight, failed mutation to get him to door. He does drop an Earl along with some willing tributes but I don't take the bait for trades and push damage. He goes out with a bang by managing to hit for a solid amount of damage with the Earl sac'ing one tribute but it's not enough to door me. I rip a bitten off the top, move units into position and beat a dead horse by also wiping the board including the earl with bull whip + bitten.


The next day a thought popped into my head for my favorite trade of all time. I signed my hyper parasite and traded it for the signed GBD by John. A card that I will forever cherish as a good memory and that I hope John can too.

decks.name: HELLAMENTALIST - 3rd in Grand Contest Vegas 2026 - “All The Best”
decks.primer:
** NOTE!!** 07/17/2026 - With the change to Lord of Lies, I would either go MUCH heavier on water, or I would remove it entirely. Probably remove it.


MIT Opensource license - use as is, modify, commercialize this deck list. A common modification would be to add more to the higher end of the curve for more staying power if you don't knock somebody out immediately. Also more blinks and flanking maneuvers, if so inclined.


Over the past several months, I have played numerous games of various mixes of [[Elementalist]]. I have played with high threshold bombs in multiple thresholds like [[Morgana Le Fay]] and [[Mesmerism]], heavy "[[Ghoul]]" sites like [[Forsaken Crypt]], [[Assorted Animals]] with numerous 1 cost ordinary beasts and [[Hamlet]], I have tried all of the knights, and multiple variations of light exposure to different mixes of double threshold.


NOTE: For a lower cost version, substitute [[Ring of Morrigan]] with an additional [[Blink]]. It was a last moment change before the tournament to help deal with wards, and shore up the bad matchup against (F)(F)(F) Fire [[Pathfinder]] (F)(F)(F). Additionally, Colour out of Space and Tintagel are great, but not hyper impactful. You could probably get the proper threshold mix by replacing them and 1 village with dual threshold sites. Everything else is either fairly reasonable or downright cheap for cards (I think).


This is the best mix of all of the ideas that I have come across so far, and with the 3rd place finish at Grand Contest in Vegas, 2026, I am not sure that I will explore further ideas on my own. Now, for exposure to the main concept, it is simple, but also effective:


This deck is build to rip the face off of the opponent in a burst of higher than curve minions with extra mana. It is hard to beat a turn 2 or turn 3 [[King Arthur]] and I have yet to lose when that happens. Or the old turn 3 [[Pudge Butcher]] followed by [[Sinkhole]]. Need to move pudgie? Invest in a [[War Horse]] or [[Blink]]. Now, I will cover the reasons for each card, mostly, and in some order of importance:


Best card in the deck - [[Gift of the Wolf]]

Ramp Sites - City of Souls, Glass, and Traitors. - Go fast. Don't worry about your opponent using [[City of Traitors]], they won't have time.

Ramp Sites - Towers, Dark, Lone, Gothic, Merlin's. - Go fast.

Ghoul Sites - [[Peculiar Port]] & [[Forlorn Keep]] - With 5, you ofter get to play a 3 power minion you didn't need to draw on turn 2-5.

Villages (7) - Pile on the early aggression, early foot soldiers combined with the other better than curve minions adds up.


[[Root Spider]] Hate - This horrible little jerk can just win an opponent the game. We are looking to do quick and persistent damage early, and all [[Root Spiders]] must die. -- [[Geyser]], [[Silver Bullet]], [[The Black Plague]], [[Apply Alkahest]], [[Kingdom of Agatha]]


Above curve powered minions - [[Bosk Troll]], [[Autumn Unicorn]], [[King Arthur]], [[Pudge Butcher]], [[Sir Perceval]]


Anti-Sites, NO DEFENSE FOR YOU! - [[Sinterfee]], [[Sinkhole]]


Busted Cards - [[Atlantean Fate]], [[Book of the Dead]] - We get to cast nearly everything of our opponents too, [[Lady Iseult]], [[Sir Bors the Younger]], [[Gargantula]], [[Sir Gawain]], [[Lord of Lies]], [[Grapple Shot]], [[Whirling Blades]]


The great glue, cards that play their roles exceptionally well and we are nearly always glad to see, [[Daperyll Vampire]], [[Onslaught]], [[Blink]], [[Sir Perceval]], [[Sir Lamorak]], [[Doctor Demetrius]] (a ward or two will quickly secure a win given the likelihood of being ahead), [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]], [[War Horse]], [[Arjaro Exorcist]], [[Sir Tom Thumb]], [[Silver Bullet]], [[Wizard's Den]]



------

A few notes on choices. It seems like 3 [[Onslaught]] and 3 [[Whirling Blades]] would be optimal, but I had plenty of experience with all 6 and I just drew them too much and didn't have anything great to do on the board. Additionally, when I went from 0 Geyser to 3 Geyser, I found that when I need Geyser, I need it, and it would be better to have 4 with [[Silver Bullet]]. I also found that I would sit there with Silver Bullet in play and nothing great to do with it. So, I put 1 each of Onslaught and Whirling Blades into the collection.


Why not any double fire threshold? You get great cards like [[Balor of the Evil Eye]], [[The Great Famine]], and [[Sir Agravaine]]. Well, when you run double fire threshold in addition to the others (and I need earth/air, and love the water), then the adjustment to sites reduces ramp sites from 6 to 2. And it dilutes the deck enough that it suffers significantly.


Why not [[Archangel Michael]]? Well, I played him. Generally this deck will draw one site for turn, and I would want to have significantly more earth sites. More like 60-63% to be able to play Michael if you get him, and that skews the available mixes on sites to require more dual threshold sites which in turn reduces the sites that can either give you a Foot Soldier, or ramp, or a [[Ghoul]] type of minion.


Build the deck, and go forth and smash.

decks.primer:
Hi there! Please note that this Primer is a work in progress as I have time to write down my thoughts on the deck. In general this deck was an experiment to see if this archetype is currently viable (and because I love and always want to play Deathspeaker). As of right now I think that this deck, while fun and sometimes very powerful, is probably too high variance to post good results consistently. It has some very busted possible openings and can have a strong late game, but struggles a bit in the mid-game as it's minions start to get outclassed. Water is also a tough matchup due to having so much burrow removal, which is rough in the current water-heavy meta. All that being said, if you like to have explosive starts reanimating a vampire on turn 2 or 3, and like to grind incremental value out of your graveyard, this deck is a blast to play.


Minions

The Deathspeaker's bread and butter, minions with genesis or genesis-like abilities. This deck currently runs 39 minions, of which 26 have a genesis ability. It's my opinion that while you want a lot of genesis with DS, you really want to prioritize the cheap genesis minions and look for higher impact minions in the 4+ parts of the curve. I rarely want to deathspeak the more expensive minions in this deck, preferring instead to double spell one with some removal or another cheap minion. The exceptions to this are those minions like Bane of Aventis or Archangel Michael that can shore up a tough matchup, get you back in the game, or win out of the graveyard. The knights, pudge, witherwing, returned king, and the vampires are just there as strong minions at their point in the curve, and for undead to work with carrionette.


Auras and Artifacts

I originally had the two relevant cores in the deck and decided for this playstyle that they just aren't necessary. You'd rather be milling or reanimating in the early turns and the cores don't really help with that, and they always feel terrible to draw in the late game. Ring is ring, it's just too good not to play, even though we aren't super mobile with our avatar. Book of the dead provides additional recursion to help us profit from the self mill, and can get back some of our non-undead stuff in the late game. The black plague is our best answer to root spider and coy nixie, and the deck is otherwise soft to those most annoying of minions.


Magic

Our magic is generally one for one removal and sweepers, with the additional reanimates in 3 Carrionettes. I think Carionette is just great with the 5 vampires, and I love to see it early or late. The Bolts and Burys are just ways to help keep pace with stronger minions in the early game. Gift of the wolf is great with the small minions and the vampires as a way to trade up or gain some extra life, or both. Earthquake does a lot of work to stabilize, though it often will get less value than you want because of the abundance of water sites running around. Craterize has been good occasionally, but I intend to cut it from the deck. I almost always am too far gone/on DD to play it effectively, or have enough relevant minions that I don't want to kill them. I will probably add the fourth Gift of the wolf and maybe another Bury instead, or possibly keep just one.


Sites

Building a wall up front of bridges, hollows, and heights is ideally what you want to be doing, which you can then fly around later or traverse with your small minions. Gumming up the ground for the first few turns is pretty critical against the more aggressive strategies. The self-mill sites are so good in this deck, it can't be overstated. I often mulligan aggressively to find one, especially if I have Boneyard or Orpheus' Crossing in hand.


Both Boneyard and Orpheus' Crossing are high risk, high reward plays, but I think the potential is worth it. Both feel insane on turn 2, though you have to be very careful with Crossing to consider how your opponent might kill you the next turn. Having blockers for minions and projectiles is highly recommended. Both the reanimate sites feel bad in the mid-game unfortunately, and I sometimes got stuck holding them. However, if you can get a Gargantula in the cemetery it effectively negates whatever your opponent might summon on Boneyard (for the most part). Crossing is also amazing for getting you back in the game if you are already on DD.


I often drew Apex of babel without the Base, and I would probably cut these sites for something better. The idea is fun, but I can't run the full 3 bases without making cuts to better sites. Would consider replacing them with Mount Ussar Sanctuary and a watchtower or other air utility site. The misers lookout is just another ordinary site to help mitigate Atlantean Fate blowouts.

decks.primer:
If you’re wondering “Why not card X?” Well…I’ve been playing this game for less than a month if you can believe it. I fell in love with the game and dove right in. During the event I traded my tickets for AL packs and opened the ring you see in the list at the end of round 4!!! I was so excited =). No Decklists…so in it went. Edit: I was asked to add a note to the primer. Judges were aware that I replaced a card in the middle of our no decklist tournament that wasn’t at compREL. Is it technically allowed? I honestly don’t know. I wasn’t shy about how excited I was and was telling everyone around me though =)


There were a lot of cards that didn’t really come into play much, but the early game and the repeated value are the core of the deck. We can play 1:1 removal because we’re going to get SO much value out of our cards. The mill sites were amazing. Observatory plus rats is incredible. Archangel Michael and Gargantula along with grandmaster wizard and master necromancer are our all star value cards to play from the cemetery.


The bolts and gifts were very often used to surprisingly put our opponent to door when they least expect it, doing 10 or more quite suddenly in one turn using the skeletal mages.


I’ve already taken the silver bullets out. Added a shrine of the dragon lord picked up at the event and making room to bump apprentice and novice back up to 4. Removed Gall as well. My opponents just weren’t using their collections enough, although I could see those coming back later in the year.


I want to try the 6 cost angels but I’m just trying to stay VERY focused on our plan at the moment and they don’t do anything from our cemetery.


My first 3 rounds all involved root spiders. I read the card before the event but didn’t realize so many people play these things. They constantly locked down angels, but I still found a way to chip damage and close with blots plus zap. After my third round I brainstormed with my opponent how to kill root spiders and all we could come up with is a burrowed rat with gift of the wolf for now. Every time I drew a toolbox I made sure to ask myself “should this just be zap or do I need it now”.


Water opponents are a problem. I lost to Mitch who played an unanswered Lilith into Pied Piper, two cards I didn’t even read before the event. After reading pied piper I just said “uh…yeah okay, I’m gonna go walk the hall. Congratulations.” lol…maybe I should have toughed it out, but he had already lured a unit, got a hit off of Lilith and established a frontline of troll bridge and thin ice. It was round 5 and I made the choice to relax before the last round.


6 rounds of Sorcery was incredible. I would repeat that day several times over if given the choice. I’ll definitely be back! Thanks for reading =)


Things I want to try next: I want to find some more room for top end. We can get a bit grindy with our tiny dudes and have some trouble closing. The bolts and gifts are really important for pushing damage but a touch more top end or mid could help. I want to try splashing red, but I feel like the double threshold sites really reward us for playing two elements right now with these powerful angels and triple threshold cards like gargantula. I do see how the red cards could give more closing power though. I didn’t like the tap requirement of silver bullets and the fact that we only have 2. I’m not sure what else to do with our collection yet but honestly it could just be 10 ordinaries.


I also want to try playing all of the cores with the red splash and the tri sites to have more access to playing from the opponents cemetery. ATM I do think the consistency of two elements is worth it.

decks.name: Cornerstone Archie (Top 8) - 8/1/26 - Tokyo Toybox
decks.primer:
Archie Lists tend to follow similar patterns, but where mine diverges are on a couple of important points. Kettletop vs. Land Surveyor. I've land on Land Surveyor because there are many turns where I find that a land in hand immediately is much better than an additional damage here and there.


An example play that came up recently was me starting on 6 mana with no sites in hand, but I had a Craterize that I wanted to work towards. I play Landmass, pull my 7th site, play it. Play the Common Sense from hand, have 2 mana left, and get a Land Surveyor. This gives me my 8th land immediately in hand for the following turn, whereas Kettletop is not guaranteed to give me an additional land (and remember that Craterize requires you to discard a site to cast).


Another place of divergence, I still run Mirage because I want to replay certain sites like Pillar of Zeiros, Funeral Pyre, and Fields of Camlann. It also make a Fire threshold, so it's not totally useless on its own. Just gives me a little late-game utility.


Finally, most lists run Major Explosions. I have opted instead for full-on militia-attack. Another reason I like Land Surveyor over Kettletops in THIS list is because I'm regularly pumping my dudes up with spells like Onslaught, Gigantism, and Gift of the Wolf. I don't really care if they're 1 power to start with. I run 2x Assorted Animals, as well, and 1 War Horse, which is both aggressive (if they're on death's door) and defensive (if I'm on death's door - it will help me get out of harm's way).


Hope you enjoy! I've certainly been having a great time being the bad guy.

decks.name: Lava is Good - 2nd place - MA Cornerstone (61p)
voidwalk mist harbinger (1st place cornerstone)
decks.primer:
this is my most successful comp deck, currently sitting at a 75% wr on summit across all iterations and the last 4 seasons! for in person prized matches im currently 16-1 :)


mulligan - always try and get 2 of each threshold in your starting hand, or 2 and 1 and then scry the atlas for the other, if going second. aim for forsaken, dreamers, nixies, phantom steeds, stargazers in your opening spells


strategy - the biggest advantage to playing voidwalk is that your minions are difficult to remove! the enemy cant target them, mass remove them, or trade efficiently vs them. this often gives them options like the following:


a) defend sites and wait for an opportunity

b) play sites under voidwalk minions and attempt to kill them off one by one

c) full attack to try and race


this deck can hopefully exploit all three of these options. if its a), we have plenty of time to play stargazer and GMW to outdraw them and overwhelm them. if its b) we can encourage the enemy to play sites in a subpar formation and eventually exploit that by attacking where they cant defend. and if c), we have plenty of defensive sites like thin ice and babbling brook and board wipes like call of the sea and whirling blades to swing the game in our favor!


the best players (assuming they are playing a balanced midrangey deck) tend to choose option C. due to this, its imperative that we plan for a big board wipe! leave a 4 power minion safe in the void to prepare for whirling blades, keep a scatter in hand for a big thin ice push, or turn your brain off and afate them!


as for harbinger itself, versatile movement minions like steed and ophanim + void friendly movement spells like second wind counteract harbinger's positional restriction. a common line is to play phantom steed turn 2 on one of your sites, then something valuable like succubus or sacred stag, pick up with steed, and bring them safely into the void to save for later, as well as adding fuel to stargazer. second wind is preferred over blink as it crosses regional boundaries and has double the range, if cast twice. this allows something like dormant monstrosity that is normally very positionally restricted to survive its first turn in the void and then immediately join the fight!


weaknesses - any deck with more engineless card advantage and tokens like archimago or ramp geo is an uphill battle. eventually they will craterize or onslaught you... gotta play aggressive into those decks and hope for the best. fire aggro can also be super tough if you cant keep a succubus or thin ice nixie alive. battlemage also a bad matchup as they tend to play fewer minions and hit for 3 every turn, or land a huge ruler of thuul combo. best option is to try and race them

decks.name: Lethal Savior (Cornerstone 8/16 6th place)
decks.primer:
Sorry I wanted this to be short but ended up a little long. The main idea is play minions give them Wards and keep pressure on your opponent


NOTE: You can not ward Evil Minions. This means you cannot Ward [[Noxious Corpse]] or [[Daperyll Vampire]] but that is fine, play them and let your opponent worry about them.


Theme: Warded Lethal Minions that Strike your opponent.


Strengths: Everything you play is a threat causing strong early game pressure and mid game pressure.


Weaknesses: End game. The deck doesn't have a lot of draw or sustain so hit them hard and hit them quick. Overrun decks and burrow/submerge decks are also issues. Disable.


Strategy: Starting with Lands, try to make sure to have 2 (F)Threshold Sites and 1 (A) Threshold. You can get to 2 (A) Threshold later, the (F) is more important. Try to play [[Hamlet]] near your opponent and use [[Spore Spouts]] to drop your Minions where your opponent doesn't want them. A nasty early game combo is [[Spore Spouts]] into [[Sacred Scarabs]] dropping the Scarabs on your opponents Avatar.


This deck is built around Wards and putting those Wards on Lethal minions. 

This deck also has plenty of Charge Minions that you can play with a Ward on, crash into your opponent, then Ward again after they have done their job. As long as your Minion has been Summoned this turn you can spend as much Mana as you would like to Ward them over and over.

The basic Strategy of the deck is to try to get your opponent to use more than 1 card to answer 1 of your Minions. If you can have them Attack your Minion with 2 Minions or use a Minion to crack your Ward then use a spell to kill the Minion you are playing the deck correctly. The reason for this is most other decks will have draw that you don't, make them waste the cards they draw until you get some of your bombs like [[Panorama Manticore]] [[Siege Giant]] and [[Saracen Raiders]] then you can put some real pressure on your opponent.

Early game try to get out 2 or 3 small Warded Minions, even if this means holding off playing the Minion a turn. For example if you start your hand with a [[Sirocco Scorpions]] don't play it turn two (unless you end up with a [[Hamlet]] Land for your second Land) wait until turn 3 when you can Ward it when you play it.

If your opponent has small Minions try not to trade with them, Attack Sites and force your opponent to Block. Make them make the mistakes.

Your deck will also have plenty of Spells that allow for Movement and Striking. Try to use the Strike cards to deal with Minions your opponent wants to keep on the board. Then in the same turn Attack something else and take 2 of their Minions off the board. The Strike cards are also a way to victory if they try to keep a defender up to prevent you from Attacking their Avatar.

[[Whirling Blades]] is your nuke, try to hold onto this for situations where you need to deal with multiple enemies, or when you need to end the game. Use [[Grapple Shot]] to get your Minions into spots that make your opponent nervous, or in a spot for you to set up spells like [[Firebreathing]] since a lot of your minions are Beasts they can cast this spell from their location. 

Late Game your Strategy doesn't change too much, play your Minions with Wards and try to trade up and keep more Minions on the board than your opponent..


Even though a lot of your Minions are just 1 Power they pack quite the punch with lethal. Just play things attack and let your opponent worry about your Minions. Have fun!


Single Card discussion: There are some cards that pop wards, you don't really need to play around them but if you can remove them that would be best.


Matchup dependent advice: When playing against a deck that plays many small Minions like [[Necromancer]] try to make them block you and when you can get a [[Toolbox]] use that to play [[Murder of Crows]] once you know they have over stretched themselves. [[Firebreathing]] is in this deck specifically for Winion decks.


[[Ring of Morrigan]] is something you HAVE to deal with, this is why you have [[Shatter Strike]] and [[Disenchant]]. If you cant it will destroy your Minions and all the work you did early game.


This deck is great even without the Unique's or Elites, just swap them out for something that you like or something beefy and you will be good to go. The Ordinary cards are what make this deck click.


Collection cards (When to sub and why):

Zap!: Used to end the game when Opponents on Deaths Door.

Blink: Use when you NEED the extra movement.

Disenchant: If the opponents strategy is Aura based or if they have [[Ring of Morrigan]]

Tactical Move: When everything needs to move.

Teleport: Chase or Escape.

Boil: For pesky Submerged Minions

Grapple Shot: Why not have another

Minor Explosion: Clear out 1 Site.

Murder of Crows: Play when the opponent has over stretched their minion creation.

Angry Mob: Just in case there is a Unique you can't deal with.

decks.name: Heavy is the Crown. Top 8 Cornerstone 8/15/26
decks.primer:
"Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown.”

-Shakespeare


This list was adapted from the many Mono Fire Pathfinder lists around, not trying to pretend otherwise.


I wanted to add this primer to highlight a few tweaks for flavor/personal touch and to talk about experimenting more with the “harpy strike movement mechanic” at my most recent local Cornerstone. The deck wound up getting top 8 on 8/15/26 which I was very happy about! Role playing wise I envisioned a minion grabbing the bloody crown off their foe only to become the next “royal” target.


I made the title to this deck before playing so it would have been cool to win the Cornerstone with that title but alas I got eaten by grey wolves instead…ggs Sorcery can be a very swingy game but that’s a part of its charm!


The overall game plan for this deck stays about the same as usual. Pathfinder wants to solidify zipping around the realm reliably getting to 5-6 mana. A quick note to new Pathfinders that I learned to be helpful is to be a little patient and try trading up/waiting to strike but still use your mana. This isn’t just a turn your minions sideways kind of deck and you want to spread out your threats across the realm to help protect against board wipes. Don’t be mistaken though the deck with the right draws can become really aggressive if it needs to!


Here are a few other things that I added/observed:


-Fire Airborne minions

I really think airborne fire minions are currently under appreciated! Their diagonal movement particularly after a harpy flight can really put your opponent on the back foot.


-Giving Lethal to Dragonettes and Kobolds

It can really help win the board after your opponent commits their turn to playing a high cost minion. It gets a bit trickier when they have ward of course! I may add some fire bolts in the future to help ping targets and kill pesky early minions a bit more reliably.


-”Flying movement + Harpy Strike” (trinkets and sword /crown to boost power making the likelihood of being to target more things on the board). I had one great play to put someone on door when I flew to their 1 power token struck it and then attacked their undefended site. I think they expected to have one more turn given the position of my minions on the board as this minion did not have airborne itself.


-Unfortunately, I thought the courts would impact the meta more severely than I witnessed across my 6 games. At least so far maybe people don’t have access to the courts or simply aren’t building around them (yet). I thought a lot more exceptional “low to the ground” minions would be played so a deck like mine would take advantage of that and out value them by utilizing the lethal mechanic and the “harpy strike”. One of the LGS that I played at used a lot of fire or splash fire so I was surprised to not see that and instead faced majority of earth and root spiders galore. Askelon Pheonix was one sad fire bird :( At least I didn’t run two as I originally thought I might.


”Giants Package”

-I am not sure about this overall. Siege Giant looks great and having them possibly have charge with Balor getting charge looks very strong. At least in my 6 games Siege Giant didn’t make much of an impact compared to my other charge/strike minions. Balor did some work but I am thinking about trying a “Demon Package” instead with Fallen Angels for more Airborne support. Do you like to run the Giant package in your mono fire lists? Comment below!


Root spiders

-I guess mono fire has to have some weaknesses but this little guy can stop us in our tracks completely. If you are in a heavy earth meta not sure how to stick in enough casting ability for future lava flows. Any ideas would be appreciated. Can anything else in Pathfinder lists stop them? Splash more air mobility? Risks threshold screw though. Let me know!


Silver Bullet over Tool Box?

Not sure but maybe future iterations use exceptional spells for more diversity/aoe capability? Bullet might be too slow or even taxed making it harder to cast and play on the same turn.


RoM? or not to RoM? that is the question…

-With so few spell casters maybe RoM isn’t even worth running? Pathfinder doesn’t seem nearby much of the realm to use this so I may substitute for Flame of the First One or another weapon?


Let me know your thoughts, particularly if you are a Pathfinder enjoyer as well. I am curious about other mono element Pathfinder builds such as mono water or earth so be on the lookout for those lists on my end!


-Telos

decks.name: 2nd Place Cornerstone ECG(primer update)
decks.primer:
Dragonlord/Vatn Draconis!?


If you had this reaction when seeing this deck, you are not alone. Many consider Vatn Draconis to be a lesser dragon when it comes to your ability. I mean, Who wants to spend mana to activate an ability that only works at the end of your turn and has to be used while you’re on a water site?


So what made this deck so good? The answers…


Draw Power


Say I have 6 mana and no cards. I have two minions attacking my site and no way to deal with them. I draw an Into The Abyss. I can only remove 1 minion, which means the other will hit me next turn.


Now, what if I was playing Dragonlord and just drew a Sir Pelleas? I can move, use my ability, and play Sir Pelleas along with it, putting my own threat on the board while simultaneously removing all others at a site.


This means I can have a deck full of minions, and not have to draw extra cards to use removal.


The Element Of Surprise


Nobody expects you to play water Dragonlord at a cornerstone. Nobody. As such, people expect this to be an easy match. They might not play their mulligans as seriously, or play low on the defense.


Then, just as they think they have you, you play your ability.


Suddenly, their minions are dead, they have no defense, and they have to look at your dragon again because they can’t believe their eyes.



Each Card, It’s Weakness, It’s strengths, And My Take On It


First up is Mariner’s Curse, A surprisingly good card in a deck that has excellent removal, This card is great when paired with Winter Nymph and Riptide. Always use this card over your ability if you have the choice. A 9/10 in a starting hand, 6/10 late game.


Atlantean Fate. If you have seen any water deck, you know how good it is. Just NEVER play it on your own sites, and be strategic against fire decks. 6/10 starting hand, 10/10 late game.


Mix Aqua is probably the best card in the deck on your first turn, never mulligan this card away. 10/10 early, 4/10 late game.


Ring Of Morrigan is one of the most historically powerful cards in all of sorcery, but is dangerous to play if you play a game against a good water player. Keep this card in hand until you desperately need it if you are against water. 6/10 early, 8/10

late game.


Toolbox. Must I say more?


Tombstone Wardens is one of the most interesting cards in this deck, If you don’t like it put in a Driftwood Marrows instead. Use this card to buff your defense and go all aggressive with your minions if you get this. 10/10 starting hand, 8/10 late game.


Dank Omphalos is very good in decks that have virtually no draw power (this deck), but be careful that you remember it cannot cast artifacts. 8/10 starting hand, 8/10 late game.


Winter Nymph is overpowered when used early against fire decks. I went against multiple fire pathfinders in the tournament, and when I used Winter Nymph it shut them down. If you place it right it can eliminate all redcaps, and it also is immune to kobolds if you keep it under stealth. 10/10 starting hand, 4/10 late game.


Aino is always a debate for me, it is powerful but not much more so than many other water 3 cost minions. Use this card later in the game as damage, but honestly I would mulligan it away if I got it in my starting hand without a Mix Aqua. 4/10 starting hand, 9/10 late game.


Brobdingnag Bullfrog is ok removal on maybe turn 6+, but this one is a really bad turn 3 play. Mulligan away. 3/10 starting hand, 9/10 late game.


Coy Nixie is quite the popular card, but unfortunately it just doesn’t fit in this deck to have 3 copies. It isn’t a bad play late game, but this deck has enough removal to make this card a disappointment to draw about 80% of the time. One copy doesn’t hurt though. 6/10 early, 7/10 late game.


Lugbog Cat is probably the best turn three play in this deck, and is never upsetting if you get it on the draw. Never forget to cast this minion to any water site, this works well if you combo this effect with Ruler Of Thul. 10/10 starting hand, 9/10 late game.


Order Of The Sacred Oak is an insane value minion, considering the fact that it is not effected by any courts, the order is a very safe card to have in any water deck. Use it wisely against fire pathfinder. If you play it while there is an Ablaze! Aura on your sites, they have no chance to kill it before the aura dispels. 10/10 third turn, 7/10 any other time.


Sir Pelleas is a great option to have in a splash of air, but is killed quickly by most removal spells. Use as an attacker. 5/10 starting hand, 8/10 late game.

decks.name: Soldiers of Surtr - 1st Place Cornerstone Dane's Games 2026
decks.primer:
"We do not command fire. Ngamahu lends it, and Hinekora returns it." - Lavianga, advisor to Kaom - Path of Exile

1st Place Cornerstone - Dane's Games West Chicago - 06/28/26


Many [[Sorcerer]]s in 2026 have undoubtedly played against a [[Necromancer]]. Maybe you've already written it off as a solved Avatar. Today I would like to present an off-meta Necromancer build that is engaging, explosive, and can be built budget friendly.


As you may know the Necromancer is one of the best Avatars for minion creation and likes to take advantage of that in a myriad of ways. [[Necromancer]]s produce Skeletons, and [[Skeleton]]s produce FEAR. Use these tools to your advantage. This Deck has been designed to work well in the 5-6 mana range and most of the Sites in this deck have been chosen with [[Peasant Revolt]] in mind.


  • Our minion package is fairly standard for a mono fire deck. We use 18 Exceptional minions with 3 Towns to help get them out a little quicker. Many of our minions are chosen simply for their Charge effect, to get as much damage on the board as soon as possible


  • My favorite inclusion is the [[Siege Giant]], which can throw a weaker ally here through the air to a nearby location. Throw your [[Necromancer]] up and start making [[Skeleton]]s on your opponent's Sites. Throw a [[Sacred Scarabs]] into position and get ready to [[Detonate]]. Equip a [[Torshammar Trinket]] and throw another [[Siege Giant]] for best results.


  • [[Detonate]] is the MVP of this deck. At (1) mana this allows the potential for any of your artifacts or minions (including [[Skeleton]]s) to be a localized [[Minor Explosion]]. For (3) mana, summon a [[Sacred Scarabs]] and detonate them to deal 6 damage. Use [[Infiltrate]] and [[Betrayal]] to take control of enemy minions and blow them up as well. Use your artifacts with impunity against decks that run [[Swap]], and make them think twice about stealing your [[Ring of Morrigan]] or [[Poisonous Dagger]].


  • [[Gift of the Serpent]] and [[Poisonous Dagger]] both give our minions Lethal, which helps make efficient trades. Give Lethal to [[Colicky Dragonettes]], [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]], or [[Balor]] for best results. Combine either with a [[Blaze of Glory]] for a spectacular board wipe.


  • [[Chains of Prometheus]] allows us to control the enemy board state by forcing our opponent to tap their strongest minion. This is a symmetrical effect that also punishes you, but with the creation of new [[Skeleton]]s every turn, you should be able to power through.


  • [[Blaze of Glory]] into [[Warp Spasm]] is one of the most potent combos in Sorcery. With a 4 or 5 power minion, this combo can deal 16-20 damage in one turn.

decks.name: 🌋 Lava Flow 🌋 (3-1 cornerstone)
decks.primer:
I was inspired by the announcement of the new Lavamancer Avatar!


I used Kyle’s ‘Ramptacular’ as a bit of a shell for the deck (because it’s fun as hell) and changed around the air elements to fire. Tons of top end spells and magics as finishers, I think it’s best to mulligan searching for the ramp and you’ll draw the big baddies using Sorcerer. There’s obviously tons of ramp in the deck and innate card draw with Sorcerer, but we’re also using villages to generate foot soldiers so we can stabilize and get to the late game. Debating putting even more villages in the list as well, they’re so good against the threat of Atlantean fate.


You should have 8-9 resources by turn 4 or 5 and usually with 4-5 cards in hand. Around turn 5 you should be drawing 2 from your spell book every turn.


The MVP in the cornerstone for me was Cherubim. Warded 4 power with the threat of projectile proved impossible for opponents to deal with. I will probably increase it to 2 of him



Going to be testing and tweaking this deck for a while, any feedback/comments are always welcome!


Thanks, JKRoar

decks.name: 1st Place Cornerstone Warsaw - Lava Geomancer
decks.primer:
Intro

This version of Geomancer is focused on controlling the realm through sticky minions and powerful mass removal. It’s a midrange-control deck. Stabilize your position and outvalue your opponent.


This primer is an in-depth (subjective) strategy guide for Geomancer. Continue if you enjoy reading this kind of stuff. I wrote it as a way to thank the community and other fellow Geomancers who wrote similar guides, they were incredibly useful.


How I started with this deck.

My good friend Filip wanted us to go to a Cornerstone and familiarize ourselves with the rest of the Sorcery community. The problem was that we have been playing Sorcery for just two months and our card pool was small. My deck wasn’t even a full 60/30 yet. 

I enjoy competing, so I wanted to come up with something that I could pilot to the top 8.



(E) Why Earth?

Earth has good minions and minions in Sorcery are often a removal spell on a stick. You can play earth defensively or aggressively. I enjoy this flexibility and playing control-ish decks. This element seemed to fit my playstyle very well. Coincidentally, no one else in our local playgroup played earth, so I was able to trade nearly all of my other cards for earth cards. 


Before I ended with a Geomancer, I tried a few different avatars and elemental combos like:


  • Mud Necro
  • Mud Druid
  • Dust Sorcerer


Then I tried Geomancer. This avatar is better in practice than the card suggests. You WILL have 6 mana on turn 6 without drawing a single site. It’s not a flashy ability like Druid’s or Archimago’s, but it is a solid one. Some of your spells and sites allow you to get even more value from it (more on that in the later section).


Geomancer felt like the strongest and most consistent of all avatars I tried, so I started practicing with him hard.



(F) Why splash fire?

Fire gives access to good graveyard hate and powerful mass removal magics. 

My wife often played fire [[Persecutor]], so I felt how strong a single [[Poison Nova]] could be. 



(W) Why not splash water?

Water sites turn off your [[Root Spider]], [[Earthquake]], [[Cave-In]], and [[Bury]]. I would love to play a Mud build, but it doesn’t seem to be worth it with the current card pool.



(A) Why not splash air?

Dust build might actually be viable. [[Blink]], [[Whirling Blades]] and [[Grandmaster Wizard]] could effectively work in this shell. I didn’t have time to test this build. Try it yourself and tell me how it does! : )



Why not play [[Archimago]]?

I saw Geoffrey’s list and for some time I considered playing Archimago, as it shares a lot of cards and Archi’s ability is crazy good. So why did I ultimately decide against it? My reasons were:

  • I had no experience playing Archi and nobody in our playgroup plays him.
  • Archi seems like a very exhausting avatar to play for multiple rounds in a row.
  • Archi benefits more from Uniques that I didn’t have.
  • I was expecting an aggro meta, which sucks for Archi.
  • [[Mirage]] got fixed.
  • Archi is currently considered the most powerful avatar and I prefer to play off-meta builds.


I feel like my build of Geomancer has no really bad matchups, but it also doesn’t have any great ones either.


In preparation for the tournament I think I watched all the available recorded gameplay on Youtube, lurked through discords and looked up hundreds of different decklists on Curiosa. And of course played as much as I could. (In the few days prior to the Cornerstone, all my dreams were Sorcery related xD)



How to use Geomancer - A quick guide

1st turn - Play a Village under your avatar, summon a Foot Soldier, and place a Rubble in front of you.

2nd turn - Replace the Rubble. Play a 2-drop if you can.

3rd turn - Play a site to the left or right of the site in front of you. Place a Rubble behind it. Play a 3-drop if you can.

4th turn - Play another site and make a Rubble or replace the Rubble you made the turn before. You have to make a call depending on your opponent. Sometimes you want to go wide (and make a letter T) and sometimes you want to play your starting sites on one side (mostly when playing against aggro, so it's a bit easier to defend in the early turns.)

5th and 6th turn - by now you know what to do. 

Your main goal is to make 3 Rubble tokens nearby and then replace them with sites from the top.


Gameplan:

Vs Aggro - Stabilize! Trade, block, preserve your life total. Attack when they run out of gas and you have a blocker ready. Kill their minions that could [[Whirling Blades]].


Vs Midrange - Focus on creating more value than they do. You have [[Craterize]], [[Major Explosion]] and other late-game cards. Control the board!


Vs Control - Pressure them early if you can. Your minions aren't so easy to remove. Again, there isn't much they can do to stop 10 damage coming from your [[Craterize]]. Focus your removal on things that could provide them value every turn, like Omphalos or [[Maiden, Mother, Crone]].


My thoughts on cards from this list:

Core cards:

[[Arjaro Exorcist]] - Spellcaster with a great genesis effect. There is often a good target for his ability. You can banish a [[Pudge Butcher]], [[Mariner’s Curse]] or [[Sphere of Animosity]]. One time I even used it to banish a Keening Banshee.


[[Root Spider]] - The best earth minion. His art is sick. It can buy you lots of time or you can use it to move and disable blockers from an adjacent site. I love them.


[[Gargantula]] - What’s up with earth and powerful spiders? Due to how its ability is written it can cocoon and disable minions with stealth or ward (removing those marks permanently) 4 power allows for trading with lots of popular minions.


[[Archangel Michael]] - The reward for going heavy into earth. Great genesis effect, hard to kill due to airborne and ward. 


[[Toolbox]] - I love the utility of this card. I feel that earth and fire have a good pool of ordinary spells to prefer Toolbox over [[Silver Bullet]].


[[Mix Terra]] - Never saw it during the tournament, but I was impressed by this card during practice. Use it to play Michael, [[King of the Realm]], [[Returned King]] or [[Earthquake]] much, much sooner and use that early advantage to dominate.


[[Crusade]] - Foot Soldiers count as earth minions and you have lots of them. You can also use it to drop Pudge Butchers, Gargantulas and Michael on opposing sites. 


[[Pudge Butcher]] - 5 power is no joke. There aren’t many minions that could survive a hit from this gal(?). I am really impressed by their performance. They provide a lot of area denial and they can often remain out of reach from the opponent's removal.


[[Assorted Animals]] - Played it multiple times during the tournament. Searched for a combination of Root Spider/Gargantula/Redmane Hyena. It provides a lot of fuel. I’d consider playing a second copy of this spell in the future.



Other good cards:

[[Kettletop Leprechaun]] - They are great earth minions, but Geomancer doesn’t really benefit from drawing extra sites that much. I am considering swapping them with [[Bosk Troll]]s. 


[[Mover of Mountains]] - Never saw it during the tournament. You can use his ability to disrupt opposing defensive sites or move your [[Sinkhole]]s closer to enemy sites or your [[Roots of Yggdrasil]]. Being a spellcaster is useful.


[[Redmane Hyena]] - I played a single copy to find it with [[Assorted Animals]]. I played only 4 demons in the deck, so I couldn’t count on triggering the +2 power. Hyena is mainly for disrupting enemy Archi.


[[Saint of Redemption]] - 2 power with ward for (2) is actually alright. His ability could really mess with some decks (mostly Persecutor). Combos with [[Rhitta Gawr of Snowdonia]].


[[Autumn Unicorn]] - Good beater for cheap.


[[Order of the White Wing]] - These guys could mess up your strategy a bit, I hate the anti-synergy with the rest of this deck, but I found out they are still worth playing. They work great against necro and Archi. 


[[Paladins of Bazia]] - Good beater with ward and spellcaster. 


[[Atlas Wanderers]] - They allow you to make some cool and unexpected plays. (Like repositioning Pudge Butcher and breaking walls made of defensive sites.) 


[[Lord of Greed]] - This card is close to a pet-card status. Great art. You may steal an opposing [[Toolbox]] played too early, a Core or an Arbalest. Nobody really expects him. (6) mana is not that much for a Geomancer, so a single copy may catch some opponents off-guard. 


[[Returned King]] - Tech against Necro. Also can steal [[Daperyll Vampires]]. 


[[Rhitta Gawr of Snowdonia]] - Every time I played him, my opponent was forced to remove him, giving me more time to ramp. 


[[King of the Realm]] - There are lots of Mortals in this deck and in the meta. Play him.


[[Divine Healing]] - Good vs aggro, useful vs midrange and control decks, but I wouldn’t play more than one copy.


[[Gift of the Wolf]] - Useful card that replaces itself. You are always glad to see it.


[[Bury]] - Sometimes all you need is to get rid of an early problematic minion or artifact. Bury often gets the job done. 


[[Landmass]] - Great if you aren’t pressured early. Ramp into your big spells. Often you will play a village and make a blocker, so you aren’t punished that much.


[[Onslaught]] - There are some situations where Onslaught breaks through enemy defenses and allows you to put your opponent on death’s door in a single turn. Play more than one copy if your meta has a lot of earth.


[[Scorched Earth]] - Something to blow your Roots or defend you in a pinch. Geomancer will allow you to rebuild quickly. It’s not the best card, but you don’t have better options. Feel free to swap it with something that you like more.


[[Cave-In]] - I couldn’t find a second copy of [[Earthquake]] before the tournament. Cave-In is a weaker, but still playable alternative. It deals with warded units!


[[Infiltrate]] - Good card with a single (F) threshold requirement. 


[[Earthquake]] - That’s a powerful spell. Gets rid of multiple minions and the rearrange is very useful. I would love to find a second copy of it.


[[Poison Nova]] - This spell saved me multiple times during the tournament. This deck has a few spellcasters, so you could use them to really blow out enemy minions and keep yours at a safe distance. 


[[Guards!]] - Saw it and played it one time on turn 7 and summoned 9 minions. Felt powerful, and a turn later I drew a [[Crusade]]. 


[[Major Explosion]] - Great removal and a finisher. (7) mana is not that much for a Geomancer. Your spellcasters will often provide you range to cast for high value.


[[Craterize]] - Ah, the iconic Craterize. Very expensive to cast, but it ends games. You don’t want to see it early. When I saw this spell in other decklists I wasn’t sure how to use it properly. Don’t worry, you will see its power.



I wouldn’t play these cards:


[[Valor]] - Spicy card, but even though this deck has lots of minions, I often kept this card in my hand without an opportunity to play it. Unfortunately, Valor does nothing vs Whirling Blades, Grapple Shots and other cards that simply strike.


[[Sir Morien]] - Both of his effects are great. He stops Grapple Shots, Firebolts and Pudge Butchers. The problem is that at turn 4 you will probably have 0 or just 1 (F) affinity. (F)(F) is a big deal. 



Would play them if I had them:

[[Torrid Omphalos]] - Couldn’t find this one. It would provide good value after stabilizing on the board. Great vs control.


[[Balor of the Evil Eye]] - Strong minion and another demon. Deals with opposing root spiders or finishes bigger minions or avatars. I would love to have one.



I want to test those:

[[Powerwish]] - This one could work wonders against [[Savior]], [[The Doom of Dilmun]] and warded water minions. 

[[Siege Giant]] - Reposition your Geomancer to make and replace more rubble. 

[[Sister Stefania]] - Swing with your Pudge! Unfortunately has some anti-synergy with the rest of the deck. Still, it might be worth it.

[[The Inquisition]] - 2 for 1. Helps vs control. 



My Atlas:

Villages - Blockers are nice to have. Makes the deck resistant to [[Atlantean Fate]].


[[Bedrock]] - Creates a safe haven for your [[Root Spider]]s. Also, you play [[Roots of Yggdrasil]], so it’s nice to be able to play something the same turn you blow them.


[[Boulevard of Bones]] - Good site that makes free units. Can be moved by other cards to make even more value.


[[Desert Bloom]] - Provides fire threshold and your Geomancer sees it as an earth site the turn you play it, allowing you to place a Rubble.


[[Funeral Pyre]] - Tech against Archi and other graveyard focused strategies. I don’t like this site, but felt it was necessary.


[[Haystack]] - I like running one. In most matchups it does nothing, but sometimes it can be very relevant. If your meta has weak earth representation, cut it.


[[Mount Ussar Sanctuary]] - I felt safe with this on the board. Doesn’t cost you much, and you will have the threshold to use it. 


[[Pillar of Zeiros]] - This card really saved me one time, gaining me 11 life. Every time I played vs aggro I wished to see it. 


[[Rift Valley]] - If you replace rubble with this site, it does nothing. I’d cut it. Doesn’t work well in Geomancer.


[[River of Flame]] - Another spellcaster to center your [[Poison Nova]] on. Often you can’t control where it is placed, so I consider cutting it.


[[Roots of Yggdrasil]] - When I saw this card, I knew I wanted to play it. I enjoy resetting the board with it and then rebuilding quickly thanks to Geomancer’s ability. It’s an Unique site, so the chance of it happening is rather low (never had the opportunity to do it during the tournament), but I like knowing that I have an out somewhere in my deck. Remember that your minions with ward will survive! 


[[Sinkhole]] - Roots enabler, also you can blow up opposing sites, to slow down your opponent and quickly rebuild. Reposition Sinkholes with Atlas Wanderers or Mover of Mountains.


[[Steppe]] - An obvious inclusion.


My collection:

In order of relevance:


[[Firebolts]] - Kill small minions, end games.


[[Heat Ray]] - Different flavor - sometimes better, sometimes worse than Firebolts.


[[Bury]] - An additional removal spell.


[[Dispel]] - Awesome card vs artifact and aura heavy decks.


[[Smite]] - You can use this to door your opponent by playing this on a strong minion adjacent to their avatar.


[[Angry Mob]] - It can kill a strong minion and it leaves a body.


[[Boil] - Good card to have against water decks.


[[Scent Hounds]] - Tech against Infiltrate or non-existent stealth decks.


[[Makeshift Barricade]] - Tech against heavy aggro. Never used it, but it might come handy one day.


[[Carrion Beetles]] - Tech against Archi, feels too weak to matter. I think I will replace it with something more useful, like a second [[Dispel]].



Tournament matches summary:

5 rounds of Swiss

Win vs aggro Elementalist good stuff - I banished his turn 3 Pudge with my Arjaro, allowing me to gain some control back. Rhitta gave me a turn to catch my breath and set up Major Explosion that turned the whole game.


Win vs mono Water Harbinger - My opponent played lots of defensive sites and a Mariner’s Curse. It was really hard to attack through it, but I finally broke through.


Win vs smoke Interrogator - I drew Divine Healing in my starting hand. I denied him cards early and paid with life. Assorted Animals for a Root Spider that helped me stabilize and outvalue.


Win vs mono fire Pathfinder - My Pudge Butcher really limited his options and defended my sites. Then I played Michael that he couldn’t easily remove.


Lose vs lava Archimago - He drew an early ring and outvalued my plays. Then he Heirloom Lost my Roots. This game went to time, and he played Onslaught with Border Militia two times to put me on door. I didn’t draw my hate pieces, just a single Hyena through Assorted Animals. Rough matchup.



Top 8

Win vs dust ramp Savior - This deck caught me by surprise. Wards are annoying to deal with. We were fighting for control over the realm, then I played Pillar of Zeiros gaining me 11 life and Assorted Animals for Gargantula and Root Spider stabilizing me completely. He was out of gas by then.



Top 4

Win vs aggro Elementalist good stuff (again) - Lots of cool plays in this game. He played Rift Valley in front of my Geo and placed a Pudge there on turn 3 thanks to his City of Glass. I wanted to counter with a Root Spider that he removed by using a Geyser from a Silver Bullet. Poison Nova saved my ass, and my Foot Soldier destroyed his City of Glass. I stabilized by summoning 9 Foot Soldier with Guards! 



Finals

Win vs smoke Persecutor - The final match was vs my good friend from my playgroup. He won against Archi who beat me during swiss. 

Lady Luck was totally by my side. I drew a really good hand with Saint of Redemption and he totally turned off his deck. I knew that if I could protect Saint, this match would go in my favor. Root Spider disabled his Dragonettes and Paladins of Bazia attacked his sites. Gargantula turned off his Daperyll Vampire that could save him. I truly feel sorry for him, this game was completely one-sided. You will find the finals match on Youtube. 



Future of the meta

With the new Court sites becoming legal, I expect this deck to change. Air court punishes token strategies and earth court punishes elites and uniques. 

I think that Geo could find success by running both earth and fire courts and cutting most Villages and rare spells.



The end

Huge thanks to the whole Sorcery community. I had a lot of fun and memorable moments. Also, shoutout to a player with a similar nickname (Morgoth) that also won a cornerstone with a Lava Geomancer. What a weird coincidence. 

I hope I can see and play with all of you again soon.



About the author

My real name is Hubert, and my favorite elements are earth and water. I have been playing different card games competitively for over 15 years and I currently work as a board game designer. I enjoy brewing and testing my own decks. I love Sorcery and its community, and I’d be thrilled to contribute to Erik’s Curiosa someday if the opportunity ever arose.

decks.name: Deathspeaker Self Mill (cornerstone deck)
decks.primer:
Yo! Welcome to the primer for my DS Self Mill Deck!

To start things off a quick history on me a tcgs and why im choosing this deck as my main passion project for the Sorcery tcg.


Basically for as long as ive been playing tcgs (started with Invasion block for mtg) ive loved using the graveyard as a resource. So naturally in mtg I was the reanimator guy and when I got a good collection I competed in legacy format events using a deck called Tin Fins and Dredge as a back up. I loved every minute of it too until mtg started doing things I heavily disagreed with and I dropped the game about 7ish years ago. When Sorcery was announced on KS it immediately gave me those mtg vibes I loved as a kid so I backed it. When I got my product I saw DS and knew this was the avatar for me and ive been working on making this deck as fun as I can so here we are haha.


So for the start behind this self mill deck is ever growing as I play more games against various avatars and opposing strats. The idea is pretty simple though, mill yourself to get that advantage asap. The advantage here is tons of card draw with those wizards and lots of minion generation with the necromancers. I also run a solid ordinary package that answers various problematic cards that exist in the game. The way I look at avatars is that each one offers the player a "cheat code" to help them win paired with piloting the deck correctly. DS "cheat code" is obviously using the graveyard as a second hand. When all this self mill stuff got printed in gothic my face lit right up and I felt at home haha. Something ive learned though is to not fill that yard up too fast, especially if the opponent is on fire, the bigger a yard you have the juicier a target it can become. Try to keep it minimal until you need new targets and go from there. In my maybe board I have a short stack of cards im considering and site hate is something ive added to it thanks to that unique fire site that kills my deck lol. Youll also notice I dont run ring, p stone, cores or other obvious "staple competitive cards" and I do that for a reason. I dont find those cards fun at all to play and im all about having fun here. If you want to run those no shame on you and feel free to edit the deck as you see fit to run the cards you want to run. Im choosing to run the token generating stuff to offer me good chump blockers or easy ping damage to opposing sites. Tokens in general are just annoying so it felt right to me and so far its been fun. Hotwheel has also been an all star for me. Killing random dudes or even putting in that finishing blow has been great. 3 might be overkill but I like running max copies of stuff when I can. I will say the mvp of the deck though is Skeleton Mage. I. Love. That. Card! Its so so good at everything this deck wants to do and casting Common Sense a million times in a game just feels criminal lol. But really it helps me always have an answer to my opponent with all the 1 of ordinary cards I run to be fetched with Common Sense. I also run some pet cards that happen to be very strong like good ol pudgy but besides that I tried making the deck with cards that function in my hand and graveyard to really abuse that "cheat code" I mentioned.


Hopefully this probably poorly written primer helps you all make your own sick DS decks and show my passion for the deck! So go out there and resurrect the realm in a fashion that fits you best!

decks.name: 1st Place Cornerstone w/Gothic (6-0) The Red Comet
decks.primer:
I registered for my LGS’s Cornerstone (we put in a lot of effort to get that status - should out to Battlegrounds in Richmond, VA!) but hadn’t played for five months. Going into the tournament, I needed 1) an Avatar I had at least some experience with 2) a deck that was pretty easy to pilot 3) something that could hopefully win or not make me look entirely foolish ;)


After looking at my old pre-Gothic decks, I landed on the “red deck wins” Pathfinder in a dusty deck box. I figured, “there have to be some cool new toys and more fire sites,” and I was pleasantly surprised. There’s a fair amount of Gothic in this deck as a result! I would add a Horns of Behemoth for the Wasteland if I had pulled one and I totally overlooked Vindictive Nation, which is also an easy add in lieu of one of the duals.


The Avatar pilots no differently than before, you have to attempt the optimal pattern to enable a path to at least six sites, but either via Giant, Warhorse, or just walking over a few sites, you can easily get to 10+ simply because of the tempo you have.


The deck archetype is classic sligh/red deck wins. You simply want to be as aggressive as possible. Gift of the Serpent, especially with Dragonettes, is AWESOME for taking out problematic minions. Searing Truth is an MVP as it gets you even more cards if you need them, but can also kill an Avatar instantly on DD. I’d definitely figure out a way to cut some things (I.e. Minor Explosion) to get up to max for each of those. I didn’t bother with any of the collection artifacts as they are simply too slow. The only collection card is a Hounds in case you elect to cast it from Molten Maar.


If you’re looking for something than can simply

blitz out a win, particularly before folks figure out deck efficiency and the meta, this may be a good choice for you. I’d you’re looking for something with some neat combos and cool interactions, there are a few, but really this is all about the burn. Enjoy the heat!
