decks.name: FE Archimago - Top 8 SCGCon DC Grand Contest
Dust Reanimator 8th SCGCon Richmond (3-2)
decks.primer:
Hi there! Please note that this Primer is a work in progress as I have time to write down my thoughts on the deck. In general this deck was an experiment to see if this archetype is currently viable (and because I love and always want to play Deathspeaker). As of right now I think that this deck, while fun and sometimes very powerful, is probably too high variance to post good results consistently. It has some very busted possible openings and can have a strong late game, but struggles a bit in the mid-game as it's minions start to get outclassed. Water is also a tough matchup due to having so much burrow removal, which is rough in the current water-heavy meta. All that being said, if you like to have explosive starts reanimating a vampire on turn 2 or 3, and like to grind incremental value out of your graveyard, this deck is a blast to play.


Minions

The Deathspeaker's bread and butter, minions with genesis or genesis-like abilities. This deck currently runs 39 minions, of which 26 have a genesis ability. It's my opinion that while you want a lot of genesis with DS, you really want to prioritize the cheap genesis minions and look for higher impact minions in the 4+ parts of the curve. I rarely want to deathspeak the more expensive minions in this deck, preferring instead to double spell one with some removal or another cheap minion. The exceptions to this are those minions like Bane of Aventis or Archangel Michael that can shore up a tough matchup, get you back in the game, or win out of the graveyard. The knights, pudge, witherwing, returned king, and the vampires are just there as strong minions at their point in the curve, and for undead to work with carrionette.


Auras and Artifacts

I originally had the two relevant cores in the deck and decided for this playstyle that they just aren't necessary. You'd rather be milling or reanimating in the early turns and the cores don't really help with that, and they always feel terrible to draw in the late game. Ring is ring, it's just too good not to play, even though we aren't super mobile with our avatar. Book of the dead provides additional recursion to help us profit from the self mill, and can get back some of our non-undead stuff in the late game. The black plague is our best answer to root spider and coy nixie, and the deck is otherwise soft to those most annoying of minions.


Magic

Our magic is generally one for one removal and sweepers, with the additional reanimates in 3 Carrionettes. I think Carionette is just great with the 5 vampires, and I love to see it early or late. The Bolts and Burys are just ways to help keep pace with stronger minions in the early game. Gift of the wolf is great with the small minions and the vampires as a way to trade up or gain some extra life, or both. Earthquake does a lot of work to stabilize, though it often will get less value than you want because of the abundance of water sites running around. Craterize has been good occasionally, but I intend to cut it from the deck. I almost always am too far gone/on DD to play it effectively, or have enough relevant minions that I don't want to kill them. I will probably add the fourth Gift of the wolf and maybe another Bury instead, or possibly keep just one.


Sites

Building a wall up front of bridges, hollows, and heights is ideally what you want to be doing, which you can then fly around later or traverse with your small minions. Gumming up the ground for the first few turns is pretty critical against the more aggressive strategies. The self-mill sites are so good in this deck, it can't be overstated. I often mulligan aggressively to find one, especially if I have Boneyard or Orpheus' Crossing in hand.


Both Boneyard and Orpheus' Crossing are high risk, high reward plays, but I think the potential is worth it. Both feel insane on turn 2, though you have to be very careful with Crossing to consider how your opponent might kill you the next turn. Having blockers for minions and projectiles is highly recommended. Both the reanimate sites feel bad in the mid-game unfortunately, and I sometimes got stuck holding them. However, if you can get a Gargantula in the cemetery it effectively negates whatever your opponent might summon on Boneyard (for the most part). Crossing is also amazing for getting you back in the game if you are already on DD.


I often drew Apex of babel without the Base, and I would probably cut these sites for something better. The idea is fun, but I can't run the full 3 bases without making cuts to better sites. Would consider replacing them with Mount Ussar Sanctuary and a watchtower or other air utility site. The misers lookout is just another ordinary site to help mitigate Atlantean Fate blowouts.

decks.name: SCGCon Atlanta 2nd place 5-1 Deathspeaker Earth Air
decks.primer:
If you’re wondering “Why not card X?” Well…I’ve been playing this game for less than a month if you can believe it. I fell in love with the game and dove right in. During the event I traded my tickets for AL packs and opened the ring you see in the list at the end of round 4!!! I was so excited =). No Decklists…so in it went. Edit: I was asked to add a note to the primer. Judges were aware that I replaced a card in the middle of our no decklist tournament that wasn’t at compREL. Is it technically allowed? I honestly don’t know. I wasn’t shy about how excited I was and was telling everyone around me though =)


There were a lot of cards that didn’t really come into play much, but the early game and the repeated value are the core of the deck. We can play 1:1 removal because we’re going to get SO much value out of our cards. The mill sites were amazing. Observatory plus rats is incredible. Archangel Michael and Gargantula along with grandmaster wizard and master necromancer are our all star value cards to play from the cemetery.


The bolts and gifts were very often used to surprisingly put our opponent to door when they least expect it, doing 10 or more quite suddenly in one turn using the skeletal mages.


I’ve already taken the silver bullets out. Added a shrine of the dragon lord picked up at the event and making room to bump apprentice and novice back up to 4. Removed Gall as well. My opponents just weren’t using their collections enough, although I could see those coming back later in the year.


I want to try the 6 cost angels but I’m just trying to stay VERY focused on our plan at the moment and they don’t do anything from our cemetery.


My first 3 rounds all involved root spiders. I read the card before the event but didn’t realize so many people play these things. They constantly locked down angels, but I still found a way to chip damage and close with blots plus zap. After my third round I brainstormed with my opponent how to kill root spiders and all we could come up with is a burrowed rat with gift of the wolf for now. Every time I drew a toolbox I made sure to ask myself “should this just be zap or do I need it now”.


Water opponents are a problem. I lost to Mitch who played an unanswered Lilith into Pied Piper, two cards I didn’t even read before the event. After reading pied piper I just said “uh…yeah okay, I’m gonna go walk the hall. Congratulations.” lol…maybe I should have toughed it out, but he had already lured a unit, got a hit off of Lilith and established a frontline of troll bridge and thin ice. It was round 5 and I made the choice to relax before the last round.


6 rounds of Sorcery was incredible. I would repeat that day several times over if given the choice. I’ll definitely be back! Thanks for reading =)


Things I want to try next: I want to find some more room for top end. We can get a bit grindy with our tiny dudes and have some trouble closing. The bolts and gifts are really important for pushing damage but a touch more top end or mid could help. I want to try splashing red, but I feel like the double threshold sites really reward us for playing two elements right now with these powerful angels and triple threshold cards like gargantula. I do see how the red cards could give more closing power though. I didn’t like the tap requirement of silver bullets and the fact that we only have 2. I’m not sure what else to do with our collection yet but honestly it could just be 10 ordinaries.


I also want to try playing all of the cores with the red splash and the tri sites to have more access to playing from the opponents cemetery. ATM I do think the consistency of two elements is worth it.

Main recommendation if you want to try this deck is to mulligan to early game curve spells + removal, bottom uniques and late game unless it's your best card in the matchup by a lot. And then draw a site for turn early at least once on any turn where you have a clear play in hand. Even on your first draw of the game. Very important to be able to space your sites based on the most info you can to get the most out of the early game tempo. I see a lot of druids refuse to draw a spell for turn for value reasons. But this deck wants to go a little bigger and play carefully around site distruction and flood based decks.

decks.name: Muddy Godzilla (Top Waveshaper Gen Con 2026)
decks.primer:
First I want to shout out everyone who helped make the deck possible.


@Ianm for coming up with the concept

@vitaminyon for testing the deck on TTS constantly 

@b_2_3_n and @ZenatheShadow for keeping me on [[Waveshaper]] after all this time 


This deck wouldn't exist without you guys coming up with ideas, testing them, and talking about them with me.


The deck is a mud midrange deck, balancing between good relatively early pressure, and a slower defensive grind. The idea was to have a deck hardened vs the new Court sites, that was proactively good into the unknown meta of Gen Con. Lets go over some of the cards.


[[Autumn Unicorn]], [[Lugbog Cat]], [[Order of the Sacred Oak]], [[Sacred Stag]] all have really good stats for their cost. They're able to provide solid offensive pressure vs slower decks, or "bigger" defensive bodies vs faster aggressive decks. They're sort of the raw backbone of the deck. There isn't too much to say about these minions other then that. [[Order of the Sacred Oak]] stops your opponent from blowing up you sites which is a bonus.


I'm sure everyone knows how good [[Pudge Butcher]] is. He demands respect from your opponent, able to drag them into the water and where you can initiate the beat down without overextending. He has a couple cool advantages in water decks though. [[Riptide]], [[Coy Nixie]], [[Undertow]], [[Rift Valley]], and [[River Rapids]] are all able to move the otherwise immobile minion into better position or slide an enemy in front of the projectile.


[[Giant Shark]] is very good. With all the forced movement in the deck, and the [[Waveshaper]]'s ability to extend the body of water, its easy to get shark coverage over the whole board. This can stop aggression in its tracks or suddenly bring an opponent to Deaths Door. [[Coy Nixie]], [[Undertow]], [[Riptide]], [[River Rapids]], and [[Pudge Butcher]] can all force your opponents Avatar to move into the water and be attacked by the Shark. In the case of [[Pudge Butcher]], the opponent will be bitten for each site they move through on their way to the Butcher. Playing minions into the Sharks body of water will result in them immediately getting attacked. This is great at stopping your opponent from playing minions to contest the realm, but can prevent you from playing minions of your own if you aren't careful.


[[Assimilator Snail]] is an underrated card in my opinion. Suddenly transforming into a 4th copy of [[Giant Shark]] or [[Pudge Butcher]], becoming a [[Coy Nixie]] when you need one, changing all the math out of nowhere with [[Ruler of Thul]], turning into [[Lilith]] for a funny flip, or just being the best minion in your opponents cemetery. It also banishes the dead minion so that's upside.


I was pretty medium on [[Archangel Raphael]] going into the event, but after the event I love this card. The Airborne, Ward, and 4 power makes him very obnoxious to interact with. Airborne especially is not something water really has access to and the mobility for both offense and defense feels really good. The Genesis is mostly a fun bonus used to Ward you, but it can be a clean way to finish an opponent who's too close and on Deaths Door.


I've brought up [[Coy Nixie]] in some of the other card sections. She's a minion who's power shines in the context of other stuff. Moving units for Shark attacks. Moving units in front of [[Pudge Butcher]]. Stacking minions in one spot for your Avatar to lockdown or to be [[Stormy Seas]]'d. Pulling stuff into [[Thin Ice]] or [[Troll Bridge]]. Tapping units that were going to block. Overextending your opponents units to be attacked. Breaking Wards for free. I'm sure I'm missing plays, the list of stuff this stupid card does is very long.


Why play [[Shellycoat]] when [[Shield Maidens]] makes all nearby allies [[Shellycoat]]. This lets your minions battle your opponents without trading, and forces your opponent to over commit damage to remove yours. Getting incremental advantage like this is critical since the [[Waveshaper]] has no built in card advantage.


I feel like people ask me about [[The Green Knight]] a lot. Yes, [[The Green Knight]] is fantastic. The ability enables so much more then you might expect on first read. In [[Waveshaper]] he piles adjacent minions into one space for you to use your ability on, or stack everyone onto a [[Thin Ice]] to be drowned. Its also a forced move for [[Giant Shark]]. It can move enemies into weird positions making them unable to block future attacks. The strike on death hits nearby enemies, everyone forgets this ability. Because of his 3/7 stat line and the strike on death, he's able to kill 4 adjacent 3 power enemies. The strike can also clean up larger minions that survived initially fighting him, or hit the enemy Avatar.


[[Overflow]] is an awesome card. Getting to 5-6 mana so you can start using your Avatar ability without thinking is very important and [[Overflow]] lets that happen early. Playing [[Overflow]] on turn 3 is a clean play you should aim for. You'll want to be careful though. There is nothing worse then hitting a land site off the [[Overflow]]. I recommend having a water site in your hand before you cast the spell, just to be safe and keep your options open. [[Kettletop Leprechaun]] can enable this without having to draw a site for turn too.


I guess now that I'm talking about sites, [[Ersatz Platz]] is a cool site. A pocket [[Babbling Brook]], or [[Undertow]] is very clutch. It can also grab [[Fertile Earth]] to cleanly hit the Earth threshold. At Gen Con I also ran [[Mudslide]] and [[Quagmire]] in the collection, but I plan on cutting those for more [[Toolbox]] spells. The cases for those cards was just too narrow and I'd rather have other things. [[Ersatz Platz]] also has a fun interaction with mana. Sites generate mana at the start of your turn and when they enter play, which means [[Ersatz Platz]] makes mana at the start of your turn and the site you replace it with will also make its mana. Just know that it works that way. 


I want to talk about a few cards that I played at Gen Con that I was less impressed with. [[Acid Rain]] was in the deck to help with Courts, but the deck was built around Exceptionals so I was not punished by Courts in a serious way. Because of that [[Acid Rain]] always felt kind of lame. Its literally a good card, but its probably coming out for something else. [[Abaddon Succubus]] is another card I've been low on lately. She's great at cleaning up aggro boards and giving you some life back, but she only pulls adjacent minions. I've really been feeling not being able to hit nearby or Avatars. She doesn't have Submerge either so she can't safely pull stuff onto [[Thin Ice]]. Being Elite means you get hit by Courts too. [[Mariner's Curse]] is awesome but playing 1 felt weird. I'm either going to cut the 1, or go up to 3.


Ok that's enough rambling. If anyone got this far, and still has any thoughts or questions, feel free to comment. I also hang out in the Sorcerers Summit Discord, specifically the Waveshaper Cove channel. We talk about [[Waveshaper]] entirely too much, and its where the deck was brewed.

decks.name: Sobeit (5th place Gen Con)
decks.primer:
This is my deck I have been working on since gothics drop after I heard from numerous people say that landmass was a bad card. That's obviously been proven wrong. My 5-1 record at gen con was a good showing and there was a good chance of being 6-1 3rd or 4th place overall if the convention didn't start flooding. My only loss was to Ira on Earth/Fire Deathspeaker. Twas a good game but he had Garden of Eden early and i was not able to answer it. And then finished me off with 2 craterizes in a row followed by a Balor for the confirm. So was quite the sequence of events.


While being a ramp deck my main goal for this deck is not to get to 10 site as fast as i can but actually 5-7(depending on your first few draws) and start double drawing every turn. The goal here is to be playing 2 cards a turn and overwhelm your opponent with value. I originally had a few more elites and uniques in the deck but with the advent of the Court of Equity i felt i needed to trim down to the essentials. No more conqueror wurm or Rhitta Gawr. I use later drawn ramp to hit my 7-10 sites. There is potential with some draws to go for a land lock strategy and block them for getting any further sites. Opening hand I am looking for a couple simple things. Ramp(Core, Frontier Settler and Landmass) as many as possible. I'll keep starting hand of 3 ramp spells but I wont mulligan to try and achieve this. Stabilizers like Earthquake and Archangel Michael I almost will never mulligan.


Garden of Eden. The bane to our whole strategy. Its beatable and I have well positioned the deck to counter it without losing much identity. Sinkhole an Heirloom lost are our best answer to it. I'll even earthquake to move the garden up and sinkhole. When garden of eden is out with sorcerer it is better to draw sites for turn and if not the ones you need then tap the avatar to draw a spell.


Site placement. My favorite site to start on is Impenetrable copse followed by a briar patch to halt early ward aggression or pebbled paths. I tend to not like using sinkhole early unless i have site advantage via ramp or land surveyor. I dont like holding sites in hand and will play out my heirloom losts and such as needed. I feel its better to hit curve over losing tempo to maybe make better use out of the utility sites.

decks.primer:
Finished 5-2


Shifty's Revenge


Shifty crouched low in the underbrush, his fingers pressing into the cold earth. The mountain air bit at his skin, but he welcomed the chill — it reminded him of the battle he lost, the shame he carried. That day still burned in his mind, the moment another druid shatter struck and sent him tumbling from victory’s peak. But Shifty was no coward. He was no forgotten warrior. He was back.


A sharp screech cut through the twilight. Tawny, his ever-loyal hawk, circled above, scouting their prey. Shifty smirked. His enemy thought themselves untouchable, but he had learned, he had adapted. They might have won before, but this time, the mountain itself would strike for him.


He gave a subtle signal, and Tawny dove, talons releasing a carefully perched boulder from the ridge. The massive stone rumbled down, gathering speed, picking up a thick layer of snow as it roared toward the unsuspecting enemy camp below. Shifty was already moving, his team of quick-footed raiders darting through the shadows, ready to charge the moment the chaos erupted.


A satisfying boom echoed through the valley as the avalanche of stone and ice slammed into their defenses. Cries of panic filled the air.


Shifty emerged from the frost-laden mist, a wry grin on his lips. “Remember me?” he called, his voice carrying through the shattered battlefield.


This time, revenge would be his — and with it, his Pact with the Devil would be complete.

decks.name: Gen Con 2023 Tournament Winner - Jarrett Messing's Impstorm  (Deathspeaker Air/Fire)
decks.primer:
I find myself in the surprising position to provide insight into the deck that won the Sorcery constructed tournament at Gen Con 2023. You might find this less of a deck tech and more of my thought process going into the event. The decisions that led me to this deck were as much personal as game related. The former, the personal, is inherently so specific as to be rarely addressed in analysis, but it is an equally important element in tournament success. I don't have any astonishing insights into how to build a meta-breaking, tournament-dominating deck. This is more of a lesson in how to stumble forward with what you know.


I prepared with a pair of assumptions:


1) It seemed likely that Air/Earth midrange would be the predominant build. Early successes established this as the preeminent powerhouse, and with limited card supply I suspected this would be one of the easier decks to build for folks who didn't pledge or pledge big. Much of the power is in the ordinary and exceptional slots, and many of the key cards are contained in the preconstructed decks, including one of the best avatars for it (Earth). A Pathfinder based version of this deck seemed on the verge of winning the second season of the TTS league. It's just a damn good, consistent deck that runs a lot of the best cards in the game, capable of big bursts of damage, strong board presence, board manipulation, burst healing, with great removal and maneuver.  


2) I would be playing [[Deathspeaker]]. It seemed close in power to the air/earth deck, if a bit less consistently good, and I had far more reps with it in and out of the TTS league. I did not have time to deviate from my comfort zone and get sufficient practice with anything before the con. The goals of the deck are straightforward. Draw as much as possible through recursion, don't allow heavy hitters to stick around, and maximize damage until you can [[Major Explosion]] or [[Nimbus Jinn]] the opponent to Death's Door. Finishers abound. Pretty simple, right? 


My most difficult choice came down to elements: Air/Earth/Fire, Air/Earth or Air/Fire? Air has the wizards for the card draw, so that was automatic, and Alpha Thunderstorm*. Earth has possibly the best overall suite of spells. Fire offers some of the best options for Deathspeaker in [[Vile Imp]] and [[Death Dealer]], one of the best removal spells in [[Infiltrate]], and best damage in Major Explosion. Take all three perhaps? Well, truthfully, there are more good options with the three elements than fit in a deck, and taking all three elements comes with the cost. Occasionally you will bump into a threshold problem and that can throw a wrench in things, especially if you're running triple threshold cards like [[Divine Healing]] and [[Browse]]. This makes you more dependent on Cores which can be ripped away at inconvenient times. There were three main reasons I decided against Earth. The [[Avatar of Earth]], playing into Earth, is especially devastating. She can grapple across the table with impunity as you're bolstering her with your own sites. I want my opponent to stay on their side of the table. Also, I knew of several off-meta Water decks in attendance, and suspected more. Water hampers many of Earth's best spells. Thirdly, Earth seemed like the slower road to the end game. [[Wraetannis Titan]] requires Sphere offensively, [[Craterize]] is a turn and a tax behind Major Explosion, and healing is prolongation, not acceleration. I felt like I would want the most linear path to Death's Door possible, and to win a race in the mirror match. 


Somewhat ironically, my game 5 finals opponent, Adam (Zalem), consistently one of the best Sorcery players throughout the league and playtests, helped solidify my choice and finalize my deck. After hammering out my idea on Curiosa I decided to see if anyone was running something similar. Lo, Zalem had built an Air/Fire Deathspeaker deck! And it was nearly identical! This gave me a huge confidence boost. His differences were one less Thunderstorm and an additional two [[Chaos Twister]]. I liked my four [[Firebolts]], and I hadn't considered the latter at all in any kind of serious format. But upon checking the Twister FAQ, and with some consideration I saw the incredible upside. You are very likely to remove the target, between the void and sites, and with some luck you have a potential 2-for-1 by slinging it into another minion, or direct damage by hitting the opposing avatar. Funnily enough, when I told this to Zalem, he said it was one of his cuts before the event due to inconsistency! 


Key Cards

[[Thunderstorm]]. *A note on Alpha Thunderstorm. This event used the RAW version of Thunderstorm, the Alpha high T version. It's extremely powerful as it ticks down only when you shoot a bolt, and can linger and move until exhausted. 4 mana, 9 damage. This is amazing, almost immediate pressure. Thunderstorm pairs extremely well with some of the other spells and sites in the deck. Fire's Deserts can clear bolt-absorbers, as can Firebolts, assuring the bolts hit the enemy avatar. I wasn't going to play this event without three. This card will be brought in line for Beta. Three Thunderstorms was a winning choice.


[[Infiltrate]]

Arguably the best removal spell in the game, this card takes your opponent's minion from them and gives you control of that minion with stealth until they deal damage. Notably, when attacking an undefended enemy site, you cause a loss of life rather than damage. Incredible potential, and a huge swing when you can eliminate a beater. I was particularly keen on this as if I stole a 5-power minion from an Earth deck I would now be able to trade their minion with another of their 5-power beaters. 


[[Summoning Sphere]]

Part of the win condition of this deck, a Summoning Sphere + Imp can finish an avatar on Death's Door. It allows me to play a Djinn and dump my hand to bring an avatar to 0. Alternatively, a sphere opener can allow me to play an Imp on their avatar turn 2, which puts a lot of pressure on the opponent to spend removal or get their own minion out at home. 


[[Vile Imp]]

The magnificent Imp! Pinpoint damage, harassment, finishing blow all in an inexpensive and annoying body. 


Apprentice/[[Grandmaster Wizard]]

Draw/Draw more. X2. Maybe x3 or x4 with Geistwood and Pact.


[[Major Explosion]]

The finisher. It's very hard to do sufficient chip damage to finish off an avatar, even with Thunderstorm. Seven mana is not that difficult to cast, and you're often one move away from launching this across the table. The 5 damage splash zone clears Earth heavies. It has the added benefit of clearing the immediate area of Thunderstorm bodyguards. 


[[Highland Falconer]]/[[Sacred Scarabs]]

Exploding flying bugs! Easy four damage and 2-for-1 retrieval. I got rid of scarabs with mulligans every game I drew them in my opening hand. Better to draw some kind of ramp or a recurrable falconer to fetch one. 


So it all worked out! It took some luck as it always does, but the deck performed extremely and consistently well. I stayed within myself, and the flow of play was very familiar despite the lack of reps with this particular build. Most importantly, I played five great opponents who were a pleasure to share the table with, foremost among them being Adam in the final. Nerves came with the stakes, but the game could not have been more friendly. And, despite his rough opening, he had me on Death's Door and was one turn away from snatching away the victory! Wild end to the event!

decks.name: Tri Speaking Ill of the Dead (4-2 at GenCon)
decks.primer:
This is my silly little high synergy, value, control deck that I think I'm decent enough to give a primer on at this point. The general idea you are trying to go in with this deck is just survive until you get a tempo advantage. Or even simpler, just survive. This deck is like an ant colony in that all the individual parts are kinda terrible but once you put them all together it's extremely hard to stop.


Generally you going to want to mulligan aggressively for (1), (2), and (3) cost cards that draw, give mana or remove enemy cards with exceptions against specific decks. Against [[Enchantress]] always keep [[Ajaro Exorcist]], against [[Battlemage]] and other voltron style decks keep [[Toolbox]] for [[Dispel]], against [[Savior]] keep [[Bane of Aventis]] and against [[Imposter]] keep [[Legion of Gall]].

For sites, mulligan to get as many different kinds of threshold possible generally. Although it sometimes is wise to keep single threshold sites if it works for curving out your hand. If you have a [[Toolbox]] maybe keep that [[Dark Tower]] for early plays. Some matchups benefit greatly from site as well, [[Wormelow Tump]] being the best thing to keep against opponents that may have cemetery hate. [[Fields of Camlann]] is also great for aggro matchups. Notably if you get [[Orpheus' Crossing]] in your opening hand, only keep it if you think your opponent 1. won't have burn early on and 2. you have something that can put stuff in the cemetery early on i.e [[Cemetery Rats]], [[Shallow Grave]] or [[Forgotten Tomb]]. Its best to think of [[Orpheus' Crossing]] as a spell rather than a land, don't always play it if there is any possibility you could die.


Early turns should be spent playing early value drops that fill up your cemetery or give card advantage like [[Cemetery Rats]], [[Land Surveyor]] and [[Sisters of Avalon]]. If you hit a dead draw in the matchup [[Sisters of Avalon]] is one of the best cards in the deck for filtering cards, like pitching [[Courtesan Thais]] as its only use to play from the cemetery once you get your opponent to death's door. Also [[Landmass]] on turn 3 into [[Skeleton Mage]] playing the [[Landmass]] again is like my favorite shit ever.


Once your opponent starts playing stuff, kill everything they play. Okay not everything, often times a big skill check with this deck is not figuring out how to kill something, its just should you. Threat evaluation is important. Often times you can get away with building up your board even more and just chump blocking whatever they throw in front of you, and then you get to piss them off by playing those cards again! Also always check to see if you can use your opponents genesis abilities and ordinary magics against them as [[Deathspeaker]] and [[Skeleton Mage]] are not exclusive to your own cemetery. Although remember to always savor your life total, I've found its easy to get lost chump blocking or taking a bit of chip here and there and then you find yourself to far behind to catch up.


After you get back tempo its a pretty simple way of winning, just kill them with a thousand little dudes over many turns and kill all there stuff some more. Also [[The Doom of Dilmun]] just kinda wins games sometimes.


Other miscellaneous synergies that are important for the deck include [[The Doom of Dilmun]] not being banished after playing it from your cemetery, allowing you to trash it early on as it functionally is an extra card in hand. [[Pact with the Devil]] is never cast on yourself, always sacrifice a spellcaster with it. You can also sac [[Merlin's Tower]] if you really need those cards. Often [[Common Sense]] is just there to smooth out you curve, getting a [[Landmass]] or [[Land Surveyor]] for the next turn usually isn't bad. Remember [[The Inquisition]] when your opponent is searching your hand or deck. [[Amulet of Niniane]] is one of the best cards in this deck as you get fetch it with [[Highland Princess]] and it prevents most ways an opponent will trying to kill you at death's door, allowing you to use your powered up ability for longer. Also it's one of the only ways to guarantee [[Orpheus' Crossing]]. [[Skeleton Mage]] is the best card in the deck and no one will talk shit on its name, as I said before it can ramp you even further, fix your draws with [[Common Sense]], and often it just wins me games as it sits in my cemetery with a [[Common Sense]] to find [[Lightning Bolt]]. [[Vivien the Enchantress]] is a special addition as it functions really well with all the spellcasters in the deck. If you discard Vivien you can still play it from the cemetery to copy the genesis effects of all spellcasters in the realm. Also sometimes it just wins the game as long as your opponent doesn't remove it (which can be pretty funny against an [[Ironclad]]), playing two minions from the cemetery a turn is a lot better than one, and remember to draw/play a site with her!


This deck still struggles against decks that can slam down a powerful game ending threat each turn like water necro and is part of the reason I used to have [[Drown]] and [[Boil]] in my collection. Its gotten a little more even with the addition of (F) cards that allow for efficient threat removal but its something I would consider adding if you expect a lot of necro. There are some cards I would considering taking out if you have other options or want to test the waters like [[Morgana le Fay]] as she is very threshold heavy early on, [[Bane of Aventis]] who has rarely ever come up in my games or [[Archangel Michael]] as he is very threshold heavy and at the time of writing is like 90$ what the fuck.


Possible additions include everything in the maybeboard but I would mostly consider [[Funeral Pyre]] and [[Mismanaged Mortuary]] as cemetery hate. [[Amethyst Core]], [[Onyx Core]] and [[Ruby Core]] for better fixing. [[Boil]] as said before. [[Jack the Ripper]] and [[Varistus the Evictor]] for mortal and voidwalk heavy decks respectively. Also [[Clamor of Harpies]], [[Hotwheel]] or [[Sir Morien]] if you want actual (4) drops. Also [[Mountain Peaks]] and [[Fertile Earth]] for other good fixing.

decks.name: 🎉#1 Ironclad @ GenCon 2026🎉
decks.primer:
Technically this deck went 3-3 on paper because the event was cancelled early due to a tornado warning. But I played my opponent out and it was clear to both of us that I was going to win that match. So, in my mind, this deck went 4-3!


UPDATE:

Going to add a quick primer to this one, because this deck is getting more attention and I'm bored at work. But for a more thorough breakdown, look at my older "Trench Warfare" deck primer. It's slightly out of date, but most of it still holds true. It goes over site placement and mulligans.


Since GenCon, I've gone to 2 Cornerstones and secured winning records (4-2 and 3-2). Feeling confident for November! I've made a bunch of changes event since GenCon, but I think I'll wait until after AotR to post my current deck list. Unless I make a video on it.



COMMON ERRORS:


  • [[Ironclad]] reduces the damage you take. This means that when something says you lose life, you take the full effect and lose that life. This includes damage done to sites, because striking a site causes life loss, not direct damage to your avatar.


  • [[Golden Harp]] does not have to be equipped to work. It says nearby, meaning you can play it to an ally site and have it sit there. This is good for spreading out your defensive pieces.


  • [[Makeshift Barricade]] damage does not add up between actions. They have to do the damage to break it all at once or not at all.


  • Do not stack all your artifacts on one site if you can help it. One [[dispel]] will destroy of your whole defense.


  • DO NOT put a minion on your site if you are under a [[Makeshift Barricade]]!!!! They will be able to attack / damage the minion and break the barricade without your damage reduction. Just 3 damage will break the barricade.



STAPLE CARDS:


[[Blasted Oak]]:

This counters [[Dispel]] / [[Disenchant]], [[Swap]], [[Lightning Bolt]], etc. To put the effect a little more simply: Anything that targets (Spell OR Ability) HAS to target either Blasted Oak, It's Site / Location, or another artifact / minion at it's site or location. In that order. This still works even if it's buried. In fact, it works better, because you can still force a [[Dispel]] or [[Disenchant]] to target this site without it doing anything to the Oak itself.


If you are on Death's Door and trying to prevent your [[Makeshift Barricade]] from being [[Swap]]ed, you might want to keep a minion or another artifact on the site that you don't mind losing, just to prevent them from swapping you barricade and oak. With a minion on the site, they will be forced to select both the minion and the oak for both targets. Just keep in mind, this works both ways.


If the Blasted Oak is too far away from your home site and they have [[dispel]], they can just move away from the blasted oak until it's more than 2 steps away, and then target your site. You'll need to balance this distance problem with threats like [[Craterize]].


[[Makeshift Barricade]]:

This protects you from all damage, and only is destroyed after taking 3 or more damage. This effect happens when you take damage, meaning it happens after you lower the damage by 2. That means that your opponent needs to do 5 or more damage in one instance of damage to break the barricade. The damage DOES NOT add up between attacks or magics. So this cannot be broken with an [[Arcane Barrage]] or anything like that. Very hard for most decks to deal with. Then, even if they break the barricade, they have to have a follow-up to finish you off.


[[Golden Harp]]:

Almost self-explanatory. The harp makes all strikes nearby it deal 2 or less damage. You take 2 less damage. This means you take no damage from strikes. Now, you will still lose life from strikes on your sites, but they will be lowered to 2 life lost while nearby the harp. Because the effect is nearby, YOU DO NOT HAVE TO HOLD THE HARP TO GET THE EFFECT. This means you want to try to play it nearby if you can get away with that, to prevent your opponent from taking out all your defensive pieces at once with a single disenchant.


[[Gnome Hollows]]:

Amazing site. Putting it as your home site is good against water decks that have access to [[Ruler of Thul]] or [[Polar Explorers]]. It's also good as a home site against decks with lots of airborne minions. When going against earth and / or fire, though, you'll want to put it in front of you when you're making the M. This blocks any minions from entering your home site. If both can be Gnome Hollows; that's amazing! Throw down a [[Tragedy Worrywart]], [[Blasted Oak]], and have yourself a nice tea party to pass the time.


[[Mobbed Court]]:

This site has won me a lot of games. I have taken away upwards of 12 life from an opponent over the course of the game with 2 of these out. You will maybe lose, like, 3-5 life a game from these. But opponents seem to be less conservative with their unique picks.

decks.name: Aquaphile - GenCon 2026
decks.primer:
The main idea for this deck is to build an advantage on the board by getting 2-for-1s and 3-for-1s (snowball, Atlantean fate, etc.) and having powerful minions that are not so easily removed.


Mulligans:

Some of our toughest matchups are against aggro decks, so try to mulligan for a defensive site. Innsmouth dock, river rapids, and maelstrom are almost always useful to maneuver minions. This can be especially helpful in the long run with omphaloses, as they it enables them to attack next turn. If playing against a deathspeaker or imposter, mulligan hard for bureau, as it instantly makes the game much more difficult for them. If playing against flamecaller, archimago, or another avatar that deals with their own cemetery, do the same for mortuary. As for spells, it’s very important that you play something on turn three, so mulligan hard for that. Playing something on turn two is less significant, but if playing aggro I would recommend going for a winter nymph, as it is solid defense against their charge. You play it, and walk it over to a place where it doesn’t affect you.


Various ideas:

If you are in a situation where it is turn four, and you could draw a site to play something, or you could draw a spell, I would suggest taking the site. This deck likes to try to get high amounts of mana relatively quickly, or at least up to six (highest mana cost of a card). If you ever feel like you could have a nice play with snowball, ice lance, or something similar, go for it! As long as you stay in a body of water, it should turn out ok. If playing against a control deck, I would strongly advise you build up a small number of minions, and then all attack the same site. While this seems counterintuitive, if you then flood the site, it will make the removal of your minions much harder for your opponent. Of course if they are playing water then this is a bad play, but if not, it usually works. I would just like to note that while the above info is generally good advice, there are definitely times when you should not do these things, so make sure to think for yourself!


Not-so-frequently-asked-questions:

Q. Why ice lance, and not something like ice shards?

A. I find that they are pretty similar, but given the avatar you can usually make good use of it. It also is a death blow for ironclad, which shards is not.

Q. Why AoW for that matter?

A. Most water minions don’t actually have submerge, so waveshaper isn’t as good, but I really like the ability to flood a site. It makes pirate ships and stoor worm way better. Also, the teleporting ability makes getting death blows ridiculously easy. I’ll sometimes go a whole game without using it once, get the death blow with the avatar, and feel like “yep, that’s worth it.” I also find it fun to play an avatar that is slightly subpar, because winning is more satisfying.

Q. No aino or captain?

A. One of the main issues I was facing was the courts, so I tried to minimize the elites and uniques. That’s also the purpose of acid rain.

Q. What does aquaphile mean?

A. *sigh* Didn’t feel like taking two seconds to look that up, did you? It means a person who loves water.


Thanks so much for taking the time to read this, and if you play the deck, I hope you enjoy!

decks.primer:
Draft deck for the GenCon 2026 Limited Grand Contest.


I first picked Barging Barghest into Flame Strike, but the fire cards dried up rather quickly, but I started wheeling aggressive air minions so leaned air/fire aggro.


Pack 2 picked up some powerful red minions (Greater Blood Demon and Lord of Destruction) which solidified us into air/fire.


Pack 3 - Michael P passed me Harbinger and said no way you're playing this right? i initially passed it, but it came alll the back around and i last picked Harbinger. Turned it around and immediately sleeved it up to Michael's chagrin ;)



Game 1 (Quarterfinals): Joe G

Harbinger high-roll'ed with a portal on Joe's 2nd site. Turn 2 Earl of the Ivory Towers placed a lot of pressure on Joe. He ended up taking a lot of damage and losing a couple ordinaries to the Earl, until he drew a Silent Hills to turn off the Earl and trade for it. Brutal game for Joe.


Game 2: (Semifinals): Julian R

Harbinger mid-roll'ed with a portal on Julian's corner which allowed 2x Forsaken to start charging in early (Turn 1 forsaken, Turn 2 Bats; Turn 2 Forsaken + another 2-drop. Just a crazy start). Julian had The Void on his home site which actually wombo-combo'ed with my forsaken. He was in a very hard spot, but was able to battle back with larger more impactful minions and some 2:1's. Harbinger ran out of gas with Julian at 4 life, but were able to squeak out 4 more damage and get him to door. I had 2 very good cards in hand (Flame Strike and Zeppelin), but only 1 fire threshold, so I started drawing sites with Harbinger instead of moving up to try and knock on his door. Ended up drawing air sites and started to get worried. By this time, Julian has KO'ed most of my minons and stabilized the board. My life quickly ticked down from 20 to DD.


Finally i drew a fire site, played it and passed the turn. Julian surrounded my avatar with multiple minions and... passed the turn. Luckily, his minions were tapped so Harbinger could step up 1 site and Flame Strike his avatar on the other side of the board. Crazy game and I really want to give Julian credit for how he recovered from my crazy start.


OK onto the finals against xNattu. The last time he played he stomped my face in. I'm spooked.


Game 3 (Finals): Sean D (xNattu)

On Camera.

I have the play.

Harbinger rolls 2 bad portals, then hits a great spot. My 2nd site.

I have the actual nuts. Den of Evil. Portal on 2nd site. Greater Blood Demon. mull 1 site.

Turn 1: site. pass

Turn 2: Den of evil. Cast Greater Blood Demon (6 power) for 2 mana. Pass the turn.

Turn 3: Nattu is on full defense mode here and is playing sites on the back row. I play my 3rd site in his zone. Move up demon. Cast Hollow One (4 power) for 2 mana. I have 2 ways to kill his 2drop mortal, so i feel confident that i can disable the Hollow One quickly. Pass the turn. (10-power on Turn 2 in limited!)

Turn 4: Nattu has a 2drop mortal with ward and 3drop undead. Demon attacks the mortal & he allows it to pop the ward. Then I cast Ravenous Werewolf (4mana on my portal) to attempt to kill his mortal to wake up the Hollow One. He correctly blocks with an undead to trade. Hollow One is still disabled, but i'm feeling good. the Demon is still wreaking havoc on his side of the board. Pass to Nattu and drops his own Elite bomb which completed FLIPS THE GAME. Hyperparasite on his home site. Pick up and disable my demon. Hollow One is still disabled. Pass to me.

Turn 5-7: No minions in hand. A flame strike which can't kill hyperparasite. Full on panic sets in. Cycle a Gift and tank for about 6min after drawing another 3-dmg removal spell. This is essentially the end of the game.... pass to nattu. he double teams to kill the disabled demon. then kills my disabled hollow one. i land an Earl and a couple willing tributes and HOPE to draw witching hour to pump my earl then untap earl with the tributes... but alas the game is over. GG Nattu.

His list and game report are here: https://curiosa.io/decks/cmsde663u000c0akqcrl42bri?tab=primer


(After watching the replay, I think playing out the Accursed desert on turn 1 may have lost me the match... That would have been very helpful in killing the warded mortal and waking up my hollow one Sooner.... Alas I didn't sandbag it... Played it instead of a twilight bloom as I typically hold them to help with threshold costs. In Retrospect the bloom on 1 and desert on 3 might hang swung the game my way. Welp def need more practice!)


I had a great time and am so happy to have this story :D


Nattu and I are signing each other's Elite bombs (hyperparasite and greater blood demon) and exchanging them. Looking forward to a rematch at AotR.

decks.primer:
GenCon 2026 Constructed Championship – Top Battlemage


Another phenomenal year in the books! Erik’s Curiosa and the event staff did a wonderful job of running this championship, so I would first like to express my appreciation for everyone involved in delivering a welcoming and exciting TCG experience at GenCon this year. Special shout-outs to Ira for handing out exciting prizes, and to Drew for keeping the vendor booth fresh and fun. Additional shout-outs to Corey (@morticor) and Rudeasaurus (https://www.youtube.com/@ArchivesOfTheRealm) for sharing endless insights into Sorcery, both with respect deckbuilding and strategy, and with respect to the community. 


(F)(A)(E)(W) DISCLAIMER: (F)(A)(E)(W)


Pardon the [[Imposter]] syndrome, but I feel compelled to inform the reader that this deck list was changed significantly the night before the tournament, I was operating on 5 hours of sleep (new parent) and I hadn’t played a full match of Sorcery since a crossroads in May. This Primer is by no means backed up by extensive research or any particular degree of talent. I am a former Magic player with just over a decade of experience who simply loves Sorcery and played what I thought was fun. My record at GenCon is more likely than not a stroke of luck. If anything, my lesson learned from this event is that we can all win some matches even if we’re playing something we strictly enjoy rather than a meta powerhouse strategy.

Finally, I would be remiss not to direct players interested in battlemage to take a peek at @CountTolstoy’s list (https://curiosa.io/decks/cmjnle8qi252izofnrghywj88), which is likely a more robust list that accounts for a greater amount of the meta. Another shout-out to @Rata (or @Maubuss?) for the advice they gave me in passing at SorceryCon 2026, see their Top8 list here: https://curiosa.io/decks/cmm2ez0b0006h04jvvqyat5n1. 


Overall Theme


The deck is obviously a Voltron-style deck leveraging the Battlemage’s innate power and his particular disposition toward munching on minions. The deck aims to load up Battlemage with equipment and get his hands dirty in the realm, going toe-to-toe with the opponent’s minions. 

This deck was previously mobility-oriented, utilizing a much greater amount of movement spells and teleport abilities (hence the reference to folk dance) to dance around targets and stay alive at Death’s Door. After SorceryCon2026 it became clear to me (and was recommended to me) that leaning more heavily into an all-in aggro strategy could yield better results, and so it has.


Strengths and Weaknesses


Battlemage’s strengths are well established. Token strategy and aggro strategies with smaller, less robust minions provide a favorable environment for most Battlemage lists. This list is particularly weak against [[Savior]] strategies and other lists that employ Ward to a significant degree. 


As most Battlemage scholars will agree, the Battlemage Action Economy is essentially the entire deck. This is felt even more acutely when you approach the build from a Voltron angle and minimize further the presence of minions in your list. As the reader will notice, this list is extremely light on minions, leveraging [[War Horse]] for mobility and the occasional body, alongside a suite of highly impactful uniques, namely [[Courtesan Thaïs]] [[Highland Princess]], and [[Cerberus Unchained]]. I am sad to say that Man’s Best Friend did not make an appearance in this tournament, but the Mistress’ ROI was noteworthy. Running so few minions means that every turn must be sculpted carefully, as missing a site drop or passing with mana in your pool can shift the tempo dramatically in your opponent’s favor. 


Thus, the worst match-ups in my experience are those against lists that either impose a restriction on the Battlemage’s Action Economy, or again those lists that do not leverage smaller/utility minions. Archimago and Savior come to mind as some of the toughest match-ups, though my experiences against Pathfinder were also Sisyphean. I do not have any matches against Realm-Eater, but I am inclined to think that site-destruction or resource-denial lists in general would present a significant hurdle for Voltron Battlemage lists, as needing to commit more than 5 mana to the realm often puts you on the back foot. Archimago lists present a unique challenge for Voltron Battlemages, as you will be unable to leverage killing minions for card advantage. Archi will outpace you on card advantage and has many, many ways of dealing with your scarier pieces of equipment. 


Notes on Specific Cards I Like


Here are the spells I find most impactful in my matches. I am setting aside the obvious powerhouses in the deck, such as [[Grapple Shot]], [[Whirling Blades]], and [[Ring of Morrigan]]. I am also setting aside Battlemage staples like [[Flaming Sword]], [[Screaming Skull]] and the newer includes, [[Peacemaker Arbalest]] and [[Plate of the Whale]]. I feel discussion on these items are straight-forward, though please feel free to reach out if you would like me to ‘splain myself.


  • [[Flanking Maneuver]] is a card that almost none of my opponents ever calculated for. A well-timed flank in one of my matches this weekend clinched the win, both by virtue of being an uninterruptable three-site move, but also by virtue of the spell replacing itself a la cantrip. While this selection is largely a hold-over from the previous iterations of the deck that focused more heavily on maneuverability, being able to jump across the realm without tapping opens up a lot of outs in the late-game, and allows a particularly aggressive hand to leap into your opponent in a manner not much different than [[Grapple Shot]]. 
  • [[Blaze]] is consistently very powerful in this list. While it feels great to gobble up skeletons with Attacks, sometimes, it is often far more advantageous to get the 3-for-1 with Blaze and forego the draw. Blaze is a mobility spell with a Diet Board Wipe attached to it. Blaze is also a strong tool for the Savior match-up, or other Ward strategies, helping to alleviate the two-action hurdle that Ward presents for the list.
  • [[Displace]] is a personal favorite of mine, both for its utility in snatching artifacts from my opponent and in its ability to disrupt my opponent’s board presence. My first match this weekend involved Displacing my opponent’s Ring of Morrigan and then top-decking my own, making it a two-ring match. Lots of fun. Displace can also come in handy when your opponent is playing it safe with their minions. More than once I have displaced a minion within munching range of my Battlemage, to tip the tempo back in my favor. Finally, while the applications can sometimes be limited due to the rulings on this spell, Displace can be extremely helpful with moving enchantments. Displacing an opponent’s Abundance onto your sites is cheeky, and moving a Sphere of Animosity off of yourself and onto your opponent always feels good. 
  • [[Chains of Prometheus]] needs no introduction, and its effects are uncomplicated. Being able to suppress your opponent’s largest threat is extremely important for Battlemage, especially in circumstances where your spellbook has not given you any other options for dealing with large, imposing threats like [[Lord of Lies]] or the various dragons that haunt the realm. The upsides of this spell are enough to warrant including in the list, and the fact that list utilizes so few minions means that the symmetrical aspect of Chains rarely effects the Battlemage’s board presence.


The Collection


Another under-tuned aspect of the deck. [[Mortality]] can probably go. These ten cards are your answers to specific strategies and your outs when you’re at Death’s Door. Also, Zap. Candidly, I feel the collection is extremely meta dependent and I am not qualified to offer much advice on this front.


Looking Ahead


This deck list is far from optimized. More experienced players are probably frustrated with my sporadic one-of includes and seemingly random distribution of threat/removal/tempo suites. Here are a few things I am considering in the immediate aftermath of GenCon26:


  • [[Tabula Rasa]]: a no-brainer. Frankly I am foolish for not having employed this card sooner. Silence is a powerful effect and this include can be the lucky draw you need to get out from under a Warded threat, or the essential cog in your opponent’s gameplan.
  • [[Dwarven Forge]] seems like a solid option. By virtue of this list previously having included an (E)Earth(E) splash, the site selection was a bit haphazard and last-minute. Dwarven Forge can help significantly with putting impactful threats on Battlemage in the first few turns, rather than needing to balance answering your opponent’s turn 4 threat while also attempting to equip yourself appropriately.
  • The sites in general. As above, the last-minute changes warranted ensuring I had the threshold coverage I needed to cast my spells. Now, with the Courts, and with a more straight forward game-plan that does not include a third element splash, I will be revisiting the sites for this list and injecting more utility. Along with [[Dwarven Forge]], I am considering [[Heirloom Lost]] (to answer [[Garden of Eden]], mostly), but I am skeptical of its feasibility in the Battlemage Action Economy. I have not tested [[Trade Encampment]], but subject to the final section of this Primer concerning the Collection, this would require extensive testing and is perhaps not the avenue this list should be taking.



Passing the Turn


I would like to invite you all to chime in in the comments for recommendations, suggestions, comments, questions, concerns, theories, inquiries, dad jokes, or bad puns. As I mentioned above, the Sorcery community impresses me every time I interact with it, and I think the best way for us all to enjoy this game to its fullest is to share our personal insights and experiences. 


I appreciate you taking the time to peruse my ramblings. Please do not hesitate to hit me up on discord with any questions or comments: @ArchmageJudex.


Thanks again, and I’ll pass turn.

Mike “Archmage Judex” P.

decks.name: Soldiers of Surtr - Gencon 2026 Top 8
decks.primer:
"We do not command fire. Ngamahu lends it, and Hinekora returns it." - Lavianga, advisor to Kaom - Path of Exile

6th Place Gen Con - #1 [[Necromancer]] - 08/01/26


It was a great pleasure to participate in the 2026 Gen Con Grand Contest, let alone finish in the top 8.


When a [[Sorcerer]] sees a [[Necromancer]] at the table, thoughts of water always rise to the surface. The water Necromancer deck pioneered by [[@Ceej]] still inspires and terrifies players to this day, and at Gen Con I hoped to do the same... but with fire (F).


During the Grand Contest, over half of my opponents remarked they would have played or mulliganed differently had they known how different my list was. And while my hopes of winning the Contest were washed away after Round 6 as water splashed down from the convention center ceiling, I am still happy to present an off-meta Necromancer build that is as surprising as it is explosive.


SPELLBOOK: The minion package is fairly standard for a mono fire deck. It includes 18 Exceptional minions with 3 Towns to help get them out a little quicker. Many of these minions are chosen simply for their Charge effect, to get as much damage on the board as soon as possible.


  • My favorite inclusion is the [[Siege Giant]], which can throw a weaker ally here through the air to a nearby location. Throw your [[Necromancer]] up and start making [[Skeleton]]s on your opponent's Sites. Throw [[Sacred Scarabs]] into position and get ready to [[Detonate]]. Equip a [[Torshammar Trinket]] and throw another [[Siege Giant]] for best results.


  • [[Detonate]] is the MVP of this deck. At (1) mana this allows the potential for any of your artifacts or minions (including [[Skeleton]]s) to be a localized [[Minor Explosion]]. For (3) mana, summon [[Sacred Scarabs]] and [[Detonate]] them to deal 6 damage. Use [[Betrayal]] to take control of enemy minions and blow them up as well. Use your artifacts with impunity against decks that run [[Swap]], and make them think twice about stealing your [[Ring of Morrigan]] or [[Poisonous Dagger]].


  • [[Gift of the Serpent]] and [[Poisonous Dagger]] both give your minions Lethal, which helps make efficient trades. Give Lethal to [[Colicky Dragonettes]], [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]], or even a [[Skeleton]]. Combine either with a [[Blaze of Glory]] for a spectacular board wipe.


  • [[Blaze of Glory]] into [[Warp Spasm]] is one of the most potent combos in Sorcery. With a 4 or 5 power minion, this combo can deal 16-20 damage in one turn.


  • [[Lava Flow]] sends [[Root Spiders]], [[Coy Nixies]], and other bottom-dwelling pets back where they belong: the cemetery. [[Siege Giant]]s and [[War Horse]]s can also position us to cast [[Lava Flow]] in the perfect line.


  • [[Chains of Prometheus]] allows you to control the enemy board state by forcing our opponent to tap their strongest minion. This is a symmetrical effect that also punishes you, but with the creation of new [[Skeleton]]s every turn, you should be able to power through.


  • Play a game of hot potato with your [[Rolling Boulder]]! Tap an unanswered [[Skeleton]] to roll a boulder from your opponents site, removing threats and causing damage along the way. Then summon a minion with Charge to push it again on the very same turn. If they summon a minion in hopes of rolling your boulder, [[Detonate]] it in their face like a Saturday morning cartoon.


ATLAS: Sites have been chosen carefully to counter opposing strategies, especially against earth and water strategies. Your mulligan will depend on what Avatar is seated across from you at the table.


  • Deserts are key for dealing with wards and controlling enemy [[Necromancer]]s.


  • [[Mobbed Court]], [[Vindictive Nation]], and [[River of Blood]] allow you to deal some incidental damage while preventing enemy healing.


  • [[Kor Crematory]] is great against [[Archimago]] and [[Deathspeaker]] decks. Trying to mulligan for this card when facing either of these Avatars is a good idea.


  • [[Sinkhole]]s can disrupt the opponent's early game, providing you a few more turns to safely produce [[Skeleton]]s.


  • [[Hellmouth]] and [[Vesuvius]] are ways to deal with burrowed or submerged minions. While [[Hellmouth]] serves as [[Earthquake]] protection for your [[Skeleton]]s, it also allows you to use a [[Toolbox]]to cast a [[Vile Imp]] underground.


  • [[River of Flame]] allows you to use [[Disintegrate]], [[Immolation]], or [[Betrayal]] to target burrowed minions. Try to place this on a different row or column than your Avatar's or near the potential underground threats.


  • [[Wuthering Heights]] is the only air site in the deck. How could you not love "[[Siege Giant]]: The Site?" It's especially good when you place it close to your [[Necromancer]]'s [[Skeleton]] production line.


  • If you do not plan on using courts or the many Unique utility sites feel free to check out this variation of the deck that uses [[Peasant Revolt]]: https://curiosa.io/decks/cmnajthf800n404l2lj6um5wx?tab=view

decks.name: GenCon 26 LC Sealed 1st - Another bigger man
decks.primer:
Full write is work in progress


With this deck I managed to go 4-0 for sealed making the top pod for the 1st Grand Contest Limited Championship. If you're interested in seeing that list you can check it out here:

https://curiosa.io/decks/cmsde663u000c0akqcrl42bri?tab=view


THE POOL:


I ended up with a pool that contained almost everything I want! A full set of heavy mud minions that allow you to take broad control, with early game minions that get you into the late game. The things it lacked in removal and finishers it made up for in one of the most insane minion curves I've ever had for limited. Specifically the card I missed the most was smite, what I consider to be one of the best cards in gothic limited.


The biggest deliberation I had was wether to splash for air. If I included air I would of been able to cut some of the weaker minions in my build such as sea witch and a drowned or entombed. Which would of allowed me to add both a [[Scatter]] as well as a [[Kiss of Death]]. Providing me with some much needed removal and possible finisher in the form of scatter. If I did include air it made both [[Kiss of Judas]] & [[Ghost Town]] awkward so ultimately I opted to just keep two utility sites.


Looking back I should have included [[Guardian Angel]]. When initially assessing the card I was focused on it's genesis ability and how many targets it would have. Which was not enough, but realistically just having a 4 power body with airborne is probably good enough to include.


Having stuck to straight mud with such a gradual curve I've named this deck Another Bigger Man. Since I often drew more sites than I wanted, landing me in top deck mode. But ultimately would draw another bigger minion to play than the previous turn, gradually increasing pressure and board presence.


The Strategy:

Use early anti-aggro minions to stop possible aggro, such as [[Drowned]] & [[Entombed]] being careful to put the appropriate site forward. Pairing that with anti-aggro site warding to further slow down the game. I believe I drew my blessed well & night watchmen multipel games. Allowing for a setup where on turn three both my forward sites were warded. Then curve out playing larger threats over time, draw into more large threats or double spell on a key turn.


THE GAMES:

Game 1: Stealth Cat

A pleasant game and great time getting to finally play in paper. A generous player who definitely let me tap to draw some sites when I forgot. Thank you again! I hope you had a great time for the rest of the convention. I got a lot of value out of a safely played [[Regurgitator]].


Game 2: Lucy

A difficult game that I thought I had lost after making a play mistake. Lucking into some good draws followed up by a mistake on Lucy's end that let me take the game with [[meat hook]] which was an mvp card for the game.


Game 3: Pete

Playing Pete just after his daughter gave me flashbacks to some twin matches from last year. A game where I made a play mistake (hard for me to remember in the moment that Monks doesn't work with meat hook). Pete was awesome about the role back. We continued play and I managed to grab and hold on to the board from there.


Game 4: Stars4Everyone

One of the most interesting and challenging competitive games I've ever played. Another game where I opted not take my front site, due to opening with Lucid Dreamers. The dreamers managed to get a lot of damage in, and applied extra pressure over the course of the game! One of the craziest site layouts where the main line was full, but there were two squares of void giving my opponent a space to hide.


I took the board after an initial fight, managed to door him then opted to keep some defense's back. The right call... as he took out my hyper parasite and failed mutation with a single call of the sea. From there I switched to a more defensive strategy.


This was another game where [[meat hook]] was my mvp.


After getting home the deck and pool was one card short. I'm 99% certain that it was a Penitent Knight, or Horrible Hybrids that I took out to place into the tokens pile. I put in a penitent knight for now.

decks.name: GenCon 26 Limited Grand Contest 1st - Forecast
decks.primer:
If you want to see the sealed list that got me here you can see that here:

https://curiosa.io/decks/cmsdce2et00040aj2txr7cgol?tab=view


The Draft:

I went into the draft wanting to pull mud, having successfully piloted a sealed version of it to 4-0. Ready and willing to adapt as needed but w/ a build in mind.

Over the course of the draft I managed to build up a decent mud back bone, but felt a bit light on the top end. Around pack two or early pack three I managed to pick up the [[dreadwing]] and then those who linger along with two [[den of evil]]. Meaning I'd be three element, but able to sneak some large threats without worrying about threshold as much.


Game 1 Cameron on [[Spellslinger]]:

I was going second, against another spell slinger iirc. He opened with a two drop. I had [[bitten]] in my hand, left my front square open opting to build to the side hoping to slow the game down to reach my bigger threats. He took my front square moved his 2 power minion up and dropped another 3 power minion in front of me. I ripped [[Instigator imp]] off the top, dropped two bodies down while removing his board. A play that caught him so off guard he couldn't help but express his... bewilderment. From there I wrapped my sites in a U around his froward site. Then I managed to build up some decent threats including [[Failed Mutation]], which he had no way to deal with. Eventually I got [[bull whip]] out my on avatar which allowed me to deal with a lot of skeletons efficiently while also getting effective trades. Bullwhip almost didn't make the cut, but ended up being huge for this game in allowing me to deal with the very wide boards Cameron threw at me.


Game 2 (Justin I think?) on [[Persecutor]]:

I don't remember the early game as well, but know that my opponent didn't put out many early game threats which was a huge boon for my build. The board ended up building to my right, his left because of how I wanted to position my [[peculiar port]]. We made some incremental trades and I started to take board control, leading into him dropping his first real threat, an [[undesirables]]. He ended up using a [[stage coach]] to move that away from the fight on the right. A play that had me cautious, because it left him open to taking damage that put him close to door. He opted to start swinging in to my center site with his [[persecutor]] his [[undesirables]] behind him. I felt as though I hadn't seen much removal so was hesitant but willing to drop the [[Ten-tonne slug]] on his face. Putting him in a position where he was 100% going to door the following turn. He gave me one last surprise by opting to swing at an the open site to the left with his avatar, allowing me to door him on his turn. He then swung in with his undesirables for 5 and followed it up w/ desecrate. I went close to door but not quite and had enough threats surrounding him that the game was over.


The Finals

Game 3 John aka FooPossum on [[Harbinger]]:

Another game where I lost the die roll. Meaning I'd be on the back foot but against a non-spell slinger flush with options and knowledge. I did not expect what was one of the craziest openers I've ever seen of a turn 2 [[greater blood demon]]. I did thankfully have a decent amount of anti-aggro tech, sitting on a [[holy warrior]] and [[hyper parasite]] in hand. I was hoping to pick up the demon and slay it before it dealt to much if any damage.


The turn 3 follow up of a [[Hollow one]] changed my perspective. Knowing when my warrior died it would enable the hollow one that was sitting on the site in front of me. Looking at my hand I have a [[Penitent Knight]] and [[Crawler]], and I know this is a play I can not mess up. I need to play the crawler to help ensure my [[holy warrior]] survives. Keeping his hollow one at bay. Doing my best to keep my poker face on because I want him to swing in with the GBD, knowing I'll go to 4 mana next turn to disable it with [[hyper parasite]].


I also know that if the holy warrior dies too soon the board will turn against me fast. I pass the turn with a warded holy warrior and crawler facing down a GBD and disabled hollow one. Praying he doesn't have a trail by fire, or another way to remove the warrior once it's bare. He swings with GBD, my holy warrior lays bare, I anxiously await to see my fate. Foo follows it up with a Ravenous werewolf for 4, a very unexpected play from my side. It trades with the crawler keeping the hollow one still disabled and unable to trade with my hyper parasite. I managed to take the right gambit. He passes I draw, immediately deal with the GBD by swinging at the disable minion with the parasite and holy warrior, successfully flipping the board.


I then follow that up by playing a forward site to the right and dropping dread wing, opting to take the damage. The following turn he manages to kill my holy warrior to turn on his hollow one and attempts to remove the hyper parasite. I opt to block with my dreadwing, knowing that with no mana left next turn the hyper parasite can land a hit on his site making his next blocks awkward. From there I continue to build a larger board through turns dropping a Penitent knight, failed mutation to get him to door. He does drop an Earl along with some willing tributes but I don't take the bait for trades and push damage. He goes out with a bang by managing to hit for a solid amount of damage with the Earl sac'ing one tribute but it's not enough to door me. I rip a bitten off the top, move units into position and beat a dead horse by also wiping the board including the earl with bull whip + bitten.


The next day a thought popped into my head for my favorite trade of all time. I signed my hyper parasite and traded it for the signed GBD by John. A card that I will forever cherish as a good memory and that I hope John can too.
