decks.name: Play Dodge Roll You Cowards - GenCon 2026
1st Place GenCon HOT SPRINGS
decks.primer:
Hi Team,


Excited to share about the deck, but first would be remiss if I didn't give credit and thanks to my team, Chris @Ismarkthelesser and Nick @Astronomonov, as well as John @PorkchopSandwitches and Blake @Collision for the insight and countless games that provided the context into many of these choices. As much your win as mine!


Also, to Pascal, my finals opponent. Thank you for one of the hardest, funnest, and friendliest games I've ever played. Despite the stakes, I appreciate how we approached the game as though we had already felt like winners just being in the seat, and counter each other. You are a champion.


Hot Spring has been a work in progress for ~8 months, after countless iterations, this is where we have landed currently.


Original deck list of where it all started.


GenCon 2025 Finals Match


Deck spotlight with Chase and EC team.


Now, into the deck.


Weaknesses: Fire and Water offer NO aura hate (outside of Scorched Earth), which means impactful auras stick around. Generally, you can outpace a deck with aura strategies, but not always. This also means no Monument hate either. This wouldn't have been a problem pre-Archimago's rise to fame, but now we're seeing more and more Orbs. Luckily, you are able to capitalize on the orb as well, with double Shatter Strikes and Minor Explosions worst case. This has changed with the inclusion of Swap; however, these problems do persist. Ironically, I think the biggest nemesis to the deck is itself, as in the last 5 major tournaments, I lost in the top 16 or higher against the mirror match. It was my bane.



A quick breakdown of each section of the deck and logic behind the card:


Auras:

  • Jihad: Self-explanatory. One of the most powerful fire cards ever printed. This card allows 5 power Monstrous Lions on turn 3 with a pond.


  • Atlantean Fate: Look at that, also one of the best cards ever printed. This primary function is to allow you to disrupt the Archimago's and other greedy threshold decks. It also provides a path to clear out popular problematic sites, like Free City, Pebbled Paths, and even Perilous Bridges. Also kills root spiders if they are on a sight that can be affected.


Artifact:


  • Torshammar Trinket: Druid can abuse this by always having access to Tawny. Probably a 3 of in most decks at this point.


  • Ring of Morrigan: IMO the strongest card in a vacuum ever printed, but particularly abusable in this deck. In conjunction with Drums, the ability to IG-88 your way through your opponent's team while also gaining life is backbreaking to say the least.


  • Mask of Meyham: With the strike change, we felt this or GG were too valuable to run, but the questions were, which one, and how many copies? Assuming there would be a concentration of Archimagos, we felt 1 Mask and 1 drums was the right call, as drums can feel dead against the few creatures in most Archimago's lists. This has a synergy with Sir Agravaine (we will cover that on his bullet point) and with the concentration of smaller minions, we thought the mask was better than GG.


  • Drums of Doom: Can lock down the game in a (candidly) un-interactive way. In a minion-heavy meta, expect druids to have 2x of these in their deck. Ring + this. Deserts, Tawny, vile Imp, all kill spells now. Also, the only way to protect against Nymbus Djinn otk.


Minions:


  • Polar Explorers: This quickly became one of my favorite cards in the deck. It enables SO much and makes cards like Redcap Poweries and Monstrous Lion have less drawback by evading problematic sites.


  • Vile Imp: 2 damage on entry, Kill spell with Drums. Takes out knights holding lances often and is just one of the best 2 drops in the game.


  • Kobolds: With the 3 of trinkets, and the prominence of Gnome Hollows, these angy little dudes provided, in most cases, bare minimum, 3 extra copies of Vile Imp, but with an insane ceiling. Also combos with strike synergy, kills tough airborne minions like Plumed Pegasus if comboed with deserts or Trinket. Very easy to deal with their tempo play with one of these early.



  • Lugbog Cat: Amazing tempo play with Pond, can reach into opponents' site with Floodplain. Solid beast.


  • Morgana le Fay: Soooo much value with this card. Boneyard target at the very least for more cards. Helps in grindy games.


  • Redcap Powries: Cheapest charge minion for the stats. Almost no downside at this point with the immobilized nerf.


  • ***MVP Sir Agravaine***: Self-protecting unit that buffs Tawny's attacks. Has proven to be a huge problem and is not answered with non-targeting damage. Enables one to turn deaths doors with only a few minions striking the avatar. With the recent attack trigger change, he will always strike the *original* target. Meaning, while adjacent to an enemy avatar being attacked, he will ALWAYS strike the avatar regardless of whether there are blockers around. This singlehandedly won me 2 of my games late in the bracket and is an absolute kill on site card.



  • Boudicca: Buffs Tawny and can just be a sudden death's door machine. Boneyard target for surprise extra damage due to getting value off her passive immediately. (if they aren't already dead by then).


  • Monstrous Lion: Has been one of the biggest standout cards. Combos with Pond, great target for Guyer to be used as a kill spell on a body. Great with all of the Battle Mages, as it gets value immediately, and also serves the 3 power.


  • Selfsame Simulacrum: After the recent revision of how multiple Bruins interact, this became too good not to run, though it never came up in my finals match. With multiple other targets, or your opponent's best minion, plenty of value to be had with this card.


  • Ruler of Thul: Similar role to Boudicca. Burst potential. Awesome surprise play with flipping Druid into Bruin, then following that up on the next turn with a Ruler for 8 in their back row with the free unit in Bruin. Also recursive with Lady of the Lake.


  • Sir Gaheris: Decent stats, and it does play well against many aggro decks, by being able to keep life parity and block, which is nice.


  • Panorama Manticore: Similar role to Phoenix, early bruiser that is hard to deal with. Untaps regularly and trades well.


  • Questing Beast: Also a Bruiser, awesome burst potential with attack from stealth and shatter strike. Mastering the art of the end-of-turn step turns this card from a great card to an absolute menace! With the ability to attack, then step back onto a watersite protects this to get you multiple strikes of 25% of their starting health.



Magics:


  • Geyser: Started out as a way to deal with Root Spider has quickly become one of my favorite cards. Providing airborne to these units increases their lethality dramatically, allowing them to avoid many problematic defensive sites. Also is a good combo with Blaze as it really extends the range with + movement and the ability to fly nearby.


  • Pollimorph: hard removal is pivotal right now with the abundance of 5+ power minions and vampires' abilities to Deaths Door you and heal for a billion while attacking sites. Also, the fact that it banishes the transformed card is actually a huge boon.


  • Minor Explosion: I started with 3 firebolts; however, the prevalence of Morgana Le Fey ultimately had me consider this instead. The indiscriminate 3 damage has a higher ceiling and, with the reach of Tawny, can easily be a 2 for 1.


  • Disintegrate: Similar to Pollimorph. Hard removal easily cast from Tawny.


  • Pact with the Devil: This has been one of my favorite cards. Combining with Tawny, Adept Illusionist, and Morgana (more niche) allows you to keep up with Sorcerer and Archimage in the mid-late game.


  • Swap (Placeholder in deck as Font of Life because they have the same mana and threshold): My friends and I had a feeling this card would be absolutely broken, and it sure felt good. This replaces Shatter Strike in the deck, and I have 0 regrets. Super flexible, and stealing Pstone and Rings while putting your guy directly on them feels AMAZING.


Key Sites:


  • Floodplain: Always been one of my favorites due to its ability to allow you to play more greedy with your threshold in Water, but also serves the purpose to kill root spiders and other burrowed minions and to extend reach on Lugbog cat.


  • Pond: MVP site: So many beasts in the deck make a dramatically increased impact by coming out a turn earlier. Tower for beasts, but better. Also amazing that with the prominence of earth still, being summoned onto a water site protects the beast you curved out from burry effects.


  • Desert: Are key to taking momentum. Also protects against enemies, Atlanian Fate turning off the critical threshold needed to cast key spells.


  • Boneyard: Though I never saw it at gencon, in my testing this card has been an amazing addition to the atlas. With several of the hard removals banishing, and access to Funeral Pyre, you can construct a sided resurrection. Also, with the concentration of charge units, you are able to bring back a Redcap, for instance, and attack with it, and because the unit they brought back entered the same turn, it will have summoning sickness. It also lets you bring back your "Win button" unique for its powerful genesis or passive abilities. Lastly, in what I presumed to be a Archimago heavy meta, the lack of minions they generally have allow this to be onesided even more regularly. It was my favorite spice in the deck.


  • Kelp Cavern: I originally hated this card when it was first printed. I thought the lack of "may" made it unplayable. I was wrong. This lets you comfortably mulligan to get better gas early, then go back and find your spells later when needed. I have been very, very impressed with it.


You may notice a lake of Smokestacks. I found, with a number of key genesis, and the draw cadence of the deck, you end up having to play it earlier than you'd like. This turns off your important sites, like deserts and flood plains, which can be really detrimental. Also, with flooding being an ability, smokestacks removes your ability to flood and kill rootspider. So I found it more detrimental than helpful in many matchups.

decks.name: GenCon 11th - F/W/A Sirprise it's Aggrovaine
decks.primer:
Font of life = +1 Swap


F / W / a Steam Mage

Elements: Fire, Water, Air

Archetype: Midrange Tempo


It's an update version of these decks:

  • Detroit 2024 - https://curiosa.io/decks/cm3iwz25l0018bpm7ka2yh6bq
  • Explorer Series Ohio - https://curiosa.io/decks/cmc4tb7bw003nkw0491vbl26g
  • League 8 Top 16 - https://curiosa.io/decks/cm3iwz25l0018bpm7ka2yh6bq


Event Information

I piloted this deck to 11th place in the first crossroads event at Gencon 2025. Below are game recaps as best I can recall them.


I went 5-2 at Gencon, losing to Duo (the Champ) and CJ (another 6-1 player).


Game 1: vs Druid (win) Murray - Turbo Redneck

Great first match that came down to the wire. Managed to maneuver my way into a win with a well timed shrink + grapple shot. Was against a fellow league player who was playing large charge minions. I managed to stabilize and find a good turn for door, where I moved over to shrink a Pellinore preventing my opponent from dooring me the following turn. Followed by a grapple shot to get across the map with a Cerberus in Chains in tow to door him.


Game 2: vs Archi (win) - IDK

I had a semi slow start on this game, but the Archi was attempting to burn me out instead of removing early threats. I drew into Ring cleared his few minions and doored him a turn before he could craterize.


Game 3: vs AoA (win) - Nick

Cerberus in Chains put in a lot of work this game, before getting polli'd. A very scary game where I had Grim in hand with the opponent at 12. I drew into a lighting bolt hoping my opponent would think that a cloud city was enough to get away. I doored him in those two turns while he doored my through hippogriffs. And the opponent did move onto cloud city to get out of line of sight.


Game 4: vs Druid Steam (win) Bruce - Golden Eagle

Extremely close game, where I made a huge mistake in playing a grapple that I shouldn't have been able to. Which would have been a near 20 to door play. Golden handled my mistake really well and we managed to reset the game state to where the error occurred. It was easily the most intense game of sorcery I've played in my life where every little maneuver mattered. After a decent back and forth I managed to stabilize by drawing into a ring and making odd plays like casting a grapple into nothing just to kill a minion with a ring ping.


Game 5: vs Druid Steam (lose) Nate - Duo

Very close game that in retrospect I could of won. I missed a game winning play through defenders that I'm kicking myself pretty hard about. The setup was my BM with on his forward center site, with a Cat and Adept behind. A twany to the left and an Agravaine with his Avatar, I was not aware of a rule change to Agravaine trigger where he now hits the original attack target. An embarrassing blunder since I play the card so frequently. It's hard to explain my head state during the game, but I was definitely thrown for a loop. After trinketing his Agravaine, and moving it into a space out of his next play a Mask of Mayhem I didn't have a way to not end up at door. I ended up not blocking the Twany which was the right move. But my brain went a bit haywire and kept thinking the cat could die to Agravaine. So with no mana left for my opponent I should have blocked the avatar attacking my BM with the cat in addition which would have doored my opponent on his own turn and left me with two attackers to one blocker. But alas Duo took a risk and it paid off, he played well and patiently and the better player won the game. Was a fun but disheartening game.

Also it was the game of a Twins revenge since Duos brother is the AoA I had beat in round 3.


Before the last turn I also believe I made a few other mistakes that include

  • Placing my third site incorrectly allowing my opponent to connect a land bridge onto my side, which allowed him to kill my first adept. I ended up drawing into the second, but if I had been able to pull the other out I would of had another card to help me fight. The misplacement of the site also led me to use my minor explosion to get rid of a 3 power charger, a card that would have been very useful against Agravaine.


Game 6: vs Druid Shapeshift (lose) CJ

Nerves got to me after my first loss and I got hyper aggressive too early with bad reads into a hand that was well suited against my deck. They were the kind of mistakes that you can't make at that level and against a player as good as CJ who won't hesitate to capitalize. Very quick game


Game 7: vs Druid (win) Seth

A scary start turned into a steam roll of a game. Starting sites were two troll bridges + a tower. For spells I had Polar explorers and Rhongomyniad. I think the winning play was moving BM to backline with polar explorers, leaving them with Rhon to throw killing a Leprechaun and Phalanx after shrinking it, while also hitting the opponent for 6. All to have the BM pick up the spear on the opponents back row to start applying real pressure. I slow played it a bit after that to get thresholds right for Morgana and drowned the opponent in card advantage.


The Game Plan:

Build an efficient and sticky early game board, win the board with efficient removal and good movement tech. Then transition to hard hitting combos and don't let up the pressure. There's also a couple of very early game doors hidden in here with the right board state.


The Deck:

A long continuation of a deck I started back when decks were still 40/20. I've brought a variation of this deck to every tournament I've gone to with some decent success. Opening hands vary quite a bit, but it has a lot of hard and fast hitting lines to find. Early minion & site placement matter a lot, and typically you'll want to play sites more defensively than you might first guess.


Packages:

Here's an outline of how I think about what roles each card fills, with some duplication entries as there are cards that fill multiple roles.


Pull package: reduced down from it's original iteration but still a strong way to build an early board and thin the deck.

  • [[Adept Illusionist]] -> [[Adept Illusionist]]
  • [[Highland Falconer]] -> [[Palliburrie Bats]]

I choose bats over scarabs for a couple of reasons, bats having 2 power makes a huge difference. Especially with the prevalence of druid. The bugs might be better against Vamps, but bats feel stickier because they have burrow and don't immediately die to a desert.


First Strike:

  • Forges
  • Rhongomyniad


Heavy Hitters - Well statted minions

  • [[Lugbog Cat]]: A 4 for 3 that can be placed on top of a enemy water site, which I would highly recommend is possible.
  • [[Cerberus in Chains]]: 5 power for 3 that can produce extra pressure or extra defense. Don't forget that this can move with forced movement like grapple shot. Typically better in games you want to be offensive in


Finishers - Get them to door

  • [[Ruler of Thul]]: Skip the road blocks if any and add extra damage the turn you play him, turning the pull package into real threats.
  • [[Sir Agravaine]]: Get him into a position where he can at least be near the enemy avatar on the next turn, then swing as many dorks directly into their avatar as you can stacking extra 3 damage for each. I've had a turn five 20 to door (sorry Glenn).
  • [[Cerberus in Chains]] + [[Grapple Shot]]


Ramp - Get more mana make things cheaper

  • [[Ruby Core]]: Early ramp, easier to hit that third fire threshold
  • [[Philosopher's Stone]]: Don't be afraid to hold this back if drawn later for a huge swing turn, and try to play knights second so they don't take up 2 color slots.


Equipment Package - Turn your avatar into a direct threat

  • Increase power: [[Torshammar Trinket]]
  • [[Rhongomyniad]]: Permanent first strike on your battle mage, making it easier to use your avatar as removal + card draw


Removal - Deal with minions to save your life total

  • [[Shrink]]: Best on big minions but can also turn the tides against aggro
  • [[Pollimorph]]: Best single target removal in the game currently for [[Battlemage]]
  • [[Grapple Shot]]: Can remove larger minions by following up with an attack. Also useful to remove a flying unit if you don't have a [[firebolts]] or [[lightning bolt]]


Sites:

Sites are almost completely focused around hitting threshold requirements while drawing the least amount of sites possible. You want 3-5 mana depending on your opening hand and subsequent draws with a real cap at 6. If you have a stone or a core in your opening hand it's usually safer to mulligan less sites and keep a lower count before putting on pressure. If going up to 5 or 6 it's often weaved into a turn after moving onto the opponents side.


In the end 3 Fire, 2 Water, 1 Air is what you're looking for. Theres are two triple fire threshold in [[Morgana le Fay]] & [[Immolation]]. This means if you have 3f, 2w, 1a in your opening hand you're golden on sites. A good opening hand typically has 2f, 2w, 1a. I've done quite a few pulls, if you don't hit 2f, 2w, 1a by site 5 that's typically rare. By 6 you should commonly see all your thresholds, but at 5 sites total pretty consistently.


Sites that produce Fire & Water are the best, sites that produce multiple threshold are good, and usually more water sites will keep your minions safer until you decide to move out since they can't be buried and drowning effects seem less meta.


Mulligans:


Mulligans for spells

The deck shuffles a decent amount so don't be too discouraged if you have to pitch a higher cost card that might be great later in the game, it might not stay at the bottom of the deck for long!


I feel like Mulligans in this deck require a decent understanding of how it needs to play against different avatars in different ways. Mixed with watching your thresholds and finding lines to consistently win the board in the early game, which can vary greatly. There are cards that are good against Archi, that will do less against Druid and vice versa. There are site placements you really want to hit against Druid that don't matter in other matchups.


An example to look at is sinkhole vs troll bridge. Sinkhole CAN be good against druid, but you won't always know what you're sitting across from before starting the game. Sinkhole is however amazing against Archi, even if you're going second. It delays their mass removal by an extra turn, allowing you to push their life lower earlier and possibly unexpectedly by removing their center forward defensive site. Troll bridge, doesn't usually do a lot against Archi, but a center forward site against a druid allows you to funnel their twany and other charge minions into a meat grinder.


Mulligans for sites

If you see 3f 2w 1a, you're golden and it's usually not worth pitching sites. If you see 2f, 2w, 1a you likely still want to keep that hand 90% of the time.


Match Ups

Aggro: You want forges some early minions. You often still want to get to 3-4 lands so early minions are more important than equipment. If you survive to the mid to late game [[Rhongomyniad]] can put in work, but you need early minions to get there.


Control: If it seems like it's a non-minion based deck it's ok to hang some creatures back and wait for something that will give a big burst of damage. Especially if you're going second! You can build a board on the back line waiting for the right timing of [[Polar Explorers]], [[Ruler of Thul]]. This is of course contingent on them hitting their defensive sites at the right times.


Some interesting hands I've seen.


The Big Doggy

[[Ruby Core]], [[Cerberus in Chains]], [[Grapple Shot]], [[Ruins]], [[Sinkhole]]. These five cards allow you to play out Cerberus on turn two followed up by grappling him into their face. The last site doesn't even matter that much. The hardest question you'll have to ask yourself is if you grapple shot the BM or the Cerberus.


[[Adept Illusionist]] can pair really well with troll bridge. It can sometimes work well with forge depending on your opponents hand.

decks.name: GenCon 2025 Crossroads 6th Place, 6-1 (E/F Sorcerer 55/31)
decks.primer:
Ideally, you want an aggressive or low to the ground start with some sort of card advantage. If you have multiple 4 cost minions in hand pitch them and dive deeper for more aggression and value.


Infiltrate is usually a snap keep in opener along with kettletops, imps and other aggro pieces under 4 mana. Slumbering giants is also a keeper but I will usually hold a desert to play on turn 4 if I don't have another way to wake her. From there get to 5 sites and start double drawing spells until you need the additional mana to outvalue the opponent by casting 2 spells per turn.


Don't get greedy with board presence if you have control, play this like a midrange build that has the capacity to go aggressive. Don't be afraid to sandbag spells you don't necessarily need to play and always be aware of Atlantean fate when moving around onto your sites. The ordinary sites in the deck will naturally help with this, but still be aware of wide area removal as it will almost always happen eventually. Just do your best to minimize risk.


Thanks for checking this out, I hope this helps!

decks.name: GenCon 2025 Crossroads - Mono Air (4th Place)
decks.primer:
Intro 🌟

Hello all - my name is Joey. This is a list that I created and refined off of originally from the BIRDS BIRDS BIRDS (1st Place League S4) deck created by @Nvekmm which won season 4 of the TTS League. After playing a version of this deck at SorceryCon 2024 and missing out on the top cut (9th place, 5-2) due to getting blasted by two Archimagos, I decided to attempt a swing at a Mono Air deck that deviated more from the pure cheap minion aggro of BIRDS.


To be clear, relatively cheap airborne minions and the wildly flexible ability of the Avatar of Air are still the bread and butter of this deck, but it can now curve out into a mid-range game if neccesary. At Gen Con 2025, it went 6-1, beating 2 Druids, 2 Pathfinders, 1 Archimago, and 1 Enchantress. It only lost to a nasty Geomancer deck played by Ira.


Like BIRDS, the list is mostly aggro fliers with artifact support. You slap down as many bodies as you can, split them up to avoid Poison Novas and Earthquakes, then use your aerial advantage to strategically pick your opponent apart while slowing downthe enemy with defensive sites like Bottomless Pits, Sinkholes, Perilous Bridges, and even Bower of Bliss.


Below are some highlights of why certain cards made the cut:


Card Explanations 📄

Tooth Faeries

Potentially controversial, but I've never been big on Palliburrie Bats or their combo with Highland Falconer. Yeah, you can get two bodies on the board quick with 2 mana, but the 1 health non-airborne unit is too easily dealt with and doesn't jibe with the deck. Plus, the burrowing feature of the bats isn't very helpful now that I took out Devil's Eggs. Tooth Faeries have a special ability that - let's be honest - won't be helpful 80% of the time. However, it has won me games when I can prevent a chunky opposing minion from blocking at the start of my turn. Definitely a Bats upgrade in my opinion.


Cloud Spirit

An airborne 2 power minion that can effectively reach anywhere on the board. Especially in a game where the opponent has Gnome Hollows, they're amazing. Vastly underrated even in the midgame.


Headless Haunt

I was on the fence for the longest time with these (what if they fall into the Bottomless Pits!?) but now I'm a believer. Lots of people think that the randomness is a downside - it really isn't, it's more of a weird form of evasion - and that 3 cost 4 body is amazing. Play this deep in the void and watch your opponent sweat figuring out how to block it.


Daperyll Vampires

A must add with new rules noting that attacks on sites are strikes. Important for midrange beef.


Hounds of Ondaros

Very hard to remove 4 power minions. Again, important for midrange beef.


Castle Haunt

Getting too cute? Maybe. But these won me at least 2 games at the Gen Con Crossroads tourney. Still a 3 for 4 like Headless Haunt, but with the abiliy to be cast to your opponent's site directly. Worst case, I can usually cast him to one of my unique/elite sites for defense if my opponent has no sites to use. Yes, it's still risky, but IMO less risky than Headless Haunt.


Chain Lightning

An automatic finisher for only 2 mana with AoA's positioning ability. If in a rough spot, the ability to do 2-4 damage to a crowded minion field is also versatile.


Attack By Night

What's better than Disenchanting your opponent's artifacts? Taking them for yourself. Controversial within my local play group, but I believe this to be a versatile card that's worth a deeper look. Against an opponent who's artifact heavy (Battlemage, Archimago, Deathspeaker), you can force your opponent to drop all their items and then typically swoop in with your AoA's superior movement ability (or Cloud Spirit) to grab them. If you're not playing against an artifact heavy deck, the first strike for all your minions ability can be extremely helpful for clearing things out if you have plenty of minions on the board but the opponent is matching you.


Chaos Twister

Still the ultimate removal spell with upside. Just practice your blowing technique.


Mask of Mayhem / Grim Guisarme

With the rules change noting attacks on sites are strikes, Mask is a Godsend for decks with a lot of minions (of which, this is 60% minions). Be sure to not play it too early - typically only if you can take someone to door. Nothing like having a couple of Assassins come from the void to strike out of nowhere for 12 damage. Guisarme I am less convinced of in this deck - it was my 50th addition, and I might take it out for future use. The likely quick loss of it into the enemy's hands is a big negative in my opinion, and doesn't work as well in a deck full of several smaller to midrange minions.


Cut Cards ✂️

Devil's Egg

Getting these early and burrowing them has won me a few games back in the 40/20 days, but it's not consistent enough to get that off. So otherwise, they often just don't work fast enough to be worth it, or are completely dead draws in the late game. Add that they can potentially come back to haunt you in teh right situation, and it's just not worth the hassle.


Maddening Bells

Have come back to haunt me much more often than they've helped. Especially with AoA's movement ability, you don't want to constrain yourself to one part of the board like that.


Headless Haunt

Yes, 3 cost 4 power is amazing, but the randomness was useless to me in games maybe 50% of the time. When it works, it's great, but when it doesn't it just loses you games.


Palliburrie Bats / Highland Falconer

See my note under Tooth Faeries. I never feel like I'm building value when I cast these guys.


Credits 🎉

Shawn for getting me into this game, and spending way too much time theorycrafting and playing test games.

Pascal for being a great hang at Gen Con and also helping with playtesting!

CJ for being a great guy in general and helping me with a few suggestions (Bower of Bliss helped win me a Gen Con game!)

Nvekm for the original Birds list - it made me realize AoA was always going to be my favorite avatar!


Hope to get to see you, dear reader, at any events I may attend in the future!

decks.name: Gencon 2025 7th place
decks.primer:
Pathfinder is probably the riskiest avatar to run, especially when considering the atlas draw. That said it can offer the most explosiveness..potentially landing 6 sites while drawing 6 cards.


This deck hopes for at least 2 of the first 4 sites to be fire, otherwise you won't get enough speed to win.


MULLIGAN EVERYTHING EXCEPT.

  1. Ring of Morrigan.
  2. Ruby Core
  3. Jihad
  4. Boudicca.

Against Archimago do not mulligan Courtesan Thais.

Against Sorcerer keep Warhorse.


Playing.

It's a race....decimate before you are decimated.


Block only if you are losing the race.

Attack sights wherever profitable. Trade attack when you have more minions.

If your opponent allows Pathfinder to get upfield early, do so.

Save your blinks for when you really need a site or to get adjacent to an enemy avatar on deaths door.

Late game airborne minions should be used like chess pieces to contain the enemy avatar.

Don't play cerebrus if there are more aggressive options.


Card selection


I didn't put 2 monstrous lions because I wanted to be able to attack sites, nothing worse than a monstrous lion without any food.

I only have 1 manticore and 1 infernal legion ( which explains the phoenix and ancient dragon).

Shackles are great Against big minions...but the deck was fire / earth for a while, and really I was worried about missing bury.

There is only one siege giant because I wanted immolation and major explosion ( for protection and late game victory).

Pellinore is explosiveness, kill a big minion and draw a card??

Coutesan is to be played against Archimago as soon as you see craterize in the graveyard or thier hand ( via lookout ).

regarding sites, i wanted pillar of Z, but i left it in buffalo and didn't have it with me.

Also I like randomness!


My experience.

Gen con was my first time playing in an actual event. The community of players and organizers were fantastic. That was the biggest takeaway.

Technically tho.

Game 1, I drew 3 of 4 air sites and lost convincingly. The sight that shuts of charge minions was a major kryptonite.


I drew good sites games 2-7, and fortunately did not run into any avatars who disrupted my site placement which guaranteed me 6 or more sites in the early going.

Manticore hit the table once.

I drew ancient dragon 3x but never played it. There were some close calls , but I think this deck has decent chance against druid, deathspeaker is a favorable match up as well (as the deck has almost zero genesis minions). I was fortunate to not run into battlemage, archimago OR any heavy water decks.

I had alot of fun and in truth I got lucky catching the right card in a few close matches.


I have a small 5-6 person play group just south of Buffalo NY, that meets up at kitchen tables. The closest gamestore to carry it is 90 minutes away. This game is great, I hope it grow legs and thrives..Can't wait for gothic.!!

decks.name: GenCon_2024 - 8th Place Constructed
decks.primer:
Kythera Mechanism: The ability to control my Haunt’s location and keep my opponent’s Haunts stuck in the void or dying in a Bottomless Pit in the mirror match was too good of an idea to pass up. If it ever mattered, I'd be able to determine my opponent’s lightning bolts if I had to choose between one of my minions and my AoA.


No Lightning Bolts for me? Yea... I was conflicted about that. Looking back, bye-bye Land Deeds, hello Lightning Bolts!


Sling Pixies: The MVP. Airborne + Ranged is a nasty combo. No wonder the design team only granted the Pixies with 1 power. As a fan of beefy minions, I never understood the significance of those little, early game pings until I played AoA. The goal is to create enough of a disparity in life total that your opponent feels like they're on their back foot by Turn 4 or 5; and while they continue to try and stabilize, you're still dropping minions, or Devil's Eggs and Madd. Bells to make their life even more miserable. Pixies can just hang out and ping the enemy with an undefendable strike every turn; it's Airborne makes it invulnerable to ground minions (without the help of additional spells); and with 3 Trinkets in the deck, it has the potential to deal up to 4 damage in one Ranged strike.

Against Roots, Pixies are FANTASTIC blockers against the opponent’s Amazon Warriors post-Root detonation. Post-Roots, the opponent's got 5-mana and casts Warriors. On our turn, we’ve got 1-mana, drop Pixies and block for days until we stabilize.




Splashing for Fire:

Smokestacks was already in the Atlas to turn off Roots or a Cloud City in the mirror match. My question became, how much more fire affinity can I add to the Atlas without detracting from my Air affinity while also providing enough Fire sites to run single-fire-threshold spells? The deck was already running Lighthouse, so swap those out for Ruins; that's 4 fire resources. Colour out of Space seemed so obvious for multiple reasons: 1. It provides Air and Fire, 2. It offers the same defensive capability as the Lighthouses (water sites) to ward off Root Spider, 3. AoA decks cap at 4 or 5 sites, so the chances of keeping Colour next to a void is pretty high; and in the extreme case I draw Colour and Smokestacks, Smokey just turns off Colour's limiting factor. Oh, and AoA can still treat it as an Air site to push things.

But what to remove? Every other site seemed so integral. As big of a fan boy as I am for Free City, one of the 3 copies had to go. Yes, they offer insane protection and can force your opponent to stall out while trying to figure out how to storm the castle. BUT, in a mirror match, Free City is lackluster being unable to attack enemy Airborne minions, AND it doesn't offer elemental affinity, so one copy had to go.


What fire spells are worth making the cut?

THIS was a tough question, but the end result (for better or worse) was a pair of Scarabs and a pair of Kobolds.


Sacred Scarabs: In my experience, fetching Scarabs with a Falconer feels like a total win until your opponent 2-for-1's you and removes both minions (it's happened more times than I care to admit). But in those situations, I wasn't piloting AoA. Simplest explanation: make sure AoA is on an Air site > cast Falconer on same site as AoA > fetch Scarab > use AoA to fly Scarabs to a nearby site where they won't grenade the home team for 3. Then your opponent has a much more difficult decision to make. If they stay on board until your next turn, ideally strap them with a Trinket or two, swing in, explode, and deal a total of 5 or 6 damage with Trinket(s) returning to your hand.


Quarrelsome Kobolds: Aggression. Aggression. Aggression. Cast them and push them as close to enemy unit as possible with AoA, then end the turn with a free, undefendable strike for 2 damage. Or is it 3 damage? Or 4, or 5? Because we're crazy enough to run 3 Trinkets. AoA loves its Gyre Hippos. Those Charging winged beasts feel so good to drop on turn 3 after a Dark Tower (my personal favorite Tower). From my pov, Kobolds are a 3-mana, 2-power minion with faux-Charge. If your opponent has played their sites aggressively enough to meet you in the middle of the board, ideally you've flown AoA to your forward most site on a previous turn > cast Kobolds on the same site as AoA > fly them straight ahead to bonk the enemy Avatar EOT who is probably still hanging out on their initial square.


Fire's Honorable Mentions: Blaze, Petrosian Cavalry, Pit Vipers, Wils-o-the-Wisp, Clamor of Harpies, Firebolts, Infiltrate and Poison Nova.


What did I learn after going 4-0 and then losing in the 5th and 6th round?

  • Land Deed wasn't worth it. I didn't get enough playtesting in to determine if I really wanted a pair of Land Deeds in there. However, in playtesting, I managed to get Madd Bells out by Turn 3 on the wings of a Bat and it caused such massive setbacks for my opponent it made me ask, "how can I make THAT more consistent?" Land Deed was the answer. In hindsight, I wish I could go back in time, slap me on the wrist and say "NO. Either you put the Bolts back in there or the Flanking Maneuver, but you are taking those Deeds out. Hell, put in a 4th Grapple Shot!"
  • In order to learn from my losses, it helps to remember the sequences that led to the loss. My Round 5 match against Zalem was brutal. By T3 he’d played (in this order): Free City, G Hollows, and Mirror Realm to copy Free City. The game was basically over; G Hollows locks out nearly 50% of my minions (Haunt, Phase Ass, Gyre Hippo and Dap Vamp); and Free City prevents me from attacking with 80% of my minions! For better or worse, I’m wired to never give up, so the game continued. I tried my best to attack his Hollows with my Bats and his Free Cities with my Haunts, until he dropped 2 Root Spiders by T4 and T5 under is Hollows. My only options at that point were to draw into a Smokestacks to shut down his FC and GH or put a Sling Pixies on his Free City and ping his Seer for 2 with Trinket. He Infiltrated my Bat on his third Hollow (the only one without a burrowed Root Spider) and used it to kill my Cloud Spirit attempting to enter the Hollows and join the meager assault. The most disheartening series of turns was when he cast a Scarecrow into the hands of Root Spider which prevented my burrowed Bat from entering and killing the Spider. The next turn he dropped 1 Angel’s Egg to the spider, and the turn after, a 2nd Angel’s Egg. In a matter of turns he'd completely inverted the life total. The entire game I never saw my Devil’s Eggs, Madd Bells or Boulders. All would’ve helped in their own way.
  • AoA benefits from splashing an element. Is Fire the best element to splash? I've been asking that since playtesting for GenCon. How I'd love to run Windmills for Earth, push my opponent's minions onto Air sites above my burrowed Root Spider, or Common Sense for a Grapple Shot or Bolt. Put the Lighthouses back in for Water and use Shrink help my small minions take out larger threats. But that's just one element (no pun intended) of the beauty of this game. There are so many options for creative answers. If I could go back, I would've put in 2 Pit Vipers, maybe 3, to handle enemy Root Spiders.
  • My Round 6 loss against Chris (I forget his last name) was pretty straightforward. He piloted AoE and ran me over with Earthquake and big minions. What can you say? Earth is good. Again, Pit Vipers would've been ideal, surviving Earthquake, and easily trading with any minion he put down. I don't recall drawing into my FC or BP which would've kept those ground minions at bay. Ultimately, I think I played my hand and the game in front of me the best I could. As the saying goes, you win some, you lose some.
  • Cheers!

decks.name: SorceryFest 11th Place | Fire (Air-Splash) Imposter
decks.primer:
Flamecaller Fetish for Beginners


Intro

After a hiatus from other TCGs, I decided to give another game a chance. I previously played MTG Legacy and Premodern, and I picked up Sorcery in mid-May 2026. I immediately fell in love with the artwork, the gameplay, and the community. After a few games at my local LGS, I found out about the Summit (a big thank you goes to the organizing team). I got my ass handed to me pretty badly in my first few games. However, after a while and with a lot of support and coaching from the other players, I started to find a deck that I enjoyed. Once again, the community has been amazing. I then decided to give the whole TCG tournament experience a try. This was the first TCG tournament I had ever travelled to attend. Below is a quick report on my experience and some of my notes


Overall Record: 11th place out of 128 players at SorceryFest 2026


Matchups

  • Archimago (Win)
  • Fire Pathfinder (Win)
  • Mud Sorcerer (Loss - Opponent ended in 10th place overall)
  • Interrogator (Win)
  • Deathspeaker (Win)
  • Water Pathfinder (Loss - super close game, made a misplay with [[Warp Spasm]], but at least I learned my lesson)
  • Archimago (Win)


Tournament Notes


Comments on key spells:

  • [[Flamecaller]] was the MVP, dealing more than 8-10 damage in four matches. Paired with [[War Horse]] movement or [[Flanking Maneuver]], it can catch the opponent completely off guard
  • The early ramp from [[Mix Ignis]] and [[Four Waters of Paradise]] once again proved that this is exactly what an Imposter wants. Cheating out threats early gives you more room to breathe when using the Pathfinder mask. Two plays stood out: (i) playing [[Mix Ignis]] into [[Morgana le Fay]] on turn one felt almost disgustingly good and (ii) using [[Four Waters of Paradise]] in the late game to cast an [[Infernal Legion]] and then teleport it with [[Flanking Maneuver]] to put the opponent at death’s door and clear the blockers made a compelling case for why the card is strong in both the early and late game
  • [[Courtesan Thaïs]] was incredibly strong against Archimago. She won me Game 7 by blowing up the Archimago with his own [[Major Explosion]]
  • I was not sure about [[Inquisition]] before the tournament, but it turned out to be a real MVP. Sniping a key card from the opponent’s hand and later animating it with [[Deathspeaker]] is incredibly strong
  • [[Asmodeus]] felt great in testing, but was somewhat clunky during the tournament. Without a way to move him onto an enemy site on the turn he enters, you lose much of his immediate impact. Note: moving him via [[Wuthering Heights]] or [[War Horse]] worked well in testing
  • Cutting two [[Redcap Powries]] to make room for [[Swiven Scout]] felt like a good decision. I was hesitant to give up three points of charge damage, but knowing the opponent’s hand had a meaningful impact in two or three games
  • I am considering replacing one [[Infiltrate]] with one [[Betrayal]]. Infiltrate is good, but sometimes you need the immediate damage - or simply want to steal the minion and [[Warp Spasm]] it immediately
  • [[Peasant Revolt]]: There is not much to say about this card. Every time it hits the board, it feels like an “I win” button. The only thing that felt mediocre this time was my inclusion of more Elite sites, such as [[Wizard’s Den]]. When I played it against the Deathspeaker opponent, however, it destroyed five sites on my opponent’s side and two Elites on mine, which felt like a good trade
  • [[Seasoned Sellsword]] is a highly debatable card. The one time it came up, however, it was extremely relevant. I played it beneath my Imposter after pathfinding, well outside the enemy Pathfinder’s range. My opponent had to respect it and make a suboptimal trade. The dream scenario would have been using [[Blaze of Glory]] with the Sellsword to wipe the opponent’s board


A few observations on the sites:

  • I never had a problem casting an Air spell when I wanted to. Of course, you need to think carefully about your mulligan and the sequencing of your site draws once you are off Pathfinder and have not yet seen an Air site
  • The heavy Fire focus allows you to play more colorless sites, such as [[Sinkhole]] and [[Wizard's Den]], which felt great. [[Wizard's Den]] was especially strong as a home site
  • [[Fields of Phyxis]] and [[Smokestacks of Gnaak]] are MVPs against decks with defensive sites, such as Archimago or Necro, although I did not face Necro at the tournament. I would always mulligan aggressively for these sites because they can be backbreaking for the opponent


Special thanks to Aadu for driving innovation within this archetype of aggressive Flamecaller Imposters - for more details about the deck philosophy & composition visit his primer

decks.name: Captain Planet [SorceryFest 2nd Place]
decks.primer:
“Earth, Wind, Fire, Water, Heart. With your powers combined.”


“I’m gunna save you the heart break, three colours won’t work. You will variance your way out of this tournament.” – Geoffrey


This deck came 2nd in the SorceryFest 2026 Grand Contest in Leeuwarden, The Netherlands.


THE DECK PHILOSOPHY

Shout out to @Aadu who I think was the first person to really figure out the Imposter theory I’m using – hit hard and early, and force your opponent to choose between putting their resources into removing the Pathfinder Mask, or removing the early game pressure we aim to apply. The first generation of decks we brewed with this philosophy (that I was involved with) were running Mixes and Four Waters, but in Earth/Fire at the moment I don’t think they are required as there are plenty of powerful 3-drops we can deploy.


The deck is designed to incrementally accrue a value differential with the opponent on board by trading with 4+ power minions, whilst drawing 1 additional card per turn with the Pathfinder Mask early.


In the late game, you have the flexibility of the 9 other masks in the collection, as well as a number of ‘tricks’ to deploy across 3 colours.


We stretch to:

4 pips for Earth (for Michael, Gargantula, and Paladins) though majority 2 pip.

3 pips for Fire (for Peasant Revolt, and Morgana) though majority 2 pip.

1 pip for Air. Towers are good enough to run in non-Air mono element decks in my opinion. That we gain access to some incredible spells is just icing on the cake.


THE ATLAS

The site selection is almost entirely threshold based, and ordinary as much as possible. 

By simulating drawing 7 sites off the top of a shuffled deck, I was able to verify that not hitting my thresholds is highly improbable (though obviously still possible) post mulligan.


I have 8/30 opportunities to hit the single air threshold I need.

I only run 3 Elite/Unique sites:

Mount Ussar – So many Sorcery games come down to a double death door situation, and fleeing with a Ward can allow you to tie-break these games.

Valley of Delight – Flexible threshold selection allows 3 elements to work.


The other benefit of this site selection is a partial immunity to Atlantean Fate (which can win games on turn 5) via the 12 ordinary sites – there will almost always be somewhere to stack up minions.


THE SPELLBOOK


Minions Package

The minion package is a fairly generic Earth/Fire selection, with a focus on being able to drop a threat on turn 3 OR a Stefania to disrupt the opponent (depending on draws and matchup). We have a reasonable curve up to 7 mana maximum.

Pudge Butcher is one minion I think has been under-rated for some time. 4 mana for 5 power, with the ability to yoink the opposing avatar or annoying minions across the realm is incredibly valuable. He can lock down columns, or be silenced/blinked to suddenly re-emerge as a threat. Far too frequently I see players ignore Pudge Butcher, because they don’t want to take a turn to step to the side, and instead rely on a blocker between themselves and the Butcher.


The Common Sense Package

I run 2xCommon Sense, which have 11 options:

1. 1xBlink – A Pudge Butcher enabler, a cantrip, or a kill spell.

2. 1xCritical Strike – One of the best ‘tricks’ in this deck, that can enable you to Door the opponent from 20 life. This works with Michael, and can also be played, flashed back with Magoo to allow you to hit the enemy avatar for 4x damage for 7 mana.

3. 1xDispel – Ompholoi and the Ring and Atlantean Fate are everywhere, this requires no explanation.

4. 1xFirebolts – Kills through Ward or blockers as the projectiles are one at a time, or just mops up token minions.

5. 2xGift of the Serpent – Excellent value with Collicky or Kobolds. Also a cantrip.

6. 1xGift of the Wolf – For value trading + a cantrip.

7. 1xLightning Bolt – Kills Ironclad.

8. 1xBury – Can be minion removal, but can also just waste an opponent’s Omphalos in minion heavy decks, or just get rid of Ring.

9. 2xGrapple Shot – One of the reasons I’m splashing Air, and an enabler for big bursty damage.


The extensive use of cheap spells means I can frequently drop a threat + gain value with a magic each turn from the midgame onwards. This also fills the Cemetery for Archimago Mask value in the late game.


The Board Wipes

1xPoison Nova – This card is so incredible, it was a tough choice to only run one. However I think given the Power of the minions being deployed, frequently I’m ahead on board, and this is more of a last resort OR fantastic in a situation where my opponent is racing me, and our minions are on opposite sides of the realm.

2xEarthquake – Really requires no explanation. Earth decks run this.

2xMajor Explosion – I chose this over Craterize because I don’t really want to be going over 7 mana if possible. This spell already does plenty enough damage.


Everything Else

1xTithe – As an Imposter, you will have games where the opponent has a Lightning Bolt from the mulligan, or some other way to get you off Pathfinder Mask quickly. In these games, Tithe enables you to continue drawing 1 spell each turn to out-value them.

1xPeasant Revolt – Truly the MVP of this deck. It can only hit 3/30 of our sites, and absolutely wrecks many other decks that have loaded up with Unique/Elite minions and sites. This card can single-handedly win the game against Air/Water Necro, who’s the big bad of this meta.

1xGigantism – Big attack good.

2xDisintegrate – Unconditional removal, and a banish for annoying deathrites or minions that could return (Green Knight).


1xRing of Morrigan – Every deck should run this, but I would mulligan it away against any Water deck. Swap is death.

2xTrinket – Value trade with your opponent! Get ahead on board.

1xRuby Core – Imposter loves ramp, and an extra Fire threshold doesn’t hurt.


THE MASKS

I think of the masks as incredible 3 mana spells, that can reuse their effect once per turn for 0 unless you take direct damage.


In rough order of importance:

Pathfinder – This is the heart of every Imposter deck. +1 card per turn.

Sorcerer - +1 card per turn from site 7 onwards.

Ironclad – Ironclad… on a Gnome Hollows… with a Spider under it…

Deathspeaker – With 3 colours, we have the opportunity to utilise our opponent’s graveyard a lot. Archangel Michael can be a big surprise.

Interrogator – One line you can take if PF Mask is destroyed, or if the opportunity presents itself, is Interrogator. The opponent will almost always allow you to draw, allowing you to draw sites for turn (effectively inversing the PF Mask).

Avatar of Earth – It’s an Earth meta at the moment, and this mask can swing for 6.

Archimago – Almost always just to flash back one spell for the finish, anything under 5 mana in the graveyard is up for grabs.

Enchantress – Almost entirely for removing the opponent’s Auras as I only run The Great Famine, but if you happen to need 4 extra damage…

Witch – Sometimes you just really need 2 damage. More rarely you can curse to stop a Craterize.

Savior – This was my flex slot, and I did consider Flamecaller instead. I think I only got value from this Mask once in the entire tournament, but if you don’t have anything else to do on a turn it can be quite threatening to leave up.


THE MATCHUPS

This deck was built to combat the AW Necro plague, and I can report it’s highly effective. We have deserts to ping skeletons, we have Dragonettes/Kobolds to ping skeletons. We have disables and defensive sites for their early big minions. We have Orders who stop skeleton production entirely. Pudge Butcher is ready to yoink them (or just remove 1 skeleton per turn for the rest of the game from the back row). And all the while they live in fear that the Peasants are coming…


The deck runs no Archimago hate, and the only 2 losses I took were to Archimago (one to Felix in the Swiss which was avenged in the semi-final, and to Geoffrey in the final). However the deck still has a decent chance (I would estimate 45:55 in favour of the Magoo). 


The games I played were:

Mud Sorceror

Water Pathfinder

Dragonlord Talamh Dreig (quite possibly the most terrifying game)

Dust Ramp Sorceror

2x AW Necro

3x Archimago

Mud Imposter

decks.primer:
VOD of this deck against Joost (Druid) and Geoffrey (Archimago): [[https://youtu.be/6IGgqONf9x4?t=26846]]


This deck is based on Steam Druid by Stirnlappenbasilisk, placing first in Sorcery Summit. Check out his great primer for the most important interactions and play patterns.


My iteration is more geared towards minion-heavy competition as you would encounter in your local tournament or playgroup. It has barely any specific tech against [[Archimago]]. Against that guy you need:

Charge - This deck barely has any. If you can't get a hit in with your minions you are basically lost, and Charge guarantees that.

Information - It helps immensely if you know what a control deck like Archie has access to at any moment. [[Swiven Scout]] helps with that.

One big turn - This aspect is kept intact in this iteration of the deck. [[Plague of Frogs]] + [[Boudicca]] / [[Sir Agravaine]], a [[Ruler of Thul]] attack, or most importantly a well timed [[Courtesan Thais]]. Getting them to Death's Door in one turn or stripping away all their resources in the late game is your best shot.


Notable Changes:

[[Golden Harp]] - Love that card in a meta with large scary minions. Performs incredibly well together with [[Panorama Manticore]], which can now kill up to two minions each turn cycle (1 attack + 1 block).

[[Green Knight]] - Another great stabilizer. While [[Infernal Legion]] fulfills a similar role, it can be a bit limited when it's used defensively due to the indiscriminate damage effect. Swap him out against another Infernal Legion if aggression is the only goal, i.e. Archimago.

[[Lady of the Lake]] - Inclusion of Green Knight and Golden Harp made it worth it to me to include this card. Other great hits include [[Morgana le Fay]] (feels really busted to draw fresh 3 cards), [[Boudicca]] and [[Ring of Morrigan]].

[[Adept Illusionist]] - Works wonderfully together with [[Pnakotic Manuscript]] and [[Pact with the Devil]]. Can trigger defensive cards ([[Troll Bridge]], [[Mariner's Curse]], [[Giant Shark]]) to free the way for your attack. Great damage sponge which forces your opponent to use removal or practically give up one attack each turn.


Cards on my mind

[[Pollimorph]] - I like frogs, thats why it's in here. [[Disintegrate]] would be better in this deck.

[[Pnakotic Manuscript]] - Always needs to have either [[Tadpole Pool]], [[Plague of Frogs]], [[Adept Illusionist]] or [[Green Knight]] on board. Just [[Tawny]] is not enough, [[Pact with the Devil]] works way better with her. I did not miss it at all when I didn't draw it, and sometimes it was just a dead draw if you have no board presence. Drawing 7 cards feels nice though.

Dang its been a while since I worked on the deck. I've been chatting with other Waveshaper players about tech and what the deck looks like in the post "Heirloom Lost / Mirage" world. Silver Bullet is gone for Meat Hook. There has been a lot of buzz about that card in the Waveshaper circle and I'm excited to try it. Same is true for Giant Shark. decks.primer:
Two events played. Was 10-1 until I lost both of games #7 and #8 in the swiss rounds of the main event. Better luck next year!


Was planning on playing my earth build in the main event but after doing so well on Friday I ended up playing my mono air list for the main event. I beat 3 water necros in swiss on day #1. The main way this deck counters water builds is by using phyxis and sinkhole. Then aggro'ing them out. The idea is to be as sticky as possible w/ voidwalk, airborne and stealth. The Hounds of Ondaros are all-stars. Having airborne and whirling blades is so crucial for removal.


The main removal of the deck is to play the sites strategically and hopefully pull a bottomless pit, the void, or manor. If I don't get one of those sites in my starting hand I hard mulligan all 3 sites. Relying on this removal strategy works when it works. Its problematic when it doesn't work. Dan, who made top cut with AoA ended up splashing fire so he could have poison nova for removal. Great idea.

decks.name: Firefinder - SorceryCon 12th Place
decks.primer:
Fire Pathfinder that I played at Sorcery Con 2026 - took 12th place on tiebreakers (6-2) with a very narrow loss in the last round (got the door first but didn't manage to top deck the kill - really epic fight and super well played by my opponent Ismark the Lesser). Pretty simple deck, not much to say about it. Definitely still lots of fine points to playing it though. In the current meta I think one of the big tricks with this deck is not overplaying onto the board while maintaining pressure. Especially into the "Creature Control" meta with lots of Water and Water/Air midrange decks this deck wins on tempo, but loses big to mass removal. You want to mulligan for minions early (maybe keep a single removal spell if you also have some low cost minions but top priority is having 2 and 3 drop minions to start the pressure game. Once you have a minion or two on board though you are just trying to maintain that.


The other common way to win with this deck is setting up a big turn where you blast in a bunch of damage with something like warp spasm, blaze of glory, betrayal, etc. Lots of other cards that go well in this deck, but everything is fighting for slots. Would love to run Shatter Strikes or maybe even Critical Strike to lean more into burst damage turns.


Really torn about Baba Yaga - I don't want more than 5 non fire sites (including mirror realm), so is the extra motion potential that is useful like 50% of the time it is played worth it, or am I better off just running a lone tower to get that ramp value..... Or wizard's Den for the extra card?

decks.name: Silent Fury SorceryCon 17th place
decks.primer:
This deck was very good, and I feel like a good choice for the field of decks present at SC. It's essentially the fury road shell with an emphasis on silence effects. I went 6-2 with this list at Sorcery Con 2026, losing round 2 to mud Geomancer, and round 8 to AoA. It won against 3 Necro decks, Avatar of Earth, fire pathfinder, and an Elementalist brew.


Notable cards:

Sister Stefánia - this card is a power house. I don't think any of the games I had it were close.

Sinterfee - this card is very good against the water decks. Paired with jihad it's amazing.

Corruptor freak - harasses well and can just move to sites forcing multiple interactions to answer it often into a just summoned fatty blocker

Rift valley/smokestacks - these are kind of the same slot because they let us bypass our opponents annoying sites. Expect your opponents to have very good sites. Having ways around them was very helpful.

Earthquake - this card does everything this deck wants. It helps get around sites, it kills stuff allowing you to attack, and most the time just moving the opposing avatar close to your attackers is good enough, get them on DD even if they are on all water sites.

Flame strike (collection) - I think I killed more avatars with this than anything else. You are pretty much always one step away from a hit on DD with this.

Onslaught - I think in many ways this is better than gift of the wolf even without the card draw. It makes spiders worthless, gives you a little charge when needed the spread out damage buff is often better than +2 on a single creature. It also lets you do silly things with your silence/disabled effects like play a slobermaw silenced then give it charge. Or allowing a sleeping giant to wake itself up by attacking a unit. I'll be testing with two copies.


Cards I'm considering cutting:

Blightstone - I got a little sold on this card by a friend. I didn't draw it very often, and each time it was kind of dead in my hand. There were a few times I wanted it. But sinterfee is almost always better.

Hyena - there's just not enough demons that are worth playing. I played it a lot as a 2 power creature, and had mixed feelings about it.

Leadworks - while annoying sites can be problematic for this deck this card never quite lined up the way I wanted. Its really hard in a deck that only wants to play 4 sites to have this line up with a threat in play and a site you need to deal with for a turn.

Slumbering giantess - this card was harder to wake up than I'd like. I still think it's good but it probably needs some other tweaks (more deserts?) to make worth it.

Critical strike (collection) - this was always supposed to be a spin attack, but I get these two chronically confused. Luckily they're pretty close to the same effect.

decks.name: SorceryCon 11th place (6-2) Salt the Wound
decks.primer:
This is a mean deck. It won’t win you many friends but it will win you many games. The name of the game is burn it down or beat them down fast. Using site destruction to slow down or cripple your opponent or minions with immediate impact (i.e. charge, damage on genesis, damage at end of turn). The deck is purposefully built low to the ground for a quick start and eventually multi-spelling at higher mana totals.


Site Destruction Strategies

The main strategy of this deck is site destruction. It utilizes [[Hamlets Ablaze]] and [[Castles Ablaze]] to target defensive sites and your opponents threshold. There’s nothing worse than having a hand full of double pip spells and you constantly lose the threshold to cast them. [[Raze]] can be used to destroy opponents sites but more importantly their artifacts. It’s great for dealing with [[Dank Omphalos]] and its brethren, [[Battlemage]] with a shload of equipment, and if need be popping [[Roots of Yggdrasil]] for a complete board clear. Twice in the tournament, I cast [[Raze]] on my avatar and destroyed Roots the turn it came into play and that won me the game.


TO BE CONTINUED

decks.name: SCRCON 2026 | 7th Place | Constructed Championship
decks.primer:
"Evil, Fliers and Ranged, OH MY!"


The TLDR:


Evil:

  • Vile Imp, Redmayne Hyena, Spore Spouts and Desecrate. Do the math.
  • You know who loves Desecrated Ground? Evil minions. What's better than a 5 power Legion of Gall? A 6 power Legion of Gall.


Fliers:

  • We've got 14 fliers and over half of them are 4+ power and either gain us life, wreck our opponent's Collection, or just cause a friggin headache!


Ranged:

  • A playset of Stygian Archers and Skirmishers of Mu? Yes. And I'd play more if I could!
  • Shout out to MTR Joseph (the one and only Realm Eater pilot in the Constructed Championship at SCRCON) for enlightening me on how disgusting Skirmishers can actually be. To be continued in full primer...


Ideal Early Game Plays:

  • T1 Tower > Forsaken into a T3 Desecrate to mess with our opponent's Affinity
  • T2 Spore Spouts > Vile Imp into a T3 Desecrate
  • T3 Jack the Ripper their Aino or Morgana into a T4 Desecrate


omg why does this guy love Desecrate so much...


Desecrate:

  • Think back at games you lost because of a well placed Smokestacks, Thin Ice, Troll Bridge, Bottomless Pit, Perilous Bridge, etc... yea. Desecrate handles that.
  • Buff your minions. Forsaken seems innocent until it hits for 3, Desecrates for 3, and then becomes a 4 power minion. "We have Lugbog Cat at home, sweetie".
  • Timing is everything, though. If you can't Move and Attack with your Evil minion without risking a trade then you're not set up for a Desecrate. But we're piloting AoA baby, oh and we have even more tech for that... stay tuned for the full primer!


Other Spells:

  • Arcane Barrage beats Ward as long as you can pay the minions power + 1. It wreaks havoc on tokens, is nightmare fuel against Imposter and can close out nearly any game thanks to AoA's inherent maneuverability.
  • Browse to hunt for Desecrate... (i know, i have a problem)
  • Disenchant. Because Ring and A. Fate exist.
  • Feast for Crows. F**k Mesmerism. (Both games I've lost to CJ at major events he beat me with Mesmerism... well, and because he's a top-notch player)
  • Grapple Shot and Whirling Blades. I don't need to explain these - but - imagine your opponent plays their Archangel and you've got a Stygian Archers in play with a Trinket and Grapple Shot in hand. You Trinket your Archers, Grapple the Archangel to break ward and Ranged strike for 4 while getting an Allied Skelly to boot. It feels, so, good. Now imagine casting Whirling Blades on your Archers and killing more than one enemy minion to then replace each of them with Allied Skellys? Disgusting. Wait, Skellys are Evil right? Did someone say Desecrate?
  • Infiltrate and Poison Nova: unarguably two of the most impactful Fire spells at the single-Fire threshold level. These two spells are what forced me into splashing fire. Trust me, I hate having to run the castles, Colour and Ruins in place of other Air or utility sites, but I truly believe Infiltrate and Poison Nova are worth it.


Full primer to come...


Cheers and great games to everyone I played at SCRCON 2026!!!

Event Information

This deck took 5th place in the Columbus Ohio Explorer Series. Where Archimago and Ring of Morrigan were banned.


It's an update version of this deck:

https://curiosa.io/decks/cm3iwz25l0018bpm7ka2yh6bq

Which took 2nd place at a 20 player event in Detroit in late 2024.


The deck went 5-0 before top cut, where I lost in the first round to the same player playing a variant of the same deck that the previous iteration lost to in the finals of Detroit (before explorer series). I also played him in the Chicago explorer series event. Every game has been a nail biter where we have doored each other, and where every game I had the win on the following turn. In anticipation of playing against that exact deck I added troll bridges and a free city for this event. This is because I know in that matchup he is the aggressor, and having one turn to stabilize could mean the difference.


The Game Plan:


Build an efficient early game board using fetch minions, playing slightly defensively. Move to opponents side using movement tech like [[Ruler of Thul]] or [[Polar Explores]] to circumvent defensive sites for large amount of damage in one turn.


Heavy damage: [[Ruler of Thul]], [[Sir Agravaine]]

Enablers: [[Polar Explorers]]

The Final Blow: [[Magic Missiles]], [[Lightning Bolt]]

decks.name: Unland Cup 2025 3rd place - AoE Earth-Air Midrange
decks.primer:
Played in Unland Cup in Seattle, June 2025

Went 6-0 in Swiss, then lost in semifinals to Archimago in top 8.


I consider this a standard AoE deck. It goes for consistency, midrange minons, and attacking with the avatar asap with a few spells as finishers.

I played okay but not great, but did well mostly because I lucked out that AoE worked well in the meta and many players were unfamiliar with AoE. I played against 2 Archi decks in 5 games 3-2. If they drew Divine Healing I lost, if they didn't I won. Infiltrate on my large minions was a big problem both when it happened and in making me afraid to play them. Doing it again I would use more Hunter's Lodge and/or Watchtowers. Otherwise the deck worked pretty much like I hoped and was very consistent.


How I Play

Main goal is getting opponent to death's door asap, well before they get me there. Usually this happens by playing a few sites and minions then beating on enemy sites. Getting last hit can be a challenge but there are several cards that can do it and I'll do my best to save one of them for that purpose.


Mulligan

The deck needs 3 earth and 1 air threshold. The air usually isn't needed in the early turns but I do try to have exactly 1 threshold in my opening hand. Windmill is preferred but the extra mana from tower is also nice. Try to get at least one Land Surveyor or Kettletop.


Typical / preferred early game

Turn 1 - Earth site, prefer soldier token

Turn 2 - Earth site, Land Surveyor or Kettletop. Alternately Crusade.

Turn 3 - Third site, hopefully Earth because you had a Windmill or drew fourth site from a minion. Autumn Unicorn. I usually save Root Spider for a specific need.

Turn 4 or 5 - When you have the mana, play Atlas Wanderers and swap the middle 2 sites. Earthquake can also be used. Ideally you get one or two sites from minions or a Core and never need to tap to draw a site.

Later - Step forward and pound the enemy site that is now surrounded by your earth sites.


Sometimes it makes sense to Grapple Shot your Avatar across instead especially if they have earth sites.


Weaknesses

Mostly having lots of minions to defend and damage to get me to DD first.

Gnome Hollows is annoying especially when played in the site in front of their avatar.


A great use of Root Spider is to place under your avatar so enemy minions cannot defend the site.

Royal Bodyguard allows you to attack while on DD.


Cards

Vivien and Rhitta are not essential and could be swapped out. Biggest downside to Rhitta is the 6 cost and I don't want to play that many sites. Philo Stone is not a must either.

I used to have 4 Grapple Shots but kept finding myself not needing them as often. 4 might still be better.

There is no Whirling Blades because it needs 2 Air.

decks.name: Heavy Artillery Token Sorcerer [20th place at Ropecon 2026)
decks.primer:
Play style


Token spam is the name of the game. The core of the deck is Border Militia: cast it early, cast it often. Recast it with Skeleton Mage. Get more tokens from villages, Boulevard of Bones, and Guards! Defend your tokens with Shield Maidens.


Use your tokens defensively. Their main job is to slow down your opponent and make their single target removal inefficient.


There is a subtheme of ranged minions. They are also supposed to be defensive, restricting your opponent's movement and attack paths. I'm not sure if they belong here or not.


Wincon


The heavy artillery (Trebuchet and Catapult) is the wincon. You want to get to 5 mana, and then start double drawing to feed the Trebuchet. The artillery can kill problematic minions but is also difficult to avoid damage to your opponent.


Use cards like Tactical Move and Blink to position your tokens so they can use the artillery.


King of the Realm is either 7 damage from the artillery, or a wincon of his own if the game goes long.

decks.name: Ropecon Battlemage E/A
decks.primer:
This is the deck I played at Ropecon in Helsinki 27.7.2025, placing 6th out of 14. The tournament was best of 3 games, and I ended up with a score of 2-2-0 (two ties).


I built the deck a day before the tournament day, so I didn't have time to practice with it. What I noticed was that in the late-game I didn't actually have time to actually cast many of my bigger spells, and ended up having tons of cards in hand. Since Battlemage draws cards on it's own, I would consider lowering the curve to be able to cast the spells drawn. But while saying that, I'm not really sure how it'd change the deck. The deck might play better being a Druid list, but I just love Battlemage.


I would definitely add a 3rd Shield Maidens. That was a great card against most deck. It provides protection from the ring and from Poison Nova that my big creatures are very afraid of.


I could consider cutting the Dispel. The deck is not too worried about a ring since the creatures are quite big. I was however scared of Grim Guisarmes so wanted to have something to deal with them if necessary, and for Atlantean Fates. But I didn't end up running against anything I would have wanted to remove.


The Maybe-board includes cards I would have played if I had owned them. The changes I would have made would have been:


  • - 2 Dalcean Phalanx
  • - Tintagel
  • - Beacon
  • + Royal Bodyguard
  • + Gigantism
  • + Glastonbury Tor
  • + The Colour Out of Space

Hello there! Hope you having a lovely day.


I was recently at a tournament in Krems, Austria and did preety well for myself! Even though I am playing only for 5 months I still have a lot to learn about this wonderful game and I do believe that this deck is currently one of the strongest water decks out there.


This deck is not my own creation. The mastermind behind it is @Hicham and you should check his main decklist out on curiosa. He is a great guy, and helped me out immensely on learning the deck properly, and understanding the underlying principles of how he imagined things working.


I enjoyed playing with this deck, it is very good and for someone like me, that hasn't played much competitive rl tournaments and it made me not overthink about a lot of things, but rather play aggressive and focus on my own game plan.


The basis of the deck, if you are a magic player, this would be the most Simic experience you will have.


You want to ramp out your big guys, you want to overflow the board, and you want to use your spells to out position your opponents and do valuable trades. Card draw is king in a lot of scenarios where things go a bit late game, but in reality, water is so strong right now, that in the end you will have more value on the board compared to your opponents.


Silver bullet, Snowball, good Swaps will finish on door.


The meta is strong with Necromancers, but a Pied Piper or a Mester Stoor Worm can do a lot of work.


Hopefully you will try it for yourself and enjoy it in its own glory!


Take care and have fun sorcery buddies!

decks.primer:
This deck wants to play the [[Payload Trebuchet]] to fling big cost cards into your enemy's face.


To use a Trebuchet you need pairs of cheap minions that you don't mind tapping to use the Weapon instead of attacking. To that end we have lots of [[Foot Soldier (English)]] generation and low cost minions, especially ones that slow down the opponent or protect your cheap minions a little. The [[Siege Ballista]] are a simple alternative to this siege weapon. The [[Corpse Catapult]] is another option, and can work alongside the Trebuchet well, thorwing the card you just discarded in the same turn.


As ammuntion for the Trebuchet and Catapult you need lots of high cost cards. Lots of the Atlas is focused on stalling and slowing down your opponent until you can potentially cast these cards, in case you don't find your siege Weapons. You also have cost reducers and ramp options to help afford these big cost cards when you can.


[[Dwarven Digging Team]]s are just to try and protect your big cost Minions from being Buried.



You can see me use an earlier version of the deck on youtube here:

deffenitly take a look at his list

Elements: Water, Air
