i was surprised how versatile the list was in my first games and so I stuck with it. I have a MTG background the deck remained me on the caw/blade in standert ore the caw/gate of the pauper format and I like this kind of decks very much. The deck can play a very good tempo game ore if needed a solid grindy control like game. The first that you have to learn is which position do you have to take in every game depending on your opponent’s avatar. Do you have to play an aggressive tempo game ore do you take the slower part and build you board up to press the button later. This deck is very rewarding if you can take the game and loosing is always a lesson to take. In all my games I had not the feeling that this match was not winnable. I thing you should know if you want to play a list like this is, that the deck do not carry the player.

The main goal of this list is to time walk your opponent at every time. That meant make the turn they take the worst they can, and try to force them to take bad plays to Handel you.


The following entries are some kind of journal to track the evolution of this deck. I try my best to cover all bigger events that I play in and try to summarize all thought about my changes. Still in progress


6.7.26

im back from the sorcery fast. I went 4/3 in Swiss it could have been 5/2 if had not make an crucial misplay in my last game were I have not bring my q-beast back on a water site so it got hit with a bury so I went first on DD that play cost me the game. But all in all it was a blast to play, I never have such diverse opponents the only avatar I saw twice was the geomancer in Earth/fire.

Game 1 vs Andreas on earth geomancer

pretty long game pretty much back and forth but in the end he make a sequence mistake were I got the opportunity to play dodge roll to evade the dmg and his last minion to deff was taped so I hit him with my bm and close the game

Game 2 vs Ronnie on fire pathfinder

this is the matchup I feared most, but an early sir pilieas with a good played whirling blades hit him for 8 clear the board so I have to step on the gas. A well placed succubus got the way free for the bm and he was on dd. The only thing was, to keep him going in the right direction for my grapel and I won.

Game 3 vs Geoffrey on earth/fire archi

for this I was not prepared. Geoffrey is the man to beat in Europe and I know he and his archi do not make it easy for me. The game was a big lesson for me I thought if I am fast enough I can do some things, but a turn 2 gnomehollos cut me off so I must build my way around him. Non of my minions can enter this side and my bm neither. And arch angel Michael on Curve and some leprechaun did the dmg. Whirlingblades to step closer clear som tokens but it was not enough. The new build is insane consistent and the tokens and onslaught got me very quickly to dd so I lose.

Game 4 against BM air/water

A mirror match I have not consider. His list leans more into equipments then mine and I thought I have the upper hand with my two year experience on this avatar. It was a back and forth but in the end I stretched his avatar with the rack over 2 sides and got him to dd. He played plague of frogs but my stealthed aino and Jack the Ripper cut his way off and got me the win.

Game 5 Enchantress air/water/fire

turn two bridge and turn 3 sphere cut my avatar of turn 4 for chains to makes it round and I do not draw disenchant ore tool box ore any minions so I lose.

Game 6 Florence on Air/water Druide

i got an early falconer play followed up with a ruler and a gyre so she was quick on dd. She played black plague but it was to late….. the dmg was done she killed my falconer and my bats. Flipped into the bear but I saved my ruler in the turn before draw a ring hit the bear with the bm scatter the bear ping the bear and hit with ruler for game.

Game 7 vs mono earth geomancer

the game was intense and we both got us at some point on dd. In the end I got killed with an arch angel Michael play. My big mistake was that I forgot to move my q beast back on an water side to protect it from a bury. In the Ende this was the dmg I lost to get him first on dd. So I lost and went 4/3 in this grand contest.

over all I would say I could have won my last game if I had think about the board more but the other losses I had, I do not think I could done more Geoffrey is an excellent player were I think the skill gab hade make the big difference because I think the bm have at least a good chance against archi. Against my 2. lost I do not believe I could done more the cards were not in my favor some times it is what it is. In the end I had a blast to play at the event it is always a pleasure to go to the trolls of the realm. I would appreciate to play against a necromancer to look how Piper and screaming skull would have worked. If I have to change some cards I would cut the screaming skull and add a flaming sword the +1 dmg would have been very nice, I played trinked hammer for a long time but I think it is now Importen to have the +1 permanently on board and not floating around some minions over a couple of turns, the other thing I would like to play 2 disenchants in the main deck the los against the sphere was devastating.

Jack was good but only for his stealth Piper have done some work but I swap it for a cage. I do not need to control the 1 power minions and a well timed cage with a flame sword are so much cards so I try this out.


30.06.26

the list is cast in concert now and was submitted to the Trolls of the realm the host of sorcery fest in leuwaarden Netherlands. I tinker a bit with flex spots and ratios but I think this is my list. The Biggest change that I made on recommendation from count Tolstoy is to add sleep and dodgeroll. Dodgeroll is free movement and dmg denile. decks.name: 🎉#1 Ironclad @ GenCon 2026🎉
decks.primer:
Technically this deck went 3-3 on paper because the event was cancelled early due to a tornado warning. But I played my opponent out and it was clear to both of us that I was going to win that match. So, in my mind, this deck went 4-3!


UPDATE:

Going to add a quick primer to this one, because this deck is getting more attention and I'm bored at work. But for a more thorough breakdown, look at my older "Trench Warfare" deck primer. It's slightly out of date, but most of it still holds true. It goes over site placement and mulligans.


Since GenCon, I've gone to 2 Cornerstones and secured winning records (4-2 and 3-2). Feeling confident for November! I've made a bunch of changes event since GenCon, but I think I'll wait until after AotR to post my current deck list. Unless I make a video on it.



COMMON ERRORS:


  • [[Ironclad]] reduces the damage you take. This means that when something says you lose life, you take the full effect and lose that life. This includes damage done to sites, because striking a site causes life loss, not direct damage to your avatar.


  • [[Golden Harp]] does not have to be equipped to work. It says nearby, meaning you can play it to an ally site and have it sit there. This is good for spreading out your defensive pieces.


  • [[Makeshift Barricade]] damage does not add up between actions. They have to do the damage to break it all at once or not at all.


  • Do not stack all your artifacts on one site if you can help it. One [[dispel]] will destroy of your whole defense.


  • DO NOT put a minion on your site if you are under a [[Makeshift Barricade]]!!!! They will be able to attack / damage the minion and break the barricade without your damage reduction. Just 3 damage will break the barricade.



STAPLE CARDS:


[[Blasted Oak]]:

This counters [[Dispel]] / [[Disenchant]], [[Swap]], [[Lightning Bolt]], etc. To put the effect a little more simply: Anything that targets (Spell OR Ability) HAS to target either Blasted Oak, It's Site / Location, or another artifact / minion at it's site or location. In that order. This still works even if it's buried. In fact, it works better, because you can still force a [[Dispel]] or [[Disenchant]] to target this site without it doing anything to the Oak itself.


If you are on Death's Door and trying to prevent your [[Makeshift Barricade]] from being [[Swap]]ed, you might want to keep a minion or another artifact on the site that you don't mind losing, just to prevent them from swapping you barricade and oak. With a minion on the site, they will be forced to select both the minion and the oak for both targets. Just keep in mind, this works both ways.


If the Blasted Oak is too far away from your home site and they have [[dispel]], they can just move away from the blasted oak until it's more than 2 steps away, and then target your site. You'll need to balance this distance problem with threats like [[Craterize]].


[[Makeshift Barricade]]:

This protects you from all damage, and only is destroyed after taking 3 or more damage. This effect happens when you take damage, meaning it happens after you lower the damage by 2. That means that your opponent needs to do 5 or more damage in one instance of damage to break the barricade. The damage DOES NOT add up between attacks or magics. So this cannot be broken with an [[Arcane Barrage]] or anything like that. Very hard for most decks to deal with. Then, even if they break the barricade, they have to have a follow-up to finish you off.


[[Golden Harp]]:

Almost self-explanatory. The harp makes all strikes nearby it deal 2 or less damage. You take 2 less damage. This means you take no damage from strikes. Now, you will still lose life from strikes on your sites, but they will be lowered to 2 life lost while nearby the harp. Because the effect is nearby, YOU DO NOT HAVE TO HOLD THE HARP TO GET THE EFFECT. This means you want to try to play it nearby if you can get away with that, to prevent your opponent from taking out all your defensive pieces at once with a single disenchant.


[[Gnome Hollows]]:

Amazing site. Putting it as your home site is good against water decks that have access to [[Ruler of Thul]] or [[Polar Explorers]]. It's also good as a home site against decks with lots of airborne minions. When going against earth and / or fire, though, you'll want to put it in front of you when you're making the M. This blocks any minions from entering your home site. If both can be Gnome Hollows; that's amazing! Throw down a [[Tragedy Worrywart]], [[Blasted Oak]], and have yourself a nice tea party to pass the time.


[[Mobbed Court]]:

This site has won me a lot of games. I have taken away upwards of 12 life from an opponent over the course of the game with 2 of these out. You will maybe lose, like, 3-5 life a game from these. But opponents seem to be less conservative with their unique picks.

decks.name: Aquaphile - GenCon 2026
decks.primer:
The main idea for this deck is to build an advantage on the board by getting 2-for-1s and 3-for-1s (snowball, Atlantean fate, etc.) and having powerful minions that are not so easily removed.


Mulligans:

Some of our toughest matchups are against aggro decks, so try to mulligan for a defensive site. Innsmouth dock, river rapids, and maelstrom are almost always useful to maneuver minions. This can be especially helpful in the long run with omphaloses, as they it enables them to attack next turn. If playing against a deathspeaker or imposter, mulligan hard for bureau, as it instantly makes the game much more difficult for them. If playing against flamecaller, archimago, or another avatar that deals with their own cemetery, do the same for mortuary. As for spells, it’s very important that you play something on turn three, so mulligan hard for that. Playing something on turn two is less significant, but if playing aggro I would recommend going for a winter nymph, as it is solid defense against their charge. You play it, and walk it over to a place where it doesn’t affect you.


Various ideas:

If you are in a situation where it is turn four, and you could draw a site to play something, or you could draw a spell, I would suggest taking the site. This deck likes to try to get high amounts of mana relatively quickly, or at least up to six (highest mana cost of a card). If you ever feel like you could have a nice play with snowball, ice lance, or something similar, go for it! As long as you stay in a body of water, it should turn out ok. If playing against a control deck, I would strongly advise you build up a small number of minions, and then all attack the same site. While this seems counterintuitive, if you then flood the site, it will make the removal of your minions much harder for your opponent. Of course if they are playing water then this is a bad play, but if not, it usually works. I would just like to note that while the above info is generally good advice, there are definitely times when you should not do these things, so make sure to think for yourself!


Not-so-frequently-asked-questions:

Q. Why ice lance, and not something like ice shards?

A. I find that they are pretty similar, but given the avatar you can usually make good use of it. It also is a death blow for ironclad, which shards is not.

Q. Why AoW for that matter?

A. Most water minions don’t actually have submerge, so waveshaper isn’t as good, but I really like the ability to flood a site. It makes pirate ships and stoor worm way better. Also, the teleporting ability makes getting death blows ridiculously easy. I’ll sometimes go a whole game without using it once, get the death blow with the avatar, and feel like “yep, that’s worth it.” I also find it fun to play an avatar that is slightly subpar, because winning is more satisfying.

Q. No aino or captain?

A. One of the main issues I was facing was the courts, so I tried to minimize the elites and uniques. That’s also the purpose of acid rain.

Q. What does aquaphile mean?

A. *sigh* Didn’t feel like taking two seconds to look that up, did you? It means a person who loves water.


Thanks so much for taking the time to read this, and if you play the deck, I hope you enjoy!

decks.name: 2026 August | Mid-range Earth-Fire Sorcerer
decks.primer:
BLUF: (F) Aggro + (E) Control = Fun


Goal: is to get to (6)-(7) mana to stabilize then spam 2 beefy minions a turn.


# Deck Breakdown


## Minions

Depending on opponent and board state, can tune your play style to be more aggro or control-ly.


Lower cost minions will:

  • put combat pressure with Deathrite abilities [[Kettletop Leprechaun]] or [[Pookas]],
  • put life pressure with charge minions [[Saracen Raiders]] or [[Redcap Powries]]
  • control [[Arjaro Exorcist]], [[Vile Imp]], [[Root Spider]]


High cost minions are for stabilizing because of their board wipe tendencies, a la [[Death Dealer] or [[Balor of the Evil Eye]]


## Magics

Magics are more control-oriented, but I'm thinking of removing [[Gift of the Serpent]], I usually didn't need the draw. May depend on the meta if you find yourself getting more and more 4-power minions on enemy side, but combo of the 3-power Charge minions or control spiders, should be sufficient. Would definitely add 1x [[Blaze of Glory]] . And potentially [[Ruby Core]] and [[Onyx Core]],


## Artifact

Really hoping to get [[River of Blood]] early, so no need for but even if not, we either stabilize with [[Key to the City]] or drop a big guy with [[Four Waters of Paradise]].

[[Torrid Omphalos]] is for that third minion drop if you find yourself having more mana. 3 minion turns are nice.


## Auras

I like the [[Crusade]] even if I have less (E) minions. Very useful for spider plays to control, while you stabilize.


## Sites

[[Boulevard of Bones]] is just fun and allows you to put some pressure.

[[Imperial Road]] for ramping

Other than that, nothing too different.


## Collection

Just put something quickly together. Most susceptible to change.


# Playstyle Breakdown


Just put us much pressure as possible with your minions, in that your opponent has to answer them.

Control/remove 3-power threats ASAP, you won't be able to stabilize fast enough if they're not answered

Once stabilized, you're good to go.


Because of that, I usually wouldn't even do [[Morgana Le Fay]] on turn 3. I'd want to cast something form her hand that same turn

decks.name: Muddy Godzilla (Top Waveshaper Gen Con 2026)
decks.primer:
First I want to shout out everyone who helped make the deck possible.


@Ianm for coming up with the concept

@vitaminyon for testing the deck on TTS constantly 

@b_2_3_n and @ZenatheShadow for keeping me on [[Waveshaper]] after all this time 


This deck wouldn't exist without you guys coming up with ideas, testing them, and talking about them with me.


The deck is a mud midrange deck, balancing between good relatively early pressure, and a slower defensive grind. The idea was to have a deck hardened vs the new Court sites, that was proactively good into the unknown meta of Gen Con. Lets go over some of the cards.


[[Autumn Unicorn]], [[Lugbog Cat]], [[Order of the Sacred Oak]], [[Sacred Stag]] all have really good stats for their cost. They're able to provide solid offensive pressure vs slower decks, or "bigger" defensive bodies vs faster aggressive decks. They're sort of the raw backbone of the deck. There isn't too much to say about these minions other then that. [[Order of the Sacred Oak]] stops your opponent from blowing up you sites which is a bonus.


I'm sure everyone knows how good [[Pudge Butcher]] is. He demands respect from your opponent, able to drag them into the water and where you can initiate the beat down without overextending. He has a couple cool advantages in water decks though. [[Riptide]], [[Coy Nixie]], [[Undertow]], [[Rift Valley]], and [[River Rapids]] are all able to move the otherwise immobile minion into better position or slide an enemy in front of the projectile.


[[Giant Shark]] is very good. With all the forced movement in the deck, and the [[Waveshaper]]'s ability to extend the body of water, its easy to get shark coverage over the whole board. This can stop aggression in its tracks or suddenly bring an opponent to Deaths Door. [[Coy Nixie]], [[Undertow]], [[Riptide]], [[River Rapids]], and [[Pudge Butcher]] can all force your opponents Avatar to move into the water and be attacked by the Shark. In the case of [[Pudge Butcher]], the opponent will be bitten for each site they move through on their way to the Butcher. Playing minions into the Sharks body of water will result in them immediately getting attacked. This is great at stopping your opponent from playing minions to contest the realm, but can prevent you from playing minions of your own if you aren't careful.


[[Assimilator Snail]] is an underrated card in my opinion. Suddenly transforming into a 4th copy of [[Giant Shark]] or [[Pudge Butcher]], becoming a [[Coy Nixie]] when you need one, changing all the math out of nowhere with [[Ruler of Thul]], turning into [[Lilith]] for a funny flip, or just being the best minion in your opponents cemetery. It also banishes the dead minion so that's upside.


I was pretty medium on [[Archangel Raphael]] going into the event, but after the event I love this card. The Airborne, Ward, and 4 power makes him very obnoxious to interact with. Airborne especially is not something water really has access to and the mobility for both offense and defense feels really good. The Genesis is mostly a fun bonus used to Ward you, but it can be a clean way to finish an opponent who's too close and on Deaths Door.


I've brought up [[Coy Nixie]] in some of the other card sections. She's a minion who's power shines in the context of other stuff. Moving units for Shark attacks. Moving units in front of [[Pudge Butcher]]. Stacking minions in one spot for your Avatar to lockdown or to be [[Stormy Seas]]'d. Pulling stuff into [[Thin Ice]] or [[Troll Bridge]]. Tapping units that were going to block. Overextending your opponents units to be attacked. Breaking Wards for free. I'm sure I'm missing plays, the list of stuff this stupid card does is very long.


Why play [[Shellycoat]] when [[Shield Maidens]] makes all nearby allies [[Shellycoat]]. This lets your minions battle your opponents without trading, and forces your opponent to over commit damage to remove yours. Getting incremental advantage like this is critical since the [[Waveshaper]] has no built in card advantage.


I feel like people ask me about [[The Green Knight]] a lot. Yes, [[The Green Knight]] is fantastic. The ability enables so much more then you might expect on first read. In [[Waveshaper]] he piles adjacent minions into one space for you to use your ability on, or stack everyone onto a [[Thin Ice]] to be drowned. Its also a forced move for [[Giant Shark]]. It can move enemies into weird positions making them unable to block future attacks. The strike on death hits nearby enemies, everyone forgets this ability. Because of his 3/7 stat line and the strike on death, he's able to kill 4 adjacent 3 power enemies. The strike can also clean up larger minions that survived initially fighting him, or hit the enemy Avatar.


[[Overflow]] is an awesome card. Getting to 5-6 mana so you can start using your Avatar ability without thinking is very important and [[Overflow]] lets that happen early. Playing [[Overflow]] on turn 3 is a clean play you should aim for. You'll want to be careful though. There is nothing worse then hitting a land site off the [[Overflow]]. I recommend having a water site in your hand before you cast the spell, just to be safe and keep your options open. [[Kettletop Leprechaun]] can enable this without having to draw a site for turn too.


I guess now that I'm talking about sites, [[Ersatz Platz]] is a cool site. A pocket [[Babbling Brook]], or [[Undertow]] is very clutch. It can also grab [[Fertile Earth]] to cleanly hit the Earth threshold. At Gen Con I also ran [[Mudslide]] and [[Quagmire]] in the collection, but I plan on cutting those for more [[Toolbox]] spells. The cases for those cards was just too narrow and I'd rather have other things. [[Ersatz Platz]] also has a fun interaction with mana. Sites generate mana at the start of your turn and when they enter play, which means [[Ersatz Platz]] makes mana at the start of your turn and the site you replace it with will also make its mana. Just know that it works that way. 


I want to talk about a few cards that I played at Gen Con that I was less impressed with. [[Acid Rain]] was in the deck to help with Courts, but the deck was built around Exceptionals so I was not punished by Courts in a serious way. Because of that [[Acid Rain]] always felt kind of lame. Its literally a good card, but its probably coming out for something else. [[Abaddon Succubus]] is another card I've been low on lately. She's great at cleaning up aggro boards and giving you some life back, but she only pulls adjacent minions. I've really been feeling not being able to hit nearby or Avatars. She doesn't have Submerge either so she can't safely pull stuff onto [[Thin Ice]]. Being Elite means you get hit by Courts too. [[Mariner's Curse]] is awesome but playing 1 felt weird. I'm either going to cut the 1, or go up to 3.


Ok that's enough rambling. If anyone got this far, and still has any thoughts or questions, feel free to comment. I also hang out in the Sorcerers Summit Discord, specifically the Waveshaper Cove channel. We talk about [[Waveshaper]] entirely too much, and its where the deck was brewed.

decks.name: GenCon 2026 - Limited Grand Contest Finals (Draft) - 2nd place
decks.primer:
Draft deck for the GenCon 2026 Limited Grand Contest.


I first picked Barging Barghest into Flame Strike, but the fire cards dried up rather quickly, but I started wheeling aggressive air minions so leaned air/fire aggro.


Pack 2 picked up some powerful red minions (Greater Blood Demon and Lord of Destruction) which solidified us into air/fire.


Pack 3 - Michael P passed me Harbinger and said no way you're playing this right? i initially passed it, but it came alll the back around and i last picked Harbinger. Turned it around and immediately sleeved it up to Michael's chagrin ;)



Game 1 (Quarterfinals): Joe G

Harbinger high-roll'ed with a portal on Joe's 2nd site. Turn 2 Earl of the Ivory Towers placed a lot of pressure on Joe. He ended up taking a lot of damage and losing a couple ordinaries to the Earl, until he drew a Silent Hills to turn off the Earl and trade for it. Brutal game for Joe.


Game 2: (Semifinals): Julian R

Harbinger mid-roll'ed with a portal on Julian's corner which allowed 2x Forsaken to start charging in early (Turn 1 forsaken, Turn 2 Bats; Turn 2 Forsaken + another 2-drop. Just a crazy start). Julian had The Void on his home site which actually wombo-combo'ed with my forsaken. He was in a very hard spot, but was able to battle back with larger more impactful minions and some 2:1's. Harbinger ran out of gas with Julian at 4 life, but were able to squeak out 4 more damage and get him to door. I had 2 very good cards in hand (Flame Strike and Zeppelin), but only 1 fire threshold, so I started drawing sites with Harbinger instead of moving up to try and knock on his door. Ended up drawing air sites and started to get worried. By this time, Julian has KO'ed most of my minons and stabilized the board. My life quickly ticked down from 20 to DD.


Finally i drew a fire site, played it and passed the turn. Julian surrounded my avatar with multiple minions and... passed the turn. Luckily, his minions were tapped so Harbinger could step up 1 site and Flame Strike his avatar on the other side of the board. Crazy game and I really want to give Julian credit for how he recovered from my crazy start.


OK onto the finals against xNattu. The last time he played he stomped my face in. I'm spooked.


Game 3 (Finals): Sean D (xNattu)

On Camera.

I have the play.

Harbinger rolls 2 bad portals, then hits a great spot. My 2nd site.

I have the actual nuts. Den of Evil. Portal on 2nd site. Greater Blood Demon. mull 1 site.

Turn 1: site. pass

Turn 2: Den of evil. Cast Greater Blood Demon (6 power) for 2 mana. Pass the turn.

Turn 3: Nattu is on full defense mode here and is playing sites on the back row. I play my 3rd site in his zone. Move up demon. Cast Hollow One (4 power) for 2 mana. I have 2 ways to kill his 2drop mortal, so i feel confident that i can disable the Hollow One quickly. Pass the turn. (10-power on Turn 2 in limited!)

Turn 4: Nattu has a 2drop mortal with ward and 3drop undead. Demon attacks the mortal & he allows it to pop the ward. Then I cast Ravenous Werewolf (4mana on my portal) to attempt to kill his mortal to wake up the Hollow One. He correctly blocks with an undead to trade. Hollow One is still disabled, but i'm feeling good. the Demon is still wreaking havoc on his side of the board. Pass to Nattu and drops his own Elite bomb which completed FLIPS THE GAME. Hyperparasite on his home site. Pick up and disable my demon. Hollow One is still disabled. Pass to me.

Turn 5-7: No minions in hand. A flame strike which can't kill hyperparasite. Full on panic sets in. Cycle a Gift and tank for about 6min after drawing another 3-dmg removal spell. This is essentially the end of the game.... pass to nattu. he double teams to kill the disabled demon. then kills my disabled hollow one. i land an Earl and a couple willing tributes and HOPE to draw witching hour to pump my earl then untap earl with the tributes... but alas the game is over. GG Nattu.

His list and game report are here: https://curiosa.io/decks/cmsde663u000c0akqcrl42bri?tab=primer


(After watching the replay, I think playing out the Accursed desert on turn 1 may have lost me the match... That would have been very helpful in killing the warded mortal and waking up my hollow one Sooner.... Alas I didn't sandbag it... Played it instead of a twilight bloom as I typically hold them to help with threshold costs. In Retrospect the bloom on 1 and desert on 3 might hang swung the game my way. Welp def need more practice!)


I had a great time and am so happy to have this story :D


Nattu and I are signing each other's Elite bombs (hyperparasite and greater blood demon) and exchanging them. Looking forward to a rematch at AotR.

"We do not command fire. Ngamahu lends it, and Hinekora returns it." - Lavianga, advisor to Kaom - Path of Exile

6th Place Gen Con - #1 [[Necromancer]] - 08/01/26


It was a great pleasure to participate in the 2026 Gen Con Grand Contest, let alone finish in the top 8.


When a [[Sorcerer]] sees a [[Necromancer]] at the table, thoughts of water always rise to the surface. The water Necromancer deck pioneered by [[@Ceej]] still inspires and terrifies players to this day, and at Gen Con I hoped to do the same... but with fire (F).


During the Grand Contest, over half of my opponents remarked they would have played or mulliganed differently had they known how different my list was. And while my hopes of winning the Contest were washed away after Round 6 as water splashed down from the convention center ceiling, I am still happy to present an off-meta Necromancer build that is as surprising as it is explosive.


SPELLBOOK: The minion package is fairly standard for a mono fire deck. It includes 18 Exceptional minions with 3 Towns to help get them out a little quicker. Many of these minions are chosen simply for their Charge effect, to get as much damage on the board as soon as possible.


  • My favorite inclusion is the [[Siege Giant]], which can throw a weaker ally here through the air to a nearby location. Throw your [[Necromancer]] up and start making [[Skeleton]]s on your opponent's Sites. Throw [[Sacred Scarabs]] into position and get ready to [[Detonate]]. Equip a [[Torshammar Trinket]] and throw another [[Siege Giant]] for best results.


  • [[Detonate]] is the MVP of this deck. At (1) mana this allows the potential for any of your artifacts or minions (including [[Skeleton]]s) to be a localized [[Minor Explosion]]. For (3) mana, summon [[Sacred Scarabs]] and [[Detonate]] them to deal 6 damage. Use [[Betrayal]] to take control of enemy minions and blow them up as well. Use your artifacts with impunity against decks that run [[Swap]], and make them think twice about stealing your [[Ring of Morrigan]] or [[Poisonous Dagger]].


  • [[Gift of the Serpent]] and [[Poisonous Dagger]] both give your minions Lethal, which helps make efficient trades. Give Lethal to [[Colicky Dragonettes]], [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]], or even a [[Skeleton]]. Combine either with a [[Blaze of Glory]] for a spectacular board wipe.


  • [[Blaze of Glory]] into [[Warp Spasm]] is one of the most potent combos in Sorcery. With a 4 or 5 power minion, this combo can deal 16-20 damage in one turn.


  • [[Lava Flow]] sends [[Root Spiders]], [[Coy Nixies]], and other bottom-dwelling pets back where they belong: the cemetery. [[Siege Giant]]s and [[War Horse]]s can also position us to cast [[Lava Flow]] in the perfect line.


  • [[Chains of Prometheus]] allows you to control the enemy board state by forcing our opponent to tap their strongest minion. This is a symmetrical effect that also punishes you, but with the creation of new [[Skeleton]]s every turn, you should be able to power through.


  • Play a game of hot potato with your [[Rolling Boulder]]! Tap an unanswered [[Skeleton]] to roll a boulder from your opponents site, removing threats and causing damage along the way. Then summon a minion with Charge to push it again on the very same turn. If they summon a minion in hopes of rolling your boulder, [[Detonate]] it in their face like a Saturday morning cartoon.


ATLAS: Sites have been chosen carefully to counter opposing strategies, especially against earth and water strategies. Your mulligan will depend on what Avatar is seated across from you at the table.


  • Deserts are key for dealing with wards and controlling enemy [[Necromancer]]s.


  • [[Mobbed Court]], [[Vindictive Nation]], and [[River of Blood]] allow you to deal some incidental damage while preventing enemy healing.


  • [[Kor Crematory]] is great against [[Archimago]] and [[Deathspeaker]] decks. Trying to mulligan for this card when facing either of these Avatars is a good idea.


  • [[Sinkhole]]s can disrupt the opponent's early game, providing you a few more turns to safely produce [[Skeleton]]s.


  • [[Hellmouth]] and [[Vesuvius]] are ways to deal with burrowed or submerged minions. While [[Hellmouth]] serves as [[Earthquake]] protection for your [[Skeleton]]s, it also allows you to use a [[Toolbox]]to cast a [[Vile Imp]] underground.


  • [[River of Flame]] allows you to use [[Disintegrate]], [[Immolation]], or [[Betrayal]] to target burrowed minions. Try to place this on a different row or column than your Avatar's or near the potential underground threats.


  • [[Wuthering Heights]] is the only air site in the deck. How could you not love "[[Siege Giant]]: The Site?" It's especially good when you place it close to your [[Necromancer]]'s [[Skeleton]] production line.


  • If you do not plan on using courts or the many Unique utility sites feel free to check out this variation of the deck that uses [[Peasant Revolt]]: https://curiosa.io/decks/cmnajthf800n404l2lj6um5wx?tab=view

decks.name: Heavy Artillery Token Sorcerer [20th place at Ropecon 2026)
decks.primer:
Play style


Token spam is the name of the game. The core of the deck is Border Militia: cast it early, cast it often. Recast it with Skeleton Mage. Get more tokens from villages, Boulevard of Bones, and Guards! Defend your tokens with Shield Maidens.


Use your tokens defensively. Their main job is to slow down your opponent and make their single target removal inefficient.


There is a subtheme of ranged minions. They are also supposed to be defensive, restricting your opponent's movement and attack paths. I'm not sure if they belong here or not.


Wincon


The heavy artillery (Trebuchet and Catapult) is the wincon. You want to get to 5 mana, and then start double drawing to feed the Trebuchet. The artillery can kill problematic minions but is also difficult to avoid damage to your opponent.


Use cards like Tactical Move and Blink to position your tokens so they can use the artillery.


King of the Realm is either 7 damage from the artillery, or a wincon of his own if the game goes long.

Ended up 4-3 with this list because of misplays, but other than that the deck was indeed very strong.


Thoughts:

+ [[Lord Of Lies]] got cut due to the errata. No regrets.

+ [[Onyx Core]] was added to increase the chance of drawing core turn 0/1. I won every game with it in the starting hand (2/4 wins)

+ [[Kelp Cavern]] is quite clutch if you mulligan 1-ofs like [[Drown]] or [[Ice Lance]], but I'd prefer a 13th river over it (i.e. [[Winter River]]).

+ [[Babbling Brook]] really helped with the aggro matchups, at the cost of [[River of Blood]]. Given that I faced 4 decks with [[Divine Healing]], that choice was really bad, but I didn't mind either because it won me a game so it was worth it.

+ [[Silence]] was a really versatile tech card to bail you out of a lot of bad situations, but really hard to use without hurting your game plan as well.

decks.name: HELLAMENTALIST - 3rd in Grand Contest Vegas 2026 - “All The Best”
decks.primer:
** NOTE!!** 07/17/2026 - With the change to Lord of Lies, I would either go MUCH heavier on water, or I would remove it entirely. Probably remove it.


MIT Opensource license - use as is, modify, commercialize this deck list. A common modification would be to add more to the higher end of the curve for more staying power if you don't knock somebody out immediately. Also more blinks and flanking maneuvers, if so inclined.


Over the past several months, I have played numerous games of various mixes of [[Elementalist]]. I have played with high threshold bombs in multiple thresholds like [[Morgana Le Fay]] and [[Mesmerism]], heavy "[[Ghoul]]" sites like [[Forsaken Crypt]], [[Assorted Animals]] with numerous 1 cost ordinary beasts and [[Hamlet]], I have tried all of the knights, and multiple variations of light exposure to different mixes of double threshold.


NOTE: For a lower cost version, substitute [[Ring of Morrigan]] with an additional [[Blink]]. It was a last moment change before the tournament to help deal with wards, and shore up the bad matchup against (F)(F)(F) Fire [[Pathfinder]] (F)(F)(F). Additionally, Colour out of Space and Tintagel are great, but not hyper impactful. You could probably get the proper threshold mix by replacing them and 1 village with dual threshold sites. Everything else is either fairly reasonable or downright cheap for cards (I think).


This is the best mix of all of the ideas that I have come across so far, and with the 3rd place finish at Grand Contest in Vegas, 2026, I am not sure that I will explore further ideas on my own. Now, for exposure to the main concept, it is simple, but also effective:


This deck is build to rip the face off of the opponent in a burst of higher than curve minions with extra mana. It is hard to beat a turn 2 or turn 3 [[King Arthur]] and I have yet to lose when that happens. Or the old turn 3 [[Pudge Butcher]] followed by [[Sinkhole]]. Need to move pudgie? Invest in a [[War Horse]] or [[Blink]]. Now, I will cover the reasons for each card, mostly, and in some order of importance:


Best card in the deck - [[Gift of the Wolf]]

Ramp Sites - City of Souls, Glass, and Traitors. - Go fast. Don't worry about your opponent using [[City of Traitors]], they won't have time.

Ramp Sites - Towers, Dark, Lone, Gothic, Merlin's. - Go fast.

Ghoul Sites - [[Peculiar Port]] & [[Forlorn Keep]] - With 5, you ofter get to play a 3 power minion you didn't need to draw on turn 2-5.

Villages (7) - Pile on the early aggression, early foot soldiers combined with the other better than curve minions adds up.


[[Root Spider]] Hate - This horrible little jerk can just win an opponent the game. We are looking to do quick and persistent damage early, and all [[Root Spiders]] must die. -- [[Geyser]], [[Silver Bullet]], [[The Black Plague]], [[Apply Alkahest]], [[Kingdom of Agatha]]


Above curve powered minions - [[Bosk Troll]], [[Autumn Unicorn]], [[King Arthur]], [[Pudge Butcher]], [[Sir Perceval]]


Anti-Sites, NO DEFENSE FOR YOU! - [[Sinterfee]], [[Sinkhole]]


Busted Cards - [[Atlantean Fate]], [[Book of the Dead]] - We get to cast nearly everything of our opponents too, [[Lady Iseult]], [[Sir Bors the Younger]], [[Gargantula]], [[Sir Gawain]], [[Lord of Lies]], [[Grapple Shot]], [[Whirling Blades]]


The great glue, cards that play their roles exceptionally well and we are nearly always glad to see, [[Daperyll Vampire]], [[Onslaught]], [[Blink]], [[Sir Perceval]], [[Sir Lamorak]], [[Doctor Demetrius]] (a ward or two will quickly secure a win given the likelihood of being ahead), [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]], [[War Horse]], [[Arjaro Exorcist]], [[Sir Tom Thumb]], [[Silver Bullet]], [[Wizard's Den]]



------

A few notes on choices. It seems like 3 [[Onslaught]] and 3 [[Whirling Blades]] would be optimal, but I had plenty of experience with all 6 and I just drew them too much and didn't have anything great to do on the board. Additionally, when I went from 0 Geyser to 3 Geyser, I found that when I need Geyser, I need it, and it would be better to have 4 with [[Silver Bullet]]. I also found that I would sit there with Silver Bullet in play and nothing great to do with it. So, I put 1 each of Onslaught and Whirling Blades into the collection.


Why not any double fire threshold? You get great cards like [[Balor of the Evil Eye]], [[The Great Famine]], and [[Sir Agravaine]]. Well, when you run double fire threshold in addition to the others (and I need earth/air, and love the water), then the adjustment to sites reduces ramp sites from 6 to 2. And it dilutes the deck enough that it suffers significantly.


Why not [[Archangel Michael]]? Well, I played him. Generally this deck will draw one site for turn, and I would want to have significantly more earth sites. More like 60-63% to be able to play Michael if you get him, and that skews the available mixes on sites to require more dual threshold sites which in turn reduces the sites that can either give you a Foot Soldier, or ramp, or a [[Ghoul]] type of minion.


Build the deck, and go forth and smash.

decks.name: Dragonlord (Summer 2026 1.0 with Primer)
decks.primer:
With this dragonlord list we are doing the thing and embracing the value that the Dragonlord cards have to offer. Your intended "Champion" is Caelestis giving you an option to power out big dragons for 3 mana on early turns. Of all of the abilites that are on these unique dragons this is the one that felt like it was always going to be worth it. Maybe in the future we will play with being the Fire Dragonlord or going with Corvus and playing for mobility and removal but for this build I just want to play the big boys and let them eat.


The deck is demanding on both cost and threshold, as such we are running the full core package and stone, stone is tenuous and may get cut if it feels unnecesary but with all of the single mana spells in the deck the potential to get 2 or even 3 mana in a turn is within reason. In addition to the cores we have the Cradle and the Shrine to facilitate playing dragons, and the 4 Waters to power out a big chungus early, it is entirely possible to power out two 6 or 7 cost dragons in the same turn as early as turn 5 with the 4 Waters and the Caelestis ability. On the threshold side we are running the full package of multi-colored sites, 3 ofs of all of the dual lands except Lighthouse as water and air are the least intensly needed elements in the deck, especially water. we also have a 1 of for each of the 2 threshold lands for each element besides water. Obviously if we hit the Lair and don't see it destroyed we are living good but it can't be counted on, so we have as much fixing and threshold diversity as we can play.


We are also running the full toolbox and bullet kit with a diverse array of utility cards in the sideboard to use. Zap is a the best Death's Door spell in the game, Divine Healing lets you stabilize, Critical Strike lets you come back with some massive damage, Teleport to move into an advantageous positions, Mimic is hilarous artifact removal, Firebreathing is flavorful damage, Bury is efficient removal, and Scavenging Fiend can bring back your core or ring, or give you a second crack at 4 Waters. With the only other artifact being Ring, because its Ring.


As for the minions we are running most of the dragons in the game, I'll talk about what is not here and why below, for now lets talk about what is in. Pit vipers give you an annoying trade to guard your sites from big hits during the early game with Settlers are there for the ramp. The Mortal ladies are here for their unique abilites, Princess gets you fixing, ramp, or ring (whichever you are lacking at that time), Iseult lets your dragons have another life, Thaïs let's you setup a finishing round by taking their turn to run their stuff into your big boys, and Viv lets you have a second use of casting a 7 mana dragon for 3, not bad. The Simulacrums are here to either be a big chungus late in the game, a utility creature when called for, or in a crazy world they can make a second Vivian giving you up to 3 cracks at putting out discounted dragons, it would cost 9 mana but later in the game that is not impossible and with Pendragon Legacy and Kings Council we can live the dream for a 3 dragon turn in a long, grindy game. We also have 2 of the best utility creatures in the game in Nixie and Spider. They are used to lock a site down, Nixie pulls them in, Spider locks them down then the Falling Star lands a friggin dragon on their head, just be ready to move the spider away before the Dragon lands so that it is not disabled when it enters.


Why no Vant Draconis? Not enough of a body of water to operate in to get the drowing effect over and over. This makes him a 3 threshold, do nothing where there are just going to be better things to do most of the time.

Why no Kairos? This is more of a flavor card with 16 and couting FAQs that your opponents are going to have to be up to speed on to use him "correctly". Even when he is used his effect is not objectively positive unless you build around his ability, usually with site manipulation or token production. Most of all tho, its slow and a little rude to ask you opponent to just play your little side game. In my home pod I might think about using him, but in a deck that I would play against anyone I'm not bringing the librarian.

Why no Moonsong? He really needs wolves to be "worth it". I didn't see the upside to having an overcosted 1 power creature in the deck that will only present value when the draw lines up in your favor, if there is something that makes Gray Wolf tokens in the future I'll consider it, for now its just an airboune 3 power for 3, not "bad" but no additional upside. Its possible that I could run him if that 3 mana slot ends up being more useful than I am currently assuming it is.


The magic lineup Pendragon Legacy and King's Council are obvious upside for how greedy the deck is in terms of using uniques, Tithe might get swapped for Browse, Lifewish is there for games when an aggro deck just gets out in front of you and you need to stabilize. Its also funny to cast Lifewish, pop a toolbox to cast critical strike, give Talamh Dreig double damage and let him 20 to 0 your opponent. Lol. Raise dead is value with so many 4+ targets to bring back, Infiltrate is versitile removal with upside, Disintegrate gives you the ability to banish a pesky minion, and Pollimorph is even more mana efficient removal.


We try to ramp into dragons, use the Caelestis ability to power out big dragons early and just generally try to out value our opponent with bigger threats. We may need to focus more on drawing cards to be able to keep the value train going, I'm going to be mindful of the variance with games where I get to cast a big King's Council and ones where I don't.

decks.primer:
"Evil, Fliers and Ranged, OH MY!"


The TLDR:


Evil:

  • Vile Imp, Redmayne Hyena, Spore Spouts and Desecrate. Do the math.
  • You know who loves Desecrated Ground? Evil minions. What's better than a 5 power Legion of Gall? A 6 power Legion of Gall.


Fliers:

  • We've got 14 fliers and over half of them are 4+ power and either gain us life, wreck our opponent's Collection, or just cause a friggin headache!


Ranged:

  • A playset of Stygian Archers and Skirmishers of Mu? Yes. And I'd play more if I could!
  • Shout out to MTR Joseph (the one and only Realm Eater pilot in the Constructed Championship at SCRCON) for enlightening me on how disgusting Skirmishers can actually be. To be continued in full primer...


Ideal Early Game Plays:

  • T1 Tower > Forsaken into a T3 Desecrate to mess with our opponent's Affinity
  • T2 Spore Spouts > Vile Imp into a T3 Desecrate
  • T3 Jack the Ripper their Aino or Morgana into a T4 Desecrate


omg why does this guy love Desecrate so much...


Desecrate:

  • Think back at games you lost because of a well placed Smokestacks, Thin Ice, Troll Bridge, Bottomless Pit, Perilous Bridge, etc... yea. Desecrate handles that.
  • Buff your minions. Forsaken seems innocent until it hits for 3, Desecrates for 3, and then becomes a 4 power minion. "We have Lugbog Cat at home, sweetie".
  • Timing is everything, though. If you can't Move and Attack with your Evil minion without risking a trade then you're not set up for a Desecrate. But we're piloting AoA baby, oh and we have even more tech for that... stay tuned for the full primer!


Other Spells:

  • Arcane Barrage beats Ward as long as you can pay the minions power + 1. It wreaks havoc on tokens, is nightmare fuel against Imposter and can close out nearly any game thanks to AoA's inherent maneuverability.
  • Browse to hunt for Desecrate... (i know, i have a problem)
  • Disenchant. Because Ring and A. Fate exist.
  • Feast for Crows. F**k Mesmerism. (Both games I've lost to CJ at major events he beat me with Mesmerism... well, and because he's a top-notch player)
  • Grapple Shot and Whirling Blades. I don't need to explain these - but - imagine your opponent plays their Archangel and you've got a Stygian Archers in play with a Trinket and Grapple Shot in hand. You Trinket your Archers, Grapple the Archangel to break ward and Ranged strike for 4 while getting an Allied Skelly to boot. It feels, so, good. Now imagine casting Whirling Blades on your Archers and killing more than one enemy minion to then replace each of them with Allied Skellys? Disgusting. Wait, Skellys are Evil right? Did someone say Desecrate?
  • Infiltrate and Poison Nova: unarguably two of the most impactful Fire spells at the single-Fire threshold level. These two spells are what forced me into splashing fire. Trust me, I hate having to run the castles, Colour and Ruins in place of other Air or utility sites, but I truly believe Infiltrate and Poison Nova are worth it.


Full primer to come...


Cheers and great games to everyone I played at SCRCON 2026!!!

This deck wants to play the [[Payload Trebuchet]] to fling big cost cards into your enemy's face.


To use a Trebuchet you need pairs of cheap minions that you don't mind tapping to use the Weapon instead of attacking. To that end we have lots of [[Foot Soldier (English)]] generation and low cost minions, especially ones that slow down the opponent or protect your cheap minions a little. Lots of the Atlas is focused on stalling and slowing down your opponent until you can potentially cast these cards, in case you don't find your siege Weapons. You also have cost reducers and ramp options to help afford these big cost cards when you can.

decks.name: Silenced Bones - 3rd Place Elemental Series Q1 2026 (Sydney, Australia)
decks.primer:
Silenced Bones is a Necromancer mid-range deck supported by a Beast package and a Silence package.


Silence got a huge buff in Gothic with [[Silent Hills]] (and [[Sister Stefania]]) and I believe the archetype can be a great anti-meta option.


The Silence part of the deck shuts down the majority of the card pool, and manh ability-based archetypes like Ward. It is also the enabler for many parts of the Beast package, and other above curve minions such as [[Pirate Ship]] and [[Dalcean Phalanx]]. [[Silence]] itself is (W), so we include this element in the deck.


(E), on the other hand, is the nature (pun not intended) of the Beast archetype, and it is also the only archetype that works with Silence. The mana efficient minions like [[Sedge Crabs]] become a menace, while [[Pudge Butcher]] can transition between a hook thrower and a 4-cost 5-power demon. [[Assorted Animals]] is a 2+ card advantage for you if [[Haystack]] is not in play.


The general strategy is to pump out skeletons to attack AND defend (Silenced skeletons are great blockers!) using [[Necromancer]] with spare mana whenever possible, while taking favourable trades with above-curve Silenced minions. The deck either overwhelms the board or stalls enough time with Silence and defensive sites like [[Troll Bridge]] and [[Babbling Brook]] for a [[Craterize]] straight to Death's Door, followed by a finisher such as [[Zap]] or [[Ice Lance]].


Peculiar card choices:

  • [[Sir Yvain]] screams BEAST. If you're playing Beast, you should play him.
  • [[Garden of Eden]] is your wincon against any draw-heavy decks like [[Sorcerer]] and [[Deathspeaker]]. HARD MULLIGAN for it (3 sites + scry the sites deck). Otherwise, you'd better pray you out-draw them with [[Algor Omphalos]] or win the game in 5-6 turns (you won't, but you can try!).
  • [[Carrion Beetles]] is the vegetable that everyone refuses to play (graveyard hate) and is searchable via [[Common Sense]] and [[Assorted Animals]] with just (1).
  • [[Porcupine Pufferfish]] is an Ordinary Beast with Lethal for (1) (Don't silence him, let him speak!).
  • [[Harvest Festival]] is essentially a (3) spell for 4 in the form of two 2-power bodies. Very underrated!
  • [[Goat for Azazel]] is another good (1) Beast. You can use Silence to turn off his ability when you need to put him down early.
  • [[The Flood]] is a very good late-game board wipe in this particular deck because we play so many types of minions, letting us keep our board while deleting everything without Submerged (Silence also remove Submerged!).
  • [[Forlorn Keep]] is a 3-power body in the form of a site. Sometimes you may want to play this turn 3 to churn out [[Penitent Knight]], or turn 4 with an extra skelly instead of playing cards from your hand. [[Peculiar Port]] serves similar roles, but having an Evil minion may be disadvantaged in some matchups such as [[Persecutor]] or any [[Consecrated Ground]] users.
  • [[Pebbled Paths]], [[Impenetrable Copse]], and [[Haystack]] are interchangeable depending on your local meta. My local meta loves cards like [[Grapple Shot]] and [[Firebolts]].


Overall, this is a really fun deck to play and learn the basics of the game while being very budget-friendly. The list is kept as-is and may need to be optimised for future tournament plays (for example, [[Sister Stefania]] would be a great inclusion, if I had it...).


Shout out to Dean Gouskos and Allen Thrun for hosting the event and carrying the Sydney community on their backs!

What's so different with [[Magician]] and what makes it the best avatar to pull this combo in the Gothic era?


It's no secret that the effectiveness of this combo is linearly correlated with the Atlas size; the smaller the Atlas, the stronger the combo. We can all agree on this right?

"You have no atlas..."


I rest my case.

decks.name: voidwalk mist harbinger (1st place cornerstone)
decks.primer:
this is my most successful comp deck, currently sitting at a 75% wr on summit across all iterations and the last 4 seasons! for in person prized matches im currently 16-1 :)


mulligan - always try and get 2 of each threshold in your starting hand, or 2 and 1 and then scry the atlas for the other, if going second. aim for forsaken, dreamers, nixies, phantom steeds, stargazers in your opening spells


strategy - the biggest advantage to playing voidwalk is that your minions are difficult to remove! the enemy cant target them, mass remove them, or trade efficiently vs them. this often gives them options like the following:


a) defend sites and wait for an opportunity

b) play sites under voidwalk minions and attempt to kill them off one by one

c) full attack to try and race


this deck can hopefully exploit all three of these options. if its a), we have plenty of time to play stargazer and GMW to outdraw them and overwhelm them. if its b) we can encourage the enemy to play sites in a subpar formation and eventually exploit that by attacking where they cant defend. and if c), we have plenty of defensive sites like thin ice and babbling brook and board wipes like call of the sea and whirling blades to swing the game in our favor!


the best players (assuming they are playing a balanced midrangey deck) tend to choose option C. due to this, its imperative that we plan for a big board wipe! leave a 4 power minion safe in the void to prepare for whirling blades, keep a scatter in hand for a big thin ice push, or turn your brain off and afate them!


as for harbinger itself, versatile movement minions like steed and ophanim + void friendly movement spells like second wind counteract harbinger's positional restriction. a common line is to play phantom steed turn 2 on one of your sites, then something valuable like succubus or sacred stag, pick up with steed, and bring them safely into the void to save for later, as well as adding fuel to stargazer. second wind is preferred over blink as it crosses regional boundaries and has double the range, if cast twice. this allows something like dormant monstrosity that is normally very positionally restricted to survive its first turn in the void and then immediately join the fight!


weaknesses - any deck with more engineless card advantage and tokens like archimago or ramp geo is an uphill battle. eventually they will craterize or onslaught you... gotta play aggressive into those decks and hope for the best. fire aggro can also be super tough if you cant keep a succubus or thin ice nixie alive. battlemage also a bad matchup as they tend to play fewer minions and hit for 3 every turn, or land a huge ruler of thuul combo. best option is to try and race them

"We do not command fire. Ngamahu lends it, and Hinekora returns it." - Lavianga, advisor to Kaom - Path of Exile

1st Place Cornerstone - Dane's Games West Chicago - 06/28/26


Many [[Sorcerer]]s in 2026 have undoubtedly played against a [[Necromancer]]. Maybe you've already written it off as a solved Avatar. Today I would like to present an off-meta Necromancer build that is engaging, explosive, and can be built budget friendly.


As you may know the Necromancer is one of the best Avatars for minion creation and likes to take advantage of that in a myriad of ways. [[Necromancer]]s produce Skeletons, and [[Skeleton]]s produce FEAR. Use these tools to your advantage. This Deck has been designed to work well in the 5-6 mana range and most of the Sites in this deck have been chosen with [[Peasant Revolt]] in mind.


  • Our minion package is fairly standard for a mono fire deck. We use 18 Exceptional minions with 3 Towns to help get them out a little quicker. Many of our minions are chosen simply for their Charge effect, to get as much damage on the board as soon as possible


  • My favorite inclusion is the [[Siege Giant]], which can throw a weaker ally here through the air to a nearby location. Throw your [[Necromancer]] up and start making [[Skeleton]]s on your opponent's Sites. Throw a [[Sacred Scarabs]] into position and get ready to [[Detonate]]. Equip a [[Torshammar Trinket]] and throw another [[Siege Giant]] for best results.


  • [[Detonate]] is the MVP of this deck. At (1) mana this allows the potential for any of your artifacts or minions (including [[Skeleton]]s) to be a localized [[Minor Explosion]]. For (3) mana, summon a [[Sacred Scarabs]] and detonate them to deal 6 damage. Use [[Infiltrate]] and [[Betrayal]] to take control of enemy minions and blow them up as well. Use your artifacts with impunity against decks that run [[Swap]], and make them think twice about stealing your [[Ring of Morrigan]] or [[Poisonous Dagger]].


  • [[Gift of the Serpent]] and [[Poisonous Dagger]] both give our minions Lethal, which helps make efficient trades. Give Lethal to [[Colicky Dragonettes]], [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]], or [[Balor]] for best results. Combine either with a [[Blaze of Glory]] for a spectacular board wipe.


  • [[Chains of Prometheus]] allows us to control the enemy board state by forcing our opponent to tap their strongest minion. This is a symmetrical effect that also punishes you, but with the creation of new [[Skeleton]]s every turn, you should be able to power through.


  • [[Blaze of Glory]] into [[Warp Spasm]] is one of the most potent combos in Sorcery. With a 4 or 5 power minion, this combo can deal 16-20 damage in one turn.

decks.name: 1st Place Cornerstone Warsaw - Lava Geomancer
decks.primer:
Intro

This version of Geomancer is focused on controlling the realm through sticky minions and powerful mass removal. It’s a midrange-control deck. Stabilize your position and outvalue your opponent.


This primer is an in-depth (subjective) strategy guide for Geomancer. Continue if you enjoy reading this kind of stuff. I wrote it as a way to thank the community and other fellow Geomancers who wrote similar guides, they were incredibly useful.


How I started with this deck.

My good friend Filip wanted us to go to a Cornerstone and familiarize ourselves with the rest of the Sorcery community. The problem was that we have been playing Sorcery for just two months and our card pool was small. My deck wasn’t even a full 60/30 yet. 

I enjoy competing, so I wanted to come up with something that I could pilot to the top 8.



(E) Why Earth?

Earth has good minions and minions in Sorcery are often a removal spell on a stick. You can play earth defensively or aggressively. I enjoy this flexibility and playing control-ish decks. This element seemed to fit my playstyle very well. Coincidentally, no one else in our local playgroup played earth, so I was able to trade nearly all of my other cards for earth cards. 


Before I ended with a Geomancer, I tried a few different avatars and elemental combos like:


  • Mud Necro
  • Mud Druid
  • Dust Sorcerer


Then I tried Geomancer. This avatar is better in practice than the card suggests. You WILL have 6 mana on turn 6 without drawing a single site. It’s not a flashy ability like Druid’s or Archimago’s, but it is a solid one. Some of your spells and sites allow you to get even more value from it (more on that in the later section).


Geomancer felt like the strongest and most consistent of all avatars I tried, so I started practicing with him hard.



(F) Why splash fire?

Fire gives access to good graveyard hate and powerful mass removal magics. 

My wife often played fire [[Persecutor]], so I felt how strong a single [[Poison Nova]] could be. 



(W) Why not splash water?

Water sites turn off your [[Root Spider]], [[Earthquake]], [[Cave-In]], and [[Bury]]. I would love to play a Mud build, but it doesn’t seem to be worth it with the current card pool.



(A) Why not splash air?

Dust build might actually be viable. [[Blink]], [[Whirling Blades]] and [[Grandmaster Wizard]] could effectively work in this shell. I didn’t have time to test this build. Try it yourself and tell me how it does! : )



Why not play [[Archimago]]?

I saw Geoffrey’s list and for some time I considered playing Archimago, as it shares a lot of cards and Archi’s ability is crazy good. So why did I ultimately decide against it? My reasons were:

  • I had no experience playing Archi and nobody in our playgroup plays him.
  • Archi seems like a very exhausting avatar to play for multiple rounds in a row.
  • Archi benefits more from Uniques that I didn’t have.
  • I was expecting an aggro meta, which sucks for Archi.
  • [[Mirage]] got fixed.
  • Archi is currently considered the most powerful avatar and I prefer to play off-meta builds.


I feel like my build of Geomancer has no really bad matchups, but it also doesn’t have any great ones either.


In preparation for the tournament I think I watched all the available recorded gameplay on Youtube, lurked through discords and looked up hundreds of different decklists on Curiosa. And of course played as much as I could. (In the few days prior to the Cornerstone, all my dreams were Sorcery related xD)



How to use Geomancer - A quick guide

1st turn - Play a Village under your avatar, summon a Foot Soldier, and place a Rubble in front of you.

2nd turn - Replace the Rubble. Play a 2-drop if you can.

3rd turn - Play a site to the left or right of the site in front of you. Place a Rubble behind it. Play a 3-drop if you can.

4th turn - Play another site and make a Rubble or replace the Rubble you made the turn before. You have to make a call depending on your opponent. Sometimes you want to go wide (and make a letter T) and sometimes you want to play your starting sites on one side (mostly when playing against aggro, so it's a bit easier to defend in the early turns.)

5th and 6th turn - by now you know what to do. 

Your main goal is to make 3 Rubble tokens nearby and then replace them with sites from the top.


Gameplan:

Vs Aggro - Stabilize! Trade, block, preserve your life total. Attack when they run out of gas and you have a blocker ready. Kill their minions that could [[Whirling Blades]].


Vs Midrange - Focus on creating more value than they do. You have [[Craterize]], [[Major Explosion]] and other late-game cards. Control the board!


Vs Control - Pressure them early if you can. Your minions aren't so easy to remove. Again, there isn't much they can do to stop 10 damage coming from your [[Craterize]]. Focus your removal on things that could provide them value every turn, like Omphalos or [[Maiden, Mother, Crone]].


My thoughts on cards from this list:

Core cards:

[[Arjaro Exorcist]] - Spellcaster with a great genesis effect. There is often a good target for his ability. You can banish a [[Pudge Butcher]], [[Mariner’s Curse]] or [[Sphere of Animosity]]. One time I even used it to banish a Keening Banshee.


[[Root Spider]] - The best earth minion. His art is sick. It can buy you lots of time or you can use it to move and disable blockers from an adjacent site. I love them.


[[Gargantula]] - What’s up with earth and powerful spiders? Due to how its ability is written it can cocoon and disable minions with stealth or ward (removing those marks permanently) 4 power allows for trading with lots of popular minions.


[[Archangel Michael]] - The reward for going heavy into earth. Great genesis effect, hard to kill due to airborne and ward. 


[[Toolbox]] - I love the utility of this card. I feel that earth and fire have a good pool of ordinary spells to prefer Toolbox over [[Silver Bullet]].


[[Mix Terra]] - Never saw it during the tournament, but I was impressed by this card during practice. Use it to play Michael, [[King of the Realm]], [[Returned King]] or [[Earthquake]] much, much sooner and use that early advantage to dominate.


[[Crusade]] - Foot Soldiers count as earth minions and you have lots of them. You can also use it to drop Pudge Butchers, Gargantulas and Michael on opposing sites. 


[[Pudge Butcher]] - 5 power is no joke. There aren’t many minions that could survive a hit from this gal(?). I am really impressed by their performance. They provide a lot of area denial and they can often remain out of reach from the opponent's removal.


[[Assorted Animals]] - Played it multiple times during the tournament. Searched for a combination of Root Spider/Gargantula/Redmane Hyena. It provides a lot of fuel. I’d consider playing a second copy of this spell in the future.



Other good cards:

[[Kettletop Leprechaun]] - They are great earth minions, but Geomancer doesn’t really benefit from drawing extra sites that much. I am considering swapping them with [[Bosk Troll]]s. 


[[Mover of Mountains]] - Never saw it during the tournament. You can use his ability to disrupt opposing defensive sites or move your [[Sinkhole]]s closer to enemy sites or your [[Roots of Yggdrasil]]. Being a spellcaster is useful.


[[Redmane Hyena]] - I played a single copy to find it with [[Assorted Animals]]. I played only 4 demons in the deck, so I couldn’t count on triggering the +2 power. Hyena is mainly for disrupting enemy Archi.


[[Saint of Redemption]] - 2 power with ward for (2) is actually alright. His ability could really mess with some decks (mostly Persecutor). Combos with [[Rhitta Gawr of Snowdonia]].


[[Autumn Unicorn]] - Good beater for cheap.


[[Order of the White Wing]] - These guys could mess up your strategy a bit, I hate the anti-synergy with the rest of this deck, but I found out they are still worth playing. They work great against necro and Archi. 


[[Paladins of Bazia]] - Good beater with ward and spellcaster. 


[[Atlas Wanderers]] - They allow you to make some cool and unexpected plays. (Like repositioning Pudge Butcher and breaking walls made of defensive sites.) 


[[Lord of Greed]] - This card is close to a pet-card status. Great art. You may steal an opposing [[Toolbox]] played too early, a Core or an Arbalest. Nobody really expects him. (6) mana is not that much for a Geomancer, so a single copy may catch some opponents off-guard. 


[[Returned King]] - Tech against Necro. Also can steal [[Daperyll Vampires]]. 


[[Rhitta Gawr of Snowdonia]] - Every time I played him, my opponent was forced to remove him, giving me more time to ramp. 


[[King of the Realm]] - There are lots of Mortals in this deck and in the meta. Play him.


[[Divine Healing]] - Good vs aggro, useful vs midrange and control decks, but I wouldn’t play more than one copy.


[[Gift of the Wolf]] - Useful card that replaces itself. You are always glad to see it.


[[Bury]] - Sometimes all you need is to get rid of an early problematic minion or artifact. Bury often gets the job done. 


[[Landmass]] - Great if you aren’t pressured early. Ramp into your big spells. Often you will play a village and make a blocker, so you aren’t punished that much.


[[Onslaught]] - There are some situations where Onslaught breaks through enemy defenses and allows you to put your opponent on death’s door in a single turn. Play more than one copy if your meta has a lot of earth.


[[Scorched Earth]] - Something to blow your Roots or defend you in a pinch. Geomancer will allow you to rebuild quickly. It’s not the best card, but you don’t have better options. Feel free to swap it with something that you like more.


[[Cave-In]] - I couldn’t find a second copy of [[Earthquake]] before the tournament. Cave-In is a weaker, but still playable alternative. It deals with warded units!


[[Infiltrate]] - Good card with a single (F) threshold requirement. 


[[Earthquake]] - That’s a powerful spell. Gets rid of multiple minions and the rearrange is very useful. I would love to find a second copy of it.


[[Poison Nova]] - This spell saved me multiple times during the tournament. This deck has a few spellcasters, so you could use them to really blow out enemy minions and keep yours at a safe distance. 


[[Guards!]] - Saw it and played it one time on turn 7 and summoned 9 minions. Felt powerful, and a turn later I drew a [[Crusade]]. 


[[Major Explosion]] - Great removal and a finisher. (7) mana is not that much for a Geomancer. Your spellcasters will often provide you range to cast for high value.


[[Craterize]] - Ah, the iconic Craterize. Very expensive to cast, but it ends games. You don’t want to see it early. When I saw this spell in other decklists I wasn’t sure how to use it properly. Don’t worry, you will see its power.



I wouldn’t play these cards:


[[Valor]] - Spicy card, but even though this deck has lots of minions, I often kept this card in my hand without an opportunity to play it. Unfortunately, Valor does nothing vs Whirling Blades, Grapple Shots and other cards that simply strike.


[[Sir Morien]] - Both of his effects are great. He stops Grapple Shots, Firebolts and Pudge Butchers. The problem is that at turn 4 you will probably have 0 or just 1 (F) affinity. (F)(F) is a big deal. 



Would play them if I had them:

[[Torrid Omphalos]] - Couldn’t find this one. It would provide good value after stabilizing on the board. Great vs control.


[[Balor of the Evil Eye]] - Strong minion and another demon. Deals with opposing root spiders or finishes bigger minions or avatars. I would love to have one.



I want to test those:

[[Powerwish]] - This one could work wonders against [[Savior]], [[The Doom of Dilmun]] and warded water minions. 

[[Siege Giant]] - Reposition your Geomancer to make and replace more rubble. 

[[Sister Stefania]] - Swing with your Pudge! Unfortunately has some anti-synergy with the rest of the deck. Still, it might be worth it.

[[The Inquisition]] - 2 for 1. Helps vs control. 



My Atlas:

Villages - Blockers are nice to have. Makes the deck resistant to [[Atlantean Fate]].


[[Bedrock]] - Creates a safe haven for your [[Root Spider]]s. Also, you play [[Roots of Yggdrasil]], so it’s nice to be able to play something the same turn you blow them.


[[Boulevard of Bones]] - Good site that makes free units. Can be moved by other cards to make even more value.


[[Desert Bloom]] - Provides fire threshold and your Geomancer sees it as an earth site the turn you play it, allowing you to place a Rubble.


[[Funeral Pyre]] - Tech against Archi and other graveyard focused strategies. I don’t like this site, but felt it was necessary.


[[Haystack]] - I like running one. In most matchups it does nothing, but sometimes it can be very relevant. If your meta has weak earth representation, cut it.


[[Mount Ussar Sanctuary]] - I felt safe with this on the board. Doesn’t cost you much, and you will have the threshold to use it. 


[[Pillar of Zeiros]] - This card really saved me one time, gaining me 11 life. Every time I played vs aggro I wished to see it. 


[[Rift Valley]] - If you replace rubble with this site, it does nothing. I’d cut it. Doesn’t work well in Geomancer.


[[River of Flame]] - Another spellcaster to center your [[Poison Nova]] on. Often you can’t control where it is placed, so I consider cutting it.


[[Roots of Yggdrasil]] - When I saw this card, I knew I wanted to play it. I enjoy resetting the board with it and then rebuilding quickly thanks to Geomancer’s ability. It’s an Unique site, so the chance of it happening is rather low (never had the opportunity to do it during the tournament), but I like knowing that I have an out somewhere in my deck. Remember that your minions with ward will survive! 


[[Sinkhole]] - Roots enabler, also you can blow up opposing sites, to slow down your opponent and quickly rebuild. Reposition Sinkholes with Atlas Wanderers or Mover of Mountains.


[[Steppe]] - An obvious inclusion.


My collection:

In order of relevance:


[[Firebolts]] - Kill small minions, end games.


[[Heat Ray]] - Different flavor - sometimes better, sometimes worse than Firebolts.


[[Bury]] - An additional removal spell.


[[Dispel]] - Awesome card vs artifact and aura heavy decks.


[[Smite]] - You can use this to door your opponent by playing this on a strong minion adjacent to their avatar.


[[Angry Mob]] - It can kill a strong minion and it leaves a body.


[[Boil] - Good card to have against water decks.


[[Scent Hounds]] - Tech against Infiltrate or non-existent stealth decks.


[[Makeshift Barricade]] - Tech against heavy aggro. Never used it, but it might come handy one day.


[[Carrion Beetles]] - Tech against Archi, feels too weak to matter. I think I will replace it with something more useful, like a second [[Dispel]].



Tournament matches summary:

5 rounds of Swiss

Win vs aggro Elementalist good stuff - I banished his turn 3 Pudge with my Arjaro, allowing me to gain some control back. Rhitta gave me a turn to catch my breath and set up Major Explosion that turned the whole game.


Win vs mono Water Harbinger - My opponent played lots of defensive sites and a Mariner’s Curse. It was really hard to attack through it, but I finally broke through.


Win vs smoke Interrogator - I drew Divine Healing in my starting hand. I denied him cards early and paid with life. Assorted Animals for a Root Spider that helped me stabilize and outvalue.


Win vs mono fire Pathfinder - My Pudge Butcher really limited his options and defended my sites. Then I played Michael that he couldn’t easily remove.


Lose vs lava Archimago - He drew an early ring and outvalued my plays. Then he Heirloom Lost my Roots. This game went to time, and he played Onslaught with Border Militia two times to put me on door. I didn’t draw my hate pieces, just a single Hyena through Assorted Animals. Rough matchup.



Top 8

Win vs dust ramp Savior - This deck caught me by surprise. Wards are annoying to deal with. We were fighting for control over the realm, then I played Pillar of Zeiros gaining me 11 life and Assorted Animals for Gargantula and Root Spider stabilizing me completely. He was out of gas by then.



Top 4

Win vs aggro Elementalist good stuff (again) - Lots of cool plays in this game. He played Rift Valley in front of my Geo and placed a Pudge there on turn 3 thanks to his City of Glass. I wanted to counter with a Root Spider that he removed by using a Geyser from a Silver Bullet. Poison Nova saved my ass, and my Foot Soldier destroyed his City of Glass. I stabilized by summoning 9 Foot Soldier with Guards! 



Finals

Win vs smoke Persecutor - The final match was vs my good friend from my playgroup. He won against Archi who beat me during swiss. 

Lady Luck was totally by my side. I drew a really good hand with Saint of Redemption and he totally turned off his deck. I knew that if I could protect Saint, this match would go in my favor. Root Spider disabled his Dragonettes and Paladins of Bazia attacked his sites. Gargantula turned off his Daperyll Vampire that could save him. I truly feel sorry for him, this game was completely one-sided. You will find the finals match on Youtube. 



Future of the meta

With the new Court sites becoming legal, I expect this deck to change. Air court punishes token strategies and earth court punishes elites and uniques. 

I think that Geo could find success by running both earth and fire courts and cutting most Villages and rare spells.



The end

Huge thanks to the whole Sorcery community. I had a lot of fun and memorable moments. Also, shoutout to a player with a similar nickname (Morgoth) that also won a cornerstone with a Lava Geomancer. What a weird coincidence. 

I hope I can see and play with all of you again soon.



About the author

My real name is Hubert, and my favorite elements are earth and water. I have been playing different card games competitively for over 15 years and I currently work as a board game designer. I enjoy brewing and testing my own decks. I love Sorcery and its community, and I’d be thrilled to contribute to Erik’s Curiosa someday if the opportunity ever arose.
