decks.name: 1st Place GenCon HOT SPRINGS
decks.primer:
Hi Team,


Excited to share about the deck, but first would be remiss if I didn't give credit and thanks to my team, Chris @Ismarkthelesser and Nick @Astronomonov, as well as John @PorkchopSandwitches and Blake @Collision for the insight and countless games that provided the context into many of these choices. As much your win as mine!


Also, to Pascal, my finals opponent. Thank you for one of the hardest, funnest, and friendliest games I've ever played. Despite the stakes, I appreciate how we approached the game as though we had already felt like winners just being in the seat, and counter each other. You are a champion.


Hot Spring has been a work in progress for ~8 months, after countless iterations, this is where we have landed currently.


Original deck list of where it all started.


GenCon 2025 Finals Match


Deck spotlight with Chase and EC team.


Now, into the deck.


Weaknesses: Fire and Water offer NO aura hate (outside of Scorched Earth), which means impactful auras stick around. Generally, you can outpace a deck with aura strategies, but not always. This also means no Monument hate either. This wouldn't have been a problem pre-Archimago's rise to fame, but now we're seeing more and more Orbs. Luckily, you are able to capitalize on the orb as well, with double Shatter Strikes and Minor Explosions worst case. This has changed with the inclusion of Swap; however, these problems do persist. Ironically, I think the biggest nemesis to the deck is itself, as in the last 5 major tournaments, I lost in the top 16 or higher against the mirror match. It was my bane.



A quick breakdown of each section of the deck and logic behind the card:


Auras:

  • Jihad: Self-explanatory. One of the most powerful fire cards ever printed. This card allows 5 power Monstrous Lions on turn 3 with a pond.


  • Atlantean Fate: Look at that, also one of the best cards ever printed. This primary function is to allow you to disrupt the Archimago's and other greedy threshold decks. It also provides a path to clear out popular problematic sites, like Free City, Pebbled Paths, and even Perilous Bridges. Also kills root spiders if they are on a sight that can be affected.


Artifact:


  • Torshammar Trinket: Druid can abuse this by always having access to Tawny. Probably a 3 of in most decks at this point.


  • Ring of Morrigan: IMO the strongest card in a vacuum ever printed, but particularly abusable in this deck. In conjunction with Drums, the ability to IG-88 your way through your opponent's team while also gaining life is backbreaking to say the least.


  • Mask of Meyham: With the strike change, we felt this or GG were too valuable to run, but the questions were, which one, and how many copies? Assuming there would be a concentration of Archimagos, we felt 1 Mask and 1 drums was the right call, as drums can feel dead against the few creatures in most Archimago's lists. This has a synergy with Sir Agravaine (we will cover that on his bullet point) and with the concentration of smaller minions, we thought the mask was better than GG.


  • Drums of Doom: Can lock down the game in a (candidly) un-interactive way. In a minion-heavy meta, expect druids to have 2x of these in their deck. Ring + this. Deserts, Tawny, vile Imp, all kill spells now. Also, the only way to protect against Nymbus Djinn otk.


Minions:


  • Polar Explorers: This quickly became one of my favorite cards in the deck. It enables SO much and makes cards like Redcap Poweries and Monstrous Lion have less drawback by evading problematic sites.


  • Vile Imp: 2 damage on entry, Kill spell with Drums. Takes out knights holding lances often and is just one of the best 2 drops in the game.


  • Kobolds: With the 3 of trinkets, and the prominence of Gnome Hollows, these angy little dudes provided, in most cases, bare minimum, 3 extra copies of Vile Imp, but with an insane ceiling. Also combos with strike synergy, kills tough airborne minions like Plumed Pegasus if comboed with deserts or Trinket. Very easy to deal with their tempo play with one of these early.



  • Lugbog Cat: Amazing tempo play with Pond, can reach into opponents' site with Floodplain. Solid beast.


  • Morgana le Fay: Soooo much value with this card. Boneyard target at the very least for more cards. Helps in grindy games.


  • Redcap Powries: Cheapest charge minion for the stats. Almost no downside at this point with the immobilized nerf.


  • ***MVP Sir Agravaine***: Self-protecting unit that buffs Tawny's attacks. Has proven to be a huge problem and is not answered with non-targeting damage. Enables one to turn deaths doors with only a few minions striking the avatar. With the recent attack trigger change, he will always strike the *original* target. Meaning, while adjacent to an enemy avatar being attacked, he will ALWAYS strike the avatar regardless of whether there are blockers around. This singlehandedly won me 2 of my games late in the bracket and is an absolute kill on site card.



  • Boudicca: Buffs Tawny and can just be a sudden death's door machine. Boneyard target for surprise extra damage due to getting value off her passive immediately. (if they aren't already dead by then).


  • Monstrous Lion: Has been one of the biggest standout cards. Combos with Pond, great target for Guyer to be used as a kill spell on a body. Great with all of the Battle Mages, as it gets value immediately, and also serves the 3 power.


  • Selfsame Simulacrum: After the recent revision of how multiple Bruins interact, this became too good not to run, though it never came up in my finals match. With multiple other targets, or your opponent's best minion, plenty of value to be had with this card.


  • Ruler of Thul: Similar role to Boudicca. Burst potential. Awesome surprise play with flipping Druid into Bruin, then following that up on the next turn with a Ruler for 8 in their back row with the free unit in Bruin. Also recursive with Lady of the Lake.


  • Sir Gaheris: Decent stats, and it does play well against many aggro decks, by being able to keep life parity and block, which is nice.


  • Panorama Manticore: Similar role to Phoenix, early bruiser that is hard to deal with. Untaps regularly and trades well.


  • Questing Beast: Also a Bruiser, awesome burst potential with attack from stealth and shatter strike. Mastering the art of the end-of-turn step turns this card from a great card to an absolute menace! With the ability to attack, then step back onto a watersite protects this to get you multiple strikes of 25% of their starting health.



Magics:


  • Geyser: Started out as a way to deal with Root Spider has quickly become one of my favorite cards. Providing airborne to these units increases their lethality dramatically, allowing them to avoid many problematic defensive sites. Also is a good combo with Blaze as it really extends the range with + movement and the ability to fly nearby.


  • Pollimorph: hard removal is pivotal right now with the abundance of 5+ power minions and vampires' abilities to Deaths Door you and heal for a billion while attacking sites. Also, the fact that it banishes the transformed card is actually a huge boon.


  • Minor Explosion: I started with 3 firebolts; however, the prevalence of Morgana Le Fey ultimately had me consider this instead. The indiscriminate 3 damage has a higher ceiling and, with the reach of Tawny, can easily be a 2 for 1.


  • Disintegrate: Similar to Pollimorph. Hard removal easily cast from Tawny.


  • Pact with the Devil: This has been one of my favorite cards. Combining with Tawny, Adept Illusionist, and Morgana (more niche) allows you to keep up with Sorcerer and Archimage in the mid-late game.


  • Swap (Placeholder in deck as Font of Life because they have the same mana and threshold): My friends and I had a feeling this card would be absolutely broken, and it sure felt good. This replaces Shatter Strike in the deck, and I have 0 regrets. Super flexible, and stealing Pstone and Rings while putting your guy directly on them feels AMAZING.


Key Sites:


  • Floodplain: Always been one of my favorites due to its ability to allow you to play more greedy with your threshold in Water, but also serves the purpose to kill root spiders and other burrowed minions and to extend reach on Lugbog cat.


  • Pond: MVP site: So many beasts in the deck make a dramatically increased impact by coming out a turn earlier. Tower for beasts, but better. Also amazing that with the prominence of earth still, being summoned onto a water site protects the beast you curved out from burry effects.


  • Desert: Are key to taking momentum. Also protects against enemies, Atlanian Fate turning off the critical threshold needed to cast key spells.


  • Boneyard: Though I never saw it at gencon, in my testing this card has been an amazing addition to the atlas. With several of the hard removals banishing, and access to Funeral Pyre, you can construct a sided resurrection. Also, with the concentration of charge units, you are able to bring back a Redcap, for instance, and attack with it, and because the unit they brought back entered the same turn, it will have summoning sickness. It also lets you bring back your "Win button" unique for its powerful genesis or passive abilities. Lastly, in what I presumed to be a Archimago heavy meta, the lack of minions they generally have allow this to be onesided even more regularly. It was my favorite spice in the deck.


  • Kelp Cavern: I originally hated this card when it was first printed. I thought the lack of "may" made it unplayable. I was wrong. This lets you comfortably mulligan to get better gas early, then go back and find your spells later when needed. I have been very, very impressed with it.


You may notice a lake of Smokestacks. I found, with a number of key genesis, and the draw cadence of the deck, you end up having to play it earlier than you'd like. This turns off your important sites, like deserts and flood plains, which can be really detrimental. Also, with flooding being an ability, smokestacks removes your ability to flood and kill rootspider. So I found it more detrimental than helpful in many matchups.

decks.primer:
I registered for my LGS’s Cornerstone (we put in a lot of effort to get that status - should out to Battlegrounds in Richmond, VA!) but hadn’t played for five months. Going into the tournament, I needed 1) an Avatar I had at least some experience with 2) a deck that was pretty easy to pilot 3) something that could hopefully win or not make me look entirely foolish ;)


After looking at my old pre-Gothic decks, I landed on the “red deck wins” Pathfinder in a dusty deck box. I figured, “there have to be some cool new toys and more fire sites,” and I was pleasantly surprised. There’s a fair amount of Gothic in this deck as a result! I would add a Horns of Behemoth for the Wasteland if I had pulled one and I totally overlooked Vindictive Nation, which is also an easy add in lieu of one of the duals.


The Avatar pilots no differently than before, you have to attempt the optimal pattern to enable a path to at least six sites, but either via Giant, Warhorse, or just walking over a few sites, you can easily get to 10+ simply because of the tempo you have.


The deck archetype is classic sligh/red deck wins. You simply want to be as aggressive as possible. Gift of the Serpent, especially with Dragonettes, is AWESOME for taking out problematic minions. Searing Truth is an MVP as it gets you even more cards if you need them, but can also kill an Avatar instantly on DD. I’d definitely figure out a way to cut some things (I.e. Minor Explosion) to get up to max for each of those. I didn’t bother with any of the collection artifacts as they are simply too slow. The only collection card is a Hounds in case you elect to cast it from Molten Maar.


If you’re looking for something than can simply

blitz out a win, particularly before folks figure out deck efficiency and the meta, this may be a good choice for you. I’d you’re looking for something with some neat combos and cool interactions, there are a few, but really this is all about the burn. Enjoy the heat!

decks.name: SCG Con Las Vegas Limited Championship Top 8 Draft 1st Place
Avatar of Air - 1st Place Cornerstone Championship
decks.primer:
This is a Gothic mid-range Air/Earth deck with Avatar of Air for mobility. It's not too different from the typical air/earth mid range gameplay that encourages an aggressive early-mid game with late-game finishers. With the changes to Guisarm and other "Strike" effects, you're not going for the OTK and instead looking to constantly apply pressure.


---------- Artfiacts:

Onyx Core is to help ramp and fix Earth Threshold. Torshammer Trinkets are to help deal more damage and make trades more favorable. Toolbox is to provide answers when you need them but more often than not it is to pull Zap! out from the collection to kill your opponent at Death's Door. You could argue running a 3 of to add consistency to access to the cards.


Rolling Boulder is a typical card to have in an Avatar of Air deck, however with Gothic we have a brand new toy to play with in Lord of Greed. You can now roll the boulder and have Lord of Greed bring it back at the end of turn.


---------- Minions:

Most minions don't' need explanation as they are typical valuable creatures to fly into your opponent's board with AoA.


Men of Leng is a personal pet card of mine that if played at the right time can be very hard to deal with and can take a few cards from your opponent. Use your Blinks, Wuthering Heights, and AoA to fling them to the back row and force some discards.


Skeleton Mage is a fantastic new addition to the roster of air minions as it not only lets you recast your magic, but you can also cast opponent magics that you may need (specifically says "a cemetery" not "your cemetery").


All of the ranged units become extremely difficult to play around with air's mobility. Stygian Archers are one of my favorite new additions. Kill stuff, gain benefits. Doesn't get more satisfying than that.


Daperyll Vampires are probably the most questionable minion on the list. With the changes to how they work in that you no longer get health when striking a site, they lost a lot of luster. However, they are still an airborne minion that is hard to deal with sometimes. They are the most likely to be replaced for lower-cost aggressive targets. And they've also been outclassed by one of my new favorite Airborne minions which are:


Legion of Gall are a fantastic minion. Never would they have printed a 5 mana 5 power Airborne unit in Beta, but they did it in Gothic and gave it an upside. These guys are a monster to deal with, especially early with a tower. On top of them dominating the air, they also remove cards from your opponent's collection. So you get to see what kind of answers they may have and remove their best options.


Lord of Fear is a game ender. Enemies can't defend alone is a huge effect and makes your offense feel so much more powerful. You get to trade better. You get to attack without being blocked. And most importantly Death's Door is scarier than ever.


Lord of Greed is an answer to your opponent's artifacts and he has an upside of having some fun synergy with Rolling Boulder. I debated over 2 of Fear over Greed but there are just too many good artifacts in this game that you want to shut them down as often as you can. We don't have Swap so this is one of our best and consistent answers to artifacts.


---------- Magic:

There are a lot of typical tempo spells you will see in a deck like this but there are a few cards that I want to talk about. Namely Gift of the Wolf and Vanishment.


Gift of the Wolf is a fantastic new card and I feel it might be overlooked very often at first glance. This card is so good at making trades, or just getting extra damage in with a ranged strike or site attack. The fact that it replaces itself and also is a great target for Skeleton Mage is what helped it earn its slots in the deck. I replaced Gigantism with this because Gift of the Wolf more easily fits into turns. Gigantism is still good, but often your opponent will have chump blockers making it have less opportunities to be used.


Vanishment is another one of my own personal pet cards. I like cards that replace themselves, and this does so and protects your board state. Plenty of times I find myself just ahead enough and Vanishment guarantees I stay ahead on my opponent's next turn most of the time.


---------- Sites:


My site choices are very defensive. Stuff like Perilous Bridge, Mountain Pass, and No Man's Land let you take advantage of AoA's mobility while shutting down your opponent's ability to strike back. The quality of sites drastically increased in Gothic. Double threshold sites are an amazing new addition. Learning how to mulligan sites is a process with this deck. Placement of air sites and defensive sites is something you will get used to after playing for a bit. Wuthering Heights is a new site that replicates AoA's ability. This lets you double fly units and get them further in to enemy territory.

decks.name: Seeing Red - 1st place SCG Con Baltimore and NYC Cornerstone 2025
decks.primer:
Seeing Red

Primer by UnderSietch


*UPDATE*


I’ve updated this decklist to reflect the one I played in the SCG CON Baltimore 2025, where I took 1st place. I've also update the primer for the new list and added more specific examples of how I play special cards, artifacts and auras in addition to the turn by turn card flow breakdown. Thank you for your interest and your feedback!


*NEW* Video of the Quarter Finals Match from SCG Con in Baltimore 2025 vs Count Tolstoy


Feature article on Sorcery TCG about Seeing Red and it's pilot, yours truly!


Video of the Championship Match at SCG CON in Baltimore 2025


Interview on Common Sense Sorcery Podcast about my win at SCG CON Baltimore


Team Covenant play-tests this deck on their YouTube channel ahead of SCG CON Houston! (gameplay at 50 mins)


Check out the video of the final match of the NYC King of the Realm cornerstone!


Introduction:


I'm typically a very whimsical deck builder. I like the story and the artwork and the intricate interactions between the weirdest and coolest cards. I often even write a little bit of lore to explain the narrative of the "characters" in my deck and how they came together to do battle against strange and ominous enemies. What can I say? I'm a nerd.


But with the tournament season approaching, I've been noticing an uptick in a more competitive and aggressive play-style all around me. This deck is a response to getting my butt relentlessly kicked over and over by some very good players and deck builders in my local community, who were tuning their tournament decks at our casual meetups. The calculated and efficient competition deck is a new adventure and mindset for me. And I think a good amount of beginners luck, mixed with being thrown to the wolves (sometimes literally) again and again, led to my winning our NYC cornerstone recently. I had been so tilted, so often, that I was literally SEEING RED.


Philosophy:


I decided that I wanted to make my games as short and sweet as possible. I don't want to allow other decks to get set up and start to hit me with big, intricate plays. My goal is to get my opponent in a reactive space, having to spend their precious few actions each game removing my threats and adapting to my board position, rather than imposing their will.


Playstyle:


I chose Mono-Fire because it's a fast and nasty suit. There are plenty of places to find extra damage for removal and to lower my opponents life total, while leaving me in an advantageous board-state. And it's very low cost!


I chose the Druid as my avatar for one reason: An immortal, airborne spellcaster, TAWNY. Flying around and dealing Fire's unblockable Area of Effect (AoE) damage to both remove enemy threats and deal damage to enemy avatars simultaneously.


The basic idea behind the deck is to combine the sometimes self-destructing damage from tawny, and genesis damage from deserts, with genesis and end-of-turn bonus damage from fire minion cards to remove enemy threats and deal damage without spending mana or losing my minions in a fight.


For example:


Opponent plays an Autumn Unicorn on turn 3.

I attack it with Tawny (she dies, but there's one damage), I play a desert (one damage and summon Tawny again, she's back!), and I play a vile imp for 2 mana and the genesis damage removes the Unicorn and leaves my Imp and Tawny alive. The board now has two threats on it for me and none for them.


Tawny's bonus damage also works in the reverse. You can cast an AoE spell, then attack with Tawny to deal one damage to an enemy minion THEN cast a desert to deal one additional damage and summon Tawny again for no cost.


For example:


Opponent drops a Atlas Wanderers on turn 4 due to a Mana boost from a Gothic Tower.

I cast Firebolts with Tawny, then attack the Atlas Wanderers with Tawny dealing a 4th damage, then I tap my Druid to play a Desert nearby, dealing the Atlas Wanderers a 5th and fatal damage and summoning Tawny again for no cost.


This allows me to destroy my opponents 5-cost drop with a total expenditure of 2 mana.


The last and most important note I'll make about our magical owl friend is that she's actually the perfect foil to your Druid opponents. By using a Torshammar Trinket, you can still have Tawny fly around near your opponent's avatar when they are Flipped and Bruin is active. Now that she's a 2 power, she can take steps nearby your opponents Druid and not die from their special ability. Then, she can cast a kill spell.


Use your owl. Give it a Torshammar Trinket and hit your opponents sites as often as possible. Cast Boudicca and give Tawny a Trinket and hit your opponent's sites with your owl for 5 damage. Be very active and rude with your bird friend. If your opponent is spending cards and mana removing your owl, you are winning. They are spending time, energy and resource on something that you get for free. Try your best to get them to react to your owl.


For me? The Bruin is a "smash in case of emergency" card. I want to spend most games not needing it. I want to be able to cast tawny by playing a site all game long. She's that important.



How and when to play:


You need to be patient!

(read that again)


This deck allows you to win FAST. I've observed that, in many games, Sorcery players cast anywhere from 12-18 spells and it can take up to 50 minutes to finish. In my games, my opponents cast 7-10 spells and the game can be over in 25 minutes.


(Which resulted in a very nice long break between rounds for me at the tournaments)


That doesn't mean that you play all of your cards out fast, however. Quite the contrary. It means you need to make every point of damage count. Hit their sites and Avatars early and as often as possible, yes. BUT DO NOT EMPTY YOUR HAND. You are leading the action while tactically responding to their drops. Find ways to remove their drop and increase your board presence AND deal them a little damage each turn. It's very possible. But you are most likely playing only one spell per turn. Your owl, deserts, genesis effects and end of turn effects will make it feel like you're doing much more than that but you're not. It's very simple and very deadly. And you'll need spells in your hand if your opponent manages to slow the game down and draw things out.



Turn by turn:


Mulligan:


You want a removal or control spell like Disintegrate, Immolation or Infiltrate in your hand ideally, and at least one cheap minion and one fire damage spell. Having three minions isn't the end of the world. You can have a War Horse, Colicky Dragonettes and Saracen Raiders and play forward from a really good place. The removal and fire magics will show up when you need them.


Make sure you have a Forge and at least one Desert in your hand, trust me. If you can't do that, make sure you have two fire threshold in your opening hand. Sinkholes and Wizard's Dens are awesome, don't mulligan them unless you have multiples in hand.


Ideal sample hand:


Disintegrate, War Horse, Minor Explosion

Forge, Red Desert, Poison Well



Turn by turn breakdown:


Turn 1: play the forge, make the lance, create Tawny and have her pick up the lance.


Turn 2: If you went first, Play a Bonfire or a Funeral Pyre or something forward toward your opponent and drop the War Horse and step Tawny forward to hand the lance off to your other minion. You don't always get the charge or genesis effects of minions and sites to land, that doesn't mean it's a bad play. Remember you're increasing your board presence with each drop and they'll have to spend resources to clear those spells, which you'll replace with more powerful ones as you draw them. Of course the best sites to play forward in a central position would be a Sinkhole, Smokestacks or Vesuvius. But we can't always get what we want.


If you went second, try dropping that Poisoned Well and get a hit on their life total, if they played forward toward you. Or play a Sinkhole forward to prepare for any unwanted sites. Wizard's Den is also a fantastic starting site, or a drop on turn three on your back row to get the extra spell draw.


Going second also means you can bring the lance up from Tawny, hand it off to the War Horse and immediately step forward to deal 3 first-strike damage to either a minion or, ideally, your opponent's site.


NOTE: You will draw spells and play the sites from your hand on the first three turns.


Turn 3: I love the Redcap Powries here, or even a Trinket on Tawny and Firebolts for removal or direct damage to the enemy avatar (that's 5 damage turn 3). When in doubt, Minor Explosion is the best, most effective card in this deck. I honestly have considered adding a 4th copy recently. Explode everything all of the time. Do not hesitate to do damage. It's your whole job. Do it often. Colicky Dragonettes are good here. Save your Kobolds for later unless there's an obvious play that maximizes their end of turn strike ability.



Turn 4: You will draw and play a site. This leaves you with four sites on the board and three or four spells in hand. Great cards open up on this turn: Saracen Raiders is an awesome free 3 damage on an unprotected and unsuspecting opponent's site. Infiltrate becomes an option, but I typically save this until my opponent drops something that seems like a game-changing bomb. Think Pudge Butcher or Seirawan Hydra. These are the things you want to take and tap down and keep them out of the game. Redcap Powries with a Torshammer Trinket is a favorite of mine to remove a 4 power minion or strike a site for 4. Boudicca opens up on Turn 4, but don't drop her on the board unless Tawny and/or another minion can undoubtedly strike a site freely. Her ability is too good to waste. If you play Boudicca back and away from the fray, you may get multiple turns with her ability in play and swing the game heavily in your favor.



Turn 5: draw a spell and tap to draw a site. The only reason you would draw a site to play here is if you already have Rebecks in your hand and you see a good opportunity to use your charge giant to get a big hit in on your opponent. Otherwise, stick to the plan so you can have 5 sites next turn.


Turn 6: Draw a spell and play your 5th site. This should leave you with 3 or 4 spells in hand and five sites on the board. You can play everything in the deck besides Infernal Legion with this board state. This is where the world opens up to you. Try to spread your minions out as much as possible so that they're more difficult to remove. Your opponent is going to scratch and claw to stabilize. There may be temptation at times to play multiple cards from your own hand. Only do this if it lands your opponent at death's door or decisively swings the game toward your win.


Turn 7: Draw a spell and tap to draw a site. Now you have all of the sites that you'll ever need and you have three or 4 spells in hand. This is what I mean by BE PATIENT. You'll find yourself in a remarkable board state with plenty of spells in hand. If you can leverage your extra damage well, you might still have two or three threats on the board at this point.



How to Deal Damage:


Every time that you can, play a minion with charge and hit your opponent's sites. Every time that you can, cast fire spells that hit their avatar or groups of minions. By turn 5 or 6, you may have taken half of their life total away by chipping away with Tawny, fire damage and minions hitting sites.


I usually find that I'm holding more immediate damage threats than my opponent. If I consistently am hitting them once per turn for 3+ damage, I get them a little off their game and they start to have to waste resources and dig for answers.


Try not to win more. Win just enough. You really want those three spells in hand to deal with some of the game's inherent big swings.


How to win:


You didn't flip your Druid, did you? Good. Being able to summon Tawny (and maybe put a Trinket on her) and get her into position to deal a Minor Explosion, Firebreathing, Lava Flow, Firebolts or Firebreathing is your ticket to victory. Good players keep a kill in their hand when they can. If you can hold onto one of these spells and not use it until you get your opponent to death's door, you'll have a tidy and efficient victory on your hands.


Remove their threats when they're on death's door. Get rid of their minions, and clear your path. Sometimes you don't have the fire spell and you need superior numbers of minions to get a strike in. Don't forget to remove their blockers to make a charge minion very deadly.


Sometimes, walking your druid forward and then flipping for Bruin and your special ability, can pin their Avatar down when it's on deaths door and keep it from being able to run away from your fire damage. In this case only, you don't need Tawny, because your Avatar is your spellcaster.



Special cards and their uses:


Your damage (most of it) comes from your small minions and fire spells from Tawny. But sometimes you need to be able to flex into a more midrange role and become a bigger beast to seal the deal against a powerful opponent.


There are a few HUGE drops in this deck that help you out a lot.


Rebecks is my favorite card here, dealing 4 damage to an opponent's site on the same turn that you play it. Pair him with a Torshammer Trinket or Jihad for a bigger swing. Have him ride a warhorse to get him into a deeper and more problematic position for an opponent. On a later turn, use a fire spell to clear out a blocker before dropping Rebecks to get a free hit on your opponent's site.


Boudicca on turn 4 when you have Tawny and maybe a War Horse and a Redcap Powries on the board? Do some math here, that's 15 damage if they all go unblocked to your opponent's sites. Normally I play her very carefully away from the battle. But sometimes she can create a very welcome distraction. While your opponent focuses on removing her, you can keep hitting for 2-5 damage per turn on their life total. Remember the goal is to get them to door and ping them for the win. If you lose cards and life along the way, so be it. Don't win more! Just win. Never waste resources to save a special card.


Siege Giants are amazing. These guys are why I don't have to play Blaze or Mad Dash in this deck. I get all of the movement I need from these dudes. They can throw 21 of the cards in this deck (including Avatar and Tawny), to any nearby site without having to tap for the ability. They can even throw a War Horse that they themselves are riding. READ THAT AGAIN. They can saddle up on a horse, throw that horse diagonally, then both the horse and the giant still can take a step and declare an attack. Use Siege Giant to spread your damage out far and wide, like a joyful flaming trebuchet.


Monstrous Lion's job is actually as a removal spell. I use it to deal a surprise and tidy four damage to an enemy that's on my border or in my territory. Sometimes a BattleMage or some other antsy Avatar gets too close and catches a lion to the face. Don't expect the Lion to live for more than one turn very often. Add a Torshammer Trinket on turn 5 or later for extra Lion.


Askelon Phoenix is in the deck to provide air support and fire resistance. You'll very rarely use its ability to power it up. But it takes no damage from fire spells, minions or abilities. It survives a poison nova. Heck, it survives a direct strike from Ignis Rex holding Crown of the Victor. It's a good card, and is usually a sort of turret or defensive/support play for me, more so than a beatdown.


Infernal Legion has never been invited to a party. Nobody likes to see this thing hit the board. It's an absolutely enormous problem for most opponents. But be careful, it's also trouble for you if you don't play it right. This is another card I'd qualify as a late game or defensive bailout play.



Artifacts and Auras:


The Ring of Morrigan is the most efficient card in the game. I think it has to go in any deck right now. Its overall effect is that of a desert that can be triggered every turn and gains you life for each damage you do with it. Enjoy your bling.


Torshammer Trinket is very powerful. There is absolutely an argument for playing a third one of these in the deck and playing at 52 cards. Your opponent cannot interact with it unless they make you discard it from your hand. It can be placed on any minion or avatar in order to increase its power by 1 on your turn. Another little added single damage to reinforce the soul of the deck. Happy smashing.


Mask of Mayhem is a very tricky play. Be careful. I'd recommend dropping it when you have 2-3 minions nearby each other. Maybe one of them removes a large minion and the other two get a free hit that's big. If you can wipe the board and maybe follow it up with some Saracen Raiders or another charge minion? Go ahead. But be hyper aware that this also benefits your opponent. Battlemages love this being on the board and so do Avatars of Earth.


Drums of Doom is the one big defensive card I have in the deck. If all goes to heck and you need to protect yourself from minions, put Drums on your Avatar and flip for Bruin. Your thorns ability will now deal lethal damage to any potential nefarious trespassers.


Jihad - If you can cast Jihad on your opponent's side of the board, this deck gets very hard to deal with. This aura opens up all of your extra damage genesis and end of turn affects from minions, hitting the enemy's avatar the very first turn they're played. Don't hesitate to do damage to their life total. Take them to death's door as quickly as you can while not emptying your hand.



NOTE: I prefer to cast Jihad covering two of my opponent's sites and two of my own, so that I can summon non-charge minions and still receive the +1 power benefit.



The Great Famine very specifically removes the strongest minion in a four-square area at the end of your turn. Very often, the minions in this deck are less powerful than the average minion my opponent is wanting to cast. You can survive a turn or two under its protection and force your opponent to forego summoning in order to wait out your aura's duration. This is also our answer when someone has a big problem underneath of a site. This card also carries a very important word for our success in its text box: "occupying". This means that The Great Famine (and also Lava Flow!) can remove threats that are burrowed or submerged. So if you're struggling to remove anything from a Root Spider to a Great Old One with confidence, this is your huckleberry.



Dangers in the Meta:


Pebbled Paths, Bottomless Pit, Perilous Bridge, Troll Bridge, Gnome Hollows and Impenetrable Copse. Use your Sinkholes or Smokestacks of Gnaak in a center position to make sure you can negate these nasty sites.


Archimago. I don't know what to tell you. You will lose sometimes to someone who can cast Divine Healing 6 times during a game and then Craterize you twice. Get them to deaths door asap so that they can't benefit from healing.


Enchantress. I don't know about this one really, I'm just very afraid of how this avatar completely flips the physics of the board state. Control tends to trump aggro in these games. Speed is your best friend.


Water players or Steam Druids with Polar Explorers and Ruler of Thul. It's very hard to rush forward when you have to watch your back. I recommend sticking to the game plan and holding on to some AoE fire spells and Monstrous lions to deal with whoever decides to come in the back door with bad intentions.




IMPORTANT NOTE:


You're going to take damage during this game. Don't get me wrong, lots of time you'll be playing way ahead of slower decks. But I also won a lot of games in this tournament on double-death's door. Try to keep your cool. You've usually got more damage in hand than your opponent. Stay vigilant and trust that you can win. Stay ahead by a turn. Get your opponent to door first and use fire to finish it. Don't worry about the score, just the result.


One game, I went down to door when my opponent (another fast air/earth Druid) still had 12 life. I was so disheartened and I was sure my day was over. But he had played all of his cards that could deal damage to my Druid, which was safely nestled on my back row. I was able to infiltrate his Pudge Butcher and leave it ineffective while I flooded the board with spells from my hand. I still had 3 or 4 spells in hand and I had 6 sites down so I could drop two spells a turn to put the pressure back on him. It was a close one, and the high-heart-rate monitor on my watch went off twice. But I came back and won it.


Another game, an opponent stole my Infernal Legion using Infiltrate, then played a Grim Guisarme and Warp Spasm the next turn to hit me for 24 with it. Before this play, though, the score had been 20-2 in my favor. The Legion died and he had played all of his cards. I was able to stabilize and win in two turns.


In the finals of the Crossroads tournament final, I was down 18-2. And the 2 damage he had taken, he did to himself. Talk about a blowout. I managed the win because I stayed the course and made the best, most efficient plays. Eventually, I cleared his board and played enough threats of my own to deal two big swings and get to double death's door. The deck has your back. Trust it, and trust that no game is over until it's over.


Conclusion:


You have one job. Burn. Do not spend time entertaining or even considering your opponent's intentions, actions or feelings.


Just. Do. Damage.


Quickly and consistently lower their life total while leaving yourself some spells in hand as options for future plays.


If you want to play with feelings, play with water. If you want to play with finesse, play with air. If you want to play with muscle, play with earth. But if you want to leave your enemy in ashes, play with fire!


;0)


I hope that you enjoy playing this deck and your own variations. Please let me know how it goes for you when you try it? Looking forward to hearing from you and seeing you at an event sometime soon!



-UnderSietch

decks.primer:
Waveshaper has been my go-to avatar since I started playing with the precons. The amount of control the tap ability provides and room for interesting plays with cards that synergies with the body of water makes every game feel fresh and unique.


Strategy

This is a control deck that aims to survive the first rounds with hindering sites ([[Perilous Bridge]], [[Tadpole Pool]], [[Troll Bridge]], [[Babbling Brook]]) and sticky minions. ([[Adept Illusionist]], [[Sir Tom Thumb]], [[Lugbog Cat]])


We accrue value with [[Highland Princess]], [[Grandmaster Wizard]] and [[Captain Baldassare]]. There are multiple ways to recast and regain these effects through [[Selfsame Simulacrum]], [[Fey Changeling]] and [[The Lady of the Lake]]. To make sure we are staying ahead in resources over our opponent we have [[Atlantean Fate]], [[The Great Drowning of Men]] and [[Wrath of the Sea]].


To get our opponent to death’s door we utilize evasive and hard to kill minions such as [[Gyre Hippogriffs]], [[Daperyll Vampire]], [[Hounds of Ondaros]], [[Questing Beast]], [[Mester Stoor Worm]], [[The Green Knight]] and [[Thundering Giant]].


Other Notable Cards

  • [[Plague of Frogs]] - Gum up the board (and potentially get a big life total swing together with [[Ruler of Thul]].
  • [[Pollimorph]] & [[Mesmerism]] - Remove/turn any pesky minions.
  • [[Stormy Seas]] - Submerge artifacts that give our opponent an edge or remove one or multiple minions.
  • [[Riptide]] - We can use it on our minions to protect them if we need to overextend, pull our enemies' minions or avatar to get to them or pull them aside to get an attack we otherwise couldn’t get through.
  • [[Watchtower]] & [[Hounds of Ondaros]] - Stealth is a very strong mechanic and we use these to being able to remove [[Infiltrate]] and letting us target [[Morgana le Fay]].


Highland Princess Jewel Box

The suite of artifacts are specifically chosen for the Highland Princess and the impact they can provide for the game. Depending when you play her and what other cards you have in hand/play, the decision can turn the game in your favor.  

  • [[Amethyst Core]] & [[Aquamarine Core]] - Stable choices to secure the threshold you need.
  • [[Mix Aer]] - Usually used to get a Grandmaster Wizard into play.
  • [[Ring of Morrigan]] & [[Torshammar Trinket]] - Great against aggressive decks when you need to make sure you can kill their minions without trading with your own.
  • [[Philosopher’s Stone]] - Great for the mid- and end-game when you would like to cast multiple spells.

decks.primer:
Playstyle: Midrange with a bit of combo

Difficulty: 5/10


This deck is essentially a collection of two-card combos built on top of a solid midrange core that makes excellent use of Tawny.


Core Combos:

  • Tawny + Trinkets/Desserts – This enables efficient trades in the early game.
  • Ring of Morrigan + Trinkets – In the right matchup, this combo can be game-breaking and provides an almost unfair advantage.
  • Sir Agravaine + Frogs/Tawny – You can eliminate nearly any threat or bring your opponent’s Avatar to deathsdoor, as each Frog will deal 3 damage when attacking adjacent to Agravaine.
  • Boudicca + Frogs/Tawny – Similar to Agravaine, playing Boudicca right after casting Plague of Frogs can be devastating.
  • Ruler of Thul + Frogs – This was strong in Alpha and remains so.
  • Manuscript + Frogs – Another combo that was effective in Alpha and still holds up.
  • Pact with the Devil + Tawny – This synergy is amazing, but be mindful of the potential tempo loss.
  • Snowball + Frogs/Tawny – Once you Frogball, you never go back! 😆

Beast Package:

The Beast package is quite fun—it rarely makes a significant impact, but having a potential Lugbog Cat on turn 2 can be huge.


Card Choices:


A lot of the card choices are debatable and come down to personal preference. Generally, water minions have a harder time making the cut compared to fire minions due to Jihad.

While many Druid lists run Drums of Doom, I personally see it as more of a trap. If you’ve reached a point where its effect is beneficial, you’re already behind. I’d rather have a card that helps maintain pressure.


Sites:


Since the deck’s range is quite extreme and demanding, I don’t play a single site that doesn’t provide Threshold. So far, I’ve never had an issue reaching the required Threshold, but I also mulligan aggressively for dual/triple lands.

decks.name: BIRDS BIRDS BIRDS (1st Place League S4)
decks.primer:
Intro 🌟

Hi everyone, I'm Kevin. This is the list that I created over the course of the 4th Discord league, eventually taking the win with in the top cut. Potato Knight also ran the list, coming 3rd/4th, so effectively it went 7-0, losing only to itself.


The list is basically aggro fliers with artifact support. You slap down as many bodies as you can, split them up to avoid Poison Novas and Earthquakes, then use your aerial advantage to strategically pick your opponent apart while presenting a solid defence with free cities and bottomless pits.


Lots of the cards here are already covered by other AoA lists, so I'll stick to explaining my modifications.


Card Explanations 📄

[[Plumed Pegasus]] / [[Haast Eagle]]

The namesake of the deck, our birds (Eagles are just Pegasus with worse threshold). It took me the longest time to figure these out (thanks Duo!) but really glad I tested them. Flying [[Bosk Trolls]] might not sound impressive at first, but I believe airborne is a massively underrated ability. In Sorcery, minions are removal. Airborne removes the ability for our opponent to attack back, creating a unilateral beatdown - we can still use our minions as removal, while theirs are stuck defending. Combine this with Trinkets and you end up with an extremely annoying suite of minions (can't be easily imp'd, kolbods'd, or attacked) that usually at best is 1-for-1'd by our opponent. The best part is, we don't really care! Their low cost and our minion density means we're usually deploying a new one every turn - embracing this 'throw minions at your opponents face until they door' is the core philosophy of this deck.


Devil's Eggs

These bad boys let you win games that I otherwise consider unwinnable, or extremely grindy at best. You have many ways to get this to an annoying place (bats, cloud spirits, AoA herself), and once it sticks, it creates an immense amount of pressure for your opponent - the clock is ticking. Also cancels out Angel's Eggs, which more decks are running now to our chagrin (if you ever find a way to steal them, make sure you do!).


Maddening Bells

Bells are often seen in control/tax decks, but I think it's one of the most powerful aggro cards. Combined with your mobility and towers, you can fairly frequently land a bells on your opponent by turn 3. On the play, I've had opponents concede immediately. While one of the worst cards you can draw late game, it has led to so many blow outs I still keep it, if for nothing else but the mind games.


Cloud Spirit

A really solid 2 power minion. Sadly rarely get to play it on curve due the threshold, but a card that's as good late game as it is early - a universal blocker/attacker is a massive headache for your opponents to play around.


Headless Haunt

I was on the fence for the longest time with these (what if they fall into the Bottomless Pits!?) but now I'm a believer. Lots of people think that the randomness is a downside - it really isn't, it's more of a weird form of evasion - and that 3 cost 4 body is amazing. Play this deep in the void and watch your opponent sweat figuring out how to block it.


Sinkhole

After I tried bells, I had the realization that this is exactly what the deck needed - a way to keep the game in 'early game' for as long as possible. Sinkholes not only acts as an amazing utility card (blow up the roots combo, get rid of their threshold etc.), but is most importantly free mana denial. While you vomit fliers onto the board, your opponents are stuck with an earthquake and 3 mana. One of the best cards in the game, never remove this.


Cut Cards ✂️

Skirmishers of Mu

One of the more controversial cuts, but after testing a bunch I've decided it's for the best. While the synergy with AoA is undeniable, for a 4 cost investment (your whole turn in this deck), Skirmishers are too easy to play around and remove for opponents that know what's coming. It's one of those cards that feel great when you get to trinket it, swing for 8, but then you forget all the times it dies to a lightning bolt, or a firebolts, or swings for 3 then dies to a unicorn, etc.


Phantasmal Shades

Just barely cut, could be in sideboard. 3 cost 4 power is amazing, but it's ability requires too much baby-sitting for our liking. One theme you will notice with our minions is that they're all very 'independent'. We spread them out like little missiles and then forget about them. This causes all sorts of headaches for our opponent and allows our Avatar to boulder, swing herself, defend the sites, etc.


Daperyll Vampires

Extremely powerful against mirror match, and aggro in general. Sadly too expensive, slow, and vulnerable for our deck (read above). A great sideboard card though, I'll have a minimum of 2 of these there.


Hounds of Ondaros

I really like these guys - they're a massive PITA to remove, so don't fall under the same umbrella as Mu/Vamps/Shades - they're about as resilient/independent as it gets. Unfortunately, they also do nothing for the first 5 turns of the game, and their upside is an evasive bird with +1 power for +2 cost...so they're a cut.


Spectral Stalker

Cute turn 1 tower play aside, these don't do much but die to imps/kobolds.


Browse

Another controversial cut - this is probably the best late game top-deck in the game. Unfortunately, there will be many games where this sits dead in your hand for the first 5 turns - we often have trouble hitting 3 x Air due to the neutral sites, and 1 mana is also non-trivial due to our super low curve.


Chain Lightning

Arguably the best finisher in the game - with AoA it's basically an guaranteed kill. Unfortunately outside of that one specific use-case, I found the card to be quite underwhelming - while it can be used for 4 mana to kill 2 small minions, you usually have much better uses of 4 mana. The 2 mana mode is terrible (bolts is much better), and you'll basically never do it with 6+.


Thunderstorm

Very matchup dependant card; I just found it too clunky to use. Haven't tested with this enough though, PK insists it's the best card since Poison Nova. 4 mana is just a lot, and our list is already very tight.


Credits 🎉

Potato Knight for all the help with playtesting, repping the deck, and being awesome in general!

Wulfinite, DarthNunu, MattdogNZ, and CJ for being top blokes and encouraging me through the league!

Duo for our chat that inspired my initial testing of Plumed Pegasus!

Jacksun and Drew from OnThePlay for the initial inspiration behind playing the deck!

All the cool peeps I met playing the game on discord - you know who you are!

My amazing gf for playtesting and moral support, and pulling my foil AoA 😁


Finally, shout out to all the people that helped run the league, it was my first foray into competitive Sorcery and you guys made it super fun. Cheers!

decks.primer:
Archie Lists tend to follow similar patterns, but where mine diverges are on a couple of important points. Kettletop vs. Land Surveyor. I've land on Land Surveyor because there are many turns where I find that a land in hand immediately is much better than an additional damage here and there.


An example play that came up recently was me starting on 6 mana with no sites in hand, but I had a Craterize that I wanted to work towards. I play Landmass, pull my 7th site, play it. Play the Common Sense from hand, have 2 mana left, and get a Land Surveyor. This gives me my 8th land immediately in hand for the following turn, whereas Kettletop is not guaranteed to give me an additional land (and remember that Craterize requires you to discard a site to cast).


Another place of divergence, I still run Mirage because I want to replay certain sites like Pillar of Zeiros, Funeral Pyre, and Fields of Camlann. It also make a Fire threshold, so it's not totally useless on its own. Just gives me a little late-game utility.


Finally, most lists run Major Explosions. I have opted instead for full-on militia-attack. Another reason I like Land Surveyor over Kettletops in THIS list is because I'm regularly pumping my dudes up with spells like Onslaught, Gigantism, and Gift of the Wolf. I don't really care if they're 1 power to start with. I run 2x Assorted Animals, as well, and 1 War Horse, which is both aggressive (if they're on death's door) and defensive (if I'm on death's door - it will help me get out of harm's way).


Hope you enjoy! I've certainly been having a great time being the bad guy.

Heavy is the Crown. Top 8 Cornerstone 8/15/26
decks.primer:
"Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown.”

-Shakespeare


This list was adapted from the many Mono Fire Pathfinder lists around, not trying to pretend otherwise.


I wanted to add this primer to highlight a few tweaks for flavor/personal touch and to talk about experimenting more with the “harpy strike movement mechanic” at my most recent local Cornerstone. The deck wound up getting top 8 on 8/15/26 which I was very happy about! Role playing wise I envisioned a minion grabbing the bloody crown off their foe only to become the next “royal” target.


I made the title to this deck before playing so it would have been cool to win the Cornerstone with that title but alas I got eaten by grey wolves instead…ggs Sorcery can be a very swingy game but that’s a part of its charm!


The overall game plan for this deck stays about the same as usual. Pathfinder wants to solidify zipping around the realm reliably getting to 5-6 mana. A quick note to new Pathfinders that I learned to be helpful is to be a little patient and try trading up/waiting to strike but still use your mana. This isn’t just a turn your minions sideways kind of deck and you want to spread out your threats across the realm to help protect against board wipes. Don’t be mistaken though the deck with the right draws can become really aggressive if it needs to!


Here are a few other things that I added/observed:


-Fire Airborne minions

I really think airborne fire minions are currently under appreciated! Their diagonal movement particularly after a harpy flight can really put your opponent on the back foot.


-Giving Lethal to Dragonettes and Kobolds

It can really help win the board after your opponent commits their turn to playing a high cost minion. It gets a bit trickier when they have ward of course! I may add some fire bolts in the future to help ping targets and kill pesky early minions a bit more reliably.


-”Flying movement + Harpy Strike” (trinkets and sword /crown to boost power making the likelihood of being to target more things on the board). I had one great play to put someone on door when I flew to their 1 power token struck it and then attacked their undefended site. I think they expected to have one more turn given the position of my minions on the board as this minion did not have airborne itself.


-Unfortunately, I thought the courts would impact the meta more severely than I witnessed across my 6 games. At least so far maybe people don’t have access to the courts or simply aren’t building around them (yet). I thought a lot more exceptional “low to the ground” minions would be played so a deck like mine would take advantage of that and out value them by utilizing the lethal mechanic and the “harpy strike”. One of the LGS that I played at used a lot of fire or splash fire so I was surprised to not see that and instead faced majority of earth and root spiders galore. Askelon Pheonix was one sad fire bird :( At least I didn’t run two as I originally thought I might.


”Giants Package”

-I am not sure about this overall. Siege Giant looks great and having them possibly have charge with Balor getting charge looks very strong. At least in my 6 games Siege Giant didn’t make much of an impact compared to my other charge/strike minions. Balor did some work but I am thinking about trying a “Demon Package” instead with Fallen Angels for more Airborne support. Do you like to run the Giant package in your mono fire lists? Comment below!


Root spiders

-I guess mono fire has to have some weaknesses but this little guy can stop us in our tracks completely. If you are in a heavy earth meta not sure how to stick in enough casting ability for future lava flows. Any ideas would be appreciated. Can anything else in Pathfinder lists stop them? Splash more air mobility? Risks threshold screw though. Let me know!


Silver Bullet over Tool Box?

Not sure but maybe future iterations use exceptional spells for more diversity/aoe capability? Bullet might be too slow or even taxed making it harder to cast and play on the same turn.


RoM? or not to RoM? that is the question…

-With so few spell casters maybe RoM isn’t even worth running? Pathfinder doesn’t seem nearby much of the realm to use this so I may substitute for Flame of the First One or another weapon?


Let me know your thoughts, particularly if you are a Pathfinder enjoyer as well. I am curious about other mono element Pathfinder builds such as mono water or earth so be on the lookout for those lists on my end!


-Telos

"We do not command fire. Ngamahu lends it, and Hinekora returns it." - Lavianga, advisor to Kaom - Path of Exile

6th Place Gen Con - #1 [[Necromancer]] - 08/01/26


It was a great pleasure to participate in the 2026 Gen Con Grand Contest, let alone finish in the top 8.


When a [[Sorcerer]] sees a [[Necromancer]] at the table, thoughts of water always rise to the surface. The water Necromancer deck pioneered by [[@Ceej]] still inspires and terrifies players to this day, and at Gen Con I hoped to do the same... but with fire (F).


During the Grand Contest, over half of my opponents remarked they would have played or mulliganed differently had they known how different my list was. And while my hopes of winning the Contest were washed away after Round 6 as water splashed down from the convention center ceiling, I am still happy to present an off-meta Necromancer build that is as surprising as it is explosive.


SPELLBOOK: The minion package is fairly standard for a mono fire deck. It includes 18 Exceptional minions with 3 Towns to help get them out a little quicker. Many of these minions are chosen simply for their Charge effect, to get as much damage on the board as soon as possible.


  • My favorite inclusion is the [[Siege Giant]], which can throw a weaker ally here through the air to a nearby location. Throw your [[Necromancer]] up and start making [[Skeleton]]s on your opponent's Sites. Throw [[Sacred Scarabs]] into position and get ready to [[Detonate]]. Equip a [[Torshammar Trinket]] and throw another [[Siege Giant]] for best results.


  • [[Detonate]] is the MVP of this deck. At (1) mana this allows the potential for any of your artifacts or minions (including [[Skeleton]]s) to be a localized [[Minor Explosion]]. For (3) mana, summon [[Sacred Scarabs]] and [[Detonate]] them to deal 6 damage. Use [[Betrayal]] to take control of enemy minions and blow them up as well. Use your artifacts with impunity against decks that run [[Swap]], and make them think twice about stealing your [[Ring of Morrigan]] or [[Poisonous Dagger]].


  • [[Gift of the Serpent]] and [[Poisonous Dagger]] both give your minions Lethal, which helps make efficient trades. Give Lethal to [[Colicky Dragonettes]], [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]], or even a [[Skeleton]]. Combine either with a [[Blaze of Glory]] for a spectacular board wipe.


  • [[Blaze of Glory]] into [[Warp Spasm]] is one of the most potent combos in Sorcery. With a 4 or 5 power minion, this combo can deal 16-20 damage in one turn.


  • [[Lava Flow]] sends [[Root Spiders]], [[Coy Nixies]], and other bottom-dwelling pets back where they belong: the cemetery. [[Siege Giant]]s and [[War Horse]]s can also position us to cast [[Lava Flow]] in the perfect line.


  • [[Chains of Prometheus]] allows you to control the enemy board state by forcing our opponent to tap their strongest minion. This is a symmetrical effect that also punishes you, but with the creation of new [[Skeleton]]s every turn, you should be able to power through.


  • Play a game of hot potato with your [[Rolling Boulder]]! Tap an unanswered [[Skeleton]] to roll a boulder from your opponents site, removing threats and causing damage along the way. Then summon a minion with Charge to push it again on the very same turn. If they summon a minion in hopes of rolling your boulder, [[Detonate]] it in their face like a Saturday morning cartoon.


ATLAS: Sites have been chosen carefully to counter opposing strategies, especially against earth and water strategies. Your mulligan will depend on what Avatar is seated across from you at the table.


  • Deserts are key for dealing with wards and controlling enemy [[Necromancer]]s.


  • [[Mobbed Court]], [[Vindictive Nation]], and [[River of Blood]] allow you to deal some incidental damage while preventing enemy healing.


  • [[Kor Crematory]] is great against [[Archimago]] and [[Deathspeaker]] decks. Trying to mulligan for this card when facing either of these Avatars is a good idea.


  • [[Sinkhole]]s can disrupt the opponent's early game, providing you a few more turns to safely produce [[Skeleton]]s.


  • [[Hellmouth]] and [[Vesuvius]] are ways to deal with burrowed or submerged minions. While [[Hellmouth]] serves as [[Earthquake]] protection for your [[Skeleton]]s, it also allows you to use a [[Toolbox]]to cast a [[Vile Imp]] underground.


  • [[River of Flame]] allows you to use [[Disintegrate]], [[Immolation]], or [[Betrayal]] to target burrowed minions. Try to place this on a different row or column than your Avatar's or near the potential underground threats.


  • [[Wuthering Heights]] is the only air site in the deck. How could you not love "[[Siege Giant]]: The Site?" It's especially good when you place it close to your [[Necromancer]]'s [[Skeleton]] production line.


  • If you do not plan on using courts or the many Unique utility sites feel free to check out this variation of the deck that uses [[Peasant Revolt]]: https://curiosa.io/decks/cmnajthf800n404l2lj6um5wx?tab=view

7/14/2026 -

Current Meta ((E)/(F), (W)/(A), Mono (F))

Archimago, Pathfinder, Imposter, Necromancer, Persecutor, Battlemage


Maidenless Motherless Croneless

[[Waveshaper]] has been seen as a mid tier avatar for quite a while but with the release of gothic I believe it's able to not only hang with the cool kids at the meta table but also come out ahead of most of the meta with the right cards.


This deck maxes out at 6 cost spells and is low enough to the ground to keep up with the faster aggro strategies. Controlling the game and pressuring the opponent is the gameplan and surprising your opponent with a 10-20 damage turn is a real possibility. A healthy smattering of removal and an absolute boatload of movement effects make this a fun deck to pilot.


Opening the Game ###########

Sites are extremely important for this deck to perform well and there is a lot of site disruption out there. The decision to cut out as many non essential elite and unique sites is completely valid with cards like [[peasant revolt]] and [[heirloom lost]] running loose in the meta, but even with a decision like this we have so many powerful options in the ordinary and exceptional slots. [[autumn river]], [[river rapids]], [[maelstrom]], or [[kelp cavern]] tend to be my favorite turn 1 plays.


[[overflow]] is such a powerful card that it can often times be one of the best openings in our game plan to get to 5/6 mana as soon as possible. We run 3 main deck overflow and 3 [[toolbox]] with 6 possible overflow draws.

Some notable overflow options to cast while you have them in hand are [[babbling brook]] to get you to a 5 mana turn often times without needing to worry about anything pressuring you early.

[[bog]] is a new include in my deck specifically to slow down a [[persecutor]] or [[battlemage]] and to completely stop a [[pathfinder]] or [[imposter]] from developing early with pathfinder by forcing them to take a turn to get back to an edge of their sites.


If no overflow combination is in hand my other favorite options would be [[troll bridge]] and [[thin ice]] being a classic turn two sites to play but if you have a [[coy nixie]] in hand it can be the perfect combination to start holding down your side of the board from enemies entering your water. [[mudflow]] makes coy nixie even more annoying than it already is for your opponent by constantly dipping underneath your thin ice each turn and popping up for free on your turn.

[[tufted turtles]], [[shellycoat]], [[aino]], [[lugbog cat]], and [[order of the sacred oak]] are also great opening hand minions to begin pressuring early or defensively developing your own board presence without being pressured yourself.


Mid Game ###########

Setting up card advantage if possible is almost always best in this turn 4 or 5. [[algor omphalos]], [[dank omphalos]], [[maiden, mother, crone]], [[lilith]], and [[captain baldassare]] are the types of cards that can open up that greater advantage for us. Playing these on a home row [[river rapids]] can give you the opportunity to safely cast them and use them to attack from your back row.


if you managed to ramp into a turn 4 fifth site drop you have some very interesting plays that can completely shut off your opponent.

[[atlantean fate]] is an aura that can just flat out win you the game on turn 4 by shutting off an opponents sites and leaving them with no threshold.

[[archangel raphael]] being cast right next to them after you ramp into their side can be overwhelming.

[[giant shark]] can just come down underneath your body of water and wreak havoc on anything being cast or moving in this body of water.


At 34 minions we have plenty of strong options to come down during these turns.

I tend to hold onto [[abaddon succubus]], [[ruler of thul]] and [[assimilator snail]] until I have a good reason to play them for removal or massive damage.


End Game ###########

Once we get to 5 mana I will typically stop playing sites and begin flooding their sites with specific minions on them. If we draw [[lord of lies]], [[mester stoor worm]], [[the green knight]], or [[call of the sea]] we would typically draw that mana if we don't already have it and spend the turn to impact the board in such a more impactful way whether it be by dealing a massive hit to our opponent or wiping out all of their minions in one turn. This is when we look at how we can finish our opponent off and try to deal the maximum amount of damage possible.


[[mester stoor worm]] is a huge threat with 7 power, [[mudflow]] can make this minion a much harder to deal with threat by giving it the ability to be safely summoned submerged to come out and attack next turn or better yet just use a [[meat hook]] to pull our opponent into our body of water.


[[lord of lies]] even with his recent nerf is another massive threat especially with so many ways to pull or force our opponent into another location. [[undertow]], [[riptide]], [[coy nixie]], [[nelly longarms]] and [[meat hook]] are all excellent ways to achieve this. It hits big and it can be used as removal for multiple minions at once or just be used to get an extra hit from another minion onto our opponent.


[[giant shark]] is the final big finisher in the deck rounding it out to 7 major threats total. This minion is so special in fact that I have an entire section later on explaining how to use it properly.


Using Sharks ###########

Movement effects are the sharks best friend, the shark will most likely not survive very long because the first thing out of our opponents mouth when they read it for the first time is "oh shit you mean every water site?" There is a two card combo with the shark and [[the rack]] which is very funny to use but it's too cute to have it be used competitively.


DO NOT place a shark down into a full board unless you want it to die and kill some of our opponents minions. All they need to do is chump any minion into a water site nearby to have our pet swim right to any water site of their choice to then take care of it with some nearby or adjacent removal effect.


ONLY place a shark for the following reasons.

  1. We fully intend to be able to use it the turn it comes down by having movement effects ready to be used that turn, [[coy nixie]] or [[nelly longarms]] on the board already, [[riptide]] ready in hand with the mana to cast it, a [[meat hook]] already on a minion in position, or an [[undertow]] ready to move our opponent.
  2. We can turn off its ability for a turn cycle to set up a massive attack the following turn. [[bog]] and [[babbling brook]] are able to put a leash on our pet for a turn.
  3. We have a sparse enough board state that the shark can safely survive a turn in play. This is usually a gamble
  4. We have an [[assimilator snail]] in hand ready to come down and become a previously murdered shark. What's better than 3 sharks? How about 5 of them.


The more sites we can move our opponent through the more damage we can do, [[meat hook]] is particularly brutal since it can usually pull them through at least 2 water sites and sometimes 3, each of those water sites they enter is 5 damage, if you are able to also attack then that is a 20 point damage turn and deaths door from one single minion.


[[giant shark]] is a double edged sword, if our opponent moves us in our own body of water the shark will bite us and if we summon any minions into it's body of water the shark will travel to that minion to fight it. There are a few notable minions and one site that are able to survive being summoned into the sharks tank and also allow the shark to live as well.

  1. [[order of the sacred oak]] - ward breaks
  2. [[tufted turtles]] - tanks the first hit
  3. [[sacred stag]] - ward breaks
  4. [[archangel raphael]] - ward breaks
  5. [[the green knight]] - big defense stat tanks the hit
  6. [[mudflow]] - acts as a safe place to summon new minions since it is land.


One last note for the shark is that our ability allows us to perform a "tank change". Since the shark has waterbound it becomes disabled while on land, once we summon what we need to summon we are able to flood the position that the shark is on to effectively turn it back on and pass the turn.



When to Flood ###########

Our ability is powerful on [[waveshaper]] and it almost always takes the opponent by surprise when they learn that the site we choose to flood is not only NEARBY but it remains flooded UNTIL WE DO IT AGAIN. This give us amazing reach into our opponents side of the board.


There are only two reasons to use our ability. Sometimes we care about both but most of the time it boils down to one reason or the other.

  1. Flooding to create a water site where there was not one before.
  2. Tapping down minions without submerge.


Aggro strategies may require us to tap down a site earlier than we would normally want to. [[mazuj ifrit]] is an early threat that is very good to tap down since it will slowly sap the life from your opponent. One other situation where it’s fine to use our ability early is if we have an overflow in hand to tap down a minion or two and still develop our sites.


Our ability can be used for more than just tapping things nearby down. If we have a shark on board and a pull effect or two we can potentially create an extra water site for the opponent to stumble into for an extra 5 damage.


That flooded site of an opponent may also be the perfect jumping in point for a waterbound minion to attack or if we are afraid the opponent has an earthquake or bury in hand, we can simply flood the site for any minion to attack into and feel a sense of safety that it cannot be buried.


If none of these options are available then we can instead draw an extra site for the turn.


Toolbox ###########

There are 3 [[toolbox]] in the deck and I will never be upset to draw one because they are so very useful. I chose to go with 7 toolbox choices and will go over each choice here.

  1. [[overflow]] : This is self explanatory, 5 copies in the deck now. Sites are powerful and ramp is so important.
  2. [[drown]] : This acts as the standard removal slot in the toolbox collection but it also acts as the artifact removal which is sometimes more important.
  3. [[ice lance]] : This is the standard death's door finisher of the toolbox side of the collection, it can also be used as removal or mask breaking against [[imposter]].
  4. [[riptide]] : If I had to choose one magic in the waveshaper's arsenal that is it's bread and butter, this would be that spell. I would run 10 of this spell if I could.
  5. It can move yourself out of harms way.
  6. It can move your opponent into harms way.
  7. It can trigger a [[giant shark]] attack.
  8. It can disrupt a [[pathfinder]]'s way.
  9. It can force warded minions into unsafe water locations.
  10. It can force stealthed minions into unsafe water locations.
  11. It can be used as a psuedo death's door finisher.
  12. It replaces itself with another card after you use it.
  13. [[return to nature]] : This is another utility spell that other waveshapers have utilized much better than I ever have by using it on themselves in conjunction with [[deep sea mermaids]] or [[kelp cavern]] to reuse a powerful spell that was put into your cemetery. But it is very useful against [[archimago]], [[deathspeaker]], [[flamecaller]], and any cards that want to use things in a cemetery.
  14. [[extinguish]] : A recent addition to my collection due to the amount of fire minions are in the meta currently and the only real way to deal with [[jihad]] or the dreaded [[drought]].
  15. [[makeshift barricade]] : If you find yourself on deaths door against an aggro deck very quickly this might be the solution. It has saved me more than once by nullifying deaths door finishers like [[zap]] or [[firebolt]]. It also protects us from the inevitable [[craterize]] that [[archimago]] is so fond of.


Silver Bullet ###########

There is a single [[silver bullet]] in my list and it gives me the option for 3 very powerful exceptional spells.

  1. [[swap]] : This is such an incredible utility spell, being able to trigger a shark for removal or using this to steal a powerful artifact right out of your opponents hands and replacing it with one of your own minions is just so satisfying. This can also shut off something like an omphalos by placing it on your site where your opponent cannot cast minions to, this does not protect you from the magics or auras cast from there.
  2. [[snowball]] : This spell is removal and finisher wrapped into one. Great to use your own minions like [[tufted turtles]], [[order of the sacred oak]], [[sacred stag]], [[archangel raphael]], and [[the green knight]] since none of these will likely die from this due to ward or just great defensive abilities. Make sure you roll as many of your opponents minions in the ball as well directly into them and dealing a massive blow, bonus points if you cast [[plague of frogs]] right before this goes off.
  3. [[meat hook]] : This is a powerful effect to be given to any minion on your team, it can pull your opponent into your location and trigger a [[giant shark]] attack that can sometimes just put our opponent on death's door. It can also be used to pull our avatar out of harm's way or back into a body of water. It is a bit awkward to tap for [[silver bullet]] and tap to use this ability so it might be removed for [[wave of eviction]].
