decks.primer:
Huge thanks to GOODLUCKBAD, For giving tips and being a huge inspiration

https://curiosa.io/decks/cm7mf7rrm001ele03o1xweti9?tab=view


AGGRESSIVE WATER? BUT HOW IS IT SO DEFENSIVE?


[[Druid]] is always the answer. Trying to play [[Druid]] in the year of 2026 is different. Without tawny respawn you have to fully utilize the rest of his kit. This wasnt an easy task, one that i probably still havent fully realised. But the revelation that led to this list was found in the deepest of dungeons.


Deck origin:

On a late evening; A while after i'd given up on the quest to play druid in a deck I enjoy, one that i felt utilized his kit to the fullest. I was playing VS my boy GOODLUCKBAD on the sorcerers summit. He was piloting his signature [[Spellslinger]] water list. After the match i said to myself, ive tried alot of color combinations for druid, but never mono colored. So unbeknownst to him i copied his masterpiece and swapped [[Spellslinger]] for [[Druid]]. A few games in with the deck i felt a breath of fresh air. I didnt win them all, however its strength commanded respect. Alot of the deck changed since that however there are still plenty of remenants.


Realising the potential of the unbroken body of water, consistency with spells such as [[Riptide]] and sites like [[Undertow]] and [[Maelström]]. Aswell as access to double Omphalos.

A little bit of tweaking to the sites. Maximizing the ammount of movement and adding some spells like coy nixie was all i did in the beginning. The beast had been unleashed.


Minions were flying left and right. Being dragged in by an [[Innsmouth Dock]], [[Riptided]] onto a river, pushed from said river onto a [[Wuthering Heights]], Bounced onto a [[Troll Bridge]]. All while being pinged down. This might be a juicer fellas.


Some time after these changes i felt comfortable enough to make even more changes, No more mixes, no more rivers. Alltough rivers still have a place in my heart im currently trying out more meta cards such as [[Thin Ice]], and utility colorless sites like [[Sinkhole]]. The rivers are certainly good and could come back in the future. The curve also lowered as i realised utilizing [[Bruin]] early is a way to success.


Strategy:

Tapping and flipping our avatar early is now the name of the game. I mulligan my entire hand most games unless i have a [[Lugbog Cat]], or a real 4 mana threat in hand.

The plan is to establish a good board presence early. Putting down minions such as [[Lugbog Cat]], [[Sea raider]] and [[Adept Illusionist]]. With all this we can safely flip our avatar. Playing out both bruin and someone else to push the pressure with some real threats.

This almost always happens on turn 5. The previous turn i should have put a 4 mana minion on board. Now it is time for our fluffy friend. Aswell as (hopefully) another hard to deal with dude. Prime examples would be [[Failed Mutation]], [[Sacred Stag]] or [[Captain baldassare]]. This swarm of minions will be hard to deal with. [[Earthquake]] is hopeless, [[Poison Nova]] is weird. Suffering from an [[Atlantean Fate]] is our biggest trouble here so focus on staying spread out and keeping atleast one of your guys alive.

This heavy pressure can be enhanced with a [[Sinkhole]]. After taking away their 4th mana i dont see many ways of dealing with all of this.


During most games i only draw 1 site at the beginning of my turn. Thats before flipping. Even after flipping i keep drawing spells. Simply tapping for sites. Trying to keep up the momentum of the double threat and draw through to as many good cards as possible. Unless i ofcourse have access to a game ender like [[Atlantean Fate]] or missing one threshold for [[Mesmerism]].


In the case that you didnt draw anything aggressive even after mulligans. The luck isnt out. This deck is great at fighting in the pocket. We still have a great defensive plan. No aggressive minions on hand can only mean one thing. Only defensive spells on hand. From here on out we try to utilize our [[Riptides]], [[Coy Nixie]] and [[Nelly Longarms]] in conjunction with the sites to remove any threats and bring forth 2 for 1s. This act of attrition will sooner or later end up in a draw that allows you to swing the momentum and end the game. Dont be afraid to sacrifice little [[Bruin]] if you have to.


A mix of these two gameplans is what happens most games, Being aggressive with the fluffy guy and using thorns and spells for removal. Always looking to spend as little cards for as much impact as possible.

This needs to happen since your only way to draw cards in this deck is Omphalos. We do not have the privelege of being able to tap to draw sites or turning skeletons into huge threats.


Theres also a secret minigame here that wins many games. Trying to pull the enemy avatar onto your sites. It will cause most players to panic. This provides alot of extra damage. Hard to defend against and leads to coy nixie and riptide being a death door finisher. More on this later on.


Tawny...

[[Tawny]] shouldnt be compared to her older brother bear. They are not the same and do not serve the same purpose. I try to get as many hits in as possible with her. Some games [[Tawny]] will deal 5 damage due to nobody wanting to spend cards to remove her. If they end up doing it later down the line it just feels worse because they ended up paying 5 life for their greed. Other use cases could be such as popping wards on critical threats, Going in for that last damage on a minion that survived a fight with 1 life or sacrificing her to a [[Troll Bridge]] if thats your only alley of attack. Drowning a [[Sacred Stag]] on [[Thin Ice]] is something she excels at.

At the end of the day going in for 1 or 2 damage is still good. How many times have you been 1 away from dooring someone?


SPELLS:

We begin to summarize the cards and maybe talk some use cases in this deck.


[[Atlantean Fate]]

Best card in the entire game. Draw an extra site for turn if you have this in hand please!


[[Ring of morrigan]]

Sweet on the defense in this deck. Sometimes you're missing that single ping to kill a minion. Otherwise obviously as a finisher which water doesnt have many of. Hold it in hand vs water decks. Play it freely vs any other element.


[[Torshammar Trinket]]

Currently only at one because you want a juiced hand not one filled with trinkets. Water minions already pack a punch aswell. Could be two but i dont know what to cut. Pairs really well with tawny to strike sites or vacuum up some skellies. Love to trinket a fey changeling aswell to get in some extra chip damage.


[[The rack]]

New addition to the deck so i havent tried it too much yet. Must feel good if you can get in atleast one hit with it. If the enemy avatar is on your side its very easy and the damage will jump through the roof with your thorns. Comboes with [[Plague of Frogs]]. Slapping it on [[Tawny]] to have her hit and die and maybe a cat can pick it up and strike again isnt bad at all. With enemy stretched to your side the game should be fairly easy to play.


[[Toolbox]]

Finishers, movement, utility. Only at two because the collection in water is horrifyingly bad.


[[Truesight Crossbow]]

Classic mono water death door technology. Many usecases for this one. Could be put on your [[Druid]] for that extra ping when someone is in your business. Other things include putting it on a stag to keep it even safer than it is. Killing airborne units, ETC.

A favorite is putting it on a [[Coy Nixie]] to deal with their [[Coy Nixie]] while keeping yours alive.


[[Dank Omphalos]], [[Algor Omphalos]]

Super good, one of these on board feels like game secured. Infinite access to cards. Easier to play than in most decks because you can always play it and summon bruin for atleast some board presence.


[[Meat hook]]

Sneaky meathook to pull their avatar into your territory. Pulled through thorns + trollbridge from bruin provides a respectful 9 damage. Probably forcing them to discard and ending the game on the spot. I only play with 1 because drawing two in one game would suck so much ass.


[[Adept Illusionist]]

Crazy good with [[Thin ice]]. Sacrificing a brother after riptiding or undertowing an enemy minion onto the ice. Early chip damage and lining up [[Snowball]] in the midgame. Aswell as working togheter with tawny to take down a 3 power minion basically for free. These guys end up being utility for anything that you might need, even sacrificing one for a trollbridge or sacrificing both of them incase you need to take drastic measures against a big guy in your territory.

If cemetary hate goes beyond what we have today this will go away. Things like [[Kor Crematory]], [[Mismanaged Mortuary]] and [[Bureau of Occult Control]] makes thes guys boring to play.


[[Pied Piper of hameln]]

A card im always on the edge about. Tokens arent in every game and this card is often useless. When its good its nice because it can really ruin certain decks aswell as hinder a necromancer for a couple of turns. One day this might change into another 3 or 4 drop if the meta doesnt call for it anymore.


[[Polar Explorers]]

These guys line up perfectly with our gameplan and are almost always happy to see. Main reason for them is getting [[Bruin]] active as quick as possible. Great to summon minions in your backrow safe from [[Gargantulas]] and [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]] etc. And avoiding back breaking defensive sites.


[[Aino]]

Puts pressure on an opponent and might force out a rootspider that we will later [[Geyser]]. Its not the most OP unique but when it does its thing it feels nice.

In mono water she kind of serves the purpose as a death door finisher with stealth. Definetley keep it in hand if you draw it late unless theres a more effective finisher.


[[Coy Nixie]]

Certainly feels overpowered here. She will open up attacks that werent previously discovered. Drag in the enemy avatar towards your sites. Functions as a death door finisher aswell if your opponent stepped up to cast a [[Poison Nova]] or other. She is one of the better minions in this deck.

Popping wards. The list goes on.

A key tech ive found works well is looking to build out sites on the third row in your opponents territory. This provides a safe haven when you flip for [[Bruin]] for avoiding atlantean fate. But more importantly serves as a spawning point for Nixie. Where you can instantly pull in the enemy avatar and potentially riptide them onto your thorns.


[[Fey Changeling]]

Used on the attack when opponent plays a minion infront of your [[Lugbog Cat]] and just start pushing damage. Damage is one of the most important things in this list. We want to end the game quickly and with as few roadblocks as possible.

Used defensively it simply buys you a turn but that could be enough. Way better on the offense.

After its been deployed i just look to hit an unblocked site, participate in killing a high powered minion or blocking.


[[Lugbog Cat]]

Just a great minion and when combined with a pond its such heavy pressure that opponent often folds before they can get their foot in the game.

Not much to say here other than to keep these in opening hand and if you have two it might be worth to go looking for a pond.


[[Nelly Longarms]]

Threaten their avatar with a drag. Play it on river rapids or use riptides to reposition. Good minion that makes it awkward to play.


[[Order of the Sacred Oak]]

At two since im so scared of [[Bane of Aventis]] but other than that i dont know why im only on two. I think i drew them too much and felt that their impact was lower than expected.

Alot of good decks will have access to a silencing effect, a desert or other that kind of ruins the purpose of them.


[[Sea raider]]

Great "Counter" to [[Plague of frogs]] and Foot Soldiers. This guy lets our hand be thick and gives access to other elements spells which can prove to be useful. This guy is meant to die in the name of card draw.


[[Abaddon Succubus]]

One of the goats here, 3 damage on flipped side. Pulling into a wuthering heights. Well you can imagine the damage. Meanwhile we are healing and leaving a 3 power body on the board. Just the best minion and will be a keep in opening hand. Works well with Geyser as people will try to play far away from it however do not expect an airborne attack.


[[Captain Baldassare]]

Love this ability and provides very interesting games. Certain choices are tricky to make but provide super interesting lines of play. Discarding bangers also feels soothing.


[[Failed Mutation]]

Beast at staying around. With this classic beater we can secure a healthym, strong boardstate alongside [[Bruin]]


[[Lord of unland]]

Great to power up [[Bruin]] when you are in a defensive position. Can also chase around the opponents [[Coy Nixie]] to get them off problematic sites. Very strong now that water is so popular giving the upper hand in trades. I will usually try to walk him in under opponents water site and go in for a strike further down the line. Often hes good to just stay submerged.

Comboes with [[Geyser]] and [[Floodplain]] in non water matchups.


[[Ruler of thul]]

This is the bomb of all bombs. Bruin + tawny + ruler is 10 damage with only 1 card from hand!!! Use him wisely and dont just play it whenever. The setup here is very important and do not greed to cast it early.


[[Sacred Stag]]

Stays around, It is a boring minion but very good. These guys feel extra good into another water deck that just played a stag because their stag cannot attack into your thorns. So you will keep a stag and they wont!


[[Selfsame Simulacrum]]

Selfsame is my favorite water card of all time. The ceiling on this card is endless and ive never experienced a match where i hadnt had the opportunity to cast it. Copy a [[Morgana le fay]], [[Gargantula]] their [[Gargantula]] or just copy one of your dudes. If you have other minions to cast i would wait until a juicer hits the bord that you can copy.


[[Archangel Raphael]]

Extra good when you pull their avatar to your side or if you manage to build your sites into their row. Alot of decks cannot finish you if you have the ward + [[Bruin]] or a [[Makeshift Barricade]]. Super grateful for this instant strike as dealing the killing blow is hard in mono water.


[[Questing Beast]]

Here comes another way to kill them at door or simply just deal alot of damage. Both of my 5 drops have a reason to exist in this deck. At that point in the game i am looking for a way to end my opponent and this just helps that.


[[Lord of lies]]

Is obviously quite an overpowered minion. Its hard not to include and helps alot when games drag out due to unforeseen reasons. I think the deck can function without it and sometimes i feel bad playing it because its so OP.


[[The green knight]]

Is a saving grace when you have fallen behind. With thorns this guy will deal 4 damage, 7 on a [[Troll Bridge]]. That is enough to boardwipe an entire offense. He can also be used aggressively in some capacity to tap down blockers. Comboes super well at door with [[Bruin]] and [[Makeshift Barricade]] making a nuisance to reach your avatar.


[[Plague of Frogs]]

The frogs are super versatile. They pick up trinkets, Adept users of [[The rack]] and friends of [[Ruler of thul]]. The blocking potential slows the enemies game down heavily.

They can also go gather drowned rings and other goodies.


[[Geyser]]

[[Rootspider]] puts a stick in our wheels but the solution even draws you a card. Airborne can be hard to deal with and who doesnt like an airborne lord of lies?

This is a great card but i will cycle it for another card if i draw it early on and dont see any use case for it.


[[Pollimorph]]

[[Tawny]] can cast it and the frog cant even enter your site. The downsides to this card are almost non existent. Thanks Eriks Curiosa.


[[Riptide]]

Movement, This deck is all about movement so why not have a really good one that works for both minions and avatars. The icing on the cake is that it draws you a card. Its also used on door to dig through your deck to find that sweet finisher you are looking for. Sweeping away blockers. Love to see a [[Riptide]] in the mid game and is one of the foundational cards that make this deck work.

I could easily go to 4 of these but having one in the toolbox also seems worth it to me.


[[Ice lance]]

Might look weird but we need another finisher. Obviously they cannot banish it using [[Legion of Gall]] or put a tax on it with [[Bureau of Occult Control]]. Which is why i dont just play another [[Toolbox]].

I save it for door unless i see a sweet 2 for 1 potential off [[Tawny]]. Such as killing a Vile imp and a Dragonette. Maybe killing off 2 [[Adept Illusionist]] is worth it. Im not sure.


[[Swap]]

1 swap because even though it is strong ive found that its a little bit situational. I think i can safely go to 2 and still be happy but 3 feels way too much when i am looking to put out minions. It is very versatile because it can be used on deaths door, steal things, put unsuspecting minions on a thin ice and more.


[[Mesmerism]]

Just game winning.


[[Stormy seas]]

Found that i needed a card that was non targeted removal to get around ward and stealth but also deal with artifacts. It can put a stop for someone trying to set up a huge ruler turn.

The ceiling is so high and for only 1 more mana than [[Drown]]. But 2 less mana than [[Call of the Sea]] which feels way too expensive and combined with the movement in our list can make for similar results.


[[Snowball]]

Last spell and it is another death door finisher!! Yes, when we eventually door them we need alot of things in our deck that we can find to kill them. Heres another one. Deals alot of damage at times if you need to. Ive also used this as a delivery mechanism for [[Bruin]] picking up a 3 powered enemy guy to kill them, Deal 3 to their avatar and then another 4 with [[Bruin]]. I like to keep my possibilites open and hence im playing with so many different deaths door finishers. This style of deckbuilding has proven to feel very flexible rather than just maindecking 3 snowballs or something like that. They all serve a similar purpose but do so in different ways.


SITES:


[[Bureau of Occult Control]]

I lacked when playing versus [[Imposter]]. This is here to remedy that. Also great because i am only playing 2 [[Toolbox]] so the pain in the ass isnt huge. Also, make sure to draw another site and play this last if you have peculiar port on hand.

I'll mulligan this if im not versus [[Imposter]] or [[Archimago]] in hopes of better sites.


[[Floodplain]]

Unleaches alot of cards that relate to your body of water. Great when your 4th site isnt a water site so you can still cast [[Mesmerism]] on turn 4 if needed. Making [[Rootspider]] bad is also a big positive.


[[Innsmouth dock]]

Enables thorns to finish someone off. Played upfront it also allows you to play minions safely in your back row and then pull them in to be ready for attack.


[[Maelström]]

More pulling, More goodness. Same as dock it can be played up front to pull your minions up. Full reach over the board versus another water deck feels real sweet, especially when your sites are spiky.


[[Mirror realm]]

Goes in any deck right? You have OP sites and you can have more. I have had 2 [[River Rapids]], A [[Wuthering heights]], and an [[Innsmouth Dock]]. Makes the game impossible to play. All thanks to mirror realm.


[[Peculiar port]]

Keeps up your hand size. Kind of a nonbo with Bureau and i had to cut something so im only playing 2. Great when you manage to cast a [[Horrible hybrids]] and make opponent discard a card due to a [[Troll bridge]] in the same game. Your hand size will be massive compared to opponent almost being in a topdecking situation without sacrificing any board presence.


[[Pond]]

[[Lugbog cat]], [[Sacred Stag]] and [[Questing beast]]. All out early swarming the board. A turn 2 cat followed by a turn 3 cat is breathtaking. I dont even hate this site later on in the game as it can allow for double casting for example a [[Pollimorph]] and [[Questing Beast]] while at 6 mana.


[[River Rapids]]

You know how this deck plays by now. Push them around. i like to have ordinary rivers to work with this aswell but we will see.


[[Sinkhole]]

Destroy the OP sites. Keep them off mana after you played some big stuff. Or keep it around if you need the mana yourself. Its a very versatile site. In some use cases you can even use it to pop your own site if they have a [[Lord of lies]] trying to get in. Its fringe but has won me games.


[[Tadpole pool]]

Generates some blockers, Attackers for [[Ruler of thul]] and snowball ammo.


[[Thin ice]]

Super good to kill minions free of charge with [[Coy nixie]], [[Adept illusionist]] and [[Tawny]]


[[Troll bridge]]

4 damage with thorns!!! they must be forced to discard a card!!! This staple site gets leveled up in [[Druid]] and has led many opponents to discarding multiple cards after pulling their avatar over this troll several times.


[[Undertow]]

MORE MOVEMENT. If i have to play this as a second site i will just put up my avatar so that i can get [[Bruin]] active quicker.


[[Wuthering heights]]

Last mention of movement, sorry but this site is OP. Be wary of playing your minions onto it versus earth.

A neat trick with this site is the mind games. Now your opponent has to play around a non existent [[Grapple shot]].


Collection:


Mono water collection is bad to say the least. Not much in way of aura removal or finishers.


[[Just a rock]]

Banish their ring seems good but you could also swap it.


[[Led astray]]

Sort of here as a non conditional [[Riptide]] you can walk minions into [[The void]] or just pull their avatar closer.


[[Old salt anchorman]]

The only real anti [[Coy nixie]] technology. Since it prevents the drowning of thin ice. Prevents [[Avatar of air]] of abusing your poor minions.


[[Riptide]]

Has been explained above. One in toolbox. Love that it draws you a card so your hand size stays up.


[[Drown]]

Removal.


[[Extinguish]]

As we are not in air this is all we get to remove auras. 2 for 1 when they play a jihad!! super good.


[[Horrible hybrids]]

Peculiar port.


[[Ice lance]]

The only finisher here! Cast it off any of your minions.


[[Makeshift Barricade]]

Excellent!! Traversing your sites to deal a finisher is already hard. Then getting through a barrier of 3 and dealing another damage. This card can easily buy you multiple turns.


[[Helpful hob]]

Never actually cast this but i see a world when lord of lies deals 18 damage.

decks.primer:
F/W/A SIA Mage


Sirprise It's Agrrovaine


A unique 3 element threshold intensive deck with high roll potential.


The thresholds are designed primary around 3/2/1 - F/W/A respectively. Primary goal is to get to 2/2 F/W, splashing air mostly for grapple shots and toolbox goodies. The third fire covers Morgana and Immolation.


Note: Technically new threshold reqs are 3/3/1 due to the addition of plague of frogs


The Mulligan


You're primary goal for an opening hand is two things, hit threshold and have a decent three drop.


Openers


Site placement is critical for success in more difficult games. The most important site you place is the your center forward site. What site you want there is match up dependent. If you're against aggro you want a troll bridge. If you're the aggressor whether your primary launch pad is water or land makes a big difference. The answer is that you want the opposite of whatever you're playing against. As an example if you're playing against a geomancer, you want your launch pad to be a water site because it allows you to drop threats safely to apply pressure on a site that can't have things buried on it. If you're against water you want a land site as a launch pad so your opponent can't drown minions on your own forward sites.


3 Drop & Sink'em

If on the play with the correct threshold play a sinkhole as your third site. Followed by a three drop minion, such as a cat or dragonettes. Immediately followed by blowing up the sinkhole to knock your opponent back down to one mana. On the next turn a good follow up is a grapple, a second three drop, or a swap.


Red Rover, I send my Doggie Over

If you're opening hand contains a Cerberus and a Grapple Shot, Cerberus can be forcefully moved away. Meaning an undefended avatar can take 10 damage on your turn 4, 3 if you started with a core or a P. Stone. If you're reading removal, this can be followed up by moving your battlemage forward to teleport Cerberus back safely depending on the match up.


Mini Combos


Dragonettes + Shrink

With a spellcaster (usually your battlemage) in position to shrink a minion along with a dragonettes that can be moved into position or cast from hand into line of site unobstructed allows you to shrink and kill a minion with your dragonettes.


Sir Pelleas + Blaze

A fun interaction unique to this element combination, elevated by the current meta of water. Pelleas free movement, along with blaze's defintion allows you to blaze many many locations depending on the board. My current understanding is free movement can't repeat steps, but this still allows him to freely deal 2 to large portions of a water based board.

decks.name: Turn em n Burn em (Top 8 Euro Crossroads)
decks.primer:
Play this more midrange than aggro. It takes some getting used to, but ignore your health. It’s not worth it to chump block, for example, against a four power minion attacking your site with a two power minion. Take the damage and then next turn play a kobold or imp to finish the four power off and leave yourself still up one minion. The pathfinder has a slow card advantage. I’ve found that I don’t want to cast two spells on a single turn until I’m ready to charge for a big 10+ damage turn. Most of my matches have my health at around 6-9 health and my opponent at 15~ and then I do a sudden attack to put them at or near DD. Then it’s a matter of pinging that last killing blow. Can’t stress enough how important it is that round 6+ you have 3 more cards in hand than your opponent. You might be lower health, but while they’re top decking, you’ve got options.


Infiltrate is your best friend, but Disintegrate is a close second. Don’t hesitate to use Infiltrate early on a 4 power enemy to let you slow the opponent some. Keep the stolen minion in your back pocket for when you are ready to attack for big damage.

decks.primer:
Welcome to Sorcery's Druidic Order! You have been charged with the sacred duty of reclaiming the holy woodlands. Read on to arm yourself with the knowledge and tools needed to ensure victory!


Ever since the release of Arthurian Legends, I've been quite intrigued by [[Druid]]. In my opinion, this avatar has some of the deepest deck-building options and as such, you never know what you're up against when you see a Druid across the table. The flexibility of build options and three powerful abilities allows Druid to adapt to any metagame. This may or may not actually be a good thing from a game design perspective but it has been a very fun puzzle for me as a deckbuilder.


Sylvan Crusade was designed to attack a very specific expected meta for Season 6 of the TTS League. As this particular list evolves, I'll make notes in the "Card Choices" section to shed light on why certain cards are or are not included based on the current meta. Additionally, I’m going to preserve the original list for posterity.

If you're interested in checking out my other Druid decks, I've included a section at the very end of the primer with links and brief descriptions.


On the surface, Sylvan Crusade looks very similar to the classic Earth/Air Sorcerer Midrange decks of yesteryear and I'm honestly not certain that Druid is a more competitive choice over [[Sorcerer]] for this style of deck. The raw power of Sorcerer is undeniable at this point but, when you start to include a lot of spells that cost 5+ mana, the Sorcerer's ability to cast multiple spells each turn begins to diminish. Is a heavier top end at the expense of card quantity worth it? I think that a lot more testing is required to definitively answer that question but for now, I'm leaning towards yes! Yes, but...you need to leverage the abilities on Druid to make up for the card advantage of Sorcerer.

Historically, the Earth/Air package of beefy minions paired with [[Grapple Shot]] and [[Earthquake]] has been a very effective way to beat Fire-heavy Sorcerer aggro decks like Fury Road or Zalem's Fire/Air deck.

When I was looking at the decks used for qualifier rounds by players in the top cut for Season 6, Sorcerer aggro seemed to have a very hefty meta share. There were also a handful of other aggro decks with [[Flamecaller]], [[Avatar of Air]], and [[Battlemage]]. If players kept with whatever archetypes they used most during the qualifying rounds, there were going to be about 18-19 aggro decks (primarily Sorcerer/Fire), 8-9 [[Archimago]] decks (control or combo), and a small handful of other midrange or combo decks. This data led me to the conclusion that I wanted a deck that had an excellent matchup against Sorcerer aggro while not completely folding to Archimago control. I expected virtually no traditional midrange in this top cut as the general sentiment was that Archimago had pushed it out of the meta.

I considered just going with the old Earth/Air Sorcerer option in the hopes that the card draw would be enough to keep pace with Archimago's overwhelming amount of removal. After some deliberation though, I decided that I wanted to have fun with Druid even if it meant that I was going with a deck that might not be optimal. I still really liked the idea of out-muscling aggro with large Earth minions and I had also seen good results with Grapple Shot paired with [[Bruin]] in my Fire/Air aggro builds. I chose to lean into the aggressive end of the curve a little more to fight Archimago. I figured that most of the control versions were going to have the risk of stumbling on threshold early and the best plan was to try to Door them before they got the threshold to cast [[Divine Healing]]. While the plan of early Death's Door against Archimago is still a good one, some of the cards that I included to pursue this goal ended up being very poor choices.

If I'd had more time to test the deck before top cut submissions were due, I think I would have realized that [[Highland Falconer]] and [[Palliburie Bats]] were not good options for this deck. Despite the fact that they pair well with [[Torshammar Trinket]] and offer some resilience against Earthquake, the reality is that they don't line up well against [[Vile Imp]] and [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]] from the Fire aggro decks and they are particularly bad against all of the [[Magic Missiles]] and [[Firebolts]] from Archimago.

Overall, the deck performed very well though and with a few adjustments, I'm super happy with the current list.


Best cards for specific matchups:


Sorcerer aggro (fire) - [[Bosk Troll]], [[Autumn Unicorn]], [[Daperyll Vampire]], [[Sir Galahad]], [[Earthquake]], [[Whirling Blades]], [[Crusade]], [[Ring of Morrigan]], [[Torshammar Trinket]], [[Shield Maidens]], [[Root Spider]], [[Pillar of Zeiros]], [[Pebbled Paths]], [[Quagmire]], [[Pudge Butcher]]. If your Sorcerer opponent is on Air with Palliburrie Bats, Root Spider becomes much worse and if you're against a Water aggro deck, Earthquake is obviously pretty horrible.


Flamecaller aggro - Same list as above but include [[Funeral Pyre]].


Archimago control - [[Dwarven Digging Team]], [[Shield Maidens]], [[Pudge Butcher]], [[Grandmaster Wizard]], [[Gigantism]], [[Grapple Shot]], [[Whirling Blades]], [[Funeral Pyre]], [[Rift Valley]], [[Kingdom of Agartha]], [[Crusade]], [[Pnakotic Manuscript]].


Avatar of Air - [[Torshammar Trinket]], [[Daperyll Vampire]], [[Sir Galahad]], [[Earthquake]], [[Crusade]], [[Grapple Shot]], [[Whirling Blades]], [[Rift Valley]], [[Ring of Morrigan]]


Mirror Match - [[Torshammar Trinket]], [[Pudge Butcher]], [[Dalcean Phalanx]], [[Root Spider]], [[Earthquake]], [[Grapple Shot]], [[Whirling Blades]].



Card Choices:


[[Bosk Troll]], [[Autumn Unicorn]] - These two minions have some of the most aggressive stat lines in the game and contribute to a critical number of beaters with high power to mana ratios. This is important both for stifling early aggression from aggro opponents and putting solid pressure on Archimago in the early game. Many of the best opening hands include one or both of these cards.


[[Pudge Butcher]], [[Dalcean Phalanx]] - While these minions come with serious mobility restrictions, 5 power for 4 mana is still a fantastic rate and when you pair them with mobility spells such as [[Blink]] or Grapple Shot they become incredibly dangerous. If you don't have mobility options, both of these cards can be a liability against aggro decks. If you are playing against aggro and your opening hand has one or more of these and you don't have Grapple Shot, Blink, or an early minion such as Bosk Troll or Autumn Unicorn, you'll probably want to mulligan them away. Summoning either of these on turn 3 using the extra mana from a Tower is one of the best early plays possible.


[[Root Spider]] - Still one of the best ways to shut down aggro and with Torshammar Trinket, it gets to win the fight against opposing spiders! If you're expecting a Water-heavy meta, or a significant amount of minion-light decks like Archimago or Battlemage, you can certainly trim some number of Root Spiders.


[[Daperyll Vampire]] - While this card has my least favorite art in the whole game, it is an incredibly powerful minion and puts in solid work against most opponents. The list that I used in Season 6 only had one copy of this card and that was a mistake. If you're expecting a lot of aggro in the meta, you should run the full 3 copies. This is one of the best things you can combo with Grapple Shot or [[Whirling Blades]] and it's also dreamy with Torshammar Trinket.


[[Grapple Shot]] - Grapple is still one of the most powerful cards in the game and this list wants the full 4 copies. It is fantastic with any large minion and is particularly sweet with [[Bruin]]. The only downside to Grapple is that you need a minion on the board for it to work and keeping a suitable minion alive can often be a challenge. Being able to flip Druid and immediately Grapple with Bruin is an awesome option.


[[Whirling Blades]] - While this card doesn't work optimally with Dalcean Phalanx and doesn't work at all with Pudge Butcher it is wildly powerful and goes well with just about every other minion in the deck.


[[Earthquake]] - My vote for best Earth card to date! This deck gets to leverage the movement of sites very well with Pudge and Phalanx.


[[Gigantism]] - Another of Earth's most powerful cards here. If you've got 7 mana, Gigantism and Grapple Shot, it's usually enough to Door your opponent in one turn.


[[Blink]] - The best mobility spell there is right now. Blink is necessary for most decks that include things like Pudge Butcher or Dalcean Phalanx and surprise movement is one of the most effective ways to win games.


[[Dwarven Digging Team]] - This card is one of several concessions to the prevalence of Archimago. In many games against Archimago control, your best route to victory is to chip your opponent down to around 15 life and then set up a big attack to Door them on a single turn, thus negating Divine Healing. Being able to build up a small army underground and then pop up for a huge attack is one of the best ways that I've found to accomplish this. Dwarven Digging Team also helps combat enemy Root Spiders. This card is not very good against aggro and I would mulligan it if I was up against Sorcerer, Flamecaller, Avatar of Air, or Battlemage.


[[Kettletop Leprechaun]] - This unassuming little fellow is actually very effective in this deck. Since this deck is interested in going up to 6+ mana - especially if it's a matchup where you want to keep [[Tawny]] around as long as possible - anything that draws a site during the early game is about as good as drawing a spell. Having 2 power makes in considerably better than [[Land Surveyor]] in a deck like this that is looking to get aggressive and even smaller minions can become real threats with Torshammar Trinket and [[Crusade]]. The 4 copies that I had in the original list felt like too many and 2 copies has been feeling pretty good.


[[Shield Maidens]] - Not including this card in my Season 6 list was a mistake. It is incredibly powerful against Fire-heavy aggro and provides your whole team with protection against [[Poison Nova]] from Archimago.


[[Sir Galahad]] - This card looked like it was going to be pretty solid but I was not prepared for just how incredible it actually is in the current meta. It prevents damage from some of the most popular minions such as Vile Imp, Pudge Butcher, Daperyll Vampire, and [[Headless Haunt]]. It is very difficult to kill in combat or with damage-based removal and it even survives [[Chaos Twister]] if it lands on a site (with split power/toughness, Chaos Twister adds both numbers together and divides by 2 before rounding up. This means that Galahad only deals 5 damage if it lands on a site after being targeted by Twister). You can also use Pudge Butcher to fight Galahad if you really need to gain 3 life.


[[Grandmaster Wizard]] - The Season 6 list had a single [[Unlikely Alliance]] as a way to catch back up on cards against Archimago. Alliance worked nicely with Highland Falconer/Palliburie Bats and Tawny/Bruin but with the Falconer/Bats package out of the deck, it just isn't reliable enough. Grandmaster Wizard is 6 mana but it is a guaranteed 3 spells which is exactly what this deck wants on later turns. With 3 copies of Trinket in the deck, the 0-power body isn't completely irrelevant either!


[[Highland Princess]] - Any deck that is running good 1-mana artifacts and can get 2 Air threshold should probably include Princess.


[[Disenchant]] - This is a card that is very meta-dependent and always comes with the risk of being a dead draw. I still think it's probably worth including a single copy but I also think you could easily trim it and be fine.


[[Torshammar Trinket]] - This card is so good with Tawny that I really like including the full 3 copies. It makes most combat situations favorable for you on your turn, can't be hit with removal like Disenchant, and is insane with Ring of Morrigan. I think that Trinket is one of the best cards in the current meta.


[[Ring of Morrigan]] - Ring good.


[[Philosopher's Stone]] - With a good mix of multiple elements, Philosopher's Stone is still among the most useful cards available.


[[Pnakotic Manuscript]] - This card is very good with Tawny but can also be used by Dalcean Phalanx or Pudge Butcher of their movement restrictions are preventing them from being effective. I'm still not 100% certain that this card belongs in this list but I do like it and we'll see how further testing goes.


[[Crusade]] - Once you get to around 20 Earth minions in your deck, Crusade starts looking very appealing. Archimago uses a lot of defensive sites like [[Perilous Bridge]] and [[Gnome Hollows]] and Crusade allows you to skip right over those cards. It's also one of the best ways to fight against [[Jihad]] from the Fire aggro decks. Keep in mind that Bruin is a Earth minion and will get the +1!


[[Feast for Crows]] - while this card is particularly bad against aggro, it is incredibly useful against Archimago. I think that this deck has a good enough matchup against aggro to afford a few cards like this and still be ok.


[[Dark Tower]]/[[Gothic Tower]]/[[Lone Tower]] - The best mana accelerant sites in the game. Jumping the curve on early minions is one of the best paths to victory.


[[Funeral Pyre]] - No Fire, 3 Pyre! Archimago is this much of a problem. Typically decks with threshold requirements like this can afford 3-5 off-element, utility sites. I would love to be able to play more [[Wizard's Den]], [[Sinkhole]], [[Free City]], [[Town]], etc., but stripping Archimago of cards is just too important right now. You'll also be happy to see Pyres against any [[Deathspeaker]] opponents you run across.


[[Glastonbury Tor]]/[[The Colour Out of Space]] - While both of these sites can be a liability against opposing Earthquakes they are a necessary inclusion for the threshold requirements. If you're playing against an Earth opponent, try to spread them out so they can't both be hit by the same Earthquake.


[[Impenetrable Copse]] - Copse is fantastic against Archimago and other decks using Grapple Shot or Pudge Butcher.


[[Kingdom of Agartha]] - There is some tension between this card and the two copies of Earthquake but Kingdom is so good against Archimago that I think it's worth the risk.


[[Mirror Realm]] - It's rare that a deck doesn't want Mirror Realm and this certainly isn't one of those rare decks.


[[Pebbled Paths]]/[[Quagmire]] - These are the two most effective Earth sites when you're facing against Fire aggro. With how much charge is in the meta right now, I think that pretty much all heavy-Earth decks want a good number of these sites.


[[Pillar of Zeiros]] - Deathspeaker has fallen off considerably in past months but the healing effect from Pillar is still very useful.


[[Rift Valley]] - One of the best sites in the game, Rift Valley should be included in just about every Earth deck.


[[Valley of Delight]]/[[Windmill]] - Great fixing for multi-element decks.


[[Watchtower]] - While [[Infiltrate]] isn't seeing as much play right now, it is still out there and one of the best things against your large minions. [[Morgana le Fay]] and [[Phase Assassin]] are also two big metagame players right now.


[[Wizard's Den]] - With very few options for drawing additional spells, Wizard's Den is a welcome inclusion and I wish that I could fit the second copy in here. If you expect less Archimago, you can definitely swap out a Funeral Pyre for an extra Den.


[[Highland Falconer]]/[[Palliburrie Bats]] (currently out of the deck) - This package works really well against decks that use things like [[Bury]] or Earthquake as their primary removal. They are also fantastic at driving out enemy Root Spiders. The two bodies that you get when you cast Falconer are nice with Torshammar Trinket. This package is currently out of the deck because Archimago has a ton of things like Magic Missiles and the Fire aggro decks have Vile Imp and Quarrelsome Kobolds.


[[Unlikely Alliance]] (currently out of the deck) - With the removal of Highland Falconer and Palliburrie Bats, this card just isn't reliable enough.


[[Vanguard Knights]] (currently out of the deck) - I really like that Vanguard Knights can be played off of a turn 1 Earth site into turn 2 Tower (something that Autumn Unicorn can't). It is also really cool that you can sneak the Knights onto Gnome Hollows. If you start their movement as 2-power they don't become 4-power until they're actually on the Hollows. This card can be incredibly awkward and ultimately, I've decided to bench it for now.


[[Atlas Wanderers]] (currently out of the deck) - While the ability on this card can be very useful, the triple Earth threshold and the fact that it isn't significantly more powerful than most of the other minions at the 4-5 mana range led me to cut the single copy that I had in my initial list.


[[Bury]] (currently out of the deck) - The Fire-based aggro decks have tons of small minions that make Bury feel underwhelming. Archimago has virtually no minions that you care about so Bury is just a weaker Disenchant for their artifacts. If non-water midrange makes more of a comeback, I would put Bury back in but for now, it's out and the cut has been feeling correct.


[[Common Sense]] (currently out of the deck) - With 0 copies of Bury, the Common Sense package began to look too small. The flexibility is nice for sure but so far, I haven't been missing it much in testing.



Notable Exclusions:


[[Dream-Quest]] - Even though this deck is looking to keep Tawny around for as long as possible, I don't like that Dream-Quest is mostly dead once you flip Druid. Additionally, the core of this deck is mostly just interchangeable, large minions and removal. Many Druid decks do want Dream-Quest but I don't think that this is one of them.


[[Drums of Doom]] - This deck is already very good at beating minion-heavy aggro decks and I didn't feel like I needed the help of Drums for those matchups. Since this is a deck with lots of large minions that are already going to dominate most combat situations, Drums can end up backfiring really badly for you (particularly against Fire) by allowing your opponents' smaller minions to trade up. Finally, Drums does virtually nothing against Archimago. With all of this in mind, it didn't make sense to include them.



Other Druid lists that I've been tuning:


Sylvan Crusade with a Dash of Fire - With Glastonbury Tor, The Colour out of Space, 3 Funeral Pyre, and Valley of Delight already in the deck, I figured that I could add in a few additional Fire sites and splash for [[Poison Nova]]. Nova is really good with Tawny and Shield Maidens and while I'm not sure that this splash is better than sticking to Earth/Air, it has been working well enough to warrant further testing.


Heavy Meta Druid - This list dips deeper into Fire for things like [[Morgana le Fay]], [[Sir Balin]], [[Sir Kay]], [[Sir Morien]], and [[Pact with the Devil]] while retaining a good amount of the beefy Earth package.


Swamp Song - This is the least tested of my Druid decks and I think also the weakest in the current meta. It uses lots of Water sites to play around Earthquake while tapping into a flexible menagerie of Beasts and Mortals.


The Art of War - A hyper-aggro Fire/Air deck that goes all in on charge minions and splashes for Grapple Shot. Lots of the proximity spells in Fire work nicely with [[Tawny]]!


Druid's Deep - My original Druid deck that is mostly Water with a splash of Air for things like [[Grapple Shot]] and [[Dream-Quest]]. This deck has lots of massive, top-end minions like [[Diluvian Kraken]] and [[Great Old One]].

decks.name: ANZ Championship Top 8 Elementalist
decks.primer:
My Elementalist control deck that managed to squeak into the top 8 at Plenty of Games in Melbourne 6/7 April. Good against minion-based aggro, Ok against other control builds, very poor against Avatar of Earth.

My biggest takeaway of the weekend is that I just wish I had more time to play and practise beforehand.The top 8 game was my second match against Enchantress ever, and it was definitely a trial by fire. I learned a lot, but made some poor decisions and misplays along the way, but as long as I can get people talking about the game, then that’s a big win in my book.

The build is something I’ve tinkered with over the last couple of months in league play, and it features some of my favourite cards that may not necessarily be tournament all-stars, but I enjoy them immensely.

It was a fantastic event, so big thanks to Jesse and the team at Plenty of Games.


Edit: The deck isn’t primarily a Roots deck, but has it as a backup plan to help regain board control. As such, it doesn’t recover super well compared to other builds. Instead the deck is more ramp and control to set up the Orb combo kill. As such the deck struggles against mobile avatars that are coming into your side of the board. I was hoping to play more sorcerer, where cards like poison nova help take away their card advantage. Geistwood is the most powerful card in the deck, and is probably a better mulligan than Roots a lot of the time.

decks.name: Fury Road (The Library Edition) - Winner at Sin City Open 2025
decks.primer:
Introduction + Acknowledgments

This deck is based on the original and AL edits to Fury Road from @Sorcelled.


I've been intrigued by Fury Road ever since @abarth, a fellow Beast of the Bay, showed up to a meetup with a copy of it. I kept modifying some parts of it to better fit my play style (adding [[Sinkhole]]s, removing things like [[Gigantism]]) and played it at Quest for the Crown to a top 4 finish, losing only to the aforementioned @abarth, who won that event. I further refined my decklist to what I played in the Finals of Yeticon 2025 vs. @Sorcelled.


This is my take on the deck. It is definitely crafted to my playstyle, so there are choices that are unique to me (i.e. no more [[Sleeping Giantess]], no need for Deserts, etc.). I welcome comments and feedback.


Sin City Open 2025 Tournament Result

There were 17 players in the Sin City Open 2025 event that took place in Las Vegas, Nevada on Friday, January 17, 2025.


Round 1: Win 1:0 vs. Justin Watte with [[Archimago]] (Earth/Air)

This game went a bit over time because we got started late. Justin put together quite a lot of pressure with [[Border Patrol]], and eventually I was on Death's Door with him having prevented me from getting him to Death's Door with a [[Root Spider]] for my pair of [[Brother Knight]]s. I had cleared most of the board when he got out [[The Ninth Legion]]. They were just too slow to catch up to my [[Sorcerer]] running around the board though, and I was able to drop Justin to 0, and finish up with the killing blow.


Round 2: Win 1-0 vs. Brian Vegso with [[Deathspeaker]]

I almost lost this game essentially on turn 1. Brian started the game with a turn 2 [[Thunderstorm]] placed right atop my avatar. Rather than play a second site in front of my avatar (because it would also still be subject to the aura), I played my second site to the left. I summoned a [[War Horse]], which picked up my Sorcerer and brough them to safety on the new site. This got me away from the storm, and let me still continue to build resources. A few turns later I had enough charge minions to take Brian to Death's Door, and then win the game.


Round 3: Win 1-0 vs. Jared Miller

To be written


Round 4: Win 1-0 vs. Neil Troy with [[Druid]] (Earth/Air)

We had tested this matchup just before the event, and it very much went in Neil's favor. In this round, however, Neil didn't draw enough early pressure, and I was able to pin down Tawny + a [[Bosk Troll]] with a [[Root Spider]] early in the game. This let me build up my mana, and then switch to 2 cards/turn mode, at which point I could start making more 1-for-1 and 2-for-1 trades of my own cards for the remainder of Neil's minions. Neil had an early Angel's Egg, so instead of spending my charge minions early to just get in for ~1 damage, I saved them for getting rid of Neil's minions, and for future assaults. In discussing the game right afterwards, Neil and I settled on this being an example of properly assessing who's the beatdown. By establishing myself in a more control role, I was able to better utilize my cards to neutralize the few threats being presented. I eventually drew into a [[Morgana Le Fay]], which gave me a [[Ring of Morrigan]]! Morgana eventually helped with removing the [[Angel's Egg]], which allowed me to quickly drop Neil to 0.


Thoughts

[[War Horse]] remains one of the best cards in the deck, almost singlehandedly being responsible for my win in round 2. Charge minions are powerful (and [[Pebbled Paths]] are plentiful), so finding other interesting spots to leverage their speed is critical. I am less convinced of the powers of [[Redcap Powries]], hence already having cut them to 2. [[Sinkhole]] remains very effective for me, and there was definitely a point where I was able to destroy a site, fill it in with a new site of my own, and charge forward.


Prizes!

I won a sweet Superbowl-style ring with a Pathfinder on it that says "Sin City Open 2025 Sorcery Champion". I also selected an event-stamped [[The Colour Out of Space]] and got it signed by some of the other folks who were there. I wore the ring for the Old School event the next day as well.

decks.primer:
Intended for competitive play

*******************************************************************


Overall: This is a control combo deck. Leviathan + graple shot being your 'combo'. The core of the deck is control combo. Dont activate leviathan unless you can at least hit twice. Try to door with leviathan combo by sneaking 4 damage somewhere. Use lightbolt/graple/firebolt/kobolds as finishers.


Note: This is not an easy deck to play. Sometimes you draw the wrong half of your deck against a matchup and lose but site placement can help mitigate that quite a bit.


Matchup Info:

Deathspeaker - slight disadvantage, dont feed them free creatures. Save common sense for early summoning/jihads. play curse on you in the endgame to prevent jhin OTK for a turn or two before they have the mana. Use courtesan to waste their resources once they've started to draw a lot or door them with their own jhin! Non jhin lists are favored.

Sorcerer (Cute/Goblins) - unfavored. Their general gameplan ignores some of your defences. Mariners curse and kobolds are your mvps. It really comes down to if you can draw what you need.

Sorcerer (fury road) - slightly favored. Jihad and a good rift valley will easily tilt it in their favor

Sorcerer (Air/Earth) - slight favored. straightforward matchup

Seer(Yg combo) - playable if you tech for it... If you see seer, dig for common sense/puffer fish early and dont deploy leviathan until pop. If you don't it goes from bad to absolutely terrible.

Other(yg combo) - even / slight advantage. The weakened beatdown/control strategy is something you can easily get ahead of and they will feel safe even with an empty board. Easy to OTK.

Battlemage - Favored, frogs and wheenies stem life lost early. Common sense package destroys artifact based BM.

Avatar earth - Slightly Favored. Displacing your lands puts you on the backfoot early and easily makes up for them having dead removal. The fire variant is harder to deal with as your chumpers die efficiently.

Avatar of air (air only) - Slight disadvantage. The free movement allows their already aggressive deck to be slightly faster. Don't give them free sites to attack or place harmful artifiacts. Muligan aggressively for eggs.

Sorcerer (spirits) - Strong disadvantage/slight disadvantage. Charge and stealth is a problem. If they are running haunts the matchup is even because that deck is a lot worse than big midrange spirits.

Deathspeaker(spirits) - Favored. Clumsy early aggro is easy to chump/deal with and you door them before their top end occurs. Don't feed them free creatures.

Sorcerer/PF(spell control) - Even. Lack of healing means all their spells are good when cast on you unless you draw your eggs. Threats are stick or do something as they come down so its usually always ok to let them die to removal.

Flamespeaker - Even. Can easily lose to great starts (jihad mainly) especially if you don't place your sites correctly

Big water decks - Slight disadvantage. You draw more cards and have decent cards against them. Can't deal with submerge so play around that and it's not bad. Use mariners curse to delay their attacks until they start stockpiling submerge minions. Really its who draws better. You win sideboard hard.

Enchantress (control) - advantage, you have more card advantage and the removal they run generally is reactive while also being threat light. Easy to OTK

Enchantress (aggro/midrange) - slight disadvantage / disadvantage depending on flavor. Some of your removal is hard to use on their threats and often gum up the board.


Mulligans:

-Mulligan lands aggressively for leviathan or threshold if you happen to draw princess in your opener.

-Generally mulligan sites until you hit island leviathan/tadpole pool for placement at site (2).

-Mulligan aggressively for the matchup in the spell card slots but keep obviously (slow) powerful cards if you feel comfortable with the sites you have.

-I generally snap keep princess, curse, land surveyor, and egg


Site placement:

Generally in order of placement

**3 2 3**

4 3 1 3 4


Minor note: Don't play non water sites at 2 or 3 if you are playing something you suspect has rift valley.


1 = dual land / leviathan

2 = bottomless pit / tadpole pool / geistwood ideally / leviathan / any water site

3 = anything, ideally leviathan

4 = non water sites because its easy to protect


General tips:

-You dont win early

-Try to stall your opponent with land placement and chump blockers with the defensive site placement stated above.

- leviathans + graple or a big ruler of thule turn

-try not to activate your leviathans right away unless you can door or the coast is clear (opponent is hellbent or is unlikely to have a good answer)

-Beware of rift valley on a non water site placed forward. Rift valley is the best anything against you.


Specific Tips:

-turtles + manuscript is a draw every turn without it dying.

-Quarrelsome kobolds can safely be placed on the backrow to setup ruler of thule/polar explorer turn

-Kobolds can be used to kill your minions on geistwood if you dont need to block if you opt to run it.

-if you arent feeling extreme pressure and have angels egg + frogs, submerge them so you dont get them disenchanted

-atlantean fate can clutch out your 8 water pips when you draw a lot of non water sites or make it safe to run out leviathans into bury.

decks.name: Gen Con 2023 Tournament Winner - Jarrett Messing's Impstorm  (Deathspeaker Air/Fire)
decks.primer:
I find myself in the surprising position to provide insight into the deck that won the Sorcery constructed tournament at Gen Con 2023. You might find this less of a deck tech and more of my thought process going into the event. The decisions that led me to this deck were as much personal as game related. The former, the personal, is inherently so specific as to be rarely addressed in analysis, but it is an equally important element in tournament success. I don't have any astonishing insights into how to build a meta-breaking, tournament-dominating deck. This is more of a lesson in how to stumble forward with what you know.


I prepared with a pair of assumptions:


1) It seemed likely that Air/Earth midrange would be the predominant build. Early successes established this as the preeminent powerhouse, and with limited card supply I suspected this would be one of the easier decks to build for folks who didn't pledge or pledge big. Much of the power is in the ordinary and exceptional slots, and many of the key cards are contained in the preconstructed decks, including one of the best avatars for it (Earth). A Pathfinder based version of this deck seemed on the verge of winning the second season of the TTS league. It's just a damn good, consistent deck that runs a lot of the best cards in the game, capable of big bursts of damage, strong board presence, board manipulation, burst healing, with great removal and maneuver.  


2) I would be playing [[Deathspeaker]]. It seemed close in power to the air/earth deck, if a bit less consistently good, and I had far more reps with it in and out of the TTS league. I did not have time to deviate from my comfort zone and get sufficient practice with anything before the con. The goals of the deck are straightforward. Draw as much as possible through recursion, don't allow heavy hitters to stick around, and maximize damage until you can [[Major Explosion]] or [[Nimbus Jinn]] the opponent to Death's Door. Finishers abound. Pretty simple, right? 


My most difficult choice came down to elements: Air/Earth/Fire, Air/Earth or Air/Fire? Air has the wizards for the card draw, so that was automatic, and Alpha Thunderstorm*. Earth has possibly the best overall suite of spells. Fire offers some of the best options for Deathspeaker in [[Vile Imp]] and [[Death Dealer]], one of the best removal spells in [[Infiltrate]], and best damage in Major Explosion. Take all three perhaps? Well, truthfully, there are more good options with the three elements than fit in a deck, and taking all three elements comes with the cost. Occasionally you will bump into a threshold problem and that can throw a wrench in things, especially if you're running triple threshold cards like [[Divine Healing]] and [[Browse]]. This makes you more dependent on Cores which can be ripped away at inconvenient times. There were three main reasons I decided against Earth. The [[Avatar of Earth]], playing into Earth, is especially devastating. She can grapple across the table with impunity as you're bolstering her with your own sites. I want my opponent to stay on their side of the table. Also, I knew of several off-meta Water decks in attendance, and suspected more. Water hampers many of Earth's best spells. Thirdly, Earth seemed like the slower road to the end game. [[Wraetannis Titan]] requires Sphere offensively, [[Craterize]] is a turn and a tax behind Major Explosion, and healing is prolongation, not acceleration. I felt like I would want the most linear path to Death's Door possible, and to win a race in the mirror match. 


Somewhat ironically, my game 5 finals opponent, Adam (Zalem), consistently one of the best Sorcery players throughout the league and playtests, helped solidify my choice and finalize my deck. After hammering out my idea on Curiosa I decided to see if anyone was running something similar. Lo, Zalem had built an Air/Fire Deathspeaker deck! And it was nearly identical! This gave me a huge confidence boost. His differences were one less Thunderstorm and an additional two [[Chaos Twister]]. I liked my four [[Firebolts]], and I hadn't considered the latter at all in any kind of serious format. But upon checking the Twister FAQ, and with some consideration I saw the incredible upside. You are very likely to remove the target, between the void and sites, and with some luck you have a potential 2-for-1 by slinging it into another minion, or direct damage by hitting the opposing avatar. Funnily enough, when I told this to Zalem, he said it was one of his cuts before the event due to inconsistency! 


Key Cards

[[Thunderstorm]]. *A note on Alpha Thunderstorm. This event used the RAW version of Thunderstorm, the Alpha high T version. It's extremely powerful as it ticks down only when you shoot a bolt, and can linger and move until exhausted. 4 mana, 9 damage. This is amazing, almost immediate pressure. Thunderstorm pairs extremely well with some of the other spells and sites in the deck. Fire's Deserts can clear bolt-absorbers, as can Firebolts, assuring the bolts hit the enemy avatar. I wasn't going to play this event without three. This card will be brought in line for Beta. Three Thunderstorms was a winning choice.


[[Infiltrate]]

Arguably the best removal spell in the game, this card takes your opponent's minion from them and gives you control of that minion with stealth until they deal damage. Notably, when attacking an undefended enemy site, you cause a loss of life rather than damage. Incredible potential, and a huge swing when you can eliminate a beater. I was particularly keen on this as if I stole a 5-power minion from an Earth deck I would now be able to trade their minion with another of their 5-power beaters. 


[[Summoning Sphere]]

Part of the win condition of this deck, a Summoning Sphere + Imp can finish an avatar on Death's Door. It allows me to play a Djinn and dump my hand to bring an avatar to 0. Alternatively, a sphere opener can allow me to play an Imp on their avatar turn 2, which puts a lot of pressure on the opponent to spend removal or get their own minion out at home. 


[[Vile Imp]]

The magnificent Imp! Pinpoint damage, harassment, finishing blow all in an inexpensive and annoying body. 


Apprentice/[[Grandmaster Wizard]]

Draw/Draw more. X2. Maybe x3 or x4 with Geistwood and Pact.


[[Major Explosion]]

The finisher. It's very hard to do sufficient chip damage to finish off an avatar, even with Thunderstorm. Seven mana is not that difficult to cast, and you're often one move away from launching this across the table. The 5 damage splash zone clears Earth heavies. It has the added benefit of clearing the immediate area of Thunderstorm bodyguards. 


[[Highland Falconer]]/[[Sacred Scarabs]]

Exploding flying bugs! Easy four damage and 2-for-1 retrieval. I got rid of scarabs with mulligans every game I drew them in my opening hand. Better to draw some kind of ramp or a recurrable falconer to fetch one. 


So it all worked out! It took some luck as it always does, but the deck performed extremely and consistently well. I stayed within myself, and the flow of play was very familiar despite the lack of reps with this particular build. Most importantly, I played five great opponents who were a pleasure to share the table with, foremost among them being Adam in the final. Nerves came with the stakes, but the game could not have been more friendly. And, despite his rough opening, he had me on Death's Door and was one turn away from snatching away the victory! Wild end to the event!

decks.name: SCRCON 2026 | 7th Place | Constructed Championship
decks.primer:
"Evil, Fliers and Ranged, OH MY!"


The TLDR:


Evil:

  • Vile Imp, Redmayne Hyena, Spore Spouts and Desecrate. Do the math.
  • You know who loves Desecrated Ground? Evil minions. What's better than a 5 power Legion of Gall? A 6 power Legion of Gall.


Fliers:

  • We've got 14 fliers and over half of them are 4+ power and either gain us life, wreck our opponent's Collection, or just cause a friggin headache!


Ranged:

  • A playset of Stygian Archers and Skirmishers of Mu? Yes. And I'd play more if I could!
  • Shout out to MTR Joseph (the one and only Realm Eater pilot in the Constructed Championship at SCRCON) for enlightening me on how disgusting Skirmishers can actually be. To be continued in full primer...


Ideal Early Game Plays:

  • T1 Tower > Forsaken into a T3 Desecrate to mess with our opponent's Affinity
  • T2 Spore Spouts > Vile Imp into a T3 Desecrate
  • T3 Jack the Ripper their Aino or Morgana into a T4 Desecrate


omg why does this guy love Desecrate so much...


Desecrate:

  • Think back at games you lost because of a well placed Smokestacks, Thin Ice, Troll Bridge, Bottomless Pit, Perilous Bridge, etc... yea. Desecrate handles that.
  • Buff your minions. Forsaken seems innocent until it hits for 3, Desecrates for 3, and then becomes a 4 power minion. "We have Lugbog Cat at home, sweetie".
  • Timing is everything, though. If you can't Move and Attack with your Evil minion without risking a trade then you're not set up for a Desecrate. But we're piloting AoA baby, oh and we have even more tech for that... stay tuned for the full primer!


Other Spells:

  • Arcane Barrage beats Ward as long as you can pay the minions power + 1. It wreaks havoc on tokens, is nightmare fuel against Imposter and can close out nearly any game thanks to AoA's inherent maneuverability.
  • Browse to hunt for Desecrate... (i know, i have a problem)
  • Disenchant. Because Ring and A. Fate exist.
  • Feast for Crows. F**k Mesmerism. (Both games I've lost to CJ at major events he beat me with Mesmerism... well, and because he's a top-notch player)
  • Grapple Shot and Whirling Blades. I don't need to explain these - but - imagine your opponent plays their Archangel and you've got a Stygian Archers in play with a Trinket and Grapple Shot in hand. You Trinket your Archers, Grapple the Archangel to break ward and Ranged strike for 4 while getting an Allied Skelly to boot. It feels, so, good. Now imagine casting Whirling Blades on your Archers and killing more than one enemy minion to then replace each of them with Allied Skellys? Disgusting. Wait, Skellys are Evil right? Did someone say Desecrate?
  • Infiltrate and Poison Nova: unarguably two of the most impactful Fire spells at the single-Fire threshold level. These two spells are what forced me into splashing fire. Trust me, I hate having to run the castles, Colour and Ruins in place of other Air or utility sites, but I truly believe Infiltrate and Poison Nova are worth it.


Full primer to come...


Cheers and great games to everyone I played at SCRCON 2026!!!

decks.name: SCG Con Las Vegas Limited Championship Top 8 Draft 1st Place
Avatar of Air - 1st Place Cornerstone Championship
decks.primer:
This is a Gothic mid-range Air/Earth deck with Avatar of Air for mobility. It's not too different from the typical air/earth mid range gameplay that encourages an aggressive early-mid game with late-game finishers. With the changes to Guisarm and other "Strike" effects, you're not going for the OTK and instead looking to constantly apply pressure.


---------- Artfiacts:

Onyx Core is to help ramp and fix Earth Threshold. Torshammer Trinkets are to help deal more damage and make trades more favorable. Toolbox is to provide answers when you need them but more often than not it is to pull Zap! out from the collection to kill your opponent at Death's Door. You could argue running a 3 of to add consistency to access to the cards.


Rolling Boulder is a typical card to have in an Avatar of Air deck, however with Gothic we have a brand new toy to play with in Lord of Greed. You can now roll the boulder and have Lord of Greed bring it back at the end of turn.


---------- Minions:

Most minions don't' need explanation as they are typical valuable creatures to fly into your opponent's board with AoA.


Men of Leng is a personal pet card of mine that if played at the right time can be very hard to deal with and can take a few cards from your opponent. Use your Blinks, Wuthering Heights, and AoA to fling them to the back row and force some discards.


Skeleton Mage is a fantastic new addition to the roster of air minions as it not only lets you recast your magic, but you can also cast opponent magics that you may need (specifically says "a cemetery" not "your cemetery").


All of the ranged units become extremely difficult to play around with air's mobility. Stygian Archers are one of my favorite new additions. Kill stuff, gain benefits. Doesn't get more satisfying than that.


Daperyll Vampires are probably the most questionable minion on the list. With the changes to how they work in that you no longer get health when striking a site, they lost a lot of luster. However, they are still an airborne minion that is hard to deal with sometimes. They are the most likely to be replaced for lower-cost aggressive targets. And they've also been outclassed by one of my new favorite Airborne minions which are:


Legion of Gall are a fantastic minion. Never would they have printed a 5 mana 5 power Airborne unit in Beta, but they did it in Gothic and gave it an upside. These guys are a monster to deal with, especially early with a tower. On top of them dominating the air, they also remove cards from your opponent's collection. So you get to see what kind of answers they may have and remove their best options.


Lord of Fear is a game ender. Enemies can't defend alone is a huge effect and makes your offense feel so much more powerful. You get to trade better. You get to attack without being blocked. And most importantly Death's Door is scarier than ever.


Lord of Greed is an answer to your opponent's artifacts and he has an upside of having some fun synergy with Rolling Boulder. I debated over 2 of Fear over Greed but there are just too many good artifacts in this game that you want to shut them down as often as you can. We don't have Swap so this is one of our best and consistent answers to artifacts.


---------- Magic:

There are a lot of typical tempo spells you will see in a deck like this but there are a few cards that I want to talk about. Namely Gift of the Wolf and Vanishment.


Gift of the Wolf is a fantastic new card and I feel it might be overlooked very often at first glance. This card is so good at making trades, or just getting extra damage in with a ranged strike or site attack. The fact that it replaces itself and also is a great target for Skeleton Mage is what helped it earn its slots in the deck. I replaced Gigantism with this because Gift of the Wolf more easily fits into turns. Gigantism is still good, but often your opponent will have chump blockers making it have less opportunities to be used.


Vanishment is another one of my own personal pet cards. I like cards that replace themselves, and this does so and protects your board state. Plenty of times I find myself just ahead enough and Vanishment guarantees I stay ahead on my opponent's next turn most of the time.


---------- Sites:


My site choices are very defensive. Stuff like Perilous Bridge, Mountain Pass, and No Man's Land let you take advantage of AoA's mobility while shutting down your opponent's ability to strike back. The quality of sites drastically increased in Gothic. Double threshold sites are an amazing new addition. Learning how to mulligan sites is a process with this deck. Placement of air sites and defensive sites is something you will get used to after playing for a bit. Wuthering Heights is a new site that replicates AoA's ability. This lets you double fly units and get them further in to enemy territory.


Collection:

3 Ghouls

1 Amazon Warriors

1 Bury

1 Dispel

1 Disenchant

1 Murder of Crows

1 Gift of the Raven

1 Zap!

My Elementalist control deck that managed to squeak into the top 8 at Plenty of Games in Melbourne 6/7 April. Good against minion-based aggro, Ok against other control builds, very poor against Avatar of Earth.

My biggest takeaway of the weekend is that I just wish I had more time to play and practise beforehand.The top 8 game was my second match against Enchantress ever, and it was definitely a trial by fire. I learned a lot, but made some poor decisions and misplays along the way, but as long as I can get people talking about the game, then that’s a big win in my book.

The build is something I’ve tinkered with over the last couple of months in league play, and it features some of my favourite cards that may not necessarily be tournament all-stars, but I enjoy them immensely.

It was a fantastic event, so big thanks to Jesse and the team at Plenty of Games.


Edit: The deck isn’t primarily a Roots deck, but has it as a backup plan to help regain board control. As such, it doesn’t recover super well compared to other builds. Instead the deck is more ramp and control to set up the Orb combo kill. As such the deck struggles against mobile avatars that are coming into your side of the board. I was hoping to play more sorcerer, where cards like poison nova help take away their card advantage. Geistwood is the most powerful card in the deck, and is probably a better mulligan than Roots a lot of the time.

decks.name: Tournament Pathfinder
decks.primer:
Edit after local tournament (ended up 3:2)

Added extra sinterfree as an answer to those Coy Nixies and also 1 Infernal legion which can be realy great finisher.


Overview

This is a standard aggro build with some spicy inclusions from the Gothic set. The deck aims to apply early pressure, spread threats across the board, and force your opponent into a defensive death door as quickly as possible.


Key Card Choices

Draught — A silver bullet for water-heavy matchups. If the meta shifts toward water decks, this card can completely swing the game in your favor, especially when drawn early.

Gift of the Serpent — Excellent cycle card that also enables your low-value minions to trade up into larger threats. Never underestimate the tempo this provides.

Sinterfee — Fantastic removal bait. Opponents often feel compelled to answer this card immediately, which clears the way for your actual key threats. Whether it eats a removal spell or sticks on the board, you're winning either way.


Site Selection

Since this avatar doesn't rely on drawing a site for its power, I've included utility sites that disrupt common strategies:

  • Garden of Eden — Shuts down control decks that depend on card draw
  • Temple of Moloch — Provides extra mana for explosive combo turns
  • River of Blood — Neutralizes Ring of Morrigan healing, which works in our favor as the aggressor
  • Kor Krematory — Absolutely devastating against graveyard-reliant avatars

Mulligan Guide

Look for strong 2–3 drops. War Horse is particularly valuable for establishing sites in enemy territory, which is almost always advantageous for our gameplan.


General Tips

  • Don't stack minions together — cards like Earthquake and Atlantean Fate punish clustering
  • Spread your threats across the board
  • Prioritize attacking sites to accelerate your opponent's deaths door
  • Accept that aggro has variance — your first three draws heavily influence your win rate


Good luck and go fast!

Yo, so this list has been incredibly good in terms of results going a total of 43(61 as of 2024/01/09) wins, 7(19) losses and 1 draw(?) where we were both on deaths door and both died to a craterize. (Several hundrwd more games have been played, please refer to the bottom of this primer)


The deck's worst match up by far is avatar of earth which just aggro's you out of the game and kills you quicker than you can resource lock them, with an avatar that is big enough to fight over your bodies.

The deck has only a single loss(3 now) into death speaker so far, it becomes very easy to lock their resources before they have the djinn combo kill, and sometimes you can just avoid it entirely by sitting on a gnome hollows and deleting all the surrounding sites with lord of the voids.
